This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Apricorn
quests.subtitle: Not Apricot, that's different!
quests.description:
Apricorn Trees spawn everywhere! Just pretty rare. 

They are same size as Oak Trees, with Yellowish Brownish Leaves and Brown Logs. 

On the Leaves, Apricorns will Sprout. Once Matured, you can Right Click them to Harvest. 

There are 7 Apricorns: Red, Yellow, Green, Blue, Pink, Black, and White. The Color does matter for other Recipes.

quests.title: Remedy
quests.description:
Remedy is made from Smelting a Big Root. 

It is an Item that can be Fed to a Pokemon in or out of Battle to restore Health (not at the exchange for Friendship). 

You can Craft with it to make even better Remedies!

quests.title: 73C7479D929498AE
quests.description:
Big Roots spawn from the Ceilings of Caves, like Glowberries. 

They spawn above Deepslate! 

Sometimes it might actually be an Energy Root that looks and spawns like a Big Root.

quests.title: Pokedex
quests.description:
The Pokedex is a very important tool. It works as a Glossary for every Pokemon in the game! 

If a Pokemon is Fought in Battle, its Name, Picture, Animation, and Sound will show up. 

If a Pokemon is Captured you'll get all of those plus: Type, Entry, Ability, Height and Weight, Base Stats, and Drops. 

There is a Search Bar where you can search by Name, Ability, and Drops. So if it is set to Drops, you can look up Clay Balls to see what Pokemon Drop those on Death. Or if you want the Ability Identify, add that with the Ability Filter to see which Pokemon have Identify.

quests.title: Pokepedia
quests.description:
Once you pick a Starter you'll be granted the Pokepedia! 

This is the Guide book for all things Cobblemon. 

I guess if you wanted to just follow the book instead of the Quests you could... 

I'd prefer if you follow both!

quests.title: Pokeballs
quests.description:
The key to Catching Pokemon! The Pokeball! 

You can use them only on Wild Pokemon either in the Wild or in Battle. In the Wild just aim your Pokeball at a Pokemon, and Right Click to Throw it! 

In Battle you'll need to choose the Catch Button. This will take a break from the Battle to let you try and Catch them. 

After Throwing the Pokeball it will be used up. Either it will Catch the Pokemon and they will become part of your Team or added to your PC. 

If the Ball fails to Catch them nothing will happen unless you were in a Battle. If it fails, you will lose your Turn in Battle. 

Different Balls have different Catch Rates. The higher the better! Also weaker Pokemon and Damaged Pokemon are easier to Catch.

quests.title: Pokemon Battles
quests.description:
Battling Pokemon! Oh yeah that is what we are all here for! Finally... 

Default to Fight against Trainers or Wild Pokemon is (R). We then get a few choices in what to do. 

Each Fight goes in Turns, with you going first then them. Each time you get to pick what to do. 

Fight will open our Moves which are what we use with our Pokemon to Attack the other Pokemon. You can see the Move name, Type, and Attack Points. Once Attack Points are at 0 you can't use them. 

Switch will let us trade out our Pokemon for a different one from your Team. This will take up a Turn though. 

Catch only works for Wild Pokemon, check out the Pokeball Quest to learn more. 

Run and Forfeit work the same. You can leave the Battle. Forfeit will make you lose against the Trainer once accepted. Run, you will need to leave a certain area from the Pokemon to quit the Battle. 

Within Battle you can Press the same Button to enter it, to free roam. Here you can Feed the Pokemon Items.

quests.title: Catch a Pokemon!
quests.subtitle: Gotta Catch atleast one!
quests.description:
Now that you've got Pokemon, you need to learn how to best use them! 

Default is (R) to toss your first Pokemon on the Team out of its Pokeball. This will have them Wander around you like a Tamed Dog. 

While out they will Attack all Hostile Mobs and anything that Hits you or you Hit. But if they take Damage or Faint it counts the same as if they were in a Battle. 

Check next Page to see how to change and inspect your Team.
{@pagebreak}
The Button you used to pick a Starter is how you can see and change your Team. 

On the Left you'll see the Pokemon's Picture, Name (which you can change), the Type, Gender, and Held Item. 

Right shows your Team, you can Click the other Pokemon to inspect them as well. 

The Middle has 3 Pages each which can change to see new Stats.
{@pagebreak}
First Page: Shows more Pokemon Stats! Yay! 

It gives us the Pokedex Number, Pokemon Species, Pokemon Type again, the Owner, its Ability and Description, and its Experience.
{@pagebreak}
Second Page: Gives us the Moves the Pokemon uses in Battle. 

Tap the Move to see its Description, Power, Effect, and Accuracy in the bottom. 

You can use the arrows on the left to change the Move order. Or use the button on the right to switch out Moves.
{@pagebreak}
Third Page: and final page, is about Stats. All the Graphs show the Pokemon Health (HP), Attack (atk), Defense (def), Speed, Special Defense (Sp.Def), and Special Attack (SP.Atk). 

Stats show us the current Stats the Pokemon has. IV is the Stats the Pokemon came with, while EV shows the Stats that have grown through Battles or Items. 

Other gives us Friendship and Dynamax. Friendship is a very important Stat!

quests.title: Fishing for Pokemon
quests.description:
Some Pokemon don't Spawn like most, some like to live in the Depths of the Ocean! 

In order to get to them we'll need a Pokerod! Wait, a Pokerod? 

Yes, a Fishing Rod in order to Bait out these Pokemon. To Craft one, we'll need a Fishing Rod Template. 

You can Trade with a Master Fisherman Villager to get one!

quests.title: Leveling up your Pokemon
quests.description:
Leveling Up Pokemon will make them stronger in multiple stats and will be needed for certain Moves and Evolutions. 

Pokemon gain Experience everytime they Win a Battle, more against Trainers. Also from Catching other Pokemons. 

You can check how much Experience the Pokemon has or needs to Level up in the Team Menu!

quests.title: Ancient Pokemon
quests.description:
Some Pokemon have died out millions of years ago... 

But a lucky few have been preserved by Fossilizing! 

Let's find them! Grab your Brush and head to a Dig Site.

quests.title: Evolution
quests.description:
Radical Trainers is a Cobblemon Addon that gives us Trainers but also changes the Levels our Pokemon can reach... 

That is until we Defeat a certain Trainer! 

In order to find out, you'll need a Trainer Card. Either Craft them or Trade for them with a Trainer Associate. 

Trainer Associates will Spawn around you if you are Holding your Trainer Card out and don't have a set Series or if you are near a Village. When one is close enough, the Trainer Card will glow like it's Enchanted, and an arrow will appear above it in your hand and will point to the Trainer Associate. 

These Villagers can also give you the Series, which will tell you which Trainer you need to Defeat to raise your Level Cap. 

Right Click the Trainer Card to view who they are, and even Stats on previous Trainers you've Fought!

quests.title: Friendship
quests.description:
Friendship Value is necessary for Evolving and Fighting. 

This isn't Palworld, you can't just abuse your Pokemons and still have them work for you. 

So how do we increase our Friendship? 
Friendship will increase when you let your Pokemon outside of its Pokeball to Wander with you. Also certain Held Items and Consumables help increase Friendship! 

Careful to not decrease your Friendship as well though... some Items can take away Friendship in exchange for other help. 

If Pokemon have too low of Friendship they will refuse to Battle Trainers, so either fix that or put them away!

quests.title: 36B8B3C61E0CFAD1
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks.

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission.

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Level Caps
quests.description:
Great job! You got your (Tier 1 Evolution) Pokemon to Level 15! 

Why can't we Evolve them yet? 

Thanks to Radical Trainers, we will need to Beat a certain Trainer in Battle in order to unlock our Level Cap. 

Get a Trainer Card and find a Trainer Associate (I found them most at Villages!)

quests.title: Series
quests.description:
Trainer Associates are Villagers. They will Spawn around you if you Hold a Trainer Card in your Hand and don't have a Series. They also just Spawn in Villages, like normal Villagers. 

You can give them Items to receive a Trainer Card or give them a Trainer Card and they'll give you a Series! 

Right Click the Trainer Card to view its Information. Here you can find Infomation of every Trainer you have fought, or Information on the Trainer in your Series. 

When viewing a Trainer you can see their Name and Level Cap. Click the Right Arrow to view their Biomes they Spawn in! 

With Series Trainers their Names will start out like random until you view them. Then, it'll show the Name and Level Cap they have. 

If you beat the Trainer with a higher Level Cap in a Series, your Level Cap will increase!

quests.title: 0ADFE26AD63EC714
quests.description:
To find a specific Trainer you could use the Right Arrow to see every Biome they Spawn in. 

If you don't happen to have a million years free to wander in Minecraft then I recommend Crafting a Trainer Spawner! 

Where you can see the Biomes to find Series Trainers, you can also find a Signature Item. This Item will need to be placed within the Trainer Spawner. 

Once set, give the Spawner a Redstone Signal and it will make that Series Trainer magically appear in front of you, ready to Battle! 

I hope he wasn't doing anything important before you summoned him...

quests.title: Beat that Trainer!
quests.description:
You should know how this goes by now! 

Beat! 

That! 

Trainer!

quests.title: Evolve your Pokemon
quests.description:
Whether through Levels, Items, Trading, or who knows what! In order to get your Pokemon at the next Evolution, it works all the same. 

Once the Pokemon is ready, use (M) to open your Team. 

Here, view the Pokemon and the Evolve Button will be below the Pokemons Picture. 

Click it, and the Pokemon will Evolve!

quests.title: Dawn Stone
quests.description: Dawn Stone will Evolve Kirlia into Gallade and Snorunt into Froslass.

quests.title: Finding Dawn Stones
quests.description: Dawn Stones are found in Peaks Biomes: Stony, Snowy, any Peaks! Basically any Biome that has Blocks near Height Limit. \n\nThey are rarely found in Flower Fields, Icy Biomes, or Hills Biomes.

quests.title: 53E70A8232A8F06E
quests.description:
Wandering Traders and Trainers?!?!?! How many visitors do we need! 

Well we can get rid of the Trainers with a Trainer Repel Rod. 

Just place it down and they won't Spawn near it!

quests.title: 39E4FD684972B543
quests.description:
There's quite a few things you've got to complete in order to Evolve a Pokemon... so it is pretty hard to accidentally Evolve one... 

But I guess if you want to Devolve your Pokemon, just give them this Item! 

No, it doesn't work on first Evolution Pokemon to find negative Evolutions.

quests.title: Finding Water Stones
quests.description: Water Stones are found beneath Oceans and Rivers and Swamps. \n\nIf that isn't enough for you, try Jungles!

quests.title: Water Stone
quests.description: Water Stone will Evolve Poliwhirl into Poliwrath, Shellder into Cloyster, Staryu into Starmie, Lombre into Ludicolo, and finally Eevee into Vaporeon!

quests.title: Evolving through Trading
quests.description:
If you're playing with friends, you can use R on them to start Battles and Trade Pokemon! 

You might need to change that Keybind if it conflicts. 

Some Pokemon will Evolve after they've been Traded to someone else. 

Don't have friends? I mean, don't play on Servers? Then, don't fret, we have the Link Cable! 

Use this Item on a Pokemon to "Trade" them, which will make them Evolve!

quests.title: Dusk Stone
quests.description: Dusk Stone will Evolve Murkrow into Honchkrow, Misdreavus into Mismagius, Lampent into Chandelure, and Doublade into Aegislash.

quests.title: Finding Dusk Stones
quests.description: Dusk Stones can be found in Taigas and rarely in Swamps.

quests.title: Milcrey Evolution Item
quests.description: Alcreamie is a Pokemon based on ice cream! \n\nSo when you Evolve Milcrey into Alcreamie with these Sweets, they will use them as toppings! Very cute.

quests.title: Evolving Ursaring
quests.description:
Peat is actually a really cheap Item to Craft! 

Now just wait for a Full Moon and give it to an Ursaring to Evolve it into a Ursaluna. 

I'm pretty sure that just means bear moon!

quests.title: Charcadet Evolution Items
quests.description:
Charcadet has 2 different Evolution paths he can go through. 

First is Armarogue which is made by giving him Auspicious Armor. 

You can find Auspicious Armor in Bastion Remnant Chests! 

Second is Ceruledge which uses Malicious Armor. 

Malicious Armor spawns in Nether Fortress Chests!

quests.title: Slowpoke Evolution Items
quests.description:
Slowpoke is very similar to Charcadet, both have 2 different Evolutions they can get with Items. 

By giving Slowpoke a Glarica Cuff you will get a Slowbro. 

Use a Glarica Wreath instead and you'll get a Slowking!

quests.title: Finding Thunder Stone
quests.description: Thunder Stones spawn in Hill Biomes. \n\nSometimes in Jungles as well.

quests.title: Thunder Stone
quests.description: Thunder Stone will Evolve Pikachu into Raichu and Eevee into Jolteon.

quests.title: Trading with an Item in Hand
quests.description:
Remember Evolving through Trading? You should it was the Quest right before this one! 

This works the exact same but some Pokemon will need to Hold an Item while being Traded in order to Evolve. 

Yes, my fellow Singleplayers, we can use the Linking Cable to simulate Trading. 

I'm not listing every single Evolution you can get from these...

quests.title: Finding Fire Stones
quests.description: Fire Stones spawn in Deserts as well as some Biomes in The Nether. \n\nVery rarely in Beaches too!

quests.title: Finding Sun Stones
quests.description: Savannahs, Badlands, and Lush Caves are where you should look for Sun Stones. \n\nIf that isn't enough you might find them in Deserts too.

quests.title: Fire Stone
quests.description: Fire Stone will Evolve Vulpix into Ninetails, Growlithe into Arcanine, and Eevee into Flareon.

quests.title: Finding Ice Stones
quests.description: Any Biome with Ice or Snow is where you'll find these!

quests.title: Finding Shiny Stones
quests.description: Shiny Stones spawn in Flower Biomes and some Peak Biomes.

quests.title: Sun Stone
quests.description: Sun Stone will Evolve Gloom into Bellossom, Sunkern into Sunflora, Cottonee into Whimsicott, and Petilil into Lilligant.

quests.title: Finding Leaf Stones
quests.description: Leaf Stones spawn in Forests, Jungles, and Lush Caves. \n\nSo pretty much anywhere!

quests.title: Finding Moon Stones
quests.description: Moon Stones are found in Taigas and Dripstone Caves.

quests.title: Ice Stone
quests.description: Ice Stone will Evolve Sandshrew into Sandslash and Vulpix into Ninetails.

quests.title: Shiny Stone
quests.description: Shiny Stone will Evolve Roselia into Roserade and Floette into Florges.

quests.title: Leaf Stone
quests.description: Leaf Stone will Evolve Gloom into Vileplum, Weepinbell into Victreebell, Exeggcute into Exeggutor, and Nuzleaf into Shiftry.

quests.title: Moon Stone
quests.description: Moon Stone will Evolve Clefairy into Clefable and Jigglypuff into Wigglytuff.

quests.title: Prehistoric Birch Tree
quests.description:
The Prehistoric Birch Tree spawns wherever Birch Trees Spawn. \n\nDeep beneath the Logs of the Tree will be Suspicious Gravel.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_birch.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Dripstone Oasis
quests.description:
Deep within Dripstone Caves you might find a sort of Oasis! \n\nHere, Suspicious Gravel will spawn on the Floor of it.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_dripstone.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Enhydro Agate
quests.description:
A very fancy name for saying "Cave within Lush Cave"! \n\nThe Suspicious Gravel will Spawn under the Water.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_enhydro.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Eroded Pillar
quests.description:
Piercing through the vibrant Badlands, is the Eroded Pillar. \n\nWith this, Suspicious Gravel spawns inside the Pillar.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_eroded.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Frozen Pond
quests.description:
Frozen in time, and Frozen within any Icy Biome is the Frozen Pond. \n\nWithin the Ice you'll find Suspicious Gravel.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_frozen_pond.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Frozen Spike
quests.description:
Wherever Ice spawns, so will the Frozen Spike! \n\nLike the Eroded Pillar, Suspicious Gravel spawns within the Spike.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_frozen_spike.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Hydrothermal Vents
quests.description:
Near the Ocean floor you might get dragged down into the Hydrothermal Vents. \n\nThe Suspicious Gravel spawns near all the other Gravel on the Ocean floor!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_hydrothermal.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Lush Den
quests.description:
Venturing through the Jungles you may come across a little divot, that divot is the Lush Den! \n\nSuspicious Gravel Spawns within them.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_lush.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Mossy Pond
quests.description:
Another Structure within Lush Caves, the Mossy Pond. \n\nThe Suspicious Gravel Spawns beneath the Water.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_mossy.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Mud Pit
quests.description:
Mud Pits Spawn in Jungles, and I'm just glad they aren't quicksand! \n\nSuspicious Gravel is located beneath the Mud.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_mud.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Oak Tree
quests.description:
Anywhere you can find an Oak Tree, you can find a Prehistoric Oak Tree! \n\nBeneath the Logs will be Suspicious Gravel.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_oak.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Powdered Deposit
quests.description:
Up in the Snowy Biomes, comes the danger of Powder Snow. It can lead to a cold defeat, a large drop, or even Fossils! \n\nThe Suspicious Gravel is beneath the Powdered Snow.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_powder.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Preserved Skeleton
quests.description:
Preserved in time lays the remains of a Preserved Skeleton. \n\nAround the Bones will be Suspicious Gravel and Sand.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_skeleton.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Rooted Pit
quests.description:
Within Swamps you can find Rooted Pits. \n\nMud and Roots with a bit of Suspicious Gravel.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_root.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Sandy Den
quests.description:
Deserts have mounds of mounds. Some even Sandy Dens! \n\nSuspicious Sand spawns in the Den.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_sandy.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Spruce Tree
quests.description:
I think you know the pattern, wherever Spruce is, these are! \n\nFollow the Logs down to find Suspicious Gravel.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_spruce.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Submerged Impact
quests.description:
There's lots of strange Structures below the Ocean's depth. The Submerged Impact is definitely one of the strangest. \n\nWithin the almost Cave, is Suspicious Gravel.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_submerged_impact.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Submerged Spike
quests.description:
Above the Icy Biomes some Spikes might be like the Submerged Spike. \n\nThese come with Suspicious Sand!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_submerged_spike.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Sunscorched Den
quests.description:
Another Structure in the Badlands, the Sunscorched Den. \n\nPolitely within the Den sits Suspicious Gravel.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_sunscorched_den.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Sunscorched Remains
quests.description:
Another Badlands Structure! The Sunscorched Remains. I don't know what happened but apparently someone pissed off a Fire Pokemon. \n\nSuspicious Gravel Spawns below the Red Sand.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_sunscorched_remains.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Suspicious Mound
quests.description:
Rarely in the Plains you might find some different Blocks sticking out of the Ground. It might be a Suspicious Mound! \n\nSuspicious Gravel spawns under the Grass and some Stones.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_sus_mound.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Underwater Fissure
quests.description:
Under the Water, again, we get the Underwater Fissure. \n\nWithin it you can find Suspicious Gravel all over.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_underwater.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Prehistoric Vibrant Hydrothermal Vents
quests.description:
A different Ocean this time! The Coral Ocean. It comes with Vibrant Hydrothermal Vents. \n\nAround the Structure you'll find Suspicious Sand.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_vibrant.png width:200 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: PokeRod Upgrade Template
quests.description:
If a Villager is Unemployed (and not a Nitwit!) you can Place a Job Site Block down and they will go to it and become Employed. 

The certain Block determines the Job, and we need a Barrel for a Fisherman. 
Keep Trading with them and they will gain Experience. Once maxed out all Trades will be unlocked. We need a Master Fisherman in order to get the... 

PokeRod Upgrade Template.

quests.title: Archeology
quests.description:
Congrats on finding a Fossil Site!... now what? 

Take (or make) a Brush. Then, look at Suspicious Sand or Gravel and Hold Right Click. 

This will Brush the Suspicious Blocks and will uncover Items. The Items are set from Random Loot Pools, like Dungeon Chests. 

Different Locations give different Fossils though.

quests.title: Fossils
quests.description:
If you want a surprise on which Fossil gives what then don't turn the page!
{@pagebreak}
Helix Fossil - Omanyte 
Dome Fossil - Kabuto 
Old Amber Fossil - Aerodactyl 
Root Fossil - Lileep 
Claw Fossil - Anorith 
Skull Fossil - Cranidos 
Armor Fossil - Shieldon 
Cover Fossil - Tirtouga 
Plume Fossil - Archen 
Jaw Fossil - Tyrunt 
Sail Fossil - Amaura
{@pagebreak}
The last 4 Fossils work differently. You need to combine 2 of these Fossils to get 1 Pokemon. 

Bird + Drake = Dracozolt 
Bird + Dino = Arctozolt 
Fish + Drake = Dracovish 
Fish + Dino = Arctovish

quests.title: Fossil Resurrection
quests.description:
The Fossil Resurrection Multiblock needs 3 Blocks. The Fossil Analyzer, Data Monitor, and Restoration Tank. Place them in this design.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/pokemon/find_fossil.png width:100 height:100 align:center}
Before we start restoring or resurrecting or whatever! We need Fuel... Fuel comes in the form of a bunch of different Crops and Plant like Items. 

Food Items like Berries, Steak, and Cake. Liquids like Honey or Suspicious Stew. Even stuff we can't Eat like Saplings, Flowers, and Leaves! 

Once the Tank is full, we can place our Fossil into the Fossil Analyzer. If we're using some of the special Fossils, you'll need to place 2 unique Fossilized Pokemon into it. 

Once it starts working it will turn on, the Screen will glow, the Analyzer will be shooting red lasers, and the Tank will be bubbling. 

Finally when it is all settled and done, the Fossil will now be a fully Restored Pokemon in the Tank. Use a Pokeball on the Tank and it will Catch the Pokemon automatically.

quests.title: Making a PokeRod
quests.description:
Combine any Fishing Rod with the PokeRod Upgrade Template and a Pokeball in order to make a PokeRod! 

The Pokeball used up will only change how the PokeRod looks... don't use expensive ones for it. 

My favorite is the one with the Heal Ball!

quests.title: Fishing Bait
quests.description:
Fish (and Pokemon Fish) aren't attracted to scary hooks! Only scary hooks that have tasty Bait on them. 

To catch Pokemon, we'll need Berries! 

Different Berries give different Effects for Fishing. Whether it makes a certain Pokemon Type more common, gives better Stats, or even increases the Pokemons Level. 

To use them, Hold the Berries in your Offhand when Fishing.

quests.title: Gone Fishin'
quests.description:
Finally you can Cast your Rod. This will use up the Berry. 

Once the Bobber starts doing a boogie, Right Click to pull the Pokemon out! 

This will use start the Battle with that Pokemon. 

Then, you'll have to use a Turn in Battle to Throw a Pokeball at them.

quests.title: PokeNav
quests.description:
The PokeNav is a tool to help understand what Pokemon will (or can) Spawn near you. 

It is set to whatever Biome you are in. 

Opening up the PokeNav and you'll get a long list of Pokemon! 

The Buttons on top will change what Rarity of each Pokemon Spawn, if it's listed by most common to least or vice versa, and the last refreshes the list! 

Hovering over a Pokemon in the list will show information. Their Species, chance of Spawn, if you've encountered them, how many you've Caught or Knocked Out, and any specific Spawn Requirements. 

Requirements like Skylight, Weather, or even Time of Day!

quests.title: Find em' all!
quests.description:
With both these Tools, no Pokemon will be able to hide from us! 

Clicking on a Pokemon in the PokeNav will open their Page. If there is one near, it will show all of their Stats! And more importantly, let us Track it. 

When Tracking a Pokemon, a Pokeball on your Screen will point in the Pokemons direction and will count how many Blocks away they are. 

And if you struggle with typing Pokemon Names (like 99% of us), you can use the Button to the Left of the Track Button when viewing a Pokemon to add it to your PokeFinder!

quests.title: PokeFinders
quests.description:
PokeFinder, does as the name suggests! It gives a map of Pokemon near you, and comes with Filters to find specific Pokemon. 

You can open up your PokeFinder to type in Filters. The Species you only want, Aspects, and Labels. 

When the Filters are set, only those who fit the Filters will be shown on the map. 

Making them Strict Filters means, when there is multiple Aspects or Labels, it will look only for Pokemon with all listed Aspects or Labels.

quests.title: Saws, Cutters, and Atomic Forges?
quests.description:
4 of the ways to cut up the Halves are the same. The only new one is the...
{@pagebreak}
Atomic Forge! A very cool and flat Machine. 

Now needing 8 Machine Casings. 

The Atomic Forge doesn't get Energy like normal Machines, instead it needs it Laser-ed into it! 

With Enderic Lasers. Power up an Enderic Laser then use the Target Designator to Shift Right Click the Atomic Forge then the Enderic Laser. 

(If) It works, you can toss your Apricorn Halves in to get some Bits out.

quests.title: Bulk Washing
quests.description:
The Encased Fan is a fun Create Machine. 

When given Rotational Power Clockwise, it will blow Items and Mobs away from it. When Rotated Counterclockwise it will suck the Items and Mobs closer to it. 

Don't worry, it just gets better! We can put Water in front of the Encased Fan to Wash Items Dropped in front of the Fan. 

We can Wash our Half Apricorns to make our Ball Lids.

quests.title: Ball Lids
quests.description: The Color of the Half Apricorn determines which Lid we get. Plus we get Dye from it! \n\nIf we Smelt a Ball Lid we can get a Blank Ball Lid. These can be Dyed into other Lids.

quests.title: Allthemodium Metal Apricorn Bits
quests.description: Fun sized pieces of Apricorns perfect for snacking and Crafting our AllTheModium Metal Lids!

quests.title: Half Allthemodium Metal Apricorns
quests.description: Cut it by throwing it through the Mechanical Saw, powering and working a Sawmill or Fragment Forge. Or even process it through a whole Assembly Line! Plus there's Magic, Magic is always cool. \n\nWhatever you do, take your Apricorns and cut them in half.

quests.title: Half Apricorns
quests.description: Half Apricorns! Which don't do much but make Lids... \n\nSorry if you were expecting much from them.

quests.title: Sawing (again)
quests.description:
Sometimes we need a special Ball Lid in order to make a certain Pokeball we want. 

To get those we'll need to chop up some Ball Lids in order to get Apricorn Bits. 

So toss those Ball Lids through the Saw or whatever you want to use!

quests.title: Ways to put it all together
quests.description:
To Craft our Lids we need Blank Lids, Apricorn Bits, and a Blocks worth of the Ingot. 

As well as using the Assembly Line from the previous Quest, or Spouts and Deployers with Create, or a Pressure Chamber.
{@pagebreak}
With Create we need to use a Spout to pour 810mB of the Ingot onto the Blank Lid. That is 9 Ingots worth. 

Then, use the Deployer to smack the Lid with the Apricorn Bit to make our Lid!
{@pagebreak}
The Pressure Chamber is from Pneumatic Craft, just like the Assembly Line. 

The Pressure Chamber is a Multiblock Machine. It uses either Pressure Chamber Walls or Glass to make up most of it. While the Valves are what take in Pressure and the Interfaces take in and out Items from Inventories. 
If the Blue Face is out of the Pressure Chamber, this is the Input. If it is Orange, then it is Output!
task_titles: Ways to put it all together

quests.title: Saws, Cutters, ETC
quests.description:
The Mechanical Saw works like most Create Machines. 

Give it Rotational Power, and any Items that go through will be sliced in half.
{@pagebreak}
The Precision Sawmill is a Factory Machine from Mekanism. 

It is very easy to use! Throw some Energy into it, then place the Apricorn into the Machine, and it will slice and dice them into Half Apricorns!
{@pagebreak}
The Assembly Line will need quite a few Machines to get working: Assembly Controller, Laser, Input Unit, Export Unit, and the Assembly Platform. 

All Machines will need to be sitting next to each other connected to work. 

The Controller is the one that takes Pressure. The Input Unit will need an Inventory near it to take from, and the Export Unit will need a Chest to place Items in. If everything is working it'll say it is running. If not, the Controller will state the problem!
{@pagebreak}
The Fragment Forge, like all greedy Oritech Factories, will need Machine Casings to be made. 

3 to be exact. Once you have the 3 Machine Casings and the Fragment Forge placed down, Right Click the Forge to Build it. 

Then, it becomes much easier, just power it up and toss your Apricorns in!
{@pagebreak}
Last is the Cut Glyph. 

First, use whatever Spell Form you'd like. Touch, Ray, Projectile, Missile, whatever! 

Then, select the Cut Glyph and add Sensitive to it. This will allow Cut to work on Items Dropped. 

So now you can toss your Apricorns on the flow, hit them with the Spell, and it'll magically cut them up.

quests.description: It kinda looks like it has two eyes... \n\nTwo angry eyes...

quests.title: Apricorn Bits
quests.description: Apricorn Bits don't do much. Can't eat them or give them to Pokemon. \n\nYou can only use Deployers to mix Apricorn Bits and Dyes with Ball Lids to make other Lids.

quests.title: Allthemodium Metal Lids
quests.description: After spending our Bit, Blank Lid, and Blocks worth of Ingot, we can Craft our Ball Lids. \n\nI think the Allthemodium one looks coolest!

quests.title: Allthemodium Metal Apricorns
quests.description:
In The Other you'll find Apricorn Trees, just these come with a different type of Apricorn! 

Allthemodium and Vibranium Apricorns! 

The Trees act just like normal Apricorn Trees, you can pluck the shiny Apricorns off the Tree, chop it down for the Wood, and replant them for more Apricorn Trees.

Once you have collected Allthemodium and Vibranium Apricorns you can trade with a Poké Mart Trader for the final one, Unobtainium.

quests.title: Creating Pokeballs
quests.description:
If we want to create our favorite Pokeballs, we'll need to use Create! 

And that all starts with the Andesite Alloy! 

Follow through Creates own Quest Page to better understand how the Mod works.

quests.title: Pokeballs!
quests.description:
Now you can Create just about any Ball you want to. Some might be more expensive! 

If you want Ancient Balls you'll need to use Ancient Ball Mechanisms and Apricorn Wood Lids. 

All of these Balls are also entirely identical to normal Balls, just you made them instead of finding them!

quests.title: Combing everything to make our...
quests.description:
We got our Lids and our Mechanisms, let's finally make our Pokeballs! 

The only extra Items we'll need is a Blank Lid and an Iron Rod. 

We can use Deployers, a Pressure Chamber, or an Assembly Line to put it all together. Come on, by now you should know how to use them!

quests.title: Creating our firey Ball
quests.description:
To make our Great Ball of Fire we can use our Pressure Chamber from before, Deployers, or an Assembler. 

You know about the Pressure Chamber and Deployers. 

The Assembler will need 3 Machine Casings with it in a 1x2x2 shape to start it up. Just power it up and toss in the Items.

quests.title: Great Ball of Fire
quests.description:
The Great Ball of Fire will need its Lid, a Blank Lid, a Sturdy Mechanism, and an Iron Rod to be created. 

Once all are combined through whichever process you choose, you'll finally have it. 

This Ball has a 2x Chance at almost every Pokemon Type, except for 50x for Fire Types and 0x for Water Types. 

Yeah, not the best for Catching Mudkips...

quests.title: Burning our Great Ball Lid
quests.description:
There's 3 ways to make the Great Ball of Fire Lid. Simplest is using Create. 

Place the Great Ball Lid under a Spout to pour a Buckets worth of Soul Lava over it. 

We can also Build a Refinery by placing down the Refinery with 9 Machine Casings in the pattern shown by highlights. 

Just Right Click the Refinery to start it up. Then, once Energy is cabled in, Soul Lava piped in, and a Great Ball Lid is put in, we can make our Great Ball of Fire Lid. 

If counting Buckets worth of Fluid is too difficult, make a Pressure Chamber instead. There you can just combine the Bucket of Soul Lava with the Great Ball Lid to make the Great Ball of Fire Lid.

quests.title: Finishing our Pokeballs
quests.description:
We got our Lids and our Mechanisms, let's finally make our Pokeballs! 

The only extra Items we'll need is a Blank Lid and an Iron Rod. 

We can use Deployers, a Pressure Chamber, or an Assembly Line to put it all together. Come on, by now you should know how to use them!

quests.title: Allthemodium Vibranium and Unobtainium Balls
quests.description:
The Allthemodium Pokeball has a 4x Chance at Catching any Pokemon. No strings attached! 4x is the highest most Pokeballs will go to besides the Quick, Love, and Beast Ball. 

The Vibranium Pokeball has a 6x Chance with 50x Chance at Catching Legendaries. Legendaries are the best of the best Pokemon, also the rarest of course. 

The Unobtainium Pokeball has a 10x Chance with 100x Chance for Legendaries. The only Pokeballs that are better are the Origin Ball and...

quests.title: The best Pokeballs start in
quests.subtitle: The Other
quests.description:
In order to get our Master Ball, we're going to need the AllTheModium Metal Pokeballs. 

In order to get the AllTheModium Metal Pokeballs, we're going to need AllTheModium Metal Apricorns. 

In order to get those we'll need to visit The Other.

quests.title: Master Ball
quests.description: No matter the Pokemons Level, Type, Rarity, ETC. the Master Ball will Catch them (if they aren't already Caught). \n\nIt is also essential to Crafting the ATM Star!

quests.title: 7BFF76B27D398E62
quests.description:
With a very strange Item selection we can Craft the Rubber Stamp! 

Funny enough, you don't need Create to Craft it, just to use it. 

I wonder what the symbol is that we are stamping onto stuff though...

quests.title: Mechanisms
quests.description:
Each Mechanism makes a different Tier of PokeBall. 

Copper makes the default PokeBalls and the Safari and Heal Ball. 

Iron makes Great Balls and a few others like the Net and Dive Balls. 

Brass makes Ultra Balls, Love and Luxury Balls and a bit more. 

Sturdy Ball Mechanism will make Dream and Beast Balls!

quests.title: Allthemodium Metal Mechanisms
quests.description: Allthemodium, Vibranium, and Unobtainium Pokeballs are special Balls, so we'll need special Mechanisms for them!

quests.title: Allthemodium Metals
quests.description:
Allthemodium, Vibranium, and Unobtainium. The three AllTheModium Metals. 

Hopefully you've gone through their own Quest Chapter before using these Quests... 

In order to make the PokeBalls we'll need quite a few of these Ingots. Yeah, it is expensive. 

For Mechanisms, you'll need to turn a few of these Ingots into Plates in order to...

quests.title: 655FA86A410CE27B
quests.description:
By taking one of our Blue Lids from the previous Quests, we can make a Great Ball Lid. 

Deploy 2 Red Apricorn Bits on top of that Blue Lid to make a Great Ball Lid. 

Obviously we can use that to make a Great Ball, but why not an even greater Ball than that! 

I'm talking about the Great Ball of Fire, not a Greater Ball...

quests.title: Soul Lava
quests.description: Don't worry Soul Lava hasn't moved in any recent updates! \n\nCheck deep underground in The Other or in Piglin Villages in The Other.

quests.title: Stamped Nuggets
quests.description:
By using a Deployer, we can push the Rubber Stamps on some Nuggets to Stamp them! 

This will be necessary to make the Mechanisms. 

The Sturdy Sheet is made by processing Obsidian Dust first by Spouting Lava over it, then Pressing it, twice!

quests.title: Deploying
quests.description:
Like literally every other step, there's multiple ways to form our Mechanisms. 

You can use Deployers to smack a Ball Base with first a Nugget, then a Shaft, then the other Ball Base to create a full Mechanism.
{@pagebreak}
We also have PneumaticCraft's Pressure Chamber. 

You'll need a Pressure Chamber Interface, 2 Valves, and either Pressure Chamber Walls or Glass. 

The Interface is how you get Pressure into the Pressure Chamber, yes it will need Pressure to Craft it. 

The Valves are how Items go in (through the Blue Side) and out (through the Orange Side). 

The Walls or Glass will fill up the rest of the structure besides the center. That needs to be hollow.
{@pagebreak}
The Assembler (different from the Assembly Line) is perfect for our detailed 2x2 Crafting Recipes. 

First, we'll need to make our Machine. Place down the Assembler with 3 Machine Casings in a 1x2x2 design. Then, Right Click the Assembler to assemble it. 

Now we can give it some Energy and it will make us our Mechanisms!

quests.title: Ways to assemble everything
quests.description:
Like literally every other step, there's multiple ways to form our Mechanisms. 

You can use Deployers to smack a Ball Base with first a Nugget, then a Shaft, then the other Ball Base to create a full Mechanism.
{@pagebreak}
We also have PneumaticCraft's Pressure Chamber. 

You'll need a Pressure Chamber Interface, 2 Valves, and either Pressure Chamber Walls or Glass. 

The Interface is how you get Pressure into the Pressure Chamber, yes it will need Pressure to Craft it. 

The Valves are how Items go in (through the Blue Side) and out (through the Orange Side). 

The Walls or Glass will fill up the rest of the structure besides the center. That needs to be hollow.
{@pagebreak}
The Assembler (different from the Assembly Line) is perfect for our detailed 2x2 Crafting Recipes. 

First, we'll need to make our Machine. Place down the Assembler with 3 Machine Casings in a 1x2x2 design. Then, Right Click the Assembler to assemble it. 

Now we can give it some Energy and it will make us our Mechanisms!

quests.title: Stampers
quests.description:
Stamp them! 

Check out the Quests for all Pokeballs to see about the Rubber Stamp. 

You can Right Click the top or the hand of the Deployer to give it an Item, like the Rubber Stamp. Then, when at work, it will use that Stamp on Items below it. 

Or you can use the CNC Stamper! A Mekanism Machine that uses Energy to do the same exact thing, just easier.

quests.title: Pressing
quests.description:
Depending if your Plates are Stamped or not determines which Machine you can use. 

If it is Stamped you can use the Mechanical Press to make the Ball Bases. 

If not, try these!
{@pagebreak}
The Assembly Line connects different Assembly Machines together to work together at processing Items. 

Place down the Assembly Controller, Assembly Drill, and Input and Export Units to create our Assembly Line. 

You'll also need Chests next to the Input and Export Units for Items. 

Once ready, give the Assembly Controller some Pressure and it'll start right up.
{@pagebreak}
The Atomic Forge is a very fancy Oritech Machine. 

Place down the Forge and surround it with Machine Casings. Then Right Click the Forge to Build it. 

The Atomic Forge doesn't get Energy a normal way, because why would it be easy? Instead you'll need Enderic Lasers! 

Build an Enderic Laser, Power it up, then use a Target Designator to Shift Right Click both the Forge and the Laser to set it.

quests.title: Ball Bases
quests.description:
Ball Bases! Yeah I should have told you the Zinc will make the Iron Ball Base, I apologize. 

We'll need 2 Ball Bases for each Mechanisms. 

Plus more Items with the Deployers to create the Mechanisms.

quests.title: Allthemodium Metal Ball Bases
quests.description: However you get them... you'll need 2. \n\nSorry! I should have warned you beforehand.

quests.title: Allthemodium Metal Plates
quests.description: Okay technically you don't have to Stamp them. \n\nSome can just stay like normal Plates.

quests.title: Presses, Drills, and Atomic Forge?
quests.description:
Depending if your Plates are Stamped or not determines which Machine you can use. 

If it is Stamped you can use the Mechanical Press to make the Ball Bases. 

If not, try these!
{@pagebreak}
The Assembly Line connects different Assembly Machines together to work together at processing Items. 

Place down the Assembly Controller, Assembly Drill, and Input and Export Units to create our Assembly Line. 

You'll also need Chests next to the Input and Export Units for Items. 

Once ready, give the Assembly Controller some Pressure and it'll start right up.
{@pagebreak}
The Atomic Forge is a very fancy Oritech Machine. 

Place down the Forge and surround it with Machine Casings. Then Right Click the Forge to Build it. 

The Atomic Forge doesn't get Energy a normal way, because why would it be easy? Instead you'll need Enderic Lasers! 

Build an Enderic Laser, Power it up, then use a Target Designator to Shift Right Click both the Forge and the Laser to set it.

quests.title: Terastallizing
quests.description:
While wearing a Tera Orb you can use 50 of the same Tera Shards on your Pokemon to give them that Type. 

Obviously the Type is related to the Type of Shards you use. 

This will be in effect when the Pokemon is in Battle.

quests.title: Stellar Tera Shards
quests.description:
Stellar Shards have a 1% Chance of Dropping when any Pokemon is defeated. 

When you use 50 of them on a Pokemon they will Terastallize into Stellar Type. This is the only way to get it. 

Stellar Type will get a Boost for all Attacks! But it will be weak to other Stellar Types. Thankfully they are pretty rare.

quests.title: Tera Pouch
quests.description:
In order to Terastallize Pokemon we'll need a lot of Tera Shards. 

Let's make it easier to hold a lot of those Tera Shards by using a Pouch! 

The Tera Pouch can hold a Stack of each type of Tera Shard.

quests.title: Tera Orb
quests.description:
In order to Terastallize we need permission. Don't ask why, I don't know that answer. 

The way we get permission is by wearing a Tera Orb. 

You'll need to Craft it. Funny enough it is made with just Vanilla Items. 

You can just Right Click with it to Equip or use your Accessory Screen.

quests.title: Tera Shards
quests.description:
Tera Shards are rare Drops from beating Wild Pokemon. 

The type of Pokemon determines the Drop, so Normal Pokemon will Drop Normal Tera Shards, Fire Pokemon give Fire Tera Shards. 

Every Pokemon has a 10% chance to Drop them. There is also a 1% chance from all Pokemon to Drop a Stellar Tera Shard.

quests.title: Mega Bracelets
quests.description:
In order to activate the Mega Stone we'll need a Mega Bracelet. 

Yeah, yeah, yeah I know not all of them are Bracelets. 

Bracelet, Ring, Tiara, whatever! As long as it fits in the Mega Slot, wear it.

quests.title: 747580F66BCFB9B0
quests.description: The Keystone is found in the center of the Megaroid. You'll need a Diamond Pickaxe or better to Mine it. \n\nEach will give just one Keystone. Thankfully we don't need any more than that!

quests.title: Megaroid
quests.description:
Deep within the earth you might come across a Megaroid! 

No, it has nothing to do with physical enhancements... well besides for Pokemon. 

It's called roid because of Asteriods not steriods that's what I'm trying to say! 

In the center of the Mega-asteriod, lays the Keystone Ore.

quests.title: Observatory
quests.description:
The Observatory is a tall Structure with a giant telescope coming out of it. 

The first level has tons of Pots, a PC, and some Data Monitors. 

Second Level has Healing Stations and Glass I keep trying to walk through like how birds attempt to. 

The third level has Chests, Barrels, and a...

quests.title: 53A556F14187F399
quests.description:
The Blank Z-Move! 

Yep, it is Blank! 

If we want to make a specific Z-Move we'll need to Craft it with some Items to make that Z-Move.

quests.title: Z-Moves
quests.description:
Now we have our different Z-Moves. 

Some will just make one Move even Stronger, those are usually named after the Types like Normalium-Z. 

Some will change one Pokemon's Move into a different one, like Pikanium-Z. 

And a few are just strange like Ultranecrozium-Z.

quests.title: Mega Evolution
quests.description:
Let's go over our Checklist. 

Pokemon Holding their Mega Stone? Check! 

You are wearing a Mega Bracelet? Check! 

If both are checked off, when in Battle under your Moves you'll see a Button that says Mega Evolve. Click it to activate it. 

Then, select a Move and your Pokemon will transform. 

Make sure you aren't using a Z-Move with Mega Evolutions as well, you can only use 1 at a time.

quests.title: Mega Showdown!
quests.description:
Mega Showdown! Is a Cobblemon Addon that gives us... one, two, three, four! Four different ways to spice up Pokemon fights. 

We have Mega forms, Terastallization, and Dynamaxing which change our Pokemon while fighting. Plus Z-Moves which change up our Pokemon's fighting Moves. 

All of these require us to visit Structures, besides Terastallization. 

We will also need certain Accessories Equipped to use them. Look at your Inventory, then where your Skin is shown in the top right will be "Open Accessories Screen". Here is where you'll put their Items to Equip them.

quests.title: Z-Moves in action
quests.description:
Got your nice Jewelry on? Give your Pokemon a Z-Move and we'll be ready to use it! 

Also make sure your Pokemon knows the Move and that you aren't using any Mega Evolutions. You can't use Mega Evolutions with Z-Moves. 

Once in Battle, below your Moves you'll get the option to use a Z-Move! 

This will boost or change your Moves however.

quests.title: Specific Mega Stones
quests.description:
Each Pokemon needs their specific Mega Stone in order to become Mega. 

They're pretty easy to tell who is who, because they're usually named after the Pokemon they're for just with "ite" after it. 

Each needs a Mega Stone, 2 Iron Ingots, a Diamond, and a unique Item for that Pokemon. 

Also, Charizard and Mewtwo have two forms of Mega with X and Y.

quests.title: Mega Stone
quests.description:
By Mining the Mega Crystal with a Diamond Pickaxe (or better) you'll get a Mega Stone! 

These don't do anything on their own, instead we'll need to use them to Craft a certain Mega Stone for a specific Pokemon. 

Not all Pokemon can become Mega, only a select few. Each will need their specific Mega Stone, which means if you want multiple Mega Pokemon you'll need multiple Mega Sites.

quests.title: Mega Site
quests.description:
Rarely underground you might find a Mega Site. 

Looks kinda like a Megaroid if the atmosphere was much rougher on it. 

You'll find Ores in it as well as the Mega Crystal.

quests.title: Archeological Site
quests.description: The Archeological Site is a rocky cut out area filled with Suspiscious Blocks. \n\nThere is also Chests and Pots for Loot but the Suspiscious Blocks are cooler!

quests.title: Sparkling Stones
quests.description:
With a Brush we can uncover Items from Suspiscious Sand in Archeological Sites. 

Two rare Items we can get are Light and Dark Sparkling Stones. 

There isn't a difference between them besides the Rings they Craft. The Rings just change appearance, not effect or ability.

quests.title: Z-Rings
quests.description:
For some reason our Pokemon need us to wear special Rings to be able to use Z-Moves. 

Not sure why... but we'll need a Sparkling Stone to make it. Also a few other Items. 

The type of Ring doesn't matter, just changes the appearance. I like Olivia's Rings the best!

quests.title: Omni Ring
quests.description:
Hate taking up 4 Slots in order to use Z-Moves, Dynamaxing, Mega Evolutions, and Terastallizing? 

Then why not give the Omni Ring a go! 

Just wear this bad boy in any of those 4 Slots and you'll get the function of the Z-Ring, Dynamax Band, Mega Bracelet, and Tera Orb in one little package.

quests.title: Wishing Weald
quests.description:
Wishing Weald, not Well. There's no Water here, just a Structure in the Forest. 

Within the center of the Structure will be a fallen Star. 

Make a wish! Or Mine the Crystal with a Diamond Pickaxe.

quests.title: Max Mushroom
quests.description:
The Max Mushroom grows in Lush Caves. 

It will be needed for the Power Spot, plus it can make some Food Items for Pokemon. 

Dynamax Candy which will raise that Pokemon's Dynamax Level, Max Honey which will activate a Max Move, or Max Soup to Gigantamax a Pokemon!

quests.title: Wishing Star
quests.description:
"When you wish upon a Star" 

You'll be able to Dynamax your Pokemon! 

Dynamaxing is used in Battle to use a Max version of your Pokemon's Moves. 

This will make them grow much bigger in size, get more Health, and make their Moves even more powerful!

quests.title: Dynamax Band
quests.description:
To Dynamax we need a Band. 

A Dynamax Band. 

Wear it so we can Dynamax our Pokemon.

quests.title: Power Spot
quests.description:
Dynamaxing needs a Power Spot at most 20 Blocks away from the Battle. 

I don't know if that's 20 Blocks away from you, your Pokemon, or the thing your fightings... just be close to all them to be sure. 

You'll need a Wishing Star and a Max Mushroom to create one.

quests.title: Dynamaxing
quests.description:
With a Dynamax Band on your Character, a Power Spot nearby, and a Pokemon ready to fight, we can Dynamax! 

Your Pokemon doesn't need to be a higher Dynamax Level to use it, all it will do is make their Move even more powerful and give them more Health. 

In Battle you can look below the Moves to see the Dynamax Button. Click it to change our Moves into Max Moves!

quests.title: Gigantamaxing
quests.description:
Pokemon not big enough? Why not use Gigantamax! 

Only some Pokemon can use it (there's a list online but Charizard and Eevee are on it). 

Feed them a Max Soup (or if its Urshifu a Sweet Max Soup) and they will be able to use G-Max Moves.

quests.title: Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl
quests.description:
Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl is the campaign for the Sinnoh Region. 

Start it like any other Series. Find a Trainer Associate either by Villages or randomly Spawning when you hold out your Trainer Card in your Hand if it doesn't have a Series. 

Trade with him to start the BDSP Series. 

You'll need to get through this Series in order to unlock other Series, including the ATM Series!

quests.title: Gym Leader Wake
quests.description: He will raise your Level Cap, just only up to 31. \n\nHis Signature Item is the Nautilus Shell.

quests.title: Pokemon Trainer Cedric
quests.description:
He will raise your Level Cap to 36. 

His Signature Item this time is Eviolite. 

You'll need to Fight him 3 times. Not just Fight but also Win!

quests.title: Team Galactic Boss Cyrus
quests.description: He won't raise your Level Cap. \n\nHis Signature Item is a Clock!

quests.title: Commander Mars and Jupiter
quests.description: Beating them will raise your Level Cap to 48. \n\nTheir Signature Item is a Smoke Ball.

quests.title: Commander Saturn Rematch
quests.description:
He also won't raise your Level Cap. Why are we even fighting these guys! 

Oh yeah, we have to. 

His Signature Item is a Wind Charge.

quests.title: Champion Cynthia
quests.description:
Finally you're face to face with the Champion, Cynthia! 

If you beat her your Level Cap will rise to 69. 

Her Signature Item is a Prism Scale.

quests.title: Elite Four and Champion Rematch
quests.description:
The Series isn't done yet! You'll need to Rematch the Final Four and Champion Cynthia. 

You can find them on their biomes only, check Trainer Card! 

Beating Aaron will raise your Level to 71. 
Bertha to 73. 

Flint to 75. 

Lucian to 78. 

And Champion Cynthia to 79.

quests.title: Gym Leader Maylene
quests.description: She won't raise your Level Cap. \n\nHer Signature Item is the Black Belt, she must be good with Karate!

quests.title: Gym Leader Candice
quests.description: She will raise your Level Cap to 43. \n\nHer Signature Item is Ice Stone.

quests.title: Team Galactic Boss Cyrus Rematch
quests.description: This rematch will raise your Level Cap to 49. \n\nHis Signature Item this time is an Echo Shard. That's not cheap Cyrus!

quests.title: Rematch time again!
quests.description:
It keeps going? Yeah... you'll need to rematch them all again. 

Aaron will raise it to 81. 

Bertha to 83. 

Flint to 85. 

Lucian to 88.

quests.title: Gym Leader Roark
quests.description: He will increase your Level Cap to 16. \n\nHis Signature Item is the Smooth Rock.

quests.title: Pokemon Trainer Cedric
quests.description: He will raise your Level Cap to 30. \n\nHis Signature Item is the Everstone.

quests.title: Gym Leader Fantina
quests.description: She will raise your Level Cap to 37. \n\nHer Signature Item is an Eye of Ender.

quests.title: Commander Mars Rematch
quests.description: Back for revenge, now they'll raise your Level to 42. \n\nHis Signature Item is a Fire Charge.

quests.title: Gym Leader Volkner
quests.description: Volkner will raise your Level Cap all the way to 55. \n\nHis Signature Item is the Thunder Stone.

quests.title: Elite Four Lucian
quests.description: He will raise you to 66. \n\nPsychic Seeds are his Signature Items.

quests.title: Finished Series
quests.description: Now we get the last Battle of the Series. Just one last Battle with Champion Cynthia. \n\nShe won't raise your Level Cap, instead it will finish the Series. Then, you can start a new one! Like the ATM one.

quests.title: Gym Leader Gardenia
quests.description: Won't change your Level Cap. \n\nHis Signature Item is a Sunflower.

quests.title: Commander Saturn
quests.description: Also won't raise your Level Cap. \n\nHis Item is a Zoom Lens.

quests.title: Pokemon Trainer Cedric
quests.description:
This guy again? What does he have a crush on you? 

He will raise your Level Cap to 57. 

His Signature Item now is a Shiny Stone.

quests.title: Commander Mars
quests.description: She will increase your Level Cap to 20. \nHer Signature Item is the Wide Lens.

quests.title: Commander Jupiter
quests.description: She will raise your Level Cap to 22. \n\nHer Signature Item is the Scope Lens.

quests.title: Pokemon Trainer Cedric
quests.description: He will raise your Level again! Just this time to 39. \n\nHis Signature Item now is a Dawn Stone.

quests.title: Gym Leader Byron
quests.description: He won't raise your Level Cap. \n\nHis Signature Item is Metal Coat.

quests.title: Elite Four Bertha
quests.description: She will raise you from 59 to 61. \n\nHer Signature Item is Soft Sand.

quests.title: Elite Four Aaron
quests.description:
Now we're at the Elite Four! Once we beat these guys we can take on the Champ! 

The first will raise your Level Cap to 59. 

His Signature Item is Silver Powder.

quests.title: Elite Four Flint
quests.description: He will raise your Level Cap to 63. \n\nHis Signature Item is a Fire Stone.

quests.title: Leader Sabrina
quests.description:
Level Increase to 63.
Can be found randomly at Gyms that spawns on #minecraft:village

quests.description:

quests.title: Boss Giovanni
quests.description:
Level Increase to 59.
Signature Item is Dubious Disc.

quests.title: Radical Red
quests.description: Radical Red is a ROM Hack for Pokemon Red, it follows the same story as Pokemon Red... just much harder. \\n\\nYeah, this won't be easy. \\n\\nYou can start the Series by Trading with a Trainer Associate to give him your Trader Card so you can start Radical Red.

quests.title: Rocket Admins Archer and Ariana
quests.description:
Level Increase to 56.
Signature Item is Black Sludge.

quests.title: Trainer Brendan
quests.description:
Level Increase to 85.
Signature Item is Choice Scarf.

quests.title: Kanto Gyms
quests.subtitle: WARNING
quests.description:
Some leaders ONLY spawn in the Gyms that spawn in villages, so keep notes on which Gym Leaders you found!
You will need them later!!!

quests.title: Rival Terry
quests.description:
Level Increase to 82.
Signature Item is Lucky Egg.

quests.title: Trainer Brendan
quests.description:
Level Increase to 68.
Signature Item is Expert Belt.

quests.title: Kanto League Gym
quests.description:
If you want to fight the Elite Four and Champion you'll need to make your way to the Kanto League Gym! 

This is a giant tower found in The End. It is made of Purpur, End Stone, and has a giant Orange Pokeball in the front. 

The first floor has a few Pokemart Traders, Nurses, and Loot you can take. The next few floors have each of the Elite Four. The highest floor having the Champion!

quests.title: Rival Terry
quests.description:
No Level Increase.
Signature Item is Soothe Bell.

quests.title: Leader Brock
quests.description:
Level increase to 21.
Can be found randomly at Gyms that spawns on #minecraft:village

quests.title: Leader Clair
quests.description:
Level Increase to 81.
Can be found randomly at Gyms that spawns on #minecraft:village

quests.title: Elite Four Agatha
quests.description:
No Level Increase.
Found at 3rd floor of Kanto League.

quests.title: Elite Four Lance
quests.description:
No Level Increase.
Found at 4th floor of Kanto League.

quests.title: Leader Koga
quests.description:
Level Increase to 73.
Can be found randomly at Gyms that spawns on #minecraft:village

quests.title: Champion Terry
quests.description:
Still no Level Increase but hey you beat the Champ!
Found at last floor of Kanto League.
Champion Terry is the last person to beat in the Series, but that isn't it for the Kanto Region...

quests.title: Boss Giovanni
quests.description:
Level Increase to 81.
Signature Item is Destiny Knot.

quests.title: Elite Four Bruno
quests.description:
No Level Increase.
Found at 2nd floor of Kanto League.

quests.title: Elite Four Lorelei
quests.description:
No Level Increase.
Found at 1st floor of Kanto League.

quests.title: Trainer May
quests.description:
Level Increase to 76.
Signature Item is Vivichoke.

quests.title: Boss Giovanni
quests.description:
Level Increase to 55.
Signature Item is Upgrade (that's the full name).

quests.title: Rocket Admin Archer
quests.description:
No Level increase.
Signature Item is Black Tumblestone.

quests.title: Trainer Red
quests.description:
Once you've beat Radical Red you can find Trainer Red the main character of the earliest games and media! 

He is an optional fighter. This means he doesn't have a Signature Item, instead you'll need to find him wandering around in a certain Biome. That being any that can have End Cities. 

All the years of fighting Trainers throughout multiple games and media made him a pretty good fighter, so bring your best! 

If you can beat him you'll become the Kanto Legend!

Beat all of them and you'll win the Battleground!

quests.title: PrincessStellar
quests.description:
Ladies first I suppose! 

The first streamer you'll need to beat is PrincessStellar! 

She helps a ton in ATM including in the Quests! If you're reading this in Brazilian Portuguese, then thank her for that!

quests.title: Joeychin01
quests.description:
Next on the chopping block is Joeychin01! 

Joey doesn't have a Channel but he helps a ton with our Modpacks! 

I mean, hey that's still Content and he is making it. So I count him as a Content Creator.

quests.title: Mitinho Player
quests.description:
3rd person to beat is Mitinho Player. 
Just look for an Emerald on the back of his skin, that'll help you find him. 

Also not all of the Content Creators have english as their primary language! It's true, ATM spreads past the language barrier!

quests.title: Pilpoh
quests.description:
After Minitho Player is Pilpoh. 

Instead of using an Allthemodium Ingot he actually uses White Concrete to summon him with a Trainer Spawner. 

Knowing him he'll make a series of him playing AllTheMons... does that mean he'll end up fighting himself? That feels... weird.

quests.title: Virtuositas
quests.description:
Next up is Virtuositas! 

He's known for using Create Mod and Cobblemon! We have both in AllTheMons, but just stick to beating him with Cobblemon. 

I think you'd lose in a Create battle... whatever that means.

quests.title: Danrique
quests.description: Danrique! The only one who came with a Skin that matches the theme! \n\nLook for the Content Creator who is styled after someone who'd beat you in a Pokemon Battle... then beat him instead!

quests.title: Direwolf20
quests.description:
Going from a Pokemon themed Skin to someone using the Steve Skin, it's Direwolf20! 

Known for making and playing Mods for years. Now he'll be known for losing to you as well! 

Just Dire Things won't help you here Direwolf!

quests.title: Chosen Architect
quests.description:
From one of the most well know Minecraft streamers to another, now it's time to face off against Chosen Architect. 

Don't let all those feelings of love and nostalgia for his videos and Modpacks prevent you from beating him. 

Pokemon comes before love, you should know this by now!

quests.title: Nofaxu
quests.description:
Last but certainly not least is Nofaxu! 
If you do beat him, 1. give yourself a pat on the back because you just won against a guy with over a Million Subscribers on Youtube! And 2. you will have finished the Series. 

But hey, if you do start feeling regret and guilt for mercilessly destroying your favorite Creators in AllTheMons, you know, the ones who spent their whole careers helping you to better understand and enjoy the games you love so much... you can make it even, by checking out their channels!
