quests.title: Apotheosis Adventure
quests.description:
If you want good gear you're gonna need Apotheosis Gear, and that all starts with a Gem! 

Gems are rare Drops from any Mob, they are also confirmed Drops from Invaders. 

You'll learn more about those later, for now Farm those Mobs!

quests.title: AllRightsReserved
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks. 

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission. 

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: World Tier: Pinnacle
quests.description:
The last World Tier, World Tier: Pinnacle. To get it, you'll need to Kill the Ender Dragon atleast once, and equip all Epic or Mythic Armor and Tool/Weapon. 

Now Epic and Mythic are most common for Gems and Tools, plus we are more likely to get &zPerfect gems! This comes at the loss of Common and Uncommon but hey, who'll miss them! 

On the same pattern of upgrades we'll get 125% Experience Gained and 100% Luck increase. 

Monsters will receive their final upgrade, getting: 16 Armor Points, 20 Armor Toughness, 25 Armor Pierce, and 20 Protection Pierce.

quests.title: World Tier: Summit
quests.description:
World Tier: Summit will need you to upgrade your Armor and Tool/Weapon from Uncommon to Rare (or better)! You'll also need to kill The Wither. 

The Wither doesn't need to be an Invader and honestly, it'll be easier if he isn't. 

In Summit Epic Items and Gems will be the most common, and for Items you can now get Mythic and with Gems you can find &zPerfect. Again, both being extremely rare! 

Now we'll get 75% Experience Gained and 50% Luck. 

Monsters will also be buffed to get 12 Armor Points, 10 Armor Toughness, 15 Armor Pierce, and 10 Protection Pierce. 

Is it just me or are their upgrades better than ours?

quests.title: Sigil of Socketing
quests.description:
To those new to Apotheosis, Sockets can be confusing and irritating. 

In short, your Weapons and Armor need Sockets to use Gems with it. 

But what if it doesn't have a Socket? 

Then you'll need a Sigil of Socketing! 

Combine your item and Sigil in a Smithing Table and boom you can get up to 2 Sockets.

quests.title: Sigil of Unnaming
quests.description: Sigil of Unnaming does as the name suggests, when you have an Affixed Item with an awkwardly long name, you can combine it with the Sigil in a Smithing Table to get rid of most of the name. \n\n(Only the Material and Item Type as with the Rarity color will stay).

quests.title: 2E5E129F25707C5D
quests.description:
The Sigil of Supremacy!

Another sigil that cannot be crafted, similarly to Malice. Like Malice, it can make affixes stronger. Unlike Malice, it does this to EVERY affix on the gear, and will not sacrifice any in the process.

You can obtain this by beating 100 waves of the &zEndless Gateway of Apothic Invaders.

quests.title: World Tier: Ascent
quests.description:
For Frontier the Rarity of Affixes didn't matter, but now for Ascent you'll need everything being Uncommon or better. 

You'll also need to kill an Invader aka an Apothic Boss, to upgrade your World Tier. The Rarity of Boss doesn't matter! 

Affixes will only stay up to Epic but now Rare is more common than the rest. We can also get Mythic Gems... just only with Lady Luck's Favor! 

Speaking of Luck, our Luck will increase to 30% and Experience will jump to 55%. 

Monsters in return will now have 8 Armor Points and 5 Armor Pierce.

quests.title: Invaders/Bosses and World Tiers
quests.description:
Invaders are what we know as Apotheosis Bosses. 

These are Mobs that can spawn in any Dimension and they will always be buffed and have Affixed Items equipped. 

Most will have more Hearts, Damage, and Effects than normal Mobs! When Killed they'll drop Affixed Items and Gems. 

They have their own Rarities align with Apotheosis Rarities. Their Rarities determine what they spawn with and their stats. 

Their Rarities are determined by the World Tier! World Tiers are new additions to Apotheosis, they will change the Rarity of Loot and Bosses you can find. 

To access the World Tier Menu, Hold CTRL and press T.

quests.title: Gem Dust
quests.description:
To get Gem Dust you need an Apotheosis Gem and an Anvil. 

Any Apotheosis Gem (Recommended only Common and Uncommon)! 

Once you get your Gems, smash them with a falling Anvil! 

Then, you can use your Gem Dust to Craft a Salvaging Table.

quests.title: Vials and Sigils
quests.subtitle: Just Sigils now!
quests.description: Sigils are items used to change your Apotheosis Affixed Items; whether it be clearing Sockets, adding more Sockets, or removing the Name! \n\nAll are used with your Item in a Smithing Table, Reforging Table, or Augementing Table.

quests.title: Sigil of Withdrawal
quests.description:
Thankfully Apotheosis has made taking Sockets out of Tools much easier! 

Now instead of having to choose whether to save the Tool or Gem you can now keep both. 

Use the Sigil of Withdrawal with an Affixed Tool in a Smithing Table and you'll separate the Gem from it.

quests.title: 552BA5E6FA987256
quests.description: The Sigil of Malice is a mysterious sigil. No one knows how to craft it. Rumors circulate about it being dropped by Invaders.\n\nWhat it does is another mystery, though some players found that they lost an affix from gear they used it on, making a different affix stronger. The affixes chosen for this are, much like the sigil itself, yet another mystery.

quests.title: World Tier: Frontier
quests.description:
To get the World Tier: Frontier, you'll obviously need Haven done, but also need a few Affixed Items! 

How many? You need a full set of Affixed Armor plus an Affixed Tool or Weapon. 

Now Uncommon Invaders and Gems are most abundant, with the rest following in order: Common, Rare, and also Epic. 

The Player with World Tier: Frontier will get a 35% Experience Boost plus 20% Luck! 

Hey, not everything will be easy though, now Monsters will gain 4 Armor Points extra.

quests.title: Sigil of Rebirth
quests.description:
The Sigil of Rebirth is Fuel for all the Reforging Tables. 

They still need the other Material, and obviously the Item it'll change to work though... 

Atleast they're relatively easier to Craft!

quests.title: Sigil of Enhancement
quests.description:
The Augmenting Table needs different Fuel to work, and that Fuel is Sigils of Enhancement. 

Each Reroll will cost 1 Sigil of Enhancement while each Upgrade will cost 2! 

You'll need a Godforged Pearl for 4 of them.

quests.title: World Tier: Haven
quests.description:
The 1st World Tier is Haven! It being the first makes it the easiest to explore with and easiest to obtain. 

To get it you just need to hold an Affixed Item in your Hand! It will automatically be set when unlocked. 

The World Tier: Haven has highest chances for Common Gear and Gems. It can also have Uncommon and very rarely, Rare.
This is also the only World Tier where Invaders cannot spawn naturally.

quests.title: Applying Gems (and others)
quests.description:
You got Tools and you got Gems... so how do we combine them? 

First, make sure your Tool has an open Socket. (For more on Sockets check the Sigils section). 

If one is open, you can combine your Tool and Gem in a Smithing Table. 

If you aren't happy with your current Gems then you might need a different Table!

quests.title: Getting better Gems
quests.description:
Don't like your Gems? Then, change them! 

To change the Rarity of your Gem you'll need to use this Table. 

By using 2 of the same Gem and Rarity Materials, you can increase your Gems Rarity and that increases its power.

quests.title: Godforged Pearl
quests.subtitle: Mythic
quests.description:
Mythic are some of the greatest we can get! 

Mythics are found only in World Tier: Summit and in World Tier: Pinnacle, where they are most common. 

Godforged Pearls are made from using Mythic Items in a Salvaging Table.

quests.title: Mysterious Scrap Metals
quests.subtitle: Common
quests.description:
Common is the most basic Rarity. This makes it most common to find early game, but also the weakest. 

Common shows up most at the World Tier: Haven, and will stop appearing after World Tier: Summit. 

Mysterious Scrap Metals are made from using Common Items in a Salvaging Table.

quests.title: Salvaging Table
quests.description:
The Salvaging Table can finally get you Materials and Gem Dust without using Anvils. 

You can recycle Tools and Armor with Affixes to get their Materials. 

The Materials you get are based on the Rarity of Item, Common Items will give Common Materials. 

And break down Horse/Dog Armor for some reason.

quests.title: Augmenting Table
quests.description:
This is what you really need for perfect Affixes. 

First you need the Table, a Tool, and Sigils of Enhancement. 

Once you have all those, the world is all yours! You can reroll Affixes, choose a specific Affix, or upgrade set Affixes!

quests.title: Arcane Sands
quests.subtitle: Epic
quests.description:
Epic is finally climbing more to the overpowered side. 

Epic appears after World Tier: Frontier and is most common in World Tier: Pinnacle. 

Arcane Sands are made from using Epic Items in a Salvaging Table.

quests.title: Timeworn Fabric
quests.subtitle: Uncommon
quests.description:
Uncommon is the second Rarity. 

It starts appearing in World Tier: Haven, most abundant in World Tier: Frontier, and stops in World Tier: Pinnacle. 

Timeworn Fabric is made from using Uncommon Items in a Salvaging Table.

quests.title: Luminous Crystal Shard
quests.subtitle: Rare
quests.description:
Rare is the middle ground of Rarities. 

It appears in all World Tiers but most common in World Tier: Ascent. 

Luminous Crystal Shards are made from using Rare Items in a Salvaging Table.

quests.title: Simple Reforging Table
quests.description:
The Simple Reforging Table is used like an Enchantment Table but with Affixes! 

To add an Affix to any Item, place the Item in the center Slot. Then, add your Rarity Material to the left Slot. 

The Rarity Material will determine what Rarity Affix you get on your Item. This can be used to upgrade some Items, like from Common to Uncommon. 

You will get 3 choices of Affixes you can pick, also similar to an Enchantment Table the second and third get more expensive. 

With the Simple Reforging Table we can only get up to Rare Affixes.

quests.title: (Better) Reforging Table
quests.description: The Reforging Table does everything the Simple one will do, but better! \n\nIt can give us Epic and Mythic Affixes along with our previous ones!

quests.title: Night Vision Goggles
quests.subtitle: Head
quests.description: I see you! \n\nWhen wearing Night Vision Goggles you get the ability to see in the dark! Not much else to them...

quests.title: Novelty Drinking Hat
quests.subtitle: Head
quests.description: 'It was his Hat Mr Krabs! He was Number 1!' \n\nDoes the same exact thing as the normal Drinking Hat, just looks much cooler!

quests.title: Snorkel
quests.subtitle: Head
quests.description: The Snorkel gives you a small amount of Water Breathing when you enter Water. Similar to a Turtle Helmet! Careful though it runs out.

quests.title: Plastic Drinking Hat
quests.subtitle: Head
quests.description: Why spend time sitting down and eating a nice Home-Cooked meal when you can just Eat and Drink quickly! \n\nWith this very stylish Hat, Eating and Drinking is much faster.

quests.title: Angler's Hat
quests.subtitle: Head
quests.description: By tonight he'll be sleeping with the Fishes. \n\nThe Angler Hat helps you Lure Fish in and makes your chances at getting a Rare Drop higher!

quests.title: Superstitious Hat
quests.subtitle: Head
quests.description:
'They're magically delicious!' 

The Superstitious Hat grants you an extra level of Looting to Mobs you kill! 

It does stack with Enchants!

quests.title: Villager Hat
quests.subtitle: Head
quests.description: One of us! One of us! \n\nThe Villager Hat makes the Villagers believe you're from the same Town so they get rid of the Out-of-Towners Tax. Villager Trades are cheaper.

quests.title: Cowboy Hat
quests.subtitle: Head
quests.description: Wearin' this here Hat makes yer critters run like the wind! \n\nIt's right purty too.

quests.title: Artifacts
quests.description:
Artifacts is a wonderful Mod that adds Artifacts that will make your Minecraft expereince much easier and much more fun!

All Artifacts can either be found from exploring, archeology, or killing Mimics!

Mimics are found in Campsites underground, looking like normal Chests! But once you get too close they'll attack!

quests.title: Charm of Sinking
quests.subtitle: Necklace
quests.description: What Water? \n\nWith the Charm of Sinking you move through the Water as if it were Air! Still can't breath underwater though...

quests.title: Thorn Pendant
quests.subtitle: Necklace
quests.description: Gives you Thorns. Not your Armor, you! Like a Pufferfish!

quests.title: Charm of Shrinking
quests.subtitle: Necklace
quests.description: Where'd you go?\n\nOh you're just half your previous size. Small enough to fit beneath a 1 Block gap.

quests.title: Cross Necklace
quests.subtitle: Necklace
quests.description: Most games that have a Health and Damage system, have Invincibility Frames. After you take Damage you will have a few Invincibility Frames so 1. You don't die in an instant by a simple attack and 2. Gives you time to fight back. \n\nWith Cross Necklace you get a few more Invincibility Frames. Which means a few more times to fight back!

quests.title: Scarf of Invisibility
quests.subtitle: Scarf (Necklace)
quests.description: Where'd you go?

quests.title: Pocket Piston
quests.subtitle: Hands
quests.description: With the Pocket Piston your Attacks will hit your Enemies much farther! \n\nI wonder which wins, Pocket Piston or Steadfast Boots?

quests.title: Feral Claws
quests.subtitle: Hands
quests.description: Wearing these Claws just makes you feel a certain way. Adrenaline pumping, thoughts ceasing, strength rising like no other! \n\nWith Feral Claws you will Attack much faster with your Weapons or Fists.

quests.title: Digging Claws
quests.subtitle: Hands
quests.description:
Now these are one of my favorites! 

Digging Claws will 1. Increase your Mining Speed, so basically a level of Efficiency on all Pickaxes, and 2. Makes your Fists act as a Stone Pickaxe! 

Super helpful for building and just playing in general!

quests.title: Golden Hook
quests.subtitle: Hands
quests.description: Wearin' dis Golden Hook will increase yar yield of experience from keel-hauled enemies!

quests.title: Flame Pendant
quests.subtitle: Necklace
quests.description: Similar to Thorn Pendant, just a little hotter. No wait way hotter! \n\nThe Flame Pendant has a chance to light your attackers on Fire! When they are lit on fire the Pendant will also give you Fire Resistance.

quests.title: 5FD6A738754F6013
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks. 

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission. 

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Lucky Scarf
quests.subtitle: Scarf (Necklace)
quests.description: This and the Superstitious Hat gives you all the lucky charms you can need!\nThe Lucky Scarf gives you an extra level of Fortune to your Pickaxes.

quests.title: Pickaxe Heater
quests.subtitle: Hands
quests.description:
Don't you hate having to Mine then Smelt your Ores with two different Items? Well now you can be lazier than ever with the Pickaxe Heater!

While wearing the Pickaxe Heater, Ores that you Mined will automatically be Smelted!

Might want to be careful with it if you want Ore Processing.

quests.title: Everlasting Steak
quests.subtitle: Unique
quests.description: Like regular Raw Beef, you can cook the Everlasting Beef to get Eternal Steak!\n\nWorks just like Everlasting Beef but more Food Points and Saturation.

quests.title: Everlasting Beef
quests.subtitle: Unique
quests.description:
When slaughtering hundreds of Cows you might come across a Rare Beef. Not one with Mad Cow Disease, I mean the Everlasting Beef!

Everlasting Beef can be eaten like a normal Raw Beef, but it won't be deleted when consumed! Instead it will have a cooldown before you can eat it again.

(Also works with autofeeding backpacks!)

quests.title: Whoopie Cushion
quests.subtitle: Unique

quests.title: Umbrella
quests.subtitle: Unique
quests.description: 'I'm Marry Poppins ya'll!' \n\nThe Umbrella is a very useful tool added by Artifacts! It can be held infront of you to work as a Shield, by holding Right Click. Or it can be used to slow your fall by just holding it!

quests.title: Fire Gauntlet
quests.subtitle: Hands
quests.description: Everything I hit, bursts into Flames!!!!!

quests.title: Shock Pendant
quests.subtitle: Necklace
quests.description: Like the other Pendants this has a chance to hurt your attacker, just with Lightning! \n\nAlso makes it so if you're (un)lucky enough to be hit by Lightning, it won't hurt you.

quests.title: Panic Necklace
quests.subtitle: Necklace
quests.description: Some times the best way to fight, is not to fight.. it's to run away! \n\nWith the Panic Necklace, when hit you will get Speed Effect for a small time. Just enough time to get away!

quests.title: Withered Bracelet
quests.subtitle: Wrists (Hands)
quests.description: While wearing the Withered Bracelet Melee Attacks have a chance to give the Wither Effect.\n\nSorry Bow users!

quests.title: Power Glove
quests.subtitle: Hands
quests.description: The other side of the Feral Claws, these increase the Damage you deal while wearing them.

quests.title: Vampiric Glove
quests.subtitle: Hands
quests.description: With this Glove you will steal the life from any enemies you hit!\n\nOh yeah sorry I forgot... bleh bleh blehhh!

quests.title: Onion Ring
quests.subtitle: Hands
quests.description: Food by itself can get pretty boring, but it gets much better when you have a side with your dish! More specifically some (a) Onion Ring!\n\nWhen wearing the Onion Ring, everything you eat will give you slight Haste.

quests.title: Warp Drive
quests.subtitle: Belt
quests.description: Enderpearls are a fun way of travel! (Helpful for the Bumblezone, I wonder if we'll get a Quest chapter for that Mod!) But don't you hate that the Enderpearl gets consumed on use and takes 2 Hearts of damage with each use? \n\nWith Warp Drive that all goes away, clearly making Enderpearls the greatest transportation! Hunger gets consumed instead of the Enderpearl and no longer take damage from using an Enderpearl. When all Hunger Bars are depleted it will go back to consuming Enderpearls.

quests.title: Chorus Belt
quests.subtitle: Belt
quests.description: Don't you hate when you're just about to kill an Endermen and it teleports away? Well you don't hate you, you love it! You're just angry because you're envious! You want it! \n\nAnd with the Chorus Belt you can get it! You will teleport from a hit that would kill you.

quests.title: Helium Flamingo
quests.subtitle: Belt
quests.description:
Perfect for Pool Parties! 

Besides looking cute and funny the Helium Flamingo allows you to swim in Air. Yes you heard me! Swim... in... Air... 

When in the Air, like jumping, you can press CTRL to start Swimming in Air. You can move around just like in the Water: Swim up, Swim down, Swim all around!

quests.title: Obsidian Skull
quests.subtitle: Belt
quests.description: After you take a hit from Fire Damage, the Obsidian Skull will activate giving you a period of Fire Resistance. Hopefully long enough to escape the flames!

quests.title: Cloud in a Bottle
quests.subtitle: Belt
quests.description: With the Cloud in a Bottle equipped you can hit Space Bar twice to double jump! Very helpful for parkour! \n\nAlso increases the height you can fall from, like Bunny Hoppers!

quests.title: Crystal Heart
quests.subtitle: Belt
quests.description: 'Also try Terraria!'\n\nWhen equipped you will gain 5 extra Hearts! Or 10 whole points of Health! Adding up to on default 30 Health.

quests.title: Antidote Vessel
quests.subtitle: Belt
quests.description: Do you have to drink it? Idk it kinda just stays there and works... \n\nWith the Antidote Vessel, negative Effects (like Wither or Poison) will have their durations cut short! Very helpful when facing Witches or Wither Skeletons.

quests.title: Universal Attractor
quests.subtitle: Belt
quests.description: It's a Magnet.

quests.title: Aqua-Dashers
quests.subtitle: Feet
quests.description: While wearing these on your Feet you can preform a miracle! Walking on Water! \n\nWell actually running on Water, you have to be Sprinting to be able to run over Water. Once you stop Sprinting you will start Sinking.

quests.title: Flippers
quests.subtitle: Feet
quests.description: I don't have Hands, I have Flippers. \n\nFlippers will act like a much better Depth Strider. You can Swim and Walk through Water much faster!

quests.title: Running Shoes
quests.subtitle: Feet
quests.description: I don't believe I have permission to use a specific brand name of Running Shoes so use your imagination on which these are. \n\nRunning Shoes will give you a Speed Boost when Sprinting so you will be even faster when Running! Also gives you auto-jump when Sprinting...

quests.title: Kitty Slippers
quests.subtitle: Feet
quests.description:
For some reason Creepers are scared of Cats. Creepers are also extremely dumb and believe the Cats that your Slippers look like are real. 

All Creepers will run away from you and won't be hostile when these Slippers are worn. 

Also makes Kitty noises when you take damage! (Can't assure you that you will always land on your Feet though).

quests.title: 74B352457BF1541B
quests.subtitle: Feet
quests.description: If you're like me, or any sane person you despise Powdered Snow. Thankfully Artifacts gives us a tool for dealing with it! Snowshoes! \n\nSnowshoes will allow you to safely walk over Powdered Snow just like how Leather Boots do. You will also get a Speed boost when walking on any Snow!

quests.title: Steadfast Boots
quests.subtitle: Feet
quests.description: Spikes, Cleats, Crampons whatever they are! \n\nSteadfast Boots keep you steady on your Feet. You won't be knocked back from attacks and you won't slip on Ice anymore.

quests.title: Rooted Boots
quests.subtitle: Feet
quests.description: Like get in touch with Mother Nature man. \n\nWith Rooted Boots nature is your Bestfriend! When standing on Grass you will Regenerate Hearts. Also when you Eat Food when standing on Grass it will act as if you Bonemealed it.

quests.title: Bunny Hoppers
quests.subtitle: Feet
quests.description: Bunny, hop. Bunny, hop. Bunny, hop.\n\nWith Bunny Hoppers on you can jump twice as high and take half the fall damage as usual! Doesn't make you invincible to Fall Damage, you can still die it's just harder.

quests.title: Strider Shoes
quests.subtitle: Feet
quests.description: The Strider's secret to walking on Lava is within their Legs. So we took their Legs off of them and have you use them instead! \n\nWhen Sneaking you can walk safely ontop of Lava! When you stop Sneaking you will fall into the Lava though. These also allow you to safely walk over Magma blocks and other hot blocks!

quests.title: Arcanist Outfit
quests.description: Iron Armor of Ars Armor.

quests.title: Geomancer Outfit
quests.description: Ars Elemental Earth Armor!

quests.title: Aquamancer Outfit
quests.description: Ars Elemental Water Armor!

quests.title: Utherium Armor
quests.description: Utherium Crystals drop from Rotbeasts in the Undergarden!

quests.title: Pyromancer Outfit
quests.description: Ars Elemental Fire Armor!

quests.title: Aethermancer Outfit
quests.description: Ars Elemental Air Armor!

quests.title: Battlemages Outfit
quests.description: Diamond version of Ars Armors!

quests.title: Steel Armor
quests.description: Steel is used for most Machines in Mekanism... plus Armor which is nice!

quests.title: Allthemodium Arcanist Gear
quests.description: Allthemodium Armor but with buffs to Ars Nouveau Spells!

quests.title: Vibranium Arcanist Gear
quests.description: Vibranium Armor but with buffs to Ars Nouveau Spells!

quests.title: Unobtainium Arcanist Gear
quests.description: Unobtainium Armor but with buffs to Ars Nouveau Spells!

quests.title: Sylvan Gear
quests.description: Basic Armor added by Roots Classic, you'll need a Ritual to get it though!

quests.title: MekaSuit
quests.subtitle: As much Energy you can supply
quests.description:
With a ton of super expensive Mekanism Items you can upgrade Unobtainium Armor to the MekaSuit! 

Now it can hold Energy and instead of taking hearts from damage, it will take Energy. 

You can use Upgrade Units to make it even better!

quests.title: Bee Armor 1
quests.description: Checkout the Bumblezone Quest Page to learn more!

quests.title: Glacite Armor
quests.description: Glacite is found in the cold biomes of Eternal Starlight!

quests.title: Froststeel Armor
quests.description: Froststeel is a common Ore in the Cold Biomes of the Undergarden.

quests.title: Inferium Armor
quests.description: With Diamond Armor and a few Inferium Items we can craft Inferium Armor! \n\nThey can also be upgraded with Tinkering!

quests.title: Tertium Armor
quests.description: Upgraded version of Prudentium.

quests.title: Neptunium Armor
quests.description: Neptunium is a reward from Neptune's Bounty which is gotten through Fishing! \nIt also grants buffs to being Underwater.

quests.title: Refined Obsidian Armor
quests.description:
By infusing Obsidian with Diamonds we can get Refined Obsidian Dust! 

Then, we can compress Osmium into it to get it in Ingot form. 

After that, we can turn those Ingots into Armor with better stats than even Allthemodium Armor!

quests.title: Leather Armor
quests.description:
Leather Armor is the worst Armor set you can get. 

That is mostly because Mojang expected you to get it before any other. 

I almost never get it though because I struggle to find that many Cows, sorry Mojang!

quests.title: Lapis Lazuli Armor
quests.description: Thanks to Mekanism we can now make Armor out of Lapis Lazuli! \n\nIt kinda blows though...

quests.title: Golden Armor
quests.description: Golden Armor is right between Iron and Leather. But its Durability is much closer to Leather. \n\nThere is not much use for it besides having Piglins Neutral towards you when wearing some Gold Armor.

quests.title: Chainmail Armor
quests.description: Chainmail Armor is a little worse than Iron. Its main use in Minecraft was its elusive nature, only being obtained through Trades and Mob Drops. \n\nOf course this is modded though, so we can craft it now! Which takes away its purpose...

quests.title: Copper Armor
quests.description: Finally Copper has a real use!

quests.title: Aethersent Armor
quests.description: Aethersent Ore is found during Meteorite Showers in Eternal Starlight. Small ones break on impact, you'll need to wait for big Meteors! \n\nOr is it Meteorites? What's the difference?

quests.title: 497D222F74A52DF5
quests.description: Now this is what I like! Iron is very common and its Armor is incredible for early game. \n\nZombies and Skeletons stand just about no chance!

quests.title: Thermal Springstone Armor
quests.description: Thermal Springstone spawns in hot ponds found rarely in Eternal Starlight!

quests.title: Diamond Armor
quests.description: Diamond Armor is the next on the Vanilla chain, this is also usually where we start Enchanting it as well! \n\nI recommend Protection and its various forms, we don't have to be picky with modded!

quests.title: Netherite Armor
quests.description: Netherite Armor is the best Vanilla can get. It has same Armor Points as Diamond but more Armor Toughness. \n\nProbably because you need Diamond to make it!

quests.title: Prudentium Armor
quests.description: Upgraded version of Inferium.

quests.title: Allthemodium Armor
quests.description:
What you think Vanilla was all we got? 

Allthemodium Armor has more Armor Points and Armor Toughness, plus increased Protection against Magic and other buffs you can read about in Allthemodium Quest Page! 

BTW you will need Netherite to craft it.

quests.title: Vibranium Armor
quests.description: Much higher stats in everything with the next in line for Allthemodium Armors, Vibranium! \n\nYou will need Allthemodium Armor to create it.

quests.title: Awakened Supremium Armor
quests.description: You'll need to use an Awakening Ritual to get the Items to do another Awakening Ritual on Supremium Armor. \n\nI think it is worth it; it's the best Armor you can get from Mystical!

quests.title: Unobtainium Armor
quests.description:
The greatest Armor we can get from Allthemodium, Unobtainium! 

Now with 100% Knockback Resistance and higher stats everywhere! 

Also needs Vibranium Armor to make it.

quests.title: Bee Armor 2
quests.description: This ones not any different, why are you checking it?

quests.title: Wildwood Gear
quests.description: Late game Armor for Roots Classic

quests.title: Bronze Armor
quests.description: Bronze is a combination of Copper and Tin. \n\nThere is a dozen different ways to make the alloy, I won't tell you the right way to do so.

quests.title: Osmium Armor
quests.description: Osmium spawns around Deepslate and only needs Iron to Mine but it gives better stats than Netherite!

quests.title: Imperium Armor
quests.description: Upgraded version of Tertium.

quests.title: Supremium Armor
quests.description: Upgraded version of Imperium.

quests.title: Quantum Armor (AE2)
quests.subtitle: As much Energy you can supply
quests.description:
You think Mekanism and Modern Industrialization can have all the fun? 

This Quantum Armor has default stats similar to Netherite Armor but, like the MekaSuit it can use Energy as a shield. 
It also has upgrades which can be installed to make you even more powerful! Like Flight, Night Vision, and even the ability to recharge. 

But the best part is that it can Linked to your Storage System! Then, you can automatically take Energy out from it and take out any Item from it no where you are.

quests.title: Cloggrum Armor
quests.description: Cloggrum is the Iron Ore of Undergarden. It spawns everywhere.

quests.title: Sorceror's Outfit
quests.description: Gold version of Ars Armors!

quests.title: Blazegold Armor
quests.description: Blazegold has same stats as Iron but has other abilities Iron wishes it had! \n\nCheck out the Item descriptions to learn more of what they can do!

quests.title: Ferricore Amor
quests.description: Ferricore has same stats as Iron but has other abilities Iron wishes it had! \n\nCheck out the Item descriptions to learn more of what they can do!

quests.title: Refined Glowstone Armor
quests.description: Osmium + Glowstone = Refined Glowstone!

quests.title: Warden Armor
quests.description: Why upgrade Netherite to Allthemodium or even anything else when we can upgrade it to Warden Armor! \n\nYou'll need a few Warden Drops in order to make it though!

quests.title: Compressed Iron Armor
quests.description: This armor set has same Armor Points as Iron but is better in both Toughness and Knockback Resistance.

quests.title: Pneumatic Armor
quests.description: "I am Compressed Iron Man!" \n\nIt can be used and upgraded with compressed Air!

quests.title: Swamp Silver Armor
quests.description: Swamp Silver is found within the muddy swamps of Eternal Starlight.

Armor is a very important part of Minecraft, it is what protects you from harm. 

Different pieces of Armor give different Armor Points. These are what determine the effectiveness for your Armor, the more the merrier!

Most armor can be changed for more decoration with Armor Trims, use a piece of Armor with an Armor Trim, and an Item for coloring to change the look!

quests.title: Harvest Tier 6
quests.description: Tier 6 is the highest tier, anything that is breakable can be mined with it, including Vibranium and Unobtainium.

quests.title: Harvest Tier 5
quests.description: Tier 5 is basically just for Allthemodium Ore, not much else.

quests.title: 7B1818D2C5C2BB18
quests.subtitle: Tier: 5
quests.description: The Soulstrider's Pickaxe can be used to "vein-mine" chunks of ore.

quests.title: Harvest Tier 4
quests.description: Tier 4 is Diamond tool level, used to get Obsidian and Netherite. Also some modded ores like Uranium and Platinum.

quests.title: 5CD65553EF60029B
quests.subtitle: Tier: 4
quests.description: The Skyseeker's Pickaxe teleports blocks mined straight into the player's inventory.

quests.title: Harvest Tier 3
quests.description: Tier 3 is Iron Pickaxe level, it mines most ores like Diamond, Emerald, and Gold.

quests.title: Magic Mod Iron Pickaxes
quests.subtitle: Tier: 3
quests.description: The Botanist's Pickaxe turns blocks that it interacts with into their mossy variants, assuming they have one.

quests.title: Harvest Tier 2
quests.description: Tier 2 is the stone pickaxe level. It's almost only for mining Iron items.

quests.title: Harvest Tier 1
quests.description: Tier 1 Harvest Level is the lowest pickaxe level, needing a pickaxe. Any pickaxe can mine these. Items that are Tier 1 would be like Stone, Furnace, and Coal Ore.

quests.title: Basic Tools!
quests.subtitle: All The Tools
quests.description:
Welcome to Basic Tools!

Ever get a tool you've never seen or heard of and wanted to know where it lies among other tools? Then these quests are perfect for you!

(The swords are sorted by base damage, swords that can be upgraded or used to get more damage are not included).

The quests for all the pickaxes and swords are OPTIONAL!

quests.title: Chef's Hat
quests.subtitle: Turn the heat of battle into nourishment
quests.description:
Once worn by legendary cooks whose feasts drew kings and warriors alike, the Chef's Hat carries the scent of smoke, spices, and blazing cauldrons. Its folds hold the memory of countless meals prepared in the chaos of battle. 

 This relic rewards the wearer for their victories: when an enemy falls, it has a chance to produce meatballs, a simple yet hearty food, providing strength and sustenance in the heat of combat. 

- It has 1 ability: 

 Meatball Harvest: 
 The Chef's Hat rewards its wearer for every victory: when an enemy is defeated, there is a chance to produce a meatball, a simple yet hearty food identical to raw beef, which can be eaten directly or cooked for greater restoration. This relic turns the spoils of battle into nourishment, keeping the wearer strong even in the heat of combat. 

- A relic for those who turn every victory into nourishment… and never go hungry.

quests.title: Leafy Mantle
quests.subtitle: Sometimes, the forest itself will protect those it favors...
quests.description:
Hidden among the densest trees of Forest and Tropic biomes, the Leafy Mantle awaits the worthy adventurer. Woven from thousands of living leaves, it allows its wearer to move as if part of the forest itself. 

- It has 2 abilities: 

1. Camouflage: 
 Move freely within tree leaves, land safely without fall damage, and regenerate health slowly while in foliage. 

2. Gift of the Grove: 
 When facing fatal damage, the surrounding leaves absorb the blow, protecting the wearer from death. The amount of foliage consumed depends on the damage received. 

- A relic of nature and growth… where the forest itself fights for its chosen guardian.

quests.title: Roller Skate
quests.subtitle: Speed isn’t just a skill… it’s a legacy.
quests.description:
Hidden in the vast stretches of the Overworld, the Roller Skate awaits the daring adventurer. Once worn, each step pulls the wearer forward, turning motion into unstoppable momentum. 

- It has 1 ability: 

 Acceleration: 
 While running continuously, the wearer gradually gains movement speed, reaching the maximum bonus after a few seconds. The faster you go, the more slippery surfaces become, adding both thrill and risk. 

- A relic of speed and momentum… where every stide leaves a trail of fire behind.

quests.title: Hunting Belt
quests.subtitle: Unite with your pets and unleash a deadly pack!
quests.description:
Legends speak of hunters who trusted not only their own hands but the fangs of their companions. Their leather belts, adorned with bone charms, carry the memory of countless battles fought together. 

- It has 1 ability: 

 Pack: 
 Increases the damage dealt by the relic wearer’s pets. 

- A relic for hunters who trust their pack… and make every companion strike count.

quests.title: Springy Boot
quests.subtitle: Every step can become a leap… if you know how to use it.
quests.description:
Hidden in the rocky heights of Mountain biomes, the Springy Boot waits for those who dare to jump beyond limits. Its engineered springs transform each landing into a launch, turning movement into both escape and attack. 

- It has 1 ability: 

 Spring Dash: 
 A crouch jump launches the relic wearer in the opposite direction of their gaze with significant force. Each landing before coming to a full stop causes the wearer to bounce off horizontal surfaces, completely negating fall damage. To stop the effect intentionally, hold the jump or crouch key just before touching the ground. 

- A relic of mobility and force… where every jump is an opportunity to soar.

quests.title: Rider Flute
quests.subtitle: Call your mounts, store them safely, and master the ride
quests.description:
Carried for generations by nomads and messengers, the Rider Flute produces a sound familiar to any riding animal. A single note can call a mount to your side, while another signals it to pause patiently until needed. 

 Its mysterious power allows the wearer to store up to 2 mounts inside the flute, ready to be released or recalled at will. Switch between stored mounts by sneaking and scrolling the mouse wheel. To completely release a mount, simply sneak and right-click, giving the rider total control over their companions. 

- It has 1 ability: 

 Stable: 
 Right-click a tamed riding animal to place it inside the Rider Flute, and right-click again to release or recall it. Store up to 2 mounts and switch between them while sneaking. To fully release a mount, sneak and right-click. 

- A relic for those who guide their mounts with a song… and never leave a friend behind.

quests.title: Jellyfish Necklace
quests.subtitle: Maybe the oceans are hiding more than just fish...
quests.description:
Somewhere in the depths, a strange relic awaits the Jellyfish Necklace. A curious item that seems to carry the essence of a living creature. You may find it inside chests in aquatic biomes. 

 - It has 2 abilities: 

 1. Aquatic Regeneration: 
While submerged in liquid or standing in the rain, the necklace empowers its wearer, increasing maximum health and boosting regeneration. 

 2. Electric Discharge 
The relic stores electrical energy over time. Once charged, touching a living creature releases a powerful shock that knocks nearby enemies back, paralyzes them for a short time, and sends electricity chaining through nearby targets. 

- A relic born from the sea... and a reminder that some creatures are best admired from a distance.

quests.title: Cut Glass Boot
quests.subtitle: Walk where others sink and command the flow of liquids!
quests.description:
Forged from crystal layers by a visionary artisan, the Cut Glass Boot carries the memory of every drop of liquid it has ever touched. Its power allows the wearer to stride across water, lava, or poison as if the surface were solid glass. 

 While the boot is equipped, it can also store liquids in its internal buffer, letting the wearer choose which liquid to walk upon. The more liquid of the same type stored, the faster the steps become, turning sluggish surfaces into a swift pathway. 

- It has 1 abilities: 

 Glass: 
 This relic functions as a versatile container for liquids. When held, it can store multiple types of liquid in its internal buffer, letting the wearer choose which to use. 

 While equipped, the wearer can move across any liquid stored inside. Movement is naturally slower than walking on solid ground, but the more liquid of the same type stored, the easier it becomes to stride across it, turning otherwise dangerous surfaces into a stable, walkable path. 

- A relic for those who refuse to sink… and can glide across any liquid.

quests.title: Overworld
quests.description: These Relics can be found in the Overworld!

quests.title: Relics
quests.description:
Welcome to Relics! 
 
Relics mod is similar to Artifacts, you get many unique and powerful items all throughout the Worlds. 
 
They have many different Abilities which are obtained and upgraded through the Research Window (Hold shift on the relic). There you can exchange Vanilla XP to reroll the stats on its abilites, see your current Relic XP, gained from using the Relics, and level up their abilities! 

Each rank further enhances the abilities, making their effects stronger and more efficient. 
 
To use Relic Abilities default is Left Alt.

quests.title: Sphere of Self-Sacrifice
quests.subtitle: Power is not always taken... sometimes, it is given.
quests.description:
Deep within the burning lands of the Nether, a relic pulses with a чужое life... the Sphere of Self-Sacrifice. 

 It does not protect you from death… it teaches you to trade with it. Those who wield it learn that survival can come at a cost... one paid in their own blood. 

- It has 1 ability: 

 Sacrifice: 
 Upon use, you consume a portion of your own maximum health, converting it into powerful regeneration over time. This effect can stack, but using it again will refresh all active healing durations. 

- A relic of pain and resilience... where every second of life is earned.

quests.title: Kinetic Belt
quests.subtitle: Not all relics are meant to keep you grounded...
quests.description:
Hidden within the mysterious dungeons of the End, the Kinetic Belt awaits those willing to master movement itself. 

This relic bends the rules of physics, responding not to weight, but to motion. In the right hands, even the air becomes something you can control. 

- It has 2 abilities: 

 1. Arsenal Expansion: 
Increases the maximum number of amulets you can equip, allowing for greater combinations of power. 

 2. Gliding: 
By holding the jump key, you reduce gravity and air resistance, letting you glide through the air with increased momentum. Fall damage is reduced while gliding, though faster descents make it less effective. 

- Synergy: Electric Arc 

When the Kinetic Belt is used together with the Jellyfish Necklace, their energies combine into something far more dangerous. 

While gliding for a short duration, the wearer begins to leave behind a trail of electric chains that damage any target that comes into contact with them. 

Conditions: 
- Kinetic Belt
- Jellyfish Necklace 

- A relic for those who refuse to walk... when they can glide through the air.

quests.title: Reflective Necklace
quests.subtitle: Not all defense is meant to block...
quests.description:
Deep within the harsh lands of the Nether, a relic turns pain into power... the Reflective Necklace. 

 Forged by a master of crystals, this necklace captures the force of incoming attacks, storing it until the perfect moment to strike back. 

- It has 1 ability: 

 Damage Condensation: 
 When you take damage, there is a chance to create an orb that stores part of that damage. Upon attacking, these orbs are launched toward your target, dealing the stored damage to anything they collide with before disappearing. 

- A relic that turns pain into power... and makes every hit a mistake your enemies will regret.

quests.title: The Nether
quests.subtitle: Hope you brought fire resistance... you didn’t? Good luck.
quests.description: These Relics can be found in Ruined Portals, Nether Fortresses, and Bastions throughout The Nether!

quests.title: The End
quests.description: These Relics can be found in The End!

quests.title: Midnight Mantle
quests.subtitle: Not all power comes from the light...
quests.description:
Deep within the End, hidden among ancient ruins, lies a relic woven from night itself... the Midnight Mantle. 

This mantle shifts with the sky above, growing stronger as the Moon reaches its peak, and fading into shadow when darkness takes over. 

- It has 4 abilities: 

 1. Lunar Phase: 
 Your damage and attack speed are greatly increased, but their power depends on how close the Moon is to its full phase. 

 2. Shadow: 
 In low light, the mantle cloaks you in darkness, granting invisibility. Leaving the shadows weakens this effect for a short time, and enemies must lose sight of you before it can be used again. 

 3. Constellation: 
 Taking damage may summon wandering &zstars around you. These stars can connect into constellations, disrupting enemies who cross them, or explode when touched, damaging everything nearby. 

 4. Starfall: 
 When you strike your enemies, there is a chance to call down a falling star, creating a shockwave on impact that damages and briefly stuns targets. 

- A relic bound to the heavens... and to the darkness between them.

quests.title: Piglin Mask
quests.subtitle: Sometimes, survival isn’t about fighting… but fitting in.
quests.description:
Deep within the Nether, among the ruins of Bastions, lies a relic that lets you walk unnoticed... the Piglin Mask. 

 With it, even outsiders can blend into the chaotic society of piglins, turning enemies into uneasy allies. 

- It has 3 abilities: 

1. Neutrality: 
 Piglins will no longer attack you on sight, allowing you to move freely among them. 

2. Barter 
 When trading, piglins may reward you with multiple items for a single exchange, increasing the value of every deal. 

3. Looting 
 Defeated enemies have a chance to drop golden teeth, which can be used for trading with piglins or melted into gold. 

 A relic of greed and gold... where even monsters respect a familiar face.

quests.title: Chorus Staff
quests.subtitle: Some paths are not meant to be walked...
quests.description:
Hidden within the strange lands of the End, a relic bends space itself... the Chorus Staff. 

 Forged from the mysterious chorus plants, this staff holds the unstable power of teleportation, allowing its wielder to slip through space in the blink of an eye. 

- It has 1 ability: 

 Teleportation: 
 Using the staff instantly teleports you forward a short distance. This ability consumes charges from an internal buffer, which slowly regenerates over time. 

- A relic of movement... where every step is a disappearance.

quests.title: Ring of the Seven Deadly Sins
quests.subtitle: Some relics grant power. This one tests your soul!
quests.description:
Hidden within the burning depths of the Nether, the Ring of the Seven Deadly Sins waits for those bold enough to wear it. Each crystal bound to the ring answers to a different sin, turning weakness into strength... but never without a price. 

- It has 7 abilities: 

1. Pride: 
 Deal increased damage while standing above your target, but suffer more damage when fighting from below. 

2. Envy: 
 The healthier your enemy is compared to you, the more damage you deal. But against weaker foes, you become far more vulnerable. 

3. Wrath: 
 Each strike opens a short window of shifting power. At first your attacks hit harder, but wait too long and that same fury turns into a heavy penalty. 

4. Sloth: 
 Remain still long enough, and the ring grants immortality. But while moving, every bit of speed makes you take even more damage. 

 Next Page ->
{@pagebreak}
5. Greed: 
 The ring increases your luck and the amount of loot you gain, but sometimes it destroys the very &zrewards it helped you obtain. 

 6. Gluttony: 
 When your hunger is high, all your stats are empowered. But if your hunger drops too low, that same power becomes a weakness. 

 7. Lust: 
 Breeding animals may produce extra offspring, but those newborns are bound to a cruel fate unless the cycle is continued. 

- A relic of temptation and power... where every sin grants a blessing, and every blessing demands a cost.

quests.title: Clot of Time
quests.subtitle: Some mistakes... don’t have to be permanent.
quests.description:
Deep within fractured places of the End, where time itself once broke, a strange relic can be found... the Clot of Time. 

 This mysterious fragment holds echoes of past moments, allowing its bearer to retrace their steps as if rewriting what just happened. 

- It has 1 ability: 

 Transgression: 
 By holding the use key, you begin to rewind your movement through time, returning along your recent path for a few seconds. Once the rewind ends, the ability enters a cooldown equal to the duration it was used. 

- A relic that defies time itself... for those quick enough to rewrite their own mistakes.

quests.title: Golden Tooth
quests.subtitle: Even the smallest treasures can change fate!
quests.description:
Among the dangerous piglins of the Nether, a tiny Golden Tooth glimmers, holding the promise of wealth… and influence. 

 Those who collect these teeth quickly learn that a single piece can open doors others would never dare approach. 

- Which can be used for trading with piglins or melted into gold.

quests.title: 405DCD3E36232EEA
quests.subtitle: Release Your Inner Spartan
quests.description: Less damage than a Sword, but longer reach.

quests.title: 0D26E5EF6CFCFDBF
quests.subtitle: Stabby
quests.description: Higher Durability than a Dagger, but lower damage and speed.

quests.title: 3D2C6FF462B17205
quests.subtitle: Stabby Stab
quests.description: Low damage, very high attack speed. Reduces the invincibility time of the target.

quests.title: 39B85DB54B1037FE
quests.subtitle: Thicc Sword
quests.description: Slightly faster than a Sword, but lower damage.

quests.title: 0DF4B01CC5B49E4E
quests.subtitle: Good ol' Reliable
quests.description: With this Cast, you can make the basic sword! Reliable damage and reliable speed.

quests.title: 3722B43822F80470
quests.subtitle: Release Your Inner Samurai
quests.description: More damage than a Sword, but slower.

quests.title: Tier 2 Starlight Charger Pillar Cap
quests.description: This is a Tier 2 Pillar Cap for the Starlight Charger.

quests.title: Tier 1 Starlight Charger Pillar Cap
quests.description: This is a Tier 1 Pillar Cap for the Starlight Charger.

quests.title: Tier 3 Starlight Charger Pillar Cap
quests.description: This is a Tier 3 Pillar Cap for the Starlight Charger.

quests.title: Foundry Drains
quests.description:
Drains are what we'll use to extract our the Liquid Metals. Yes, it is unfortunately too hot for our Hands or Buckets. 

Connect the Foundry Tap to the Drain, to drain out the Liquid Metals when Right Clicking the Tap. 

You can also view the amounts of Liquids in the Foundry when viewing the Drain!

quests.title: 769D5DE66D13B256
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks.

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission.

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Silent Gear and Productive Metalworks
quests.description:
Some people like Silent Gear, while some like Tinker's Construct. 

Instead of choosing between them, we've decided to take the best of both worlds by using Silent Gear and Productive Metalworks! 

Productive Metalworks will change how we obtain our Silent Items. Instead of using Blueprints, we'll now need Casts and a Foundry. 

To start making the Foundry, start with Fire Clay.

quests.title: Foundry Controller
quests.description:
The Controller is the heart of the Foundry. 

Each Foundry will need atleast 1, to be made. 

We can use the Foundry to view the GUI of the Foundry. Here we can see the amounts of Liquids within the Foundry. 

We can also use it to put and take Items in and out of the Foundry.

quests.title: Building the Foundry
quests.description:
Now that we have a Controller, Drains, and Tanks, we'll need a few more Blocks. 

First, is Liquid Heating Coils. These will make up the floor of the Foundry, and are needed to Heat up the Foundry. 

Last is either Foundry Windows or Fire Bricks. These are what we'll use for the rest of the structure! The building blocks, quite literally. 

The Foundry will not need the frame built out, so every corner can remain empty; but it must have 4 Walls and a Floor to be completed. The Controller will tell you where a Block is missing, if there is one. 

The Foundry can be as small as 1x1 on the inside, as long as it has a Controller, Liquid Heating Coils, and the other Walls filled! 

I don't recommend making one so small though, as the bigger the Foundry, the more space it has in it! 

You'll know the Foundry is built, when the Controller lights up like a Furnace, and the Liquid Heating Coils turn Orange.

quests.title: Casting Items
quests.description:
Foundry: Check 
Liquid Metal in Foundry: Check 

Now how do we get it out? 

Remember our friend from earlier? The Foundry Drain? We'll need to acquaint him with our new friend, the Foundry Tap. 

Place the Foundry Tap on the Drain, now we can place Blocks beneath it to drain the Liquid Metal into... 

Blocks like the Casting Bin, which will turn about 900mB of Liquid Metal, into the full Metal Block. 

Or the Casting Table which is what we'll need in order to make...

quests.title: Casts
quests.description:
All Casts are made equal. In another sense I mean they are made the same way. 

By Pouring Steel onto an Item in a Casting Table! 

How do we make Steel you ask? Simply Melt down any Steel Items or Ingots. Or you can Alloy 9 Iron to 10 Coal. 

Alloying will happen when the Foundry is Heated and the right amounts of different Liquid Metals are in it. These two Liquid Metals will combine into one Liquid Metal!

quests.title: Salvager
quests.subtitle: Breaking down (some) items!
quests.description: The Salvager allows you to break down gear into the items they from.\n\nFor example: If you put in some Diamond Boots you will get 4 Diamonds back.

quests.title: 6A393C7A24899E3E
quests.subtitle: The Material Tester
quests.description:
Placing an ingot in the Grader with a Grader Catalyst will give the material a grade.

The better the grade, the better the stats are on the material.

The best grade is "MAX".

quests.title: 3930404D5C8B44EB
quests.subtitle: Combines Materials
quests.description: This is used to create custom alloys.\n\nIt is also the only way to get Tyrian Steel!

quests.title: Starlight Charger
quests.subtitle: "Enchanting" Materials
quests.description:
The Starlight Charger can "enchant" materials with the "Star Charged" enchantment.

A structure must be built with the Starlight Charger in the middle in view of the night sky. It only gains Starlight Power during the night.

The Charger must be placed in the middle of a 7x7 structure, with a Pillar in each corner. Each pillar must have a "Starlight Charger Cap".

It also requires a charger catalyst per material.

quests.title: Foundry Tanks
quests.description:
Tanks are made for adding Liquids into our Foundry. 

Mostly Fuel. 

Mostly Lava! 

That appears to be one of the only ways to actually Fuel the Foundry.

quests.title: &zDyeable Foundry &zParts
quests.description: All parts of the Foundry (except Taps, Casting Tables, and Basins) can be dyed to any &zColor. &zColors are interchangeable in a Foundry, too, so you can have multi-colored Foundries, if you like.

quests.title: 158B24939A269D83
quests.subtitle: For when you don't find 3 Diamonds
quests.description: The Tip Upgrade is used to increase the mining level of a tool.\n\nFor example: If you have an Iron Pickaxe, with 1 Diamond, you can make a Diamond Tip Upgrade, and place it on your pickaxe. This will allow it to mine Obsidian, as well as give it a stat boost.

quests.title: 3AC03D1FA5C341A7
quests.description: The Recrystallizer allows you to combine together different crystals to make new crystals to use to make weapons, tools and armor.

quests.title: 0947B4ED95B0267E
quests.subtitle: Totally not just for Netherite
quests.description: Coats an items and tools.\n\nNetherite makes a great coating material.

quests.title: 11B0B93D725ABE43
quests.subtitle: No Anvils required
quests.description:
Silent Gear gear can be repaired using a Repair Kit.

To repair an item, place the Repair Kit into a crafting grid, then place the materials needed to repair the tool in with it. This will "fill" the Repair Kit.

To repair the tool, combine the filled Repair Kit with the tool you'd like to repair in a crafting grid.

quests.title: 78E51D22C16C4686
quests.description: The Storage Controller is also able to connect to other storages wirelessly, this is possible using the Storage Tool, just right click the Storage Controller to bind it and right click the storages to link them.\n\nThe range for wireless linking is the same as regular, 14 blocks of space.

quests.title: 1FE17B1C7C639F88
quests.description:
The Storage Controller allows you to work with multiple storages as if they were one big storage multiblock.

This allows for a very large storage network, which can be combined with mods like Applied Energistics or Integrated Dynamics, as the Storage Controller acts as an in/out point for all storages attached to it.

Connecting either can be done by simply putting storages next to Storage Controller or next to others that are already connected to Storage Controller (this works up to 14 blocks away from controller in all directions).

quests.title: 0108F3EFDFD6DFD0
quests.description:
The Storage Link allows you to connect multiple storages that are not attached to a Storage Controller or any blocks that are connected to it.

So its a way to wirelessly connect a "multiblock" of storages without needing to right-click each one of them.

14 blocks of range still applies.

quests.title: Framed Drawers
quests.description: Want to have custom Drawers? Look no further, these can mimic a block's texture on the outside, and a different one in the front.\n\nFollow the tooltip on how to do it.

quests.title: Trash Cans
quests.subtitle: Getting Rid of The Excess
quests.description: Trash Cans act as a way to destroy unwanted items, liquid, and power.

quests.title: Sophisticated Storage
quests.subtitle: "Vanilla Chest"
quests.description: Sophisticated Storage allows you to upgrade your Chests and Barrels with metals to increase their storage! You can also add upgrades to increase their functionality.\n\nThese chests are just like a vanilla Chest or Barrel, but they have a slot for a Storage Upgrade!

quests.title: Copper Chest
quests.description: The Copper Chest can be made but is not needed to make an Iron Chest, it can be used if you want to save some Iron though.

quests.title: Netherite Chest
quests.subtitle: So much room for activities!
quests.description: The biggest of the chests from Sophisticated Storage

quests.title: 2B422B7E0CE3590D
quests.subtitle: Auto Compacts/Decompacts
quests.description: The Compacting Drawer can convert items placed inside to their nugget or block forms.\n\nFor example: An Iron Ingot placed in this will allow you to pull out 9 nuggets, or if more Iron is placed in, will covert it to Iron Blocks.

quests.title: Fluid Drawers
quests.description: If you thought this mod was only for storing items, you would be wrong, there are also Fluid Drawers!\n\nThey work the same way as regular Drawers, but store fluids instead.

quests.title: 4E4C8BCD45766F03
quests.subtitle: Auto Compacts/Decompacts
quests.description: This Drawer will auto convert the item placed inside it into it's compacted form.

quests.title: 1A4B1CA7EC15348E
quests.subtitle: Dimensional Drawer...
quests.description:
Using a Linking Tool, you can link 2 Ender Drawers to sync up their contents.

This works just like an Ender Chest, but as a Drawer.

To link, right-click the first Ender Drawer with the Linking Tool, then left-click the second Ender Drawer.

quests.title: 4007DFA7CC3A5FF2
quests.subtitle: The Base for Upgrades
quests.description: To save you from having this entire quest section covered with upgrades, take a look at the Sophisticated Backpack upgrades\n\nYou'll need to make the Sophisticated Storage equivalent, but they function about the same.

quests.title: Storage Controllers
quests.subtitle: The Brain of the Drawers
quests.description:
When placed and connected with the Linking Tool to other Drawers, the Controller acts as a "Hub".

If you double right-click this, all the items in your inventory that have a slot in the Drawer network will be pulled.

By sneak right-Clicking the controller with an empty hand, you can open the upgrades tab, add normal storage upgrades to those slots to increase the Controller's range. Max range is 40 blocks for all sides, or a cube of 80x80x80.

quests.title: 072FBEB0F6F1BC48
quests.description:
Used to link Drawers to a Controller and to link up Ender Drawers.

To link Drawers to the Controller, right click the Controller block to start configuration. Right clicking Drawers will add them to the network.

Holding the tool will show you what Drawers are connected to the Controller.

quests.title: Drawers
quests.subtitle: Stacks on Stacks
quests.description: Drawers can be 1x1, 2x1 or 2x2. Drawers can hold a ton of stacks of 1/2/4 items depending on the type of Drawer.

quests.title: Functional Storage
quests.subtitle: Storage Drawers Distant Relative
quests.description: Functional Storage is a storage mod that adds varuious useful items to help with storage and ways of storing stacks of the same items.\n\nThis can be useful for items like Cobblestone, Dirt and more.

quests.title: Basic Storage
quests.description: Welcome to the Basic Storage Chapter!\n\nYou'll find all of the basic ways to store items without needing power, as well as useful items for your storage needs!

quests.title: NBT and YOU!
quests.description:
Looking to create virtual storage using a mod like Applied Energistics 2?

These are great ways to upgrade your storage, but it is important to talk about NBT Items and the best way to store them.

NBT items are items with extra tags attached to them. Enchanted items, items with durability and more. These are items with NBT tags attached to them. Because of this, they don't usually stack.

When you store a lot of these into a storage system like AE2, you run the chance of creating issues for your save or server.

Because of this, it is best to store them in Chests or Bags!

quests.title: 508A8366219175FE
quests.description: The Configuration Tool is used to lock Drawers for them to remember the item it has inside.\n\nThis can be useful whenever you set up a system to push and pull from Drawers. The locked Drawer will not replace the item that was locked on it!

quests.title: 11D4EEAC61C7E530
quests.description: The Collector Upgrade will make the Drawer vacuum items in from one of the sides.

quests.title: 19DFAEB6D88F3580
quests.description: The Pusher Upgrade allows Drawers to push out items into any side.

quests.title: 61A22707DBC83818
quests.description: The Storage Access Point acts as a Storage Controller when linked to it, being able to be pushed into or pulled from. Basically a entry point for the Drawers.

quests.title: 209DC1E9AD4C5A84
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks.

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission.

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Sophisticated Backpacks
quests.subtitle: Inventories are too Small
quests.description: Sophisticated Backpacks offers upgradable Backpacks that can use filters to add nifty features!\n\nBackpacks can be put in your Curios Back slot and they can be dyed.

quests.title: 70902EF96F060672
quests.description:
This upgrade will make Drawers output a Redstone signal on all sides, signal strength saying how full/empty it is.

For multi-slot Drawers, the upgrade can be configured to which slot to monitor.

0 - means empty.
15 - means full.

quests.title: 7649D648A3688D4A
quests.description: The Puller Upgrade allows Drawers to pull in items from any side.

quests.title: 122FBF5110E4CFF2
quests.description: The Iron Downgrade will downgrade the Drawer's max space to a stack. This can be usefull for keeping items on stock, but not too many.

quests.title: 1CACE201C6AA0913
quests.description: This upgrade will void extra items that come when Drawers are full.\n\nThis can be usefull to prevent overflow or to prevent a setup from backing up due to the storage being full.

quests.title: 7F990FBC1A691020
quests.subtitle: "I wonder what's in here?"

quests.title: 5AA3E5DFECB4AC4D
quests.description: Naturally, AE2 provides its own way to dramatically speed up crystal growth.\n\nPlace these around your Budding Crystals, give them some power, and watch your crystals grow!

quests.title: Patterns
quests.description: Patterns are what hold an encoded recipe to be fulfilled by a Pattern Provider. To encode a recipe onto a Pattern, the ME Pattern Encoding Terminal must be used.\n\nPatterns can be set to hold either a regular crafting recipe, which will require the use of a Molecular Assembler on the face of its Provider, or a more general 'processing' recipe, wherein any input items can be sent out by the provider into some other machine block or specialised processing plant.

quests.title: 4597D3B3BDC2BED5
quests.description:
The Molecular Assembler is AE2's equivalent of an automatic crafting table, required to fulfil any and all crafting pattern jobs.

Molecular Assemblers are capable of transferring power and channels to other ME devices connected to it, but will not themselves take up a channel. Up to 6 MAs can be connected to a single Pattern Provider (if employed) to allow for more crafts to be done in parallel.

MAs also each have their own dedicated slot for a single crafting pattern, allowing them to function standalone when powered. When operated in this way, any matching items inserted into the MA will be automatically crafted into the result of the pattern.

quests.title: 1F7DFA5AA65F2812
quests.description: The Acceleration Card, depending on the device being upgraded with it, will either increase the speed at which the device operates or allow the device to carry out more operations in one go.\n\nIn the case of the Molecular Assembler, a full set of 5 cards reduces the time taken for the MA to fulfil a craft from one second (with no cards) to one tick.

quests.title: Auto-Crafting
quests.subtitle: Order up
quests.description:
Storage is nice and all that, but what good is a storage system if it's clogged up with raw materials needing to be crafted and processed into something and you're still stuck with having to do so manually?
AE2's auto-crafting system begins with the ME Pattern Provider. The Pattern Provider holds certain items called Patterns (covered in the next quest) which are programmed to hold some recipe that turns input items into a certain output. Up to 9 patterns can fit in one provider.
You'll often be making use of multiple pattern providers scattered all throughout your base, which is why it's useful to have a Pattern Access Terminal to remotely access the contents of any and all providers on your wider ME network.

quests.title: ME Level Emitter
quests.description: The ME Level Emitter, when configured with a specific item and quantity of it to respond to, will emit a redstone signal depending on whether that item stored in the network either falls below, goes above or equals the given quantity.\n\nThis can be used, for example, to automatically switch certain machines on with redstone to auto-craft a resource when it falls below a given minimum amount.

quests.title: Redstone-Controlled ME
quests.description: Individual ME devices can also be configured to respond to redstone signals. When upgraded with a Redstone Card, a device can be configured to do work only when powered with redstone or otherwise as needed.\n\nThis behavior can also apply to entire sections of an ME network by using an ME Toggle Bus. This allows a section of the network on the other side of the bus to come online only when the bus is powered by redstone, or to go offline if using an inverted toggle bus.

quests.title: 5E6585F7627247E3
quests.subtitle: Automation in upgrade form!
quests.description: When applied as an upgrade to any supported device such as an Interface or Export Bus, the Crafting Card allows the device in question to automatically send out its own crafting requests for a required (filtered) item. Crafting CPUs can be set to respond only to these requests to prevent taking up CPUs meant for player-requested crafts.\n\nWhen the Level Emitter is upgraded with the Crafting Card, it can be configured to emit redstone in order to directly facilitate in crafting, by emitting a signal either while a crafting job for its given item is detected or specifically to craft the item. The latter would apply for cases where the only thing needed to make a given item is a redstone signal, without even requiring a crafting pattern.

quests.title: 371A382CF1DDF2B2
quests.description: The Capacity Card allows a bus upgraded with it to carry a larger filter. Import and Export buses upgraded with capacity cards can go from supporting only one filtered item each to their maximum nine-slot filter, while Storage buses will go from 18 slots to a maximum of 63.

quests.title: Loosely Speaking
quests.subtitle: The remaining two IO cards
quests.description: The Fuzzy Card allows a filtered item to be matched regardless of any (NBT) metadata such as damage or enchantments, while the Inverter Card toggles the filter on such buses from being a whitelist to being a blacklist.

quests.title: Crafting Storage
quests.subtitle: Download more RAM
quests.description: Before you can carry out an auto-crafting job, you need a device to actually store the request itself along with any interim items for multi-step crafts. This device is known as a crafting CPU.\n\nA crafting CPU is a multiblock structure requiring at least one Crafting Storage block, optionally along with any other Crafting Unit. The multiblock can be made in any size, but must be a solid cuboid in order to form and function accordingly.

quests.title: 69B7DE2283B4EE6C
quests.subtitle: Download more CPU cores
quests.description: The Crafting Co-Processing Unit helps speed up crafting jobs by allowing pattern providers to either send items out to their connected devices faster or to work concurrently to make multiple required ingredients.\n\nThe base AE2 co-processor provides one co-processor 'thread' to assist this, while the co-processing unit from MEGA Cells provides 4 threads in a single such block.

quests.title: 1348995F64A94396
quests.subtitle: Download more VRAM
quests.description: The Crafting Monitor displays the overall item being crafted, along with the remaining quantity of that item still being crafted.\n\nBoth the base AE2 monitor and the MEGA monitor function identically, but are provided for aesthetic purposes.

quests.title: 140DE53DC0FCD9F4
quests.subtitle: GET IN
quests.description:
The ME Annihilation Plane can be used to automatically break any blocks in front of it and return anything dropped by the block directly to the ME network.
As an added bonus, the Annihilation Plane can be enchanted in the same way as a regular digging tool, affecting block drops in the same way as that enchanted tool would. This makes it ideal for processing ore blocks when enchanted with Fortune, for example.
Any added enchantments significantly increase the amount of energy used by the plane every time a block is broken. Enchanting the plane with Efficiency will decrease the overall energy use incurred by all other enchantments, while the Unbreaking enchantment gives the plane the chance to only use any energy sometimes, similarly to Unbreaking on regular tools.

quests.title: 525F25F4ADE45B50
quests.subtitle: GET OUT
quests.description:
The ME Formation Plane acts similarly to the Storage Bus, but treats the world itself as its storage medium. In other words, it will place down any block in its filter directly in front of itself.
This can be useful for situations where a block can be processed simply by placing it and breaking it with a certain tool.

quests.title: 5034A9137E0F3D3D
quests.description:

quests.title: 00611844AFD5C31E
quests.subtitle: Plug in
quests.description: While the Inscriber and Charger will natively accept RF/FE, the vast majority of an ME network uses its own dedicated power system called AE.\n\nRF/FE can be converted into the native AE at a ratio of 2:1 RF:AE, either directly through an ME Controller, or through the Energy Acceptor, which can instead be connected to any part of the network.

quests.title: 037488EF1F3581CE
quests.description: By default, an ME network on its own only has an internal buffer of 800AE without an ME Controller, with the controller adding an extra 8kAE per block. For large enough networks, this can be insufficient and may cause a network to power off intermittently when trying to recoup power for any connected devices.\n\nThe Energy Cell allows for an ME network to hold significantly more energy, adding another 200kAE per regular Energy Cell and 1.6MAE per Dense Energy Cell. These can also be placed anywhere in the network to provide the increased energy buffer.

quests.title: 6D54B45CDA70FEAB
quests.description: The Energy Card can be applied to most chargeable devices like Portable Cells and Wireless Terminals (covered later) to also increase their energy buffer.

quests.title: Network Tools
quests.description:
The Network Tool is an important tool throughout AE2, which is used to display various details of a network on-screen such as overall power consumption and storage.
As an added bonus, it also provides its own small inventory used to hold upgrade cards, which can be accessed when looking at any upgradeable device's screen for easy replacement. However, it cannot rotate blocks attached to the ME network like a regular wrench, only dismantle them when sneaking.

quests.title: 7EFBAF3E281D2EBE
quests.subtitle: The spare chest
quests.description:
The ME Storage Bus, when facing some external storage container, will allow the container to be used as though it were part of the ME network, allowing items to be taken out from the container or inserted into it purely via ME.
Storage buses can be filtered and given specific priorities such that specific items will try to go to the attached storage first, however it will not retroactively move any filtered items from anywhere else in the network to its attached storage.

quests.title: 55186B8602689B66
quests.description:
The Memory Card is a tool with two different functions. The simplest of the two is to save various devices' configurations (such as whitelist filters) to be copied over to another device of the same kind.
The second function of a memory card is to link P2P tunnels together. When doing so, the P2P tunnel being linked will be assigned a unique ID, which is stored on the memory card for further linking.

quests.title: Applied Energistics 2
quests.subtitle: Virtual Storage System
quests.description:
Welcome to Applied Energistics 2!

Applied Energistics 2 (or AE2 for short) is an incredibly versatile digital storage mod, allowing for extremely efficient storage and all sorts of automation capabilities to greatly augment your modded Minecraft experience from as early as you want to the very endgame.

For more information on AE2 beyond this chapter, consult the wiki over at
appliedenergistics.github.io.

quests.title: First Things First
quests.subtitle: First Things First
quests.description:
Two of the very first things you will need to get started in AE2 are the Charger and the Inscriber.

The Charger, when supplied with power, will take Certus Quartz Crystals and charge them. These Charged Certus Crystals can then be used in the production of Fluix, another important resource in the mod. It can also be used to charge any item that stores power.

The Inscriber can be used to turn the various quartz crystals in AE2 into their dust form, but more importantly is used to fabricate special Printed Circuits and Processors, as will become clearer in the next quest.

quests.title: Meteorite hunting
quests.subtitle: 'COMIC #42: shearching 4 bobby [Fischer]'
quests.description:
It is time to find Meteorites that contain Sky Stone. These can be either on the surface or underground, and contain a Mysterious Cube in its center.

This cube contains all of the different Presses used in the Inscriber to make AE2's special crafting components.

The easiest way to locate a meteorite is by crafting a Meteorite Compass by placing a compass inside of a Charger.

quests.title: Certus Quartz
quests.description: To get started with AE2, you will need to mine an important resource for the mod known as Certus Quartz. You will find Certus Quartz Crystals in Meteroites that you can mine for Certus Quartz Dust and Crystals.

quests.title: Processors
quests.description: Once you have obtained a full set of the required Inscriber Presses, it's time to start making some Processors. These are an important crafting ingredient used to make the large majority of ME-connected devices.

quests.title: Terminals
quests.subtitle: [Linux user joke goes here]
quests.description: Terminals provide access to any of the contents of an ME network. The standard ME Terminal simply lists everything in the network as one large grid to pull from and insert into, akin to a single inventory.\n\nThe ME Crafting Terminal is an extension of the ME Terminal which also provides a built-in crafting grid, allowing for convenient crafting using any item contained in the network and visible through the terminal screen.

quests.title: 7B7D1F0CB326B28F
quests.subtitle: Defragmentation
quests.description: The ME IO Port allows for the contents of an ME network's storage to be quickly rearranged between different storage media such as ME cells and external containers connected to storage buses.\n\nWhen a cell is inserted in an input slot on the left, the IO Port can be toggled to either empty the cell out into other ME storages or fill the (ideally, partitioned) cell with certain items spread out across other storages.

quests.title: The... Weapons?
quests.subtitle: Too hot for the ATF
quests.description:
These last three items are more or less some extra toys provided by AE2 and don't necessarily fit under any of these quest trees.

The Charged Staff is just a simple powered staff which deals 3 hearts of damage and consumes 300AE per hit. It also uses pre-1.9 combat mechanics, meaning that you can spam-click with this like in the good old days.

The Entropy Manipulator, when used on certain blocks in the world, will smelt them in-place, such as sand to glass and metal ores to metal ingots. If not, it will simply light a fire on the block.
