Finally, the Matter Cannon functions similarly to the Color Applicator as a dedicated cell for holding 'ammo' items such as Matter Balls and iron/gold nuggets, which can then be fired out to deal damage to mobs or break blocks. Heavier 'ammo'Matter Balls in a Matter Cannon can be substituted with Paint Balls, which will apply a paint splatter effect on the face of whatever block being fired at. Lumen Paint Balls are a variant of paint balls exclusively used by the Matter Cannon, whose paint splatters also give off some light once present in the world.

quests.title: Bulk Item Storage
quests.subtitle: Bulk and cut
quests.description: MEGA Cells offers the bespoke Bulk Item Storage Cell, which is limited to no more than one type of item storeable per cell but can store a practically INFINITE* number of that item type. Before it can accept an item type, it must be filtered in advance using a Cell Workbench.\n\n*Technically "max long". If you know, you know.

quests.title: 5E7E35CCAF1C88EE
quests.subtitle: The I
quests.description: The ME Import Bus periodically sucks items in from whatever external storage the bus is facing. It can optionally be filtered to only take in certain items from said inventory.

quests.title: 083D458032F0325C
quests.subtitle: The O
quests.description: The ME Export Bus periodically spits items in its whitelist filter out to whatever external storage the bus is facing. Unlike the Import Bus, the Export Bus cannot work without being filtered.

quests.title: Quartz Wrench
quests.subtitle: Does exactly what you'd expect
quests.description: The Quartz Wrench does what any regular tech mod wrench would do. It rotates blocks and devices along the face you right-click on and dismantles them when right-clicked while sneaking.\n\nThis Wrench comes in both Certus Quartz and Nether Quartz varieties.

quests.title: Fluix
quests.description:
Arguably the most important resource you will need next is Fluix, used throughout the vast majority of AE2 devices and serving as a base for crafting all of the cabling within an ME network.
You'll typically want to mass produce these, and the way to do so is to make a Fluix Crystal by throwing Nether Quartz, Charged Certus quartz and Redstone together in a pool of water. This will give you a Fluix Crystal which you can turn to dust in an Inscriber.

quests.title: Basic Cabling
quests.description:
To connect the vast majority of your ME network together, you will need some cable. ME Glass Cable is the first and most basic kind of cable, and you'll be making this all throughout as the first step towards crafting the other kinds of cable.

Both glass cables and their covered counterpart can carry up to 8 channels along a single section of cabling. Unlike glass cables, covered cables can subsequently be crafted into dense covered cables, capable of carrying up to 32 channels. However, most 'multipart' devices such as buses and terminals cannot be directly attached to dense cables, requiring normal-width cables to form a connection instead.

All cables can also be crafted with dye to colour them. Uncoloured ('Fluix') cables can connect to any other colour of cable, but otherwise differently-coloured cables will never connect to one another.

quests.title: Foreword on Channels
quests.description:
In Applied Energistics 2, every ME network has a certain number of channels available, which simply means how many networked devices can fit on the whole network.

As a rule of thumb, any device that more or less handles ME data directly (items stored within the network) and carries out some form of I/O will take up a channel. Usually components that are only concerned with the internal power storage of the network, like Energy Cells and Inscribers, do not take up channels.

Networks without an ME Controller are known as 'ad-hoc' networks and only support a maximum of 8 channels.

quests.title: 2F16B6A173525277
quests.description:
The last piece of the puzzle for any large ME network is the ME Controller.
A controller supplies an ME Network with a far larger number of channels than the standard 8 channels for ad-hoc networks, providing 32 channels out of each face of the block for a total of 216 channels.
That's only for a single-block controller, however, since the ME Controller is in fact a multi-block structure. The controller can be up to 7x7x7 blocks in size and can come in any freeform arrangement within that maximum size. Each individual block can then provide its own separate set of channels, so long as no single controller block is surrounded by 4 other blocks along the same plane.
An ME Network may only contain one multiblock controller at any given time. Attempting to connect more than one controller on separate parts of the network will cause a conflict, shutting down the whole network.

quests.title: The Storage
quests.subtitle: Items as a file system
quests.description:
Arguably the most important aspect of Applied Energistics 2 is its storage system, making use of digital Storage Cells. These cells are accessible through either an ME Chest for single cells, or an ME Drive for multiple cells.

The ME Chest holds a single Cell at a time, which can then be read from and written to from any other terminal on the same network. The ME Chest itself also provides its own terminal screen on the top with specific access only to the cell it contains.

The ME Drive can hold up to 10 assorted Storage Cells in the space of a single block and a single ME channel. However, it does not provide its own terminal screen, requiring some external terminal elsewhere on the network for storage access.

quests.title: Creating your first Storage Cell
quests.subtitle: The first kilobyte.
quests.description: Each individual cell has a certain capacity dictated by the component that the cell has been crafted with.\n\nThe first of the components is the 1k ME Storage Component, providing 1024 'bytes' of storage for a given cell. More on that later.

quests.title: Item Storage
quests.description:
With the 1k Storage Component, you can now craft yourself a 1k ME Item Storage Cell to start your digital item storage system. You'll most likely want the majority of your storage to be for items, so you'll probably want to make a few ME Item Storage Cells.
ME Item Storage Cells can each hold up to 63 different types of items. Each new type of item added to a cell will take up a certain fraction of the storage cell's total capacity in bytes. For each type already present, 1 'byte' counts for 8 items of that same type.
As an example, a 1k Item Storage Cell containing only cobblestone can hold up to 8128 cobblestone (8*1024b - 8b/type * 1 type).
If a cell is empty, it can be repurposed by disassembling it into its respective component and housing. This is done by sneaking and right-clicking in the air with the cell in your hand.

quests.title: Fluid Storage
quests.description:
Items are not the only things that can be stored in ME cells. ME Fluid Storage Cells can store liquids such as water, lava and any variety of modded oils and fuels, just to give a few examples.
Note that all storage cells, regardless of what they're designed to store, only differ in terms of their housing; both item and fluid cells use the same kind of storage component to make.
For fluids, 1 byte equals 8 buckets (8000mb).

quests.title: The IO
quests.subtitle: OI, OI, OI!
quests.description:
To make life that much easier, AE2 provides a whole suite of devices for the manipulation of ME data, i.e. moving stored items around the world.

The ME Interface is one of these devices. As an input device, the Interface allows any item/fluid/etc to be piped externally through it, which is then automatically stored in the ME Network that the interface is connected to.

As an output device, the Interface can be configured to keep a certain available amount of a stored item in stock, from the ME network to its own internal inventory. This allows items to then be received by some external source like another player or some pipe.

quests.title: P2P Tunnels
quests.subtitle: Cut out the middleman
quests.description:
P2P (peer-to-peer) is a powerful system within AE2, allowing for the transfer of items, fluids and even more without the need for any intermediary ME storage.
Right-clicking on a P2P tunnel with certain items will attune the tunnel into one capable of transferring something else, such as items through pipes, energy through cables, redstone signals and (by default) even ME connections themselves.
P2P tunnels must be linked to one another with the use of a Memory Card, detailed in the next quest.

quests.title: Cable Anchor
quests.subtitle: Under the knife
quests.description:
The Quartz Cutting Knife, like the wrench, comes in both nether and certus quartz flavours and is a useful crafting tool to have on hand.

Cables can also be separated without needing to be coloured by attaching a Cable Anchor between them, crafted using this knife and craftable up to 50 times with the same knife before it breaks.

Cable Anchors can also be used to craft Cable Facades, allowing you to disguise cables within walls by covering them with the face of an arbitrary block. While facade recipes are hidden in JEI, you can still craft them by taking any regular block and surrounding it with 4 cable anchors in the crafting grid.

Aside from crafting anchors, the cutting knife also has another use: right-clicking with the knife will open a small GUI that allows you to craft Inscriber Name Presses. When given a name, these presses can be used inside of an Inscriber to rename any input item with the name of the press. Two of these presses can be concatenated in the inscriber to rename the item to the name of the top press, followed by the bottom one.

quests.title: Color Applicator
quests.description: The Color Applicator is a chargeable tool that allows for in-world dyeing of cables. It functions more or less as a specialised storage cell to be loaded up with either vanilla dyes or paint balls for specific colours, along with snowballs to wash colours off and turn cables back to their Fluix variant.\n\nApplying colour to a cable uses 100AE of energy from its internal battery, for a total of 3400 cable segments in a single charge.

quests.title: 2F556E7919582D2D
quests.description: The Cell Workbench allows for cells to be 'partitioned' to hold specific items, i.e. given a whitelist filter. It also allows the cell to be upgraded with certain upgrade cards such as the Inverter Card, which sets the aforementioned whitelist to be a blacklist instead.\n\nCells can also be given a higher or lower 'priority' via the workbench, i.e. allow the cell to be the first to receive certain items until full, or made to wait for other higher-priority cells to fill up first.

quests.title: 33ADE41526C39AFD
quests.description: This behaviour is comparable to something like a Functional Storage drawer, wherein each compartment holds a set number of stacks as opposed to allowing items from one compartment to leak into the others and crowd other kinds of items out.

quests.title: 4k Storage Component
quests.subtitle: x4
quests.description: The second tier of storage component, providing 4096 bytes of storage.

quests.title: Portable Storage
quests.description:
Portable Cells function identically to regular cells in that they can be inserted into a chest or drive and filled accordingly.
However, unlike regular cells, their contents can also be accessed standalone via the cell item itself, a bit like a digital ME-flavoured backpack.

quests.title: Forgot to Mention
quests.subtitle: This has a use outside of crafting cables.
quests.description:
An important concept within AE2 is a technique known as 'subnetting', wherein an extra separate ME network (a subnetwork) acts in conjunction with the main network to perform some specialised function or process.
What separates a subnetwork from a completely detached separate network is usually the use of the Quartz Fiber as a cable part. When placed between two otherwise unconnected lengths of cable, the Quartz Fiber transfers no data or channels between the two whatsoever, instead only transmitting power.
Thus, a subnetwork on the other side of the Fiber can be powered wholly by the main network's power source, without requiring any extra dedicated powergen.

quests.title: Advanced Cabling
quests.subtitle: 'S.M.R.T.'
quests.description: The ME Smart Cable and Dense Smart Cable function identically to the covered cables in terms of channel distribution, but will also visibly display the amount of channels they are using as coloured lines along themselves.

quests.title: 16k Storage Component
quests.subtitle: x4^2
quests.description: The third tier of storage component, providing 16384 bytes of storage.

quests.title: 256k Storage Component
quests.subtitle: x4^4
quests.description: The fifth and final AE2-standard tier of storage component, providing 262144 bytes of storage.

quests.title: Condensed Matter
quests.description:
As for wirelessly expanding the ME Network itself, the first step is admittedly somewhat unorthodox.

The Matter Condenser is AE2's take on a trash can, voiding any items inserted into it. When fitted with a Storage Component, however, the condenser can harness some left-over energy from the item being voided and store it to make two special crafting items out of enough concentrated energy.

The first of these two items is the Matter Ball, requiring at least a 1k storage component and 256 items' worth of voided material.

quests.title: 3195A7AA874163CD
quests.subtitle: ME Storage Cells Drawers
quests.description: The Equal Distribution Card is an upgrade for storage cells that pre-allocates a certain amount of items that can be taken up by any individual type.\n\nThis behaviour is comparable to something like a Functional Storage drawer, wherein each compartment holds a set number of stacks as opposed to allowing items from one compartment to leak into the others and crowd other kinds of items out.

quests.title: 64k Storage Component
quests.subtitle: x4^3
quests.description: The fourth tier of storage component, providing 65536 bytes of storage.

quests.title: 256M Storage Component
quests.subtitle: x4^4
quests.description: The fifth and final MEGA tier of storage component, providing 268435456 (262144k) bytes of storage.

quests.title: 1M Storage Component
quests.subtitle: The first MEGAbyte.
quests.description: There comes a point in any playthrough of a large modpack where even the highest standard tier of storage cell doesn't cut it for the amount of items and resources that you may be accumulating.\n\nThis is where the MEGA Cells add-on comes in, extending the available tiers of storage into the megabyte territory. The first of these new tiers is given by the 1M MEGA Storage Component, providing 1024 kilobytes, or 1048576 bytes, of storage.

quests.title: 4M Storage Component
quests.subtitle: x4
quests.description: The second MEGA tier of storage component, providing 4194304 (4096k) bytes of storage.

quests.title: 64M Storage Component
quests.subtitle: x4^3
quests.description: The fourth MEGA tier of storage component, providing 67108864 (65536k) bytes of storage.

quests.title: 16M Storage Component
quests.subtitle: x4^2
quests.description: The third MEGA tier of storage component, providing 16777216 (16384k) bytes of storage.

quests.title: Hyper-Condensed Matter
quests.subtitle: Hyper-Condensed Matter
quests.description: When using a 64k storage component or higher, the Matter Condenser becomes able to condense significantly more to produce a Singularity. A single singularity requires 256000 items to be voided. That's exactly 4000 stacks!\n\nSee what happens when you throw this singularity on the ground with a piece of Ender Dust. You'll have to deal some damage to the surroundings while you're at it, but thankfully AE2 offers its own Tiny TNT to minimise that.

quests.title: Quantum Network Bridge
quests.description: If you did that last quest correctly, you should have turned that singularity into a pair of Quantum Entangled Singularities. These new singularities are used to link together a ring-shaped device known as a Quantum Network Bridge.\n\nWhen two of these individual rings have been linked using the Quantum Entangled Singularities and jumpstarted with some AE power (e.g. an energy cell), an ME network can be expanded wirelessly on the other side of the bridge, across either long distances or even dimensions.

quests.title: 2B31E6C1707D8195
quests.description: The next thing to make to allow for wireless network access is the ME Wireless Access Point. The Access Point is used to open the network to wireless access via a wireless terminal, and has a set (finite) range depending on how many Wireless Boosters are inserted into the access point.

quests.title: Spatial Storage Cell
quests.description:
Spatial Storage Cells are used to hold one defined volume each, and come in three different capacities allowing for a maximum of 2x2x2, 16x16x16 and 128x128x128 blocks' worth of space.
Upon encoding, a cell is allocated a section of space within the spatial storage dimension, along with a unique ID corresponding to the region allocated to the cell. An encoded cell can still be used within the Spatial IO Port to retrieve any stored blocks and entities.
From then on, any blocks contained either within the cell's region of space or in an SCS with the same size as the one used for the initial encoding can be moved back into the overworld or into the spatial dimension respectively. If there are blocks both within the spatial region and within the SCS, these will simply swap places accordingly.

quests.title: 2897FA291E5A38D8
quests.description: The Spatial Anchor is a companion device from the Spatial IO lineage that simply functions as a chunk loader. When connected to an ME network, the Anchor will force-load all the chunks occupied by the ME network across all cables and devices, excluding subnetworks, as long as the network remains powered.

quests.title: 4B76FE0348DB0E45
quests.description: The Quantum Bridge Card is an alternate method to get wireless interdimensional access to your Applied Energistics system. You will need a Quantum Bridge connected at your base and a Quantum Bridge Card in your terminal. These tunnels are then bound together with a Quantum Entangled Singularity to gain access wherever you go.

quests.title: Wireless Terminals
quests.subtitle: This is what you're here for
quests.description:
The Wireless Terminal functions identically to a regular terminal, but wirelessly.

Before it can be used to access a network, it must first be linked to the network by placing it into the top-right slot of the Wireless Access Point. If it is not linked to a network, or is out of either range or power, the terminal will not function.

Wireless terminals can also be upgraded with Energy Cards to provide a larger internal battery.

quests.title: Infinity Booster
quests.subtitle: I'm not writing the Toy Story line
quests.description: The AEInfinityBooster add-on provides two bespoke wireless boosters allowing for infinite connectivity range, with optional cross-dimensional support.

quests.title: Spatial IO
quests.description:
Aside from the storage of items and fluids, AE2 also provides a native way of storing entire structures inside of storage cells, not too dissimilarly to the Compact Machines mod.
The Spatial IO Port allows structures contained within a Spatial Containment Structure to be captured within a specially-designed storage cell, activated via a redstone signal.
If a mob or player happens to stand inside of the SCS while the space is being captured, they too will be transported to where the rest of the space goes, i.e. in a dedicated dimension. Just make sure you have a way to get back out and in if you're the one being captured.

quests.title: 18DFB25DC48D8BF7
quests.description:
The Spatial Containment Structure (SCS) consists of a cage of Spatial Pylons covering the volume you wish to enclose in a Spatial IO cell. At the absolute minimum, an SCS requires three lines of spatial pylon blocks, one for each dimension of the space being contained (length, width, height).
However, Spatial IO is an extremely power-hungry feature, especially when trying to capture much larger spaces (up to 128x128x128). Having more spatial pylons included in the SCS around the desired volume will increase its overall efficiency, allowing it to use less energy to capture.
Also, be mindful that each individual pylon (regardless of its length) takes up one channel. For particularly large spaces, you may wish to build a dedicated network with a controller to fit all the required pylons.

quests.title: Assembler Matrix Cores
quests.description:
The Assembler Matrix Cores are what determine the pattern capacity, crafting jobs, and speed of the multiblock.
Craft Cores add 8 maximum parallel crafting jobs to the multiblock.
Pattern Cores add 36 pattern slots to the multiblock.
Speed Cores work like an Acceleration Card, increasing the speed of crafting jobs. Installing more than 5 Speed Cores does not have an effect on the speed of each crafting job.

quests.title: Many Assemblers In One: The Assembler Matrix
quests.subtitle: Many Molecular Assemblers and Pattern Providers in One Channel
quests.description:
The Assembler Matrix is a multiblock that can effectively contain multiple Molecular Assemblers and Pattern Providers, all in one channel.
The Assembler Matrix must be at least a 3x3x3 cuboid and up to a 7x7x7 cuboid. It requires the following parts:
- Edges composed of Assembler Matrix Frames
- Faces composed of Assembler Matrix Wall/Glass
- Interior composed of Assembler Matrix Pattern/Craft/Speed Core
A valid Assembler Matrix must contain at least one pattern core and craft core. It must be completely filled and can't be hollow. When the Assembler Matrix is correctly formed and powered, the lines on the frame will turn blue.
{@pagebreak}
In this example, we will be making a 7x7x7 Assembler Matrix, focused mainly on balance between craft and pattern cores.
Make the first 43 Assembler Matrix Frames and the first 125 Assembler Matrix Walls. I'll give 25 of each as a gift in the rewards for this quest (to reach a total of 68 frames and 150 walls)

quests.title: Automating Entro Crystals
quests.subtitle: For when you can't deal with decay
quests.description:
Given the inevitability of the decay of Budding Entroized Fluix, you might want some other ways to automatically farm them.
Fortunately, there's a bee for that. And a seed, as well.

quests.title: Faster and Bigger: Extended Devices
quests.description:
Extended Devices are variants of AE2 devices that either have a higher capacity, are faster, and maybe even both.
For example: The Extended Pattern Provider has 36 pattern slots, 4 times as many as an ordinary Pattern Provider.
Or the Extended Export/Import Buses, they work about 8x faster than a regular one, and support more upgrades.
As most of these are just upgraded versions of the base version, I won't be making separate quests for each individual one.

quests.title: Can this Liquid: The ME Canner
quests.subtitle: not to be confused with the me caner
quests.description: The ME Canner can fill or empty containers that can contain fluids, chemicals, energy, such as buckets, chemical tanks, and more. It automatically outputs to pattern providers if a pattern is used to fill them.

quests.title: Get-Yer-Crystals-Fixed: The Crystal Fixer
quests.description:
Getting tired of your budding Certus Quartz and Entroized Fluix decaying? We can fix it! With this Crystal Fixer, you can fix Budding Certus Crystals with Charged Certus Quartz, and Entroized Fluix with Ender Dust.
It even has a small chance to make Flawless Budding Certus Quartz.

quests.title: Actively Placing From The Network: The Active Formation Plane
quests.subtitle: GET OUT: Active Edition
quests.description: Ever thought that Formation Planes acting like a Storage Bus was way too unintuitive for automation? Look no further than the Active Formation Plane. It works like an ME Export Bus but it treats the world as its medium. You don't need a subnet for this one.

quests.title: ExtendedAE
quests.description:
ExtendedAE is an addon for Applied Energistics 2, focused on adding improved versions of various devices, and bringing back some features from older versions of AE2.
To get started, get a Fluix Block.

quests.title: The Crystals of Space and Time: Entro Crystals
quests.subtitle: not to be confused with time crystals
quests.description:
Throughout ExtendedAE, you will often be using Entro Crystals as a resource.
To get the Entro Crystal, you will need a Fluix Block and an Entro Seed. Right click the Fluix Block with the Entro Seed.
This will create Budding Entroized Fluix, which will, similarly to Budding Certus Quartz, grow Entro Buds around it. Unlike with Certus, its decay is inevitable.
Budding Entroized Fluix will always drop one Entro Dust when broken, regardless of the state it's in. Entro Buds will drop Entro Shards when they aren't fully grown.

quests.title: Complex Crafter: The Crystal Assembler
quests.description:
To make all these ExtendedAE devices, a Crafting Table's hammer and pliers won't cut it.
It's time we upgrade to the Crystal Assembler, a machine capable of handling these complex operations.
With these, you can assemble the various devices of ExtendedAE.
These are also capable of handling In-World Reactions, but not quite as well as the Reaction Chamber, and also capable of assembling processors, 4 at a time.
The face that has a screen can't connect to an ME Network.

quests.title: Better Pattern Access: The Extended Pattern Access Terminal
quests.description:
The Extended Pattern Access Terminal works the same as the regular Pattern Access Terminal, but with 3 additional features.
Improved Pattern Search
You can search for a pattern by input/output ingredients' name.
Pattern Highlight
Sometimes, due to how patterns are displayed in a group, it is still hard to find the pattern you are looking for. With this terminal, the pattern you are looking for will be highlighted in the GUI.
Pattern Provider In-World Highlight
It can be annoying to find out which of your Pattern Providers are stuck when doing large crafting jobs. The Extended Pattern Access Terminal can highlight the Pattern Providers in world, making it easier to locate it.

quests.title: Blocks to Circuits: The Circuit Slicer
quests.description:
Tired of the slow speed of the Inscriber?
We present the Circuit Slicer! It can slice blocks such as Gold Blocks into circuits, making up to 9 circuits at a time (or 4 in the case of certus or entro).
The glass faces of the Circuit Slicer that don't have a port can't connect to an ME Network.

quests.title: Connections across long distances: The Wireless Connector
quests.description:
The ME Wireless Connector can be used to connect two points of an ME Network wirelessly, similarly to the Quantum Bridge. Unlike the Quantum Bridge, it can only connect to Wireless Connectors up to about 1000 blocks away, and cannot connect across dimensions.
To set up a connection, use a Wireless Setup Kit on the two Wireless Connectors you want to link.
You can also change the color of a Wireless Connector with the Color Applicator. This will make it not connect to cables or Wireless Connectors of a different color.

quests.title: Branches of Connections: The Wireless Hub
quests.description: The ME Wireless Hub is an upgrade to the ME Wireless Connector. It can now connect to 8 different Wireless Connectors or Hubs. Note that the Hub can only transfer 32 channels in total.

quests.title: Non-Entro Things
quests.description: These are things from ExtendedAE that don't require Entro Crystals.

quests.title: Matter Condenser in a Cell: The Void Cell
quests.description:
The Void Cell needs to be partitioned (filtered) in a Cell Workbench before using. It will delete anything that enters the ME system that matches the filter (assuming the void cell is prioritized), or condenses them into Matter Balls or Singularities, similarly to the Matter Condenser.
Right click it to open the configuration GUI.

quests.title: Extended & Advanced AE
quests.description: Extended and Advanced AE are addons for Applied Energistics 2. Both of them focus on improving your experience, adding improved versions of various devices, and more.

quests.title: AllRightsReserved
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks.

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission.

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: More Resources than you ever need: Infinity Cells
quests.subtitle: The Sink but in cell form
quests.description:
ExtendedAE offers a new type of cell, the Infinity Cell.
These cells provide a limitless supply of a certain type of resource, such as Water, Cobblestone, Lava, etc.

quests.title: Fully Automated Crafting: The Quantum Crafter
quests.description:
The Quantum Crafter is a powerful and configurable auto-crafter. With an entire inventory of an ME network at its grasp, crafting non-stop becomes a trivial task. It is capable of running crafting jobs at a very fast pace. It is also capable of running fluid substitutions as well as recursive crafts (such as Smithing Template Duplication).
You can also regulate how much of each ingredient you want to keep, and up to how many of the product you want to keep in stock.
Won't accept crafting requests from Pattern Providers, though.

quests.title: Co-Processing Oblivion: Quantum Computer Accelerator
quests.description: Quantum Accelerators add 12 co-processing threads each to the Quantum Computer multiblock. It's important to note that all crafting jobs being run by the Quantum Computer are able to share all co-processors, so it's a good idea to invest in a great amount of these.

quests.title: Co-Processing To Infinity: Quantum Computer Multi-Threader
quests.description:
The Quantum Computer Multi-Threader multiplies co-processing threads in the Quantum Computer Multiblock by 6. For example: A Quantum Computer Accelerator will give 72 co-processing threads with this block in the multiblock.
You can only have one Quantum Computer Multi-Threader in a Quantum Computer Multiblock.
It is also an ingredient for the ATM Star.

quests.title: Advanced AE
quests.description:
Advanced AE is an addon for Applied Energistics 2, that focuses on improving user experience whenever you handle your ME System and expanding the possibilities of end game systems.
From a Pattern Provider that can push to specific sides of a machine, to a multiblock computer that is capable of running unlimited crafting jobs, sharing co-processors among said crafts, and anything in between.

quests.title: Reaction Efficency: The Reaction Chamber
quests.description:
The Reaction Chamber is capable of accelerating various In-World Reactions within itself, using a catalyst fluid and great amounts of power. Due to the controlled environment, this machine is capable of making said reactions more efficient, allowing you to gain more material out of them.
This machine is quite power hungry, though, good power generation and energy cells in your ME Network are highly recommended.
This machine is also required for Quantum related recipes in Advanced AE.

quests.title: Quantum Ingredients
quests.description:
Some ingredients you'll need to make the Quantum Computer, Crafter, and Armor.
Shattered Singularity is made with a Singularity, 2 Ender Dust, 2 Sky Stone Dust, and 100 mB of Lava in a Reaction Chamber.
1 bucket of Quantum Infusion is made with 4 buckets of Water and a Quantum Infused Dust, which is obtained by crushing the Shattered Singularity in an Inscriber or Mekanism Crusher.
Quantum Infused Alloy is made with 1 bucket of Quantum Infusion, 4 Copper Ingots, 4 Shattered and 4 regular Singularities.

quests.title: Infinite Crafting Jobs: The Quantum Computer
quests.description:
The Quantum Computer is a powerful Crafting CPU. It is capable of running unlimited crafting jobs, and sharing co-processing threads among them, so long as it has storage available for it to use.
It must be a cuboid of at least 3x3x3 size and up to 7x7x7. Alternatively: One Quantum Computer Core is capable of being a Quantum Computer by itself.
A Quantum Computer Multiblock requires the following:
- No empty spaces can be present in the multiblock. They can be filled with Quantum Crafting Unit for no additional benefits.
- Exactly one Quantum Computer Core
- At most one Quantum Data Entangler
- At most one Quantum Computer Multi-Threader
- All blocks on the outside layer must be Quantum Computer Structural Glass
- No blocks on the inside can be Quantum Computer Structural Glass.
Hope you're ready to make a lot of Singularities.

quests.title: Heart of the Crafts: Quantum Computer Core
quests.description: The Quantum Computer Core is the heart of the Quantum Computer. It has 256M crafting storage and 12 co-processing threads by itself. It is also the only block capable of forming a Quantum Computer by itself, when powered through the Up or Down sides, where the connectors are. However, if used to create a multiblock, a much more powerful computer can be created.

quests.title: The Ultimate Quantum Computer
quests.description:
Ever wanted the ultimate Quantum Computer setup? Well, here's a setup for you, focused on maximizing co-processing threads.

218 Quantum Computer Structural Glass, 123 Quantum Computer Accelerators, 1 Quantum Computer Core, and 1 Quantum Computer Multi-Threader are what we need. This gives us a total of 8928 co-processing threads. Note that I did not include any storage here besides the core, as the 256M crafting storage from the core is plenty enough already. The Data Entangler quest is optional for a reason.

Get 200 Q.C. Structural Glass and 100 Q.C. Accelerators, and I'll give you the rest, because I'm just as generous as the Apothic Enchanting chapter.

quests.title: Massive Crafting Storage: The Quantum Computer Storage
quests.description: These blocks expand the crafting storage of the Quantum Core. They effectively increase the amount of concurrent tasks the Quantum Computer is able to run. They are also required to make a Quantum Computer Core.

quests.title: Unnecessarily Large Storage: Quantum Data Entangler
quests.description:
The Quantum Data Entangler allows items to be stored in multiple dimensions, effectively multiplying crafting storage in a Quantum Computer Multiblock by 6. For example, a 256M quantum crafting storage will now give 1.5G Crafting Storage.
You can only have 1 of these in a Quantum Computer Multiblock.

quests.title: Specific Sided Patterns: The Advanced Pattern Provider
quests.subtitle: Looking at you, Mekanism
quests.description:
The ME Advanced Pattern Provider is a new type of ME Pattern Provider that upgrades a standard or Extended Pattern Provider with the ability to configure the face to which any individual item in a pattern is sent to. This allows for automation of machines that require specific sides for specific inputs to be done with a single block and no pipes or a subnet, such as with the Metallurgic Infuser from Mekanism.
To make use of this feature, you need an Advanced Pattern Encoder, to decide which side of the machine to send each ingredient.

quests.title: ME System As Armor: The Quantum Armor
quests.subtitle: Won't make you fully invincible
quests.description:
You think Mekanism and Modern Industrialization can have all the fun with their end game armor sets? 

This Quantum Armor has default stats similar to Netherite Armor but, like the MekaSuit it can use Energy as a shield. 
It also has upgrades which can be installed to make you even more powerful! Like Flight, Night Vision, and even the ability to recharge. 

But the best part is that it can Linked to your Storage System! Then, you can automatically take Energy out from it and take out any Item from it no matter where you are. 

Furthermore, wearing the full set can prevent Radiation from killing you.

quests.title: Upgrades for Quantum Armor
quests.description:
The Quantum Armor can be upgraded with a variety of different upgrades.
To upgrade your Quantum Armor, open the Quantum Armor Configuration Menu by pressing its respective keybind (N by default).

quests.title: 38D0BBD5F699EF41
quests.description: Allows the Quantum Armor piece to charge from your ME system's energy if linked to a Wireless Access Point. If placed into a Quantum Chestplate, it also recharges items in your inventory. This has a special interaction with AppliedFlux, where, if you have FE Cells in the network, it will extract energy from those.

quests.title: Universal Pipez
quests.description:
Why worry about what's being moved when you can just move everything! Universal Pipez are even less discriminatory than Energy Pipez. They can move Items, Fluids, or Energy.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/pipez_universal.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Pressurized Tubes
quests.subtitle: Gas+More
quests.description:
Because the normal Minecraft Items, Blocks, and Fluids wasn't enough. And the added Heat and Energy wasn't either. 

The rest of Mekanism is moved with Pressurized Tubes. Gases are the main ones as if you're using Mekanism you will be using Gases like Hydrogen and Oxygen. 
Infuse Types are similar like Coal Infuse and Redstone Infuse. Slurries are used with Ore Processing. 
And Dye Pigments are the essence of Color, any item that is Dyed can be changed with that part of Mekanism.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/meka_tube.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Thermodynamic Conductors
quests.subtitle: Heat
quests.description:
Heat is another factor in Mekanism and it Fuels a lot of Machines and Multiblocks. Thermal Evaporation Plants and Fusion Reactors both use Heat to work. And Conductors is how you will be moving Heat!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/meka_conductor.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Item Importing
quests.description:
To get this working put the Item Importer onto the Inventory you want Items pulled from. Next, put the Interface on the second Inventory and connect them with Logic Cables. Then, put in the Variable Card into the Importer and change it as you please. \n\nIt can be changed to Import Items at the Integer Limit (Over 2 Billion).
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/id_item.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Fluid Importing
quests.description:
Works just like the Item Importer, put the Fluid Importer onto a Tank with Liquid. Then the Fluid Interface on where you want it to go and connect with Logic Cables. Finally Variable Card just like before! 

Also can pull Liquids at the Integer Limit. 

Does not place or take Fluid Sources from in the world, it only moves Fluids from one Tank to another.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/id_fluid.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Energy Importing
quests.description:
Just smack an Energy Importer onto a Power Source and connect it to an Energy Interface with Logic Cables! Put and edit the Variable Cards and you'll be moving Power like a pro! \n\nI do have to say I found it having problems with Importing or Exporting to Flux Plugs and Points so be mindful of that.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/id_energy.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Item Pipez
quests.description:
The simplest of the simplest of Pipes, the Item Pipe. 

It will move Items from one Inventory to another. Could be from one Chest to another, could be a Farm to a System, or even a Quarry to a Smelter. 

Very simple just connect the Pipes to what you want moved, and use your Wrench to configure which side it Pulls from.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/pipez_item.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Fluid Pipez
quests.description:
Water=Blue Water=Fluid therefore Blue=Fluid

Lots of Mods have their own Fluids, with even Minecraft having their own, with Water and Lava. You'll most likely need to move those Fluids and a good way of doing so is with Fluid Pipes. 

This can be connected to Sinks to move Infinite Water!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/pipez_fluid.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Energy Pipez
quests.description:
Every Tech Mod needs Energy, whether it's FE, RF or something else! Energy Pipez don't discriminate, it just moves! \n\nSome Machines have strict IO ports for Energy so make sure to check for those!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/pipez_energy.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Logical Transporters
quests.subtitle: Blocks+Items
quests.description:
Logical Transporters are what Meka uses to move Items and Blocks across distance. \n\nThey will need to be Configured to Pull or Push to Inventories like Chests or Drawers.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/meka_transporter.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Mechanical Pipes
quests.subtitle: Fluids
quests.description:
Mechanical Pipes are how Meka lets the Fluids flow.\n\nSome Machines in Meka will need Fluids like Electrolytic Separator needing Water or Evaporation Plants to make Lithium.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/meka_pipe.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Universal Cables
quests.subtitle: Energy
quests.description:
Mekanism is Tech Mod... why are you surprised it needs Energy for its Machines?
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/meka_cable.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: 6112956E19017D2D
quests.description: Logic Cables are different from other Pipez or Meka pipes. The other Pipes act as hoppers, the items move from 1 Inventory, into the Pipe, then into the 2nd Inventory. Logic Cables just skip the middle man which also skips a lotta lag. \n\nThey are just for connecting Importers and Interfaces.

quests.title: 03C40D6A5D722543
quests.description:
Variable Cards are necessary for starting Interactions like Importing Items. You will put them in one of the slots of the Importer to add them. 

From there you can edit everything via the + Button. You can change how much is Importer, which Item Slot, which Channel, practically everything with just that Card. 

If you're like me just wanting to move items, nothing too fancy just put it in and maybe change the Limit for how much is moved.

quests.title: Pipe Upgrades
quests.description:
Pipez move more! 

All Upgrades increase the amount the Pipez move and also grant more options to use with the Pipe. 

Basic Upgrade allows Redstone Activation with Pipez, to change distribution either:Closest First, Farthest First, Round-Robin, or Random, and to add Filters.

Improved, Advanced, and Ultimate upgrades don't grant anything new they just move more!

quests.title: Gas Pipez
quests.description:
These Pipez are mostly due to Mekanism. Mekanism adds the last state of matter in the form of Gas. Gas can't be moved with any of the other Pipez so if you need to move Hydrogen or Lithium you'll need Gas Pipez. \n\n(I've always had problems telling whether the Mekanism item is Gas, Fluid, or even Infuse Type. When it's in a Machine it might tell Gas or Fluid, which can help teach you. If it doesn't you can check JEI for other recipes that might involve it!)
{image:atm:textures/questpics/logistics/pipez_gas.png width:200 height:50 align:center}

quests.title: Pipez
quests.description:
Pipez is the simplest Logistics Mod. It's so simple that the entire mod is fit in this Quest Page while having room for more Mods!
Attach the specific Pipe to where you want to move items and use the Pipe Wrench to configure what side Pulls, Pushes, or doesn't connect.
Other Wrenches do work with Pipez as well!
(Can be laggy when used in mass, still not as laggy as Mekanism pipes though).

quests.title: Integrated Dynamics
quests.description:
Integrated Dynamics is all about Logistics! It's practically the definition of Logistic.
It's all about moving, managing, and storing items. Heck you might not even need the Wrench for it, it's so well designed! Get one just incase though.
(Least laggy pipe solution, these are recommended).

quests.title: Mekanism
quests.description:
Mekanism is a huge and popular Tech Mod, so of course it has Logistics with it.
The different Machines are picky with Configurations and will need to be changed in their GUI to properly move items. Then you can use the Meka Pipes to move whatever you need to move!
But wait it's not just Mekanism these work for! They work for plenty of other machines as well! Just need to be Configured with a Wrench to Push and Pull.
(These can cause a bit of lag when used in mass so be careful with them).

quests.title: 2A976D41F79C34B1
quests.description:
Pipez do have their own way of Filtering Items, you need atleast an Advanced Upgrade to get it though. When an Advanced Upgrade is in you can click the Add button to add Filters. 
Then you can add: Item, Tag, or NBT in the Filter. 

There you can also add the set Destination Filter. To set it, Shift Right Click an Inventory with it. 

You'll also have to set it to either Whitelist the Filter or Blacklist, so only the Filter or everything but the Filter.

quests.title: Logistics
quests.description:
Logistics: 
A system of moving, managing, and storing items or resources. 

In Modded Minecraft it's quite the same, moving items! With Modded you will need items and by the thousands, heck if you want the Star it gets in the millions! So you'll need to move items from factories, machines, farms, and especially chests. That's what Logistics is for.

quests.title: 230582AAFC0A1632
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks.

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission.

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: 7BC8F50A89A3BE1A
quests.description: These are just used to Connect Laser Nodes to each other and to Connectors. Not too important I just wanted to keep with the theme of Wrenches. \n\nIt does work as a Wrench for other Configs!

quests.title: 2A6900E87DE8BAE0
quests.description: Mod Filter is another pretty basic Filter. This one you put Items in and it will do the same with either Whitelisting or Blacklisting. But instead of only being that Item it will be any Item from that Mod. \n\nApotheosis Gem will only allow Apotheosis Items. Mekanism Alloy will only allow Mekanism Items. And so on.

quests.title: 7EE27C3908008E20
quests.description: If you need to string your Laser Nodes a far distance try using Connectors! Just use the Wrench like normal.

quests.title: 5C0F6B1C93A52113
quests.description:
Now this is the true Heart of LaserIO! The Laser Nodes are where the actual Cards will go into in order to work. 

They will move Items from any adjacent Inventory in the 4 Cardinal Directions and Up and Down. In order to move to Farther Inventories you'll need a second Node and Connect them with the Wrench by Shift Right Clicking 1 and Right Clicking the 2nd. 

You'll put the Cards into the Slots of the correct Direction and you can put Node Overclockers there as well to make it work faster.

quests.title: Laser IO
quests.description:
LaserIO is DireWolf's continuation of EnderIO's Logistics.
It's all about moving items via Lasers! Who doesn't love Lasers?!
And it all starts with the Logic Chip.

quests.title: 47A2BEFB11F4D581
quests.description:
The Basic Filter is pretty... easy to use! Simply put Items into it and they are now filtered. 

You can change it so it either Whitelists/allows only those Items or that is Blacklists/denies only those Items. 

You can also have it so it either matches NBT data or not. Matching NBT Data would mean having same Enchantments, Durabilitiy, or even Mobs inside of whatever Item. If selected to not match it will do any of that Item regardless of NBT.

quests.title: 06767BA0AFE8C1EE
quests.description:
1... 2... there's a 4 somewhere as well. 

To set a Number put the Item in then you can Left or Right Click to change the amount. Shift and do the same to go by 10s. Once you have a set Number through it into a Card! 

It will then wait until that set Number of Items is there to start taking Items. It will also leave that amount in the first Inventory.

quests.title: 3065EA195D0A36BA
quests.description:
Tags are very important part of grouping Items in Minecraft. So of course we can take advantage of that for Filters! 

You can put an Item in and select a Tag or if you know it, type it in yourself. 

Really helpful for ones like taking Gear out of a system by using Tag for Tools. 

(You can also find Tags by doing /kubejs hand to find what's the Tags of the Item in your hand.)

quests.title: Chemical Card
quests.description: DireWolf was asked to make an addition of his Cards to work with Mekanism and its... other states of matter. Everything Pressurized Tubes can move, these cards can. Gas, Infuse Types, and Pigments.

quests.title: Fluid Card
quests.description: Works exactly like the Item Cards, you need Extract and Insert Cards. Just this time you take from Tanks holding Fluids to another Tank. No, it doesn't move Sources of Fluid in or out of the World.

quests.title: Item Card
quests.description:
In order to move Items with LaserIO you'll need some Item Cards. 

Set one to Extract and put it on the side of the Laser Node you want to Import from. Then set the other to Insert and put it to the side you want the Items to Export to. 

There are mutliple settings you can change with the Extract in order of where you want the Items to go if there's multiple places to Extract from. Round Robin will make it Extract items in an order instead of closest Inventory first.

quests.title: Energy Card
quests.description: Energy has to get around somehow, preferably where we want it to go. Move it around just the same as with Items, Fluids, and Chemicals!

quests.title: Redstone Card
quests.description: Don't you just hate Redstone having to be wired to everywhere? If we can have Wireless FE why not Wireless Redstone? Finally we can thanks to LaserIO. You can Input a Redstone Signal with the Card then use an Output Card to Output the Signal somewhere else!

quests.title: 0BB562FB44B0AAA7
quests.subtitle: Max: 8
quests.description: Cards aren't the only ones with limits, so they also aren't the only ones with Overclockers! \n\nThese go into the Node itself on bottom right and boost how fast it does Operations.

quests.title: 046C417B2ADF3AA7
quests.subtitle: Max: 4
quests.description:
Cards have their limits. Item Extration can only extract 8 items per Operation. Fluid Extract at only 5 Buckets. God knows with Chemical and Energy. 

This is Modded Minecraft these limits won't suffice we need to Overclock them. 

Throw some Overclockers in the top right of the Card and it'll upgrade the cap they can transfer!

quests.title: 617695A9CA45D88F
quests.description: When using LaserIO for Logistics you might end up with MANY Cards. With each taking a slot in your Inventory it can get pretty crampt. I wish they had a storage for Cards... oh wait they do, it's the Card Holder! \n\nYou can store multiple Cards in it and when you open a Laser Node the Card Holder will open up as well like a second Inventory. Very helpful!

quests.title: 308935C85364B04D
quests.description: With each Card holding their own data it can be pretty annoying constantly changing each Cards settings. So lets just clone them instead! \n\nLeft Click a Card with the Cloner to copy its Data, then Right Click a Card to give it that Data!

quests.title: Variable Cards
quests.description:
Variable Cards are necessary for starting Interactions like Importing Items. You will put them in one of the slots of the Importer to add them.

From there you can edit everything via the + Button. You can change how much is Importer, which Item Slot, which Channel, practically everything with just that Card.

If you're just wanting to move items, nothing too fancy just put it in and maybe change the Limit for how much is moved.

quests.title: 3BC94B0B922C0708
quests.description: These are crafting ingredients for stuff that does importing, whether it be items, fluids, or energy.

quests.title: 60D9F04E91171D16
quests.description: This can act as a Chest for your Variables, or can actually be used in an advanced network.\n\nIf you want advanced networks, make sure to read about them in the Dynamics of Integration.

quests.title: Logic Cables
quests.subtitle: Making Networks
quests.description: Logic Cables are different from other cables. Other Cables act as Hoppers, the items move from 1 Inventory, into the cable, then into the 2nd inventory. Logic Cables just skip the middle man which also skips a lotta lag.\n\nThey are just for connecting Importers and Interfaces.

quests.title: Exporters
quests.subtitle: Exporting
quests.description: Works like Importers do, only they export instead.

quests.title: Importers
quests.subtitle: Importing

quests.title: 2F37E284BB83BFF6
quests.description: The Wrench is used to rotate or destroy certain blocks, shift right-click in the air to change modes.

quests.title: 6ABDBE41880CFDA9
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks.

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission.

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Integrated Dynamics
quests.subtitle: Growing Menril
quests.description:
Integrated Dynamics (ID) is a logistics mod that can be used for storage, item/power/fluid transfer and more!

Menril trees can be found in Meneglin biomes.

These quests will cover some of the basic concepts of the mod, read the guidebook given as a reward for this quest if you want to go further in depth.

quests.title: 68498ADEF9765F81
quests.description: To make Crystallized Menril Chunks you first need to place some Menril Logs in a Squeezer. Jump on the Squeezer to turn them into Menril Resin.\n\nYou can empty the Squeezer by giving it a Redstone signal.

quests.title: 62B4A37CFDECA679
quests.description: The Menril Resin will go to 2 sides of the Squeezer. Placing a Drying Basin next to the Squeezer will make the Drying Basin pick up the Menril Resin.\n\nAfter 7.5 seconds the Menril Resin will turn into a Block of Crystallized Menril.

quests.title: Crystallized Menril Chunks
quests.subtitle: The Main Crafting Ingredient
quests.description: Blocks of Crystallized Menril can be crafted into Crystallized Menril Chunks. These chunks are the main crafting ingredient of ID.

quests.title: Interfaces
quests.subtitle: Interfaces Have GUIs!
quests.description: Interfaces read whatever they're looking at. You can think of this like an AE2 Storage Bus.\n\nYou don't know what that is? Well here's an example: A chest with 100 Cobblestone in it has an interface on it, this means your ID network has 100 Cobblestone in it's system, pretty simple, right?

quests.title: Networks!
quests.subtitle: Moving Stuff!
quests.description:
It's time to move stuff from one place to another. Here are the steps:

1. Place an interface on an inventory (like a Chest or a Tank)

2. Place an Importer or an Exporter on another inventory, depending on whether you want to pull or send stuff to it.

3. Hook the both up with Cables, place a Variable Card into the Importer or Exporter, and there you go!

quests.title: 4D4152032F0410D2
quests.subtitle: Getting Advanced
quests.description: The Logic Programmer lets you set the value of variables. This can be set to to items and fluids for filtering, or even values. \n\nLet me give you a simple example: Select Item from the left side, place an item of choice into the center slot of the GUI that pops up, and place a Variable Card in the bottom right slot. If you then put that variable card in an importer/exporter, it will only import/export that block!

quests.title: 1568CBFA09827137
quests.description: Same thing as Logic Programmer, only this one can be used anywhere.

quests.title: 3C9539083BCC145C
quests.subtitle: Automating Menril
quests.description: Menril Bees can be used to automate Crystallized Menril Chunks.

quests.title: 6C9191DA4B1039D6
quests.description: Menril Berries give you Night Vision for a short amount of time when eaten.

quests.title: 44DA091B53473723
quests.description: The Mechanical Squeezer uses energy to squeeze.

quests.title: 7413BB136EF9D6C5
quests.description: The Mechanical Drying Basin uses energy to dry

quests.title: 6D75CF34957ECCD9
quests.subtitle: Storing Energy
quests.description: The Energy Battery lets you store FE. To transfer it, you will need Energy Interfaces.

quests.title: Interface GUI
quests.description:
When you right-click on an interface, it brings up several options, here's what they all do:

Set Side: At the top of the screen, you can set the side that the interface "acts" like it's on. It can be useful for machines with specific input/output sides.

Ticks/Operation: If an interface is set to 10 ticks/operation, it will import/export once every 10 ticks (0.5 seconds).

Priority: Sends items to the inventory with the higher priority interface on it.

Item/Energy Channels: This will split your system into multiple channels. You can push and pull from different places in your network.

quests.title: Importer & Exporter GUI
quests.description:
When you right-click on an Importer or an Exporter, it brings up a menu. The menu is mainly for filtering, say you have a Variable Card set to Cobblestone, your Exporter will only send Cobblestone.

There is a little "+" to the left of variables when you insert them, clicking on it opens another GUI. In here you can change transfer rates to be able to send INFINITE items/fluids/energy, as well as being able to do some other stuff.

On the top left we have settings, these are for the most part the same thing as the interface settings.

quests.title: 65D89991A45BC042
quests.subtitle: AUTO CRAFT
quests.description: Place a Crafting Interfaces on a crafting table and right-click on it, this will give you some slots for Variable Cards. \n\nUsing the Logic Programmer, search for Recipe in the top left, and create one for autocrafting, then save it to a Variable Card. If a recipe requires items that need to be crafted, create a recipe for each of those, then put everything in the Crafting Interface.

quests.title: 56BF647EA84FFF7E
quests.subtitle: Shows Recipes
quests.description: Shows which crafting recipes are happening at any time.

quests.title: 232A06C9FF0EE7B2
quests.subtitle: Automating Menril
quests.description: Menril Seeds can be used to automate Menril Berries, Menril Logs and Menril Saplings.

quests.title: 4D62C62B523C69EC
quests.subtitle: Providing Energy!
quests.description: The Generator generates FE using burnable fuels like Coal.

quests.title: 5FB29F3F4DF17765
quests.description: Sometimes you don't want every Module to move multiple stacks at a time, so when you just want 1 Modules to do so use an Augment! This does not stack with Upgrades though... infact it overrides them.

quests.title: Augments
quests.description: Augments are similar to Upgrades but for the individual Modules!

quests.title: 2DD5F0693780B10A
quests.description: Used with the Extruder MK2, blocks extruded will mimic the actual blocks. Redstone Blocks will emit Redstone, Glowstone will emit light, Grass will act transparent. But only with this Augment! \nDoesn't work with Block Entities like Furnaces or Enrichment Chambers.

quests.title: 20D4568857887D38
quests.description:
Sometimes a Router might be in a dangerous situation, like spawning a Wither. 

In order to protect it you'll need a Blast Upgrade. 

TNT won't break it, Wither won't break it, only you.

quests.title: 309B6B8368E535A0
quests.description:
A Router does it's action every time it has one of it's ticks. 

Default is 20 Ticks or 1 Second. 

This can be made to less Ticks with the Speed Upgrade!

quests.title: 4CC963F5AECF285A
quests.description: Normally the Router moves 1 item each of it's Ticks. This can be doubled and stacked! with the Stack Upgrade. \n\n1 Stack Upgrade is 2 Items, 2 Stacks 4 Items, and 6 Stacks is 64 Items a second.

quests.title: Upgrades
quests.description: Upgrades go directly into the Router and the Router can hold 5 of them. Upgrades directly affect all Modules that they can and usually can stack!

quests.title: Routers for Farming
quests.description:
Routers can also be used for Farming!\n\nFirst start off with a simple Farm. Then you'll need an Activator Module and direct it toward the Crops. After that, put a Vacuum Module in your Router to collect the Crops. Finally put it all in the Router, Power it with Redstone, and let it farm!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/router/router_farm.png width:60 height:150 align:center}

quests.title: 6B747129A85AA768
quests.description: Now even more like the Absorption Hopper! \n\nVacuum Module will now pickup XP Orbs as well as Items. Whatever you do with the XP is up to you!

quests.title: 1A806C1A54B26EB5
quests.description: You don't want everything to do their actions at a larger range? You want your Vacuum to leave some room for dropping items in your World? Then I guess you can range down.

quests.title: 4EAFE7B240AF0A4D
quests.description: Just can't reach what you need to? Try Ranging Up! \n\nWith this everything will do their actions but farther. Vacuum has higher range for picking up items. Energy goes farther. Flinger flings with more strength!

quests.title: 10672B5991E5FC34
quests.description: It's my stuff, no touchy. \n\nOnly you can use and mess with the Router after putting in the Upgrade.

quests.title: 09E25B1CD6CABD5A
quests.description:
This upgrade makes the Router similar to a Framed Block. 

Sneak Right Click a Block to change the Routers appearance to it. 

Just don't lose it!

quests.title: 2447208F1DC74FFE
quests.description: Routers can be noisy, and noise definitely stacks when you have hundreds of them.\n\nMight be nice to invest in Muffer Upgrades then!

quests.title: 5560F303C452E110
quests.description: The Extruder pushes blocks and entities by why not push it some more! \n\nThe entities not the blocks.

quests.title: 177396B9C4F9B3E2
quests.description: Why wait? Oh you have valid reasons for waiting? Like items that might despawn. Huh wasn't thinking about those. \n\nWith Pickup Delay Augment the Vacuum Module will wait 10 ticks with every Augment in it to pick up dropped items!

quests.title: 3025081DA6D2B398
quests.description: Usually the Router commands the Modules but with this Augment the Module goes rouge! AWOl! Pure anarchy! \n\nIt will listen to it's own Redstone activation rather than the Routers.

quests.title: 1069244EB72F64CA
quests.description: Takes more Energy with the Energy Modules!

quests.title: 4FA5192164E4A427
quests.description: Fluid doesn't stack like Items do, so its upgrade is a little different. Still moves more just at a different rate.

quests.title: 76062D375E4CC8DD
quests.description: We've seen Filters and we've seen Round Robins, now we're seeing both! This is useful for keeping the Items in a select order like for when making Mystical Agriculture Seeds!

quests.title: 674F28BCA2E4A3C8
quests.description: When moving items Routers can get pretty greedy, taking every single item they can get their grubby antennas on! \n\nWith Regulator Augment you can limit how much is moved.

quests.title: 0CE236731DF15DFF
quests.description:
Why wait? Usually items dropped in Minecraft have a second they need to hit the ground to be picked up again. 

But why wait?

This upgrade lets the Vacuum Module not wait and immediately pick up the items. 

Very good for less lag!

quests.title: 553C44F85E508DE3
quests.description:
This one is unique as it's not used for just 1 Router but for multiple. 

If you want mutliple Routers working at the same time then each needs a Sync Upgrade. 

Will need to be tuned in its own GUI.

quests.title: Modular Routers
quests.description:
Modular Routers is a logistics mod. 

It all starts with the Router! So make one! 

Also the Buffer is the single item slot in the Router where items will come and go through. And it will need Redstone signal for most modules to work.

quests.title: 2BB5769119BA2472
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks. 

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission. 

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: 40788326E791845D
quests.description:
Extrude is such a prude word. 

The Extruder will place the blocks in the Router's Buffer in a line in front of the Router when given a Redstone Signal. When the Signal is disabled it will break all those blocks. 

Useful for Doors!

quests.title: Modules
quests.description:
Modules determine the action the Router preforms.

They can make it so your Router pulls items from Chests, or put items into chests, or even both! And much more!

Modules go into the Router themselves and multiple can be installed.

Filtering and Upgrades go into the Modules themselves.

quests.title: 01C5D8357D8B0D62
quests.description:
If you know how a Detector Rail works then this Module will be explanatory for you. 

Basically if a certain Item is in the Router, it will emit a Redstone Signal out of the Router. 

In the Module you can set the Item, where the Signal comes from, and how strong a Signal.

quests.title: Routers for Mining
quests.description:
Don't feel like Mining a bunch of Ores you got? Why not let Routers do it for you? 

You can use a Placer to place down the Ores, then let an Enchanted Breaker Mine the Ores. Breaker needs the Pickaxe used to craft it to be Enchanted first, the Module itself can't be Enchanted. 

You might need another Router to pick up the dropped Ores.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/router/router_break.png width:150 height:80 align:center}

quests.title: Routers for Mob Farms
quests.description:
Here's a good example of using Modular Routers to make a super easy organized Mob Farm. (Does not include way of killing mobs). 

For it I'll use a Wither Skeleton Farm as example. 

First, you want to get Items into the Buffer with a Vacuum Module. Next, get rid of the Stone Swords with a Void Module. To make sure it doesn't delete everything use a Whitelist Filter with the Stone Sword in it and not matching Damage. After, that you'll need a place to put the Loot, I recommend a Drawer System. Then, use a Sender Module to send the Loot to the Storage System. 

That's all you need!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/router/router_mob.png width:200 height:65 align:center}

quests.title: 36DED7099E80ED51
quests.description: This one does as the name suggests, it places Blocks. \n\nSet the Direction you want the Block placed, preferably set the Filter, then throw the Module and Blocks into the Router! Once the Redstone is set the Blocks will be placed!

quests.title: 00E1F1279F97557B
quests.description: Similar to the Extruder MK1 but this one is more evolved! Can be used with Patterns so when Blocks are placed they will go in that pattern!

quests.title: 6063F4B7BE4D394C
quests.description: The Sender Modules will move Items in the Router's Buffer Slot into another Inventory. \n\nMK1 will only move items into Inventories on the same XYZ axis as the Router and with direct line of sight. If there is a block in the way, the MK1 Sender will not send.

quests.title: 38954551309F42A7
quests.description:
Sender Module MK2 works similar to MK1 but with less restrictions. 

MK2 doesn't need direct line of sight or to be on same XYZ axis. 

Will have to be in the same Dimension though, unless you have...

quests.title: 2405663C033CBDF1
quests.description:
MK3 doesn't worry about XYZ axis, line of sight, or Dimension. 

As long as the Inventory is in the same Minecraft World it can move items into it. 

Heck I'm not even sure if the Inventory has to be in the game of Minecraft to send to!

quests.title: 53B58FC3958750E7
quests.description:
Did you play around with the Placer too much and need to Break those Blocks? 

Its Tier and Enchants are determined by the Pickaxe its Crafted with. 

Now set the area and hopefully put a Filter and let it run! 

Can be used with a Placer to do stuff like turning Ores into Items.

quests.title: 247DAE5B4E1AC7F1
quests.description:
Water in. 
Water out. 

The Fluid Module will either take Liquid Sources from near the Router and put it into a Tank in the Buffer or take Liquid from a Tank in it's Buffer and place it in front of it. 

Only works for adjacent blocks to the Router, if you want bigger range you'll need...

quests.title: Creative Module
quests.description:
HAHAHA did I scare you with the Creative item in the quests?

Don't worry you won't need the item to finish this chapter, I just wanted to scare you

I can have fun sometimes...

quests.title: 326C63F7DC713E71
quests.description:
The Distributer is the half siblings of the Sender Modules. (The MK3 to be exact, on the MK2 side). 

Instead of sending to 1 Inventory it will send to multiple that are selected. 

It can send in multiple modes: Round Robin, Random, Nearest First, or Farthest First. Round Robin does an even amount to each in a row, like a dealer in Poker. Random will randomly choose an inventory to feed. The others are determined by the distance from the Router.

quests.title: 185074907753AE77
quests.description:
If you are using Routers I hope you have some game knowledge. 

Just incase, to void an Item means to delete it. 

Any items that come into the Router, will be deleted forever! 

Recommend using Filters with this one...

quests.title: 0DC8B68CDF945348
quests.description:
The Router giveth and the Router taketh. 

This Module is helpful for Builders or even Miners! It can be set to send items from its Buffer to your Inventory or take items from your Inventory into its Buffer. 

Perfect for Strip-Mining, have it take all the Cobble and Deepslate from your Inventory and put it in a Trash Can.

quests.title: 73D60868024FF907
quests.description: The Fluid MK2! \n\nAny Liquid Source nearby can be used with this one, not just adjacent.

quests.title: 346B9339E3D66478
quests.description: Energy is something used by practically everything so you need to send it almost everywhere. Thankfully the Energy Module will help with that! \n\nThe Energy Module will move any energy pushed into it, somewhere else! To wherever you set it to!

quests.title: 71A1FD0772453B51
quests.description:
Don't you hate Right Clicking everything? From Sheeps with Shears to Cows with Buckets? It's the 21st Century we should have Robots to everything! Or atleast Routers do everything. 

With Activator Module it will act as if it were you Right Clicking things. 

You can set what it will Right Click, if it will Attack or Use the Mob or Block, if you Shift Right Click, and how close they need to be in the Module.

quests.title: 417B88FEB1B8F44E
quests.description:
Mean these Suck! Literally! 

Vacuum Module will suck up any items in the set area and move them to the Routers Buffer. Similar to the Absorption Hopper. 

Also can be used with Experience Augment!

quests.title: 1AA81C41431FD145
quests.description:
Pull..! Pull..! Pull..! 

The Puller is the opposite of the Sender, it pulls items from Inventories into the Router's Buffer. 

The Inventory has to be adjacent to the Router.

quests.title: 475E1B94A61B9EB0
quests.description: Like the MK1 this pulls! Just not only from adjacent Inventories, but any Inventory nearby!

quests.title: 2B60D123123A5E8E
quests.description: Why set a location to where the Energy can go? Why not let it go free! \n\nLike freeing a bunch of Bees, the Energy will go everywhere almost instantly (with less buzzing). Any blocks needing Energy nearby will be charged wirelessly.

quests.title: 7F8DEDD0A54D1E11
quests.description:
I wonder what Droppers do? 
I think they drop things... 

Any item in the Buffer will be dropped on the ground. 

Could be helpful with something like Botania!

quests.title: 3C54C36CE97A48DC
quests.description:
Droppers drop,
Dispensers dispense, 
And Flingers fling! 

Instead of nicely setting down items from the Buffer, the Flinger Module will throw them? How far? You determine that!

quests.title: 143AE6889BDA9EF5
quests.description:
Modules only have so many slots for Filtered Items, if you need more than use this! Bulk Item Filter. 

You can put many more Items in to Whitelist or Blacklist in it. Then throw it in where normal Filters go! 

Will be needed to craft more unique Filters!

quests.title: 4A03A671757B2EBF
quests.description:
Durability, Fluid Level, Energy Level, Enchantment Level, and Food Value are all categories we can use with Inspection Filter.

Then we select if we want it Greater than, Lesser than, Equal to, or a mix of those with the Numbered Amount.

Next we give it a Numbered Amount and hit the Plus Button to add it to the Filter.

This can be used to only keep Tools with high Durability or Food with high Food Value.

quests.title: 6E5954C257726F86
quests.description: Filtering per mod can be very helpful.\n\nTo use it, put an item in from a certain mod, then it will show the mod name, and hit the Plus button to add it!

quests.title: 72A71E1D6D8996FD
quests.description: Is this code? I'm not a coder!? I just wanted to make these quests! \n\nHere you can type in a Regex into the Search Bar and click the Plus Button to add it to the Filter. Whenever that Regex comes up it will be filtered out.

quests.title: 37F2BE3C2BAF7C2D
quests.description:
Tags are an essential part of Minecraft. 

For all who don't know they work as an organization tool to help choose similar items for the same task. Like Crafting Table being made with any Planks or Trees being Chopped down fastest with any Axe. 

To filter by Tag put an item in, then select the tag from the groups. Like Iron Ore for Ores.

quests.title: 09D18512037386C1
quests.description:
In order to put Potion Effects into you'll need to fill a Potion Filter. 

To do so: have a Potion Effect on you, then right click with the Potion Filter to remove it from you and add it to the Filter, and repeat until it's filled and active. 

This also works with modded Potion Effects or ones you can't usually get through Potions like Haste or Resistance.

quests.title: 403F76908A8A5661
quests.description:
The Explusion Pylon pushes players out of the area, but what if you want some players nearby! Then you'll need a Player Filter. 

Right Click a Player with it to set them in it, and then put it into the Pylon to Whitelist them! 

So when everyone else is pushed out, your friend won't be! 

Also by default the Owner of the Pylon won't get expuled.

quests.title: 5E02AE661945306C
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks. 

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission. 

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: 18246A48C20B29D8
quests.description: The Infusion Pylon works similar as a Beacon just much better and cheaper! \nWhen a Potion Effect is put in by a Potion Filter, it will continuously give you the Potion Effect while you're in the set Chunk area.

quests.title: 32E52AD6EF194A60
quests.subtitle: Get off my lawn!
quests.description:
The Expulsion Pylon works as a way of keeping people off your lawn. 

When placed down it will keep any Players who aren't whitelisted from a set amount of Chunks around it. 

The Chunks are set in it's GUI in the top left from 1x1, 3x3, or 5x5 Chunks. 

Also no it can't be set too close to Spawn. We know what you trolls want and we ain't giving it! 

To Whitelist players check the Player Filter Quest!

quests.title: Pylons
quests.description:
Pylons is a wonderful mod made by our very own Mutant Gumdrop!

Don't let the size of the mod make you underestimate it! It provides many Pylons which can be used for many things to help make playing Minecraft easier.

To get started you'll need some Polished Blackstone to make them.

quests.title: 12ED1EE85E146A4B
quests.description:
Harvester Pylons work as a very simple Auto-Farm. Put the Pylon on or in the Water Source and it will automatically harvest and replant Crops that are fully grown in the set area around it. 

The area can be set to 3x3, 5x5, 7x7, or 9x9 Blocks around the Pylon. 

It will need a Hoe to use on the Plants and will need an Inventory like a chest above it to put the Crops. Do all that and if it's turned On it will start farming!

(Careful when using a lot of modifiers with it like Lilypads or fertilizer as when it goes very fast farming it can be a TPS eater).

quests.title: 5B5FC539BD1F4A73
quests.description:
This Pylon is all about blocking Mob Spawns. 

You can use Mob Filters to block spawns of only certain Mobs or use the Lifeless Filter to block all Mob spawns! 

You can stack multiple Mob Filters to block off more spawns. Plus you can change the Working Area for how far it blocks those Mob Spawns. 

If you use the Lifeless Filter it will ignore all those settings.

quests.title: 2F5263A4166BFCD6
quests.subtitle: Accidental Destruction no more!
quests.description:
This Pylon prevents you from accidentally destroying certain Blocks/Mobs in the selected Chunk radius.

You can use a Mob Filter to prevent killing a certain Mob with the Pylon, or a Block Filter to prevent destroying a certain block.

You can stack multiple Mob and Block Filters to prevent multiple different Mobs/Blocks from being destroyed.

quests.title: 5C2C29ECA67F9B49
quests.subtitle: Finally peace and quiet.
quests.description:
With the Lifeless Filter you will never have to worry about any Mob spawns within a 25x25 Block area. 

That's enough to cover every distance Mobs spawn near the player. Hostile or Passive. 

This includes every Y Level as well, above or below the Pylon, so no more worrying about lighting up caves! 

There's no Whitelisting with this Filter, it will prevent every Mob Spawn.

quests.title: Hoes
quests.description: The Harvester Pylon needs a Hoe to work. \n\n(Hoes that can't break will work forever, Hoes that can will need to be replaced).

quests.title: 77B185799366ACD2
quests.description:
To set the Block Filter you just have to click the Block you want to prevent accidentally breaking, with the Block Filter. 

Each Filter can only hold 1 Block so if you want Beehives, Cables, Chests, Furnaces, and Brewing Stands to no longer be accidentally destroyed you'll need 5 Block Filters. 

You can exchange the Block in it by simply clicking a different Block with it.

quests.title: 011F787E620DE9E8
quests.subtitle: He's uninvited!
quests.description:
