To set the Mob Filter you just have to click the Mob you never want to see again, or prevent accidentally killing, with the Mob Filter. 

Each Filter can only hold 1 Mob so if you want Zombies, Skeletons, Spiders, Creepers, and Endermen to no longer spawn you'll need 5 Mob Filters. 

You can exchange the Mob in it by simplying clicking a different Mob with it.

quests.title: Minimum Spawn Delay
quests.description: To determine when the Spawner will spawn it picks a random number between maximum and minimum spawn delay. The Minimum can be as low as 20 to as high as 32,767. Each piece of sugar modifies the min delay up or down by 10.

quests.title: Maximum Spawn Delay
quests.description: The Maximum Spawn Delay is how long it could take to spawn mobs. Just like the Minimum it can be as low as 20 to as high as 32,767. Each Clock modifies the speed of the spawner by 10. The speed is expressed in ticks where 20 ticks equals 1 second. So quickest spawn delay would be 1 second between each.

quests.title: Max Entities
quests.description: Max entities is the amount of mobs that can be spawned by a spawner and kept. If it's only 6 max entities when 6 mobs are already spawned no more will spawned until they're dead or moved. Each Ghast Tear brings it up or down 2 Entities. Max of 16 Entities and Minimum of 1.

quests.title: Activation Range
quests.description: Activation Range is how close the Player (You) must be to the Spawner for it to work. The lowest it can be is 1 block away and the highest is a 48 block radius.

quests.title: Echoing
quests.description: Echo shards give a special effect to the spawner. Any mobs spawned will have the loot that they drop multiplied.

quests.title: Opposite Day
quests.description: The Quartz makes whatever the other item does, it does the opposite for the Spawner. With Quartz in your offhand and the other Spawner Modification item in your main it will do the opposite of its role. With Quartz and Blaze Rods instead of increasing Spawn Range it will decrease it. With Quartz and Ghast Tears it'll decrease Max Entities.

quests.title: 2FE4B7B70D90A455
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks.

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission.

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Apothic Spawners
quests.description: Another game change Apotheosis brings is to Spawners. Remember being able to mine Spawners with Silk Touch? Well it's back thanks to Apotheosis! There's also many new Modifications you can add to Spawners by right clicking any of these items.

quests.title: Ignore Light
quests.description: Some mobs (mostly monsters) need certain Light Levels to spawn. Hostile ones needing lower levels and passive needing higher ones. Using a Soul Lantern makes it so you never have to worry about Light Levels as it ignores them! This does not ignore other requirements for spawning like livestock animals needing Grass.

quests.title: Redstone Active
quests.description: Redstone Activation gives your spawner an on/off switch. Without Redstone Power it will not spawn.

quests.title: Ignore Players
quests.description: A Nether Star will do what the Prismarine Shards do but much better. Players no longer need to be near the spawner. As long as its chunk-loaded it will spawn.

quests.title: Ignore All Conditions
quests.description: The must-need for all Spawners. When it says ignores all conditions, it means most. Ignores light levels, blocks needing for spawning, and biomes. Space conditions are still needed though, like slimes needing 3x3 area to spawn, and same goes with players needing to be nearby.

quests.title: 1102B27CBF564127
quests.subtitle: Don't you despawn on me, Mobs
quests.description: Spawner Agitators are different from the other listed Modification items, this one is provided by PneumaticCraft instead of Apothic Spawners. Without the Apothic Spawners mod being in the Modpack, having an Agitator on a Spawner will make it spawn mobs no matter where the Player is. With Apothic Spawners, which yes we do have, it won't change that but rather will keep spawned mobs from despawning incase you leave the chunks.

quests.title: Burning
quests.description: A Campfire used on the spawner will have the mobs spawn on fire. Perfect for a nice Steak.

quests.title: Health
quests.description: Dripstone used on the spawner will reduce the max health of the mob spawned. This can decrease their health to as low as 20%

quests.title: Quiet down you'll wake up the mobs!
quests.description: Wool only does one thing to the spawner and that's to shut it up. Don't like hearing the stupid Spawner noises? Then use Wool! Any color, thread count, or design!

quests.title: Spawn Count
quests.description: A Fermented Spider's Eye can be used to increase the amount of mobs that CAN spawn from a spawner. The Mobs spawned is random with a Maximum amount determined by the number. It goes up or down by 1 for each eye to a maximum of 16.

quests.title: No AI
quests.description: By using a Chorus Fruit on a Spawner you suck the souls out the mobs that will be spawned, only leaving a hollow husk of what they used to be. The mobs will lose all AI so they will do basically what an armor stand does. They can't hit you, can't teleport, can't move on their own. They sit there ready to be killed, how exciting!

quests.title: Spawn Eggs
quests.description: Usually you can't get Spawn Eggs, but that's the same with Spawners and here we are! There's a few ways of obtaining Spawn Eggs but once you do, right click it on a Spawner to change the mobs it spawns.

quests.title: Youthful
quests.description: This one might be new to ones returning from earlier versions. By using a turtle egg on a spawner, it will only spawn in baby versions of the mobs in it. This only works with Vanilla baby versions of mobs, not modded.

quests.title: Spawn Range
quests.description: The Spawn Range is the area of where mobs can spawn. The bigger the area, the more room for them to spawn in. The smaller the area the cheaper the factory.

quests.title: Capturing Books
quests.description: Capturing is an Enchantment for Swords to make Mobs rarely drop their Eggs. It's a rare one so keep looking for one and check out Apothic Enchanting to help. Every level gives you a 0.5% chance at getting an Egg each kill and the highest level you can normally get is VII (7).

quests.title: 77A8E8122870BBCE
quests.subtitle: That's no Spawn Egg!
quests.description: This is technically not a Spawn Egg, but I'm including it here anyway, due to its ability to bind mobs to Spawners. Check out the Apothic Enchanting chapter to learn more about how to get this Lead.

quests.title: 2D8A7065F8CDDDDD
quests.description: Swabs are my favorite way of getting Spawn Eggs, you'll need to use Mob Grinding Utils for it. Simply right click a mob with the Swab then craft Chicken Feed with it, seeds, and a bucket of any kind of XP Fluid. I don't care which type of XP Fluid you use for this. Once you have that, feed a Chicken it. Unfortunately the Chicken won't survive the procedure but hey, Spawn Eggs!\n\nNot all mobs can be swabbed, though.

quests.title: Mob Charm Fragments
quests.description: Charm Fragments can be made either into Charms or Spawn Eggs. They are from Reliquary and rarely drop from their respective mobs. Some can even be crafted! Take 2 and a normal Egg and you can craft a Spawn Egg.

quests.title: Other Spawners
quests.description: These are spawners provided by mods besides Apothic Spawners.

quests.title: 263860CADB3D76C6
quests.subtitle: EnderIO's Spawner
quests.description: Powered Spawner is the Mob Spawner made using EnderIO. First, you'll need a filled Soul Vial and a Broken Spawner. (Technically you only need the Soul Vial to change the Spawner but that's whatever). Once you have a Broken Spawner you like, craft the Powered Spawner with it! Then, place it down, give it a Capacitor, and power it. Boom! now you are spawning mobs with EnderIO.\n\nYou can also make this Spawner fill Soul Vials directly, without the need of a Clicker.

quests.title: 52FAF122466FDDC9
quests.subtitle: Draconic Evolution's Spawner
quests.description: Stabilized Spawner is Draconic Evolution's version of the Spawner. When you use one of the Cores on a Spawner it will become a Stabilized Spawner. You can swap the Cores but you won't be able to change the stats as now they are set by the Cores. The better the Core the more mobs spawn and at a faster rate.

quests.title: 6D68D9941049E806
quests.subtitle: Ars Nouveau's Spawner
quests.description: This spawner will, as its name implies, make use of Source as fuel. To decide on a mob to spawn, you'll need a Containment Jar holding the mob in the area.

quests.title: 39E822440E7D2E04
quests.subtitle: Mob Grinding Utils' Spawner
quests.description: Mob Grinding Utils is all about Mob Farming so of course it has a Spawner! The Entity Spawner! It'll need 3 things to work though: a Spawn Egg, XP Jelly Babies, and a Redstone signal. XP Jelly Babies are made by processing XP through a XP Solidifier with the XP Mould Jelly Baby. They can be eaten or used as Fuel in the second slot. Once you have the Spawn Egg in the top slot, XP Jelly Babies in the Second, and a Redstone signal it'll start spawning the mobs!

quests.title: 3F55F3CC8519D783
quests.subtitle: Mystical Agriculture's Spawner
quests.description: The Soulium Spawner is the Spawner gifted to us by Mystical Agriculture. It uses Mob Essence and Energy to spawn the mobs. Mob Essence is gotten through harvesting Mob Plants, made by Soul Jars. So you'll have to kill the mobs first, or use the Soul Extractor.

quests.title: 72AE56D34834D28E
quests.subtitle: PneumaticCraft's Spawner
quests.description: Another one from PneumaticCraft? Oh this one is the actual Spawner I see. Like the Draconic Stabilized Spawner you'll need a Vanilla Spawner first. Once you have one, place a Spawner Extrator above the Spawner and give it below -0.5 Bars to get it to work. Once it's done it'll give you a Spawner Core filled with whatever mob was in it and it will leave you with an Empty Spawner. Then use the Empty Spawner to craft a Pressurized Spawner and then put the Spawner Core into it. (To upgrade the Core use a Vacuum Trap to suck up the mobs that will go into the Spawner Core). Once you do that the Spawner will now need Pressure to work, ignores Light Level, and is Redstone Activated.

quests.title: 21C2458FED19363C
quests.subtitle: Industrial Foregoing's Spawner
quests.description: It uses Essence along with a mob in a Mob Imprisonment Tool to spawn a copy of that mob.

quests.title: Flax String
quests.subtitle: Who needs Spiders anyway?
quests.description: Flax String can be used in replace of normal String.

quests.title: 56550CD12C681B0F
quests.subtitle: Flax on, Flax off
quests.description: Flax Seeds can be found growing in fields of grass. Flax is great if you need a lot of String in the early game.

quests.title: Leather
quests.subtitle: But....Cows can't be sheared...
quests.description: I don't wanna know how you got these.

quests.title: Milk a Cow - Profit
quests.subtitle: Why aren't there Bulls in the game?
quests.description: Find a Cow and Right Click it with a Bucket.\n\nSeriously, why no Bulls?

quests.title: 0893EFCAC7031FEA
quests.subtitle: Have your Cake and Eat it too
quests.description: Time to bake a cake, if you've got some milk and eggs ready.

quests.title: Punch the Grass
quests.subtitle: Block Hand 1, Block Grass 0
quests.description: Let's gather some seeds.

quests.title: The Planter
quests.subtitle: Wait until you get Machines for this...
quests.description: To till Dirt into Farmland you'll need a Hoe.

quests.title: Food and Farming
quests.description: Welcome to the Food and Farming chapter!\n\nHere, you'll find different ways for you to grow and make food!

quests.title: We're doing this the Old Fashioned way
quests.subtitle: Get along little Doggy
quests.description: The classic Lead. Use this to get animals into your farm area.\n\nThis isn't the same thing as the ore.

quests.title: It's Clippin' Time
quests.subtitle: Pacifist Run
quests.description: To shear Sheep you need Shears, you wouldn't get Wool any other way...right?

quests.title: Mary had a Little Lamb
quests.subtitle: Whose Fleece was....Rainbow?
quests.description: Let's gather some pieces of Wool!

quests.title: Purchasing Farm Supplies
quests.subtitle: The Villager has more than one way to Spawn
quests.description: Markets provide you with a villager than can sell you anything if you have the right amount of emeralds.\n\nSpoiler: It's usually just 1 Emerald per item, luckily, they have EVERYTHING.

quests.title: You're so sweet
quests.subtitle: Pour some Sugar on me!
quests.description: You should have everything you need already.

quests.title: Sugar Sugar
quests.description: Find some Sugar Cane near some water.

quests.title: I'm not gonna make an Egg pun
quests.subtitle: ...or am I?
quests.description: Chickens will lay these naturally. I guess it's not really considered naturally...\n\nI guess the chickens are just getting... Eggs-ercise!!!.

quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks.

quests.subtitle: Willy Would be Proud
quests.description: But he usually closes by 5, so who cares?

quests.title: Making a Kitchen, with a Book
quests.subtitle: Totally won't catch on fire...
quests.description: Go ahead, put a Book in a Furnace and smelt it.

quests.title: Cooking with the power of Diamonds
quests.subtitle: This is totally worth it
quests.description: Craft the next version of the book. I promise you, it's worth it.\n\nI'll even give you a Diamond back.

quests.title: THE BEST THING SINCE SLICED BREAD
quests.subtitle: Betty White was born before Sliced Bread
quests.description:
This block is part of a multi-block kitchen.

This will show you every recipe that is available to you with the food you have in your inventory, or stored in the kitchen multi-block.

You can finally create a nice kitchen in Minecraft.

quests.title: The Sink = Infinite Water
quests.subtitle: 1 Block does the trick!
quests.description: This block provides water to the multi-block kitchen.\n\nIt can also provide infinite water by pumping water out via cables or pipes.

quests.title: Need more cooking space?
quests.subtitle: We need more cooking space
quests.description: This block stores items for cooking.\n\nYou can also place other kitchen multi-block items on it, like toasters and a Cow in a Jar.

quests.title: Honey, there's a Furnace in the Kitchen
quests.subtitle: No Timer Needed
quests.description: This block enables smelting recipes in your kitchen multi-block!

quests.title: Fridges
quests.subtitle: You'll open it, close it, then open it again, just because you're bored

quests.title: Even More Storage
quests.subtitle: So much room for activities!
quests.description: This works just like the kitchen counter, except in the air.\n\nAnd you can't put things on top of it.

quests.title: Ice Upgrade
quests.subtitle: Ice, Ice, Baby!
quests.description: Provides Ice and Snow recipes!

quests.title: Heating Upgrade
quests.description: Allows you to attach power to the Stove.

quests.title: A Cow in a Jar
quests.subtitle: Phenomenal Milking Powers....Itty bitty living space
quests.description:
This block produces milk over time, and enables milk recipes for the kitchen multi-block.

To get a cow in the jar, place the jar in a hole. Lure the cow to fall in said hole above the jar, then drop an anvil on it.

I have no clue what this glass is made of, but it's stronger than my relationship with Chicken.

quests.title: Welcome to Hostile Neural Networks!
Learning Mobs
quests.subtitle: The Learning HUD
quests.description:
The Deep Learner is one of the core components of HNN.

With this item, you can right click to open up a HUD and store Data Models to gather data while killing mobs.

Each Learner can hold 4 Data Models, and as long as you have the Learner anywhere in your inventory, it will collect data for the models placed inside!

Note: You can have multiple Deep Learners in your inventory, and it will count the kills for all Data Models inside all of the Learners.

quests.title: Leveling Up Data Models
quests.description:
Once you make your first Data Model, you'll need to level it up to be useful.

Data Models start out at the first tier: Faulty. You'll need to at least level it to Basic if you'd like to run some simulations on it!

Once placed inside of the Deep Learner, the HUD will tell you how many kills are required to level it up. You can also see this info in the tooltip of the Model itself.

quests.title: Modeling Mobs
quests.subtitle: "Gathering Data"
quests.description:
Model Frameworks are the starting point for creating Data Models.

To start collecting data on a specific mob, you'll want to make one of these then right click the mob you'd like to gather data on. When done properly, the Model Framework will turn into the Data Model of the mob you clicked on.

To gather data for that mob, place the newly created Data Model inside of a Deep Learner, then start killing that specific mob with the Deep Learner in your inventory.

quests.title: Simulating Deaths
quests.description:
The Simulation Chamber is the main machine within HNN.

When given power, it will run simulations based on the Data Model that is placed inside. The power required also depends on the Data Model placed inside, and can be seen within the Model's tooltip. 

The machine also requires at least one Prediction Matrix to run a simulation.

The result of the simulation will be output onto the Matrix. Simulations will always produce some kind of Generalized Prediction, which can be used in various crafting recipes. They also vary depending on the origin of the mob in the Data Model.

If the simulation succeeds, you will receive a Mob Prediction based off of the model. The higher the tier of the Data Model used, the higher the success rate is for a simulation.

quests.title: Creating Loot
quests.description:
The Loot Fabricator is the machine that gets you that sweet, sweet loot from Mob Predictions.

When given power and a successful Mob Prediction, you will be able to choose which item you'd like to get from that mob's Data Model. The machine will remember your choice, so it can be automated.

Examples of Mob Predictions:

- Ender Dragons for Dragon Eggs
 - Zombies for Iron
 - Withers for Nether Stars

quests.subtitle: Tier: Magical

quests.title: Wand
quests.subtitle: You're a Wizard (Insert your name)!
quests.description: The Wand can be used to activate the Infusion Alter, just right-click on the altar to activate the infusion process.

quests.title: Inferium Farmland
quests.description: You'll want to start growing Inferium as soon as you can!\n\nWhile not required for growing these seeds, you can also create Essence Farmland that will increase the growth speed of the seeds (especially Inferium Seeds). However, certain seeds will require certain farmlands to be planted on.

quests.title: Mystical Fertilizer
quests.description: Mystical Fertilizer works as Bonemeal, but better. It instantly grows whatever it is used on to full maturity.

quests.title: Enchanter
quests.description: The Enchanter is a block that allows you to add enchantments to enchantable items using items and essences.

quests.title: Witherproof Blocks
quests.description: Witherproof Blocks, Witherproof Bricks and Witherproof Glass have a very high blast resistance and cannot be destroyed by the Wither or the Ender Dragon.

quests.title: Insanium Farmland
quests.description: To grow Tier 6 or Magical Seeds you need to have a certain Crux placed directly below the Farmland they are growing on.

quests.title: Inferium Growth Accelerator
quests.subtitle: Range: 9 Blocks
quests.description:
Growth Accelerators very slightly increase the growth speed of a seed when placed directly underneath the farmland. Each tier has a range of how many blocks 'up' it can accelerate, with Inferium being the lowest at 12.
Note: Growth Accelerators of all tiers provide the same rate of growth ticks. Higher tiers however have a larger range, so you can stack more of them below a single plant. It doesn't matter which tier you use as long as the Growth Accelerator is placed within its max range.

quests.title: Inferium Apple
quests.description: Buffs:\n\n - Absorption II (3:00)

quests.title: Prudentium Apple
quests.description:
Buffs:

 - Absorption II (3:00)
 - Speed II (3:00)

quests.title: Tertium Apple
quests.description:
Buffs:

 - Absorption II (3:00)
 - Speed II (3:00)
 - Resistance II (3:00)

quests.title: Imperium Apple
quests.description:
Buffs:

 - Absorption II (3:00)
 - Speed II (3:00)
 - Resistance II (3:00)
 - Regeneration II (3:00)

quests.title: Supremium Apple
quests.description:
Buffs:

 - Absorption II (3:00)
 - Speed II (3:00)
 - Resistance II (3:00)
 - Regeneration II (3:00)
 - Strength II (3:00)

quests.title: Mystical Agriculture!
quests.description: Mystical Agriculture is a resource generation mod that allows you to grow a large variety of vanilla and modded resources using Seeds.

quests.title: Prosperity Shards
quests.subtitle: Can we finally have Prosperity?
quests.description: Prosperity Shards are a core crafting ingrediant in the mod. To find some Prosperity Ore, go mining.

quests.title: Prosperity Seed Base
quests.subtitle: I'm all about that (Seed) Base
quests.description: You will need Prosperity Seed Bases in order to create resource crops.

quests.title: Infusion Altar
quests.subtitle: Creating Seeds
quests.description: The Infusion Altar is how you make all of the seeds. Place down the Altar first and it'll show you where to place the Pedestals after.\n\nIn order for the Infusing to start, the Alter requires a Redstone signal.

quests.title: Inferium
quests.subtitle: Tier: 1
quests.description:
Essence is the starting point for all of your growing needs in Mystical Agriculture.

Inferium Essence is the base tier of all essences. You can get this from mining, killing mobs, or by making seeds to grow them! 

To make the bigger and better essences, you'll need to make an Infusion Crystal.

quests.title: Infusion Crystal
quests.description: The Infusion Crystal is need in order to "tier up" seeds. For example if you combine the crystal with 4 Inferium Essence you will get 1 Prudentium Essence.\n\nLater on you will be able to craft an Infusion Crystal that doesn't break.

quests.title: Prudentium
quests.subtitle: Tier: 2
quests.description: This is the Tier 2 Essence, made by combining 4 Inferium together with an Infusion Crystal.

quests.title: Tertium
quests.subtitle: Tier: 3
quests.description: This is the Tier 3 Essence, made by combining 4 Prudentium together with an Infusion Crystal.

quests.title: Imperium
quests.subtitle: Tier: 4
quests.description: This is the Tier 4 Essence, made by combining 4 Tertium together with an Infusion Crystal.

quests.title: Supremium
quests.subtitle: Tier: 5
quests.description: This is the Tier 4 Essence, made by combining 4 Imperium together with an Infusion Crystal.

quests.title: Master Infusion Crystal
quests.description: The Master Infusion Crystal works the same as the Infusion Crystal but it never breaks.

quests.title: Insanium
quests.subtitle: Tier: 6
quests.description: This is the Tier 6 Essence, made by combining 4 Supremium together with an Infusion Crystal.

quests.title: Creative Essence
quests.subtitle: Tier: Creative
quests.description: Creative Essence is needed to craft the ATM Star.

quests.title: Inferium Tools
quests.description: Starting with Inferium Essence, you can create ingots to make both Essence Tools and Armor.\n\nEssence tools can be upgraded to higher tiers, and just like the Armor, they can be Augmented in the Tinkering Table.

quests.title: Inferium Armor
quests.description: To start your journey making Essence Gear, you'll need to make the Inferium Armor first.\n\nThis gear can be upgraded to higher tiers, just like the Essences. You can also Augment them with the Tinkering Table!

quests.title: Creating Mob Seeds
quests.description:
Most seeds are simple to make, but to make Mob Seeds, you'll need to head to the Nether to pick up some Soulium.
With the stone and ore that you find, you'll need to use these to make the Soulium Dagger and Soul Jars. Using the dagger to kill mobs, you'll be able to gather their souls, which are used in the Infusion Altar to create the respective mob seeds.
Alternatively, you can fill Soul Jars inside of the Soul Extractor by inserting a jar and using mob items to fill them. For example, adding Rotten Flesh will give a portion of a Zombie Soul.

quests.title: Insanium Apple
quests.description:
Buffs:

 - Absorption II (3:00)
 - Speed II (3:00)
 - Resistance II (3:00)
 - Regeneration II (3:00)
 - Strength II (3:00)
 - Haste II (3:00)

quests.title: 552335ED867D6EFA
quests.description:
Great for smelting a ton of items!
An Insanium Coal Block is needed to craft the ATM Star.

quests.title: Unattuned Augment
quests.description: The Unattuned Augment is used in an Infusion Alter to create various augments. Get Haste, Night Vision, Fall Damage Resistance, Fire Resistance, and much more with these amazing augments!

quests.title: 7580037DB8ADEB3C
quests.subtitle: Tier: 2
quests.description: Meow meow I'm a Cow...

quests.title: Cognizant Dust
quests.description: This special Dust is dropped from the Wither and the Ender Dragon when killed by an Essence Weapon enchanted with Mystical Enlightenment.

quests.title: The Awakening
quests.description: To awaken your Supremium Essence, you'll need to create a new Altar and 4 new Pedestals, as well as 4 Essence Vessels.\n\nThe Essence Vessels will require the starter Element Essences to fill: Fire, Water, Earth, and Air.

quests.title: 2C73E3C5113BF2AC
quests.subtitle: Tier: 2
quests.description: Beep beep I'm a Sheep

quests.title: Sickles
quests.description: Sickles tools that can be used to clear large amount of organic materials. Sickles break blocks in an area around the block you mine.

quests.title: 1636F3F12E92CAEA
quests.description:
To use a Watering Can you'll need to fill it with Water by right-clicking on a Water source block. Once it's filled with Water you can hold right-click on a crop to water the crops within the Watering Can's AOE.
Essence Watering cans have the ability of auto-watering. Just shift-right-click the Watering Can in the air to toggle auto-watering on or off. It will look like the Watering Can is enchanted when it's turned on.

quests.title: Scythes
quests.description: Scythes are tools that can farm large areas of crops all at once. They can also be used as a fairly good weapon.

quests.title: 41DBE44D7AA0B623
quests.description: The Tinkering Table is how you add these augments to your essence gear!

quests.title: Awakened Supremium
quests.subtitle: Tier: 5 - Awakened
quests.description: This is the Tier 5 - Awakened Essence, made by combining 4 Cognizant Dust, 10 of each Elemental Essence and 1 Supremium Block together in an Awakening Alter.

quests.title: Automating Awakened Supremium
quests.description: Awakened Supremium and other tiered essences can be farmed using the Productive Bees mod.

quests.title: 3C9F5EB59D72AC90
quests.description: An Awakened Supremium Ingot Block is needed to craft the ATM Star.

quests.title: 5C590DB2F3D935E5
quests.subtitle: Recycling!
quests.description: The Seed Reprocessor can convert essence seeds back into essences.

quests.title: "Furnace"
quests.description: The "Furnace" is an upgraded version of a vanilla Furnace that can be upgraded for faster speed and better efficiency.

quests.title: 16E3031D800B40D5
quests.description: The Soulium Spawner uses mob essences to spawn mobs. For example if you put in some Ghast Essence you can spawn a Ghast.

quests.title: 0EFEDB0DD90DFC81
quests.description: The Harvester can auto-harvest crops and re-plant them. Items collected by the Harvester are put into it's internal inventory.

quests.title: 3EA2578C3A56FAE8
quests.description: The Soul Extractor allows you to fill up Soul Jars by inserting a jar and using mob items to fill them. For example, adding Rotten Flesh will give a portion of a Zombie Soul.

quests.title: Machine Upgrades
quests.description: Machine Upgrades are used to speed Mystical Agriculture machines.

quests.title: Productive Bees!
quests.description:
Welcome to Productive Bees!

To get started with the mod, you'll first need to find some Honeycombs and Honey Bottles! Find yourself a Beehive, and let the bees do their work for a little. Shearing it when it is full will give you honeycombs, and glass bottles will give you Honey Bottles!

Important Note: With the bee quests requiring combs, the recipes will not be shown. Make sure to look them up in JEI if you need them!

quests.title: 0A11725B41AB45F6
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks. 

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission. 

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Capturing Bees!
quests.description:
To get our own bee farm going, we'll have to find us some bees... and capture them.
Right-clicking a bee with this will capture it!
Adventuring can also net you some Sturdy Bee Cages, so keep an eye out!

quests.title: Searching for Nests
quests.description: Right-clicking on a Nest of the type you are looking for will point you in the direction of another!

quests.title: 128A14A3842325FE
quests.subtitle: Are the Bees still real?
quests.description:
When installed into an Advanced Beehive, bees no longer physically exit the hive. A trip to their flower block will be simulated.

Make sure to put its required flower block or a Feeding Slab in front of the hive containing the required flower blocks or items for the bee in the hive. To see how to set it up correctly, check the Feeding Slab quest.

I highly recommend getting this so your bees don't disappear and to be able to more easily put in/take out bees from the hive.

quests.title: Your First Beehive
quests.description:
Using the vanilla method, go ahead and make yourself a Beehive to have your own little setup!

These can hold 3 Bees each, but we won't be using it for long...

Bees will only create Honey and Honeycombs if they have the right flowers. Vanilla bees can use any flower, but most bees in the mod will require a specific block! Make sure to check JEI for more info.

quests.title: Productivity
quests.subtitle: The big one
quests.description:
Affects the amount of combs you receive whenever a bee produces honeycombs. There are 4 levels of this: Normal, Medium, High, Very High. Very High is what we are after.

It is found on KamikazBee and BeeBee. BeeBee is currently on vacation down below, though, so KamikazBee is our only option.

To get a KamikazBee, you need a Bee Nest Helmet. Get attacked by mobs (or shoot yourself with an arrow) while wearing the helmet for a 30% chance of having a KamikazBee emerge. It is quite fast, and will sting the aggressor (unless it's you), so better catch it quickly or use the Catcher.

quests.title: Weather Tolerance
quests.subtitle: The least big one of the big ones
quests.description: Affects the ability of a bee to work under harsh weather conditions. There are 3 levels of this: None, Rain, Any. Any is what we are after. You could leash the bee to a fence during a thunderstorm if you wanted to, but come on, that's just cruel.\n\nI offer you an easier solution. Fishing. That's right, you can fish for bees. Water or Prismarine Bees naturally come with the ability to tolerate any weather conditions. We can make use of this!

quests.title: Behavior
quests.subtitle: Sleep is for the weak
quests.description: Affects the time of day a bee can work. There are 3 levels of this: Diurnal, Nocturnal, Metaturnal. Diurnal bees can only work during daytime, Nocturnal bees can only work during nighttime, Metaturnal bees can work at any time of the day. Metaturnal is what we're after. BeeBee naturally has the Metaturnal trait, but, as mentioned in the Productivity quest, is on vacation, so we'll need to look into some alternative measures.\n\nWe will need to leash some bees to a fence during nighttime to make them Nocturnal, then leaving those bees out on a fence during daytime to make them Metaturnal. We can skip one of these steps with a Ghostly Bee or Shroombees, which are naturally Nocturnal.

quests.title: Endurance
quests.subtitle: One of the less important ones
quests.description: Affects the bee's likelihood of losing its stinger whenever it attacks something. This trait is less important compared to the first 3 I mentioned, but I will talk about it anyway. There are 4 levels of this: Weak, Normal, Medium, Strong. Strong is the one I will focus on. Certain Bees, like Draconic, Obsidian, and some other bees I may not have mentioned naturally have strong Endurance, allowing them to keep their stinger.

quests.title: Temper
quests.subtitle: Stop stinging me already!
quests.description: Affects the bee's aggression and likeliness to sting you. This is one of the less important traits, though it is worth not having an Aggressive bee when you want to work with one in world. There are 4 levels of this: Passive, Normal, Hostile, Aggressive. I'll be honest I don't really know what each level of Temper does. All I know is that Aggressive bees WILL sting you, even if otherwise unprovoked. Bees will become less aggressive if you feed them Honey Treats.

quests.title: 198EDBAC1D6E2339
quests.subtitle: Prevents Bees from Teleporting in a Hive
quests.description: You'll need these for Ender Bees.

quests.title: 397E2D14BDE7DED0
quests.subtitle: 4x Comb
quests.description: All Bees will give Comb Blocks instead of Combs, effectively quadrupling outputs!

quests.title: 2182492BCC1B33D8
quests.subtitle: Making Babies
quests.description:
When installed in a Hive, it gives a 5% chance for a new baby Bee to be spawned every time honey is delivered.

When placed in a Catcher, it only allows the catcher to catch baby Bees.

You can stack these for a greater chance.

quests.title: 196E55B64667AE35
quests.subtitle: Slapping down a Slab
quests.description:
You can place Bee Flowers on Feeding Slabs that are placed in front of Hives, as shown in the image below.\n
{image:atm:textures/questpics/bees/feeder.png width:175 height:100 align:center fit:true}

quests.title: Stopping Dripping
quests.subtitle: You got no Drip
quests.description: Do Hives annoy you when they drip? If so, you're in luck because there's an easy solution.\n\nYou can place a Sponge in the Bottle slot of an Advanced Hive to stop it from dripping.

quests.title: 1B79F794EDAA810A
quests.subtitle: Making Babies 2: Electric Beegaloo
quests.description:
The Breeding Chamber can be used to breed two bees with each other, automatically. It is capable of self breeding, as well as breeding 2 types of bees to make a third type (Example: Ashy Mining + Crystalline -> Iron). If this would result in a conflict (Continuing off of the earlier example, Ashy Mining + Crystalline -> Aluminium), take out one of the bees, then put it back in.

Provide breeding items in each slot (usually flowers, hold SHIFT on a bee cage holding a certain bee type to see what breeding item it uses (Draconic Bees use 2 Draconic Dust for example)) and some bee cages.

Just...don't do...whatever it takes to get the F.Bee.I. to go after you. I will ensure you get added to the Hall of Shame if they DO come after you.

quests.title: 3E301F3EEC8C763A
quests.subtitle: Baby Bee Daycare
quests.description:
This can be used to speed up the growth rate of baby Bees, or to create new Spawn Eggs.

Place a caged baby Bee with 20 Honey Treats to turn it into an adult.

To create Spawn Eggs, you'll need to combine the gene of the bee you want with a honey treat, then use that honey treat in this machine with an egg to create the new spawn egg.

Genes can be combined for a maximum of 100% purity, which will give you a 100% chance to convert an Egg to a Bee Spawn Egg.
{@pagebreak}
You can even apply genes to a bee without taking it out of its cage with this. Put a Honey Treat with the gene samples of your choice into the incubator along with a bee cage holding the bee you want to apply genes to.

quests.title: Gene Samples
quests.subtitle: To make the ultimate bee
quests.description: Bees have varying traits that can affect how they work, when they work, their aggression, and their likelihood to lose their stinger when they attack you. In these quests I will be going over the way to get the best traits possible, as well as how to use them.\n\nTo get these Gene Samples, check out the Bottler quest, which is a dependency of this one. To actually apply these Gene Samples to your bees, you will need to combine them with a Honey Treat in a crafting grid. All traits, except for Type, you can apply to your bees by feeding them the Honey Treat. Type works differently, and must instead be used with the Incubator to make a Spawn Egg of the respective bee.

quests.title: 66324D7D0C51AEAC
quests.description: The Upgrade Base is used to craft the various Upgrades in Productive Bees.

quests.title: 500BEAD94C97DF96
quests.subtitle: Sonic Bees
quests.description:
Can be placed in a hive or centrifuge.

When in a hive, it decreases the amount of time bees spend in the hive by 20%.

When placed in a Centrifuge, it increases the processing speed.

These do stack.

quests.title: 532F3E6868A29037
quests.subtitle: Sonic everything but Bees
quests.description:
Think of the previous Upgrade: Speed, now think of it making things even faster! 

These Upgrades can be used in the Machines to make them work 40% faster! 
Yes, their effects stack. 

No, they can not be used in Hives, that's what Productivity is for!

quests.title: Advanced Beehive
quests.subtitle: No more shearing.
quests.description:
With the vanilla Beehive, we'll use this to craft an Advanced Beehive. It can be Oak or any kind of wood.

Bees will fly in and out of these, and drop off Honeycombs in the inventory. You can also insert glass bottles to get Honey Bottles.

We'll need a lot of Honeycomb for treats!

quests.title: 419DD6FE84B91749
quests.subtitle: The Gene Combiner and Chest
quests.description: When collecting genes, you'll get a percentage of a trait. You can combine them in a crafting table to add them together, or place them in a Gene Indexer to auto-combine.

quests.title: 6F978C4D561F35EC
quests.subtitle: Honey I Squished The Bees
quests.description:
The Bottler has two uses: Bottling honey and squshing bees for genes.

To get genes from bees, place a piston above the Bottler with a block of space between them.

Place the bee on top of the Bottler, and activate the piston to squish the bee into genes. The resulting squished bottle can be then placed in a Centrifuge.

Note: Make sure to have bottles in the Bottler.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/bees/bottler.png width:100 height:150 align:1}

quests.title: 7B5A0BFD47D96BDE
quests.subtitle: Catches Bees
quests.description: Used to catch bees that are flying around it.\n\nYou can use a Filter Upgrade to filter out which bees you want to catch, as well as a BaBee Upgrade to only catch baby bees.

quests.title: 57167FE67CFAC255
quests.subtitle: Used to add Bees to a Filter

quests.title: 14623D25561BA61B
quests.subtitle: Increases the Range of a Machine
quests.description: Mostly for the Catcher.

quests.title: Centrifuges
quests.subtitle: Processing Honeycombs
quests.description:
The Centrifuge is used to process Combs from Bees into useful items and honey! While you can definitely just use a regular Centrifuge in the beginning, getting a Powered Centrifuge soon after is a must. This is a faster Centrifuge that runs off of power!

If you're looking for the best way to process your Combs, the Heated Centrifuge is even faster and processes Comb Blocks instead of Combs!

These can all be made faster by using Speed Upgrades.

quests.title: Expansion Box
quests.subtitle: Increasing our bee storage
quests.description: Expansion boxes are placed on top of your Advanced Beehives to increase the amount of bees that can be in the hive to a total of 5 slots. These are also necessary for your Advanced Beehives to support upgrades.

quests.title: 32FDC5FFA000DAF8
quests.subtitle: Showing Off Bees
quests.description:
Proud of the Bees you have?

Wanna put them into a jar to show it off?

Place a Bee Jar down and use a Pipe or Hopper to insert the caged Bee into the jar.

quests.title: 1DF026030780AE96
quests.subtitle: Extracts Genes from Bees in Hives

quests.title: 3155E4212045BC8E
quests.subtitle: Lures a Draconic Bee in the End
quests.description:
The Obsidian Nest will lure in Draconic Bees when placed in the End.
These do not accept Honey Treats, but instead use Dragon's Breath.

quests.title: 6D484150536536B9
quests.subtitle: Lures in Crystalline Bees in the Nether
quests.description:
This nest attracts Crystalline Bees. You'll need Nether Quartz instead of using Honey Treats to attract the Bee.
The easiest way to get a quartz block is by mining it with a Silk Touch pick.
Tip: Brass has the Silk Touch trait when making a Silent Gear tool.

quests.title: 264BFB8C5F79616F
quests.subtitle: Lures the Sweat Bee in Cold Biomes
quests.description: Placing a Snow Nest in a snowy biome will lure in a Sweat Bee.

quests.title: 09FD3D0B9BCAEB5A
quests.subtitle: Lures in bees in River and Beach Biomes
quests.description:
The Gravel Nest will lure bees in either a River biome or Beach biome.
It lures in the Ashy Mining Bee, Chocolate Mining Bee, and the Digger Bee.

quests.title: Emerald Bee
quests.subtitle: Diamond Bee + Slimy Bee
quests.description: Once you have a Diamond Bee, breed it with the Slimy Bee to create an Emerald Bee!

quests.title: Ender Bee
quests.subtitle: Requires End Stone Nest
quests.description: Create yourself an End Stone Nest and head to the End to capture one of these bees!

quests.title: 73C70B15582958A5
quests.subtitle: Any Overworld Biome
quests.description:
The Dirt Nest can be placed in any overworld biome to lure in bees.
It can lure the Ashy Mining Bee, Chocolate Mining Bee, and the Leafcutter Bee.

quests.title: Slimy Bee
quests.subtitle: Requires Slimy Nest
quests.description: You can lure these bees in using a Slimy Nest in a swamp biome.

quests.title: 160BD0185954C891
quests.subtitle: Lures a Gold Bee when placed in the Nether
quests.description: Instead of using Honey Treats, this hive requires Gold Ingots to attract Bees.

quests.title: 1E9BD4B74DAEA9FC
quests.subtitle: Lures in Ender Bees when placed in the End
quests.description: To attract Bees to this nest, you'll need Popped Chorus Fruit instead of Honey Treats.

quests.title: 349D19F2FCC34B84
quests.subtitle: Lures in a Magmatic Bee when placed in the Nether
quests.description: Placing the Nether Brick Nest in the Nether will lure in a Magmatic Bee when given Magma Cream.

quests.title: 5CC9CB0911954215
quests.subtitle: Lures bees in any Overworld Biome
quests.description: A Reed Nest will work in any overworld biome, and will lure in a Mason Bee or a Reed Bee.

quests.title: 06044B4452A6B720
quests.subtitle: Lures bees in Desert Biomes
quests.description: When placed in a Desert biome, the Sand Nest will attract either the Chocolate or Ashy Mining Bee.

quests.title: Nest Spawning
quests.subtitle: Honey Treats Required
quests.description:
If you want to turn your Bee Farm into a factory for resources, you'll need to start by spawning in Bees with Nests.
The nests must be placed in specific biomes, which you can find in the JEI for it (look for the I icon at the top).
To lure in a Bee to the Nest, right click on it with a Honey Treat. Nests will not work without the treats!!
Important Note: Certain Bees will only live in Nests and will not go into Advanced Hives. If they don't produce Honeycomb, they need to live in a Nest instead.

quests.title: 131EC039435B8878
quests.description:
In Productive Bees, you don't spend most of your time flying around trying to find certain bees.
Instead, you spawn them using Nests with Honey Treats.
With these, you'll create yourself some Nests and right click them with the treats to lure Bees in. Some Nests require special items instead of Honey Treats, so make sure to check JEI for more info!
Make sure to check out which biome you need to be in to lure in the right Bees!

quests.title: Allthemodium Progression
quests.description:
If you want the ATM bees, it takes a lot of capturing and breeding and feeding.
The following part of the questline outlines which bees you'll need to move forward.
Make sure to check JEI and the Big Book of Bees for more info!

quests.title: Lapis Bee
quests.subtitle: Redstone + Blue Banded
quests.description: Breed a Redstone Bee with a Blue Banded Bee to get a Lapis Bee!

quests.title: Diamond Bee
quests.subtitle: Ender + Lapis
quests.description: Breed the Ender Bee with a Lapis Bee to create a Diamond Bee!

quests.title: Ancient Bee
quests.subtitle: Feed Diamond Bee a Block of Netherite

quests.title: Allthemodium Bee
quests.description: Using a Foundry, pour Molten Allthemodium over an Ancient Bee Spawn Egg.

quests.title: Wood Nests
quests.subtitle: Can be used in any Overworld biome
quests.description:
Wood Nests are used to lure Carpenter Bees and the Blue Banded Bee.

Dark Oak Nests lures 3 different bees.

These can be placed in any Overworld Biome.

quests.title: Glowing Bee
quests.description: You'll need to grab yourself a Glowstone Nest and head to the Nether to capture this bee!

quests.title: 027FD9135DEC4949
quests.subtitle: Lures in Ghostly Bees when placed in the Nether and given Ghast Tears

quests.title: 41CF7CAEE4F60CCD
quests.subtitle: Lures a Glowing Bee in the Nether
quests.description: When placed in the Nether and given Glowstone, the Glowstone Nest will lure in a Glowing Bee.

quests.title: 25D8BE0280B6E7F1
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks. 

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission. 

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Cardboard Packages
quests.description:
Now we have our Packager we can now have Packages! 

There is 4 varients but that doesn't change anything with them besides apperance. It is entirely random which one you get. 

Packages are Items and when Placed on the Ground will become Entities. You can Right Click them after they were Placed to Pick them up, or Break them to get the Items out. You can also move them like any other Entity! 

Packages can also be used to interact with other Machines. Like being placed on Chain Conveyors or Belts!

quests.title: Stock Ticker
quests.description:
Stock Tickers can be set to the Network by Right Clicking the Stock Link with the Stock Ticker in Hand. 

Then, place down the Stock Ticker and give it a Stock Keeper by either placing down a Blaze Burner or a Mob on a Seat nearby. 

You'll know they are a Stock Keeper by their stereotypical Green Visor. We can now Right Click the Stock Keeper to view and order Items from our Network. 

When you order Items, they'll be placed into a Package from a Packager below the Stock Link.

quests.title: Stock Link
quests.description:
You like combining Inventories and making a way of viewing and interacting with all those Inventories with a few simple Machines similar to AE2 and Sophisticated Storage? 

Then, you'll need some Stock Links! 

Stock Links can be placed on Packagers to connect to the Inventory the Packager is connected to. When first placed, a new Stock Network will be created. 

These can connect to Chests, Barrels, and even Vaults! 

You can also Right Click another Stock Link with a Stock Link in hand to tune them to the same Network. When the new Stock Link is placed onto another Packager, its Inventory Block will be added to the same Network. 

If you'd like to Interact with these Networks you'll need other Blocks!

quests.title: Chain Conveyor
quests.description:
Chain Conveyors won't do much on their own. They need another Chain Conveyor, Chains, and Rotational Power! 
Chain Conveyors will need another Chain Conveyor near by in order to attach to them with Chains. 

The Chains will need to be Right Clicked onto 1 Chain Conveyor then done the same to another you want to connect it to. 

Once, one is given Rotational Power, the Chains will move at the same Speed. Don't worry about Direction, there'll be 2 Chains! 

When the Chains are a moving, you can connect to them with a Wrench to move with the Chains, you can either press Shift or switch Items to drop off the Chain. 

You can also place Packages on them, but without the Item described in the next Quest, they will just go around in a circle!

quests.title: Package Frogport
quests.description:
Package Frogports are adorable and helpful Machines used for mixing Packages and Chain Conveyors! 

First, Right Click a part of the Chain on a Chain Conveyor with the Frogport in Hand, this will set it as the Frogports destination. 

Then, when placed we can mess with its GUI. Here we can change the name of its Address, determine whether it takes and gives Packages or just gives Packages. 

They have 18 Slots to Hold Packages for moving. 

If the Address of the Package doesn't match the Address you gave the Frogport, the Frogport will send the Package onto the Chain Conveyor. 

If it matches the Address, the Package will be taken into the Frogport. If there is no matching Address the Package will just go in circles! 

Packages can also be automatically sent and taken from Frogports with Funnels and Belts.

quests.title: Packagers
quests.description:
Packagers are the new and very important Machine for Create. In order to use pretty much everything from the Update we'll need a Packager. 
Combine some of our new-found Cardboard to make a Block of Cardboard. No, these aren't Boxes yet and they certainly don't do anything. 

Well besides Crafting our Packager! The Packager will then be placed onto a Block with an Inventory, like Chest or Barrel. You'll know it is connected when one of the sides changes to appear like a wall. 

Then, when given a Redstone Signal it will pull all Items within the Inventory into a Package! More on that later! 

The Packages can then be pulled out by Hand or Belt. You can also send Packages back into the Packager to put the Items back into an Inventory. 

If you place and name a Sign on the Packager it will give all Packages that it makes an Address.

quests.title: Shops
quests.subtitle: With Table Cloths
quests.description:
Table Cloths can either be used to show off Items, or to sell off Items! 

To set up a Shop, do all the steps from the previous Quest: placing Stock Links, Stock Tickers, and a Mob on a Seat or Blaze Burner. 

Now use a Table Cloth to Interact with the Mob or Blaze Burner, this will bind the Table Cloth to that Stock Ticker. 

Place down the Table Cloth and you'll be able to place the Items you want to sell on top, and the price below. 

When someone buys an Item, it will send a message to the Stock Link, which will Package the Items bought and take the price.

quests.title: Postboxes
quests.description:
Postboxes will use Addresses and Trains to deliver Packages! 

First, Packages can be held on Trains with Depots! Obviously the Depot needs to be connected to the Train via Glue. 

Next, we can assign the Postbox to a Train Station by Right Clicking the Train Station wtih the Postbox in Hand. 

We can then place the Postbox nearby and when a Train arrives at the Station they will interact with the Postbox. 

In the Postbox's GUI we can change its Address, which will effect whether Packages are delivered or sent from it. If the Address of the Package matches the Address of the Postbox, it will be sent to the Postbox. If it doesn't match, it will go from the Postbox to your Train!

quests.title: Create 1.21
quests.description:
To start with the new Create Items we'll need Cardboard! 

Which is made from Pressing Pulp. 

Pulp is made from Mixing 4 Saplings and Water in a Mechanical Mixer and Basin. 

You can combine Cardboards to make Blocks of Cardboard which can make the new Items in Create... or Cardboard Armor!

quests.title: Weighted Ejector
quests.description:
Okay this ones fun! You like throwing Items? Like, I mean to really throw them! 

Then, the Weighted Ejector is for you! 

First, you need to Shift Right Click a Block with the Weighted Ejector to set it as the target. The target has to be in line with where the Ejector is aimed in order to hit it. 

Once it has a target and is placed down, it can be fed Rotational Power to charge it! Then, when an Item is placed on the Weighted Ejector, it will throw it! 
You can hold on some of the Sides to change the Stack Size needed to throw Items.

quests.title: Smart Chute
quests.description: The Smart Chute is a Chute with the options to Filter.

quests.title: Clutch
quests.description:
The Clutch can be connected to our Kinetic Systems where it will act like a Fence Gate. 

By giving it a Redstone Signal it will stop the flow of Rotational Power through it. 

So all Rotating will stop at the Clutch if it is powered with Redstone. The ones Rotating into it will continue Rotating as normal though!

quests.title: Water Wheels
quests.description:
Water Wheels are simple automatic Rotational Power generators. 

Simply place them down, and have Water run over them in a certain direction. If it flows over both sides, it won't move, and the direction the Water flows determines where the Water Wheel Rotates to. 

The normal Water Wheel is just 1 Block big and provides a bit of Speed but with minimal Stress Units. 

The Large Water Wheel takes up 3x3 area and grants more Stress Units, just at a lower Speed. 

You can use both together to get the same Stress Units and Speed!

quests.title: Windmills
quests.description:
Windmills are a little more complicated than Water Wheels, but they also come with more customization and of course Speed and Stress Units! 

First, you'll need the heart of the Windmill, the Windmill Bearing. This Block will send the Rotational Power out of it. It is also what we'll use to turn on the Windmill! 

Then, you'll need the Blocks to make the actual Windmill part. Blocks will automatically stick to the Bearing, but to the rest of the Windmill you'll need Glue. Besides Windmill Sails, those attach automatically! 

We'll also need atleast 8 Windmill Sail like Blocks, those being the Windmill Sails or Wool. The more we have, the faster the Windmill spins! 

Once it is all set, just Right Click the Bearing with an Empty Hand to start it up.

quests.title: Sequenced Gearshift
quests.description:
Because the Sequenced Gearshift uses much fancier Items it is clearly a much fancier Machine! 

Judging by how confusing its GUI is, I'd say so... Hopefully I can help make it less confusing! No promises though. 

Like the normal Gearshift it will need a Redstone Signal to do whatever is designed. We'll need to configure its GUI to make a "script". 

First, is the Instructions, these are the actual tasks it will preform. Here it can turn its Shaft, effect a Pulley, wait, or just stop. It will need to stop at the end, it is inevitable. 

Next, is the Angle. The Angle that either the Shaft or Pulley will turn. From 360 to 1 degree! 

Last is the Speed and Direction. It changes how quickly the Shaft or Pulley move and either Clockwise or Counter-Clockwise.

quests.title: Adjustable Chain Drive
quests.description:
Adjustable Chain Drives work like Encased Chain Drives, just with more configs. 

If we send a Redstone Signal to the Adjustable Chain Drive that the original Shaft is connected to, the other Chain Drive Shafts will double in Speed! 

If we send one to a different Chain Drive though, the Speed of that Chain Drive will be cut in half!

quests.title: Andesite Tunnel
quests.description:
Tunnels at the most basic level, will cover your Belts. This will make it so the Items can't be picked up, and hopefully the Mobs won't leave. 

If you place another Belt moving perpendicular to the Belt the Tunnel is on, the Tunnel will filter 1 Item from the Stack of Items to the perpendicular Belt, while leaving the rest of the Items on the first Belt. 

If there is just 1 Item, it will move through the Tunnel like normal.

quests.title: Depot
quests.description:
Depots will hold Items. They can hold them to process the Items, or deposit to a Chute, or even just for decoration! 

You can place a Chute near the end of a Belt to bring Items from the Belt onto the Depot. 

The Depot can also be placed beneath a Machine to process Items within it.

quests.title: Item Vaults
quests.description:
Item Vaults, while not new, will be used a ton in the new Update! 

Item Vaults will act like Chests, just we can't put Items in or out as easily as Chests... 

In order to move Items we'll need to use Funnels! Attach them to the Vaults to send Items in and out. Preferably Brass Funnels for more Item Filtering. 

Each Vault has a ton of storage but we can also place them next to each other to combine their Inventories. 

We can place them in 1x1, 2x2, or 3x3 and their length can be up to 3 times their width! So the biggest we can have is 3x3x9.

quests.title: Chute
quests.description:
These are literally just fancy Hoppers. 

They connect two Inventories, bringing Items from the Top one to the Bottom one. 

Chutes can connect to each other, even diagonally. 

You can also use them with Fans to shoot Items up the Chutes!

quests.title: Brass Tunnel
quests.description:
Brass Tunnels work like Andesite Tunnels just with so many more configurations! 

First, we now get Filters! These are per side: if you Filter the Input side, only that Filter Item will be allowed to move throught the Tunnel. If you Filter the Output sides, then only those Items will come out of its side. 

Now we can also line Brass Tunnels together. This will allow them to take all the same Inputs but Filter them out to certain Belts! 

At the top of the Tunnel we'll find the option to change its Distribution Modes. I won't explain them in too much detail, our Quests have limited space, instead I'll summarize! 

Split: will split the Item stacks evenly per how many Belts it will go to. Forced Split: will make sure every Belt will get an even amount, while normal Split might skip some. Round Robin: will alternate individually between each Belt. Forced Round Robin: won't skip some Items and instead will wait, everyone gets a turn! Prefer Nearest: will send the Items to the closest Output. Randomize: it sends the Items randomly to different Outputs. Synchronize Inputs: will only Output when every Brass Tunnel has an Item waiting to Input.

quests.title: Vertical Gearbox
quests.description:
The Vertical Gearbox is just like the normal Gearbox if someone rotated it. 

It has 4 internal Shafts just this time instead of the Cardinal Directions, they are (from where you place it) Front, Back, Up, and Down. 

Also like the normal Gearbox, it will keep the Speed and Stress Units from the original Shaft!

quests.title: Gearshift
quests.description:
Gearshifts work similar to a Clutch by connecting to our Systems and being powered by Redstone. 

Instead of stopping Rotational Power though, the Gearshift will change its Direction! 

If it is going Clockwise into the powered Gearshift, it will come out Counter-Clockwise, and vice versa.

quests.title: Encased Chain Drives
quests.description:
Encased Chain Drives will act similar to Belts, by connecting Shafts to each other in a row. 

There is quite a few differences though, like that Encased Chain Drives can be used with a Wrench to rotate. They also need to be placed directly next to other Chain Drives to keep Rotating. 

Like Belts though, they keep the same Speed and Stress Units as the original Shaft. Plus they keep the same direction!

quests.title: Hand Crank
quests.subtitle: Manual Power!
quests.description:
The Hand Crank is the simplest and worst form of Rotational Power generation. 

When you hold Right Click it'll move Clockwise and if you hold Shift Right Click it will move Counter-Clockwise. 

It only gives a tiny bit of Stress Units and will stop after you quit holding it.

quests.title: Steam Engine
quests.description:
This one's a doozy! So listen carefully! 
1st is constructing the actual Steam Engine. The Fluid Tanks will judge how much Water can be held within it and decide the Level the Steam Engine will be at. 

Then, simply attach the Steam Engine to the side of the Fluid Tanks and it'll become a Steam Boiler. After, place a Shaft on the Steam Engine to get our Mechanical Arm that will give us Rotational Power from it. 

2nd is a Heat Source. We'll need a Heat Source beneath the Fluid Tanks to heat up the Water. There's quite a few Heat Sources: Fire, Campfire, Lava, Magma Blocks but Blaze Burners are the best! 

The better the Heat Source, the more Stress Units! So feed those Blaze Burners some Blaze Cakes and you'll be rocking! 

3rd is Water. This is the fuel of our Steam Engine, there wouldn't be Steam without Water. 

However you Pipe in Water is your choice, but for ATMons I recommend a Sink and ID!

quests.title: Andesite Funnel
quests.description:
Funnels are like if a Hopper and Dispenser had a baby. 

When placed onto a Block with an Inventory, like Chests, it will automatically take Items out 1 at a time. 
If you Shift Right Click it will automatically take Items into the Inventory. 

Both can be turned off with a Redstone Signal!

quests.title: Brass Funnel
quests.description:
The Brass Funnel is placed and used similar to the Andesite Tunnel. 

But each side comes with new configs! 

The Input Side will now come with a Filter option. Just place the Item in, and it will only take in that Item. 

The Output Side will now come with a limit. You can Scroll to set a number from 1 to 64. You can also choose whether it will Output exactly that amount, or up to that amount. 

If it is exactly that amout, it will wait until that amount is within the Inventory to Output it. If it is up to, it will keep Outputting Items until that number is reached.

quests.title: Gearbox
quests.description:
The Gearbox is helpful for sending Rotational Power in a whole bunch of different directions! 

The normal Gearbox will have 4 internal Shafts, on each of the Cardinal Directions: North, East, South, and West. 

The other Shafts will match the Speed and Stress Units but they will also spin in different directions from the original Shaft.

quests.title: Item Logistics
quests.description:
Item Logistics is important to Create. Millstones need Items, Deployers need Items, Mechanical Mixers need Items, and so on. 

Now how does Create want us to move Items? With Belts! 

Belts can be attached to two Shafts to connect and move with them. If the first Shaft is moving Clockwise, the second will move same Speed and Direction. 

Same with the Belts that are placed on those Shafts, they will move same Speed and Direction as the Shafts they are placed between. 

With placing Belts they can be placed perfectly Horizontal, Vertical, or diagonal at 45% angles. 

Once placed and move, any Items or Entities will be moved with the Belt. Entities can walk off the Belts though so careful with that. Thankfully Items can't walk off or even despawn when on it! 

The Items will then be taken to wherever the Belt goes. If it abruptly ends, the Items will just be Dropped. If it goes to a Depot, the Item will be placed in a Depot. If it goes below a Machine, the Machine will use it. 

If you want to take Items off the Belt you can just Right Click it!

quests.title: Mechanical Pump
quests.description:
Mechanical Pumps will use Rotational Power to move Fluids through Pipes. 

First, replace a Pipe with the Mechanical Pump. Then, make sure it is facing the right way you want Fluids to be moved. The Arrows next to the internal Cog will tell which direction it will move, you can change that with a Wrench. 

Then, feed it Rotational Power with a Cog near it. The direction does not change anything, but the Speed will effect how quickly Fluids are moved. 

Mechanical Pumps will also be needed for other Machines like the Hose Pulley!

quests.title: Cogwheels!
quests.subtitle: I just call them Cogs
quests.description:
Cogwheels (Cogs) are the next Block needed to use Rotational Power! They can connect to Shafts or other Cogs to move the Rotational Power. 

There is two versions of Cogs: regular Cogs and Large Cogs. They will both act the same in the sense of Rotational Power but there is also a few changes! 
Regular Cogs can connect to other Cogs adjacent to them. This will move the Rotational Power into a whole different direction. When this happens the direction of the second Cog will be reversed. If the first Cog is rotating Clockwise, the second one will rotate Counter-Clockwise. 

Large Cogs are a little more difficult to use than Cogs. They can't connect to other Large Cogs adjacent, rather they can only connect to Cogs that are diagonal to them! 

Most Machines will need Rotational Power from connecting Cogs. You'll recognize if the Machine has an internal Cog, that is what must be moved in order to use the Machine.

quests.title: Smart Fluid Pipe
quests.description:
Smart Fluid Pipes will give us Filtering for Fluid Pipes. 

When put on the Machine that the Pipes are extracting from, it can be set to only take out the one Fluid. This is set by adding a Bucket full of that Liquid in the Filter Slot. 

You can place the Smart Fluid Pipe later in the Pipe system to only send that certain Fluid through the Pipes after it. 

This is helpful for mass sorting a bunch of Fluid Tanks!

quests.title: Basin
quests.description:
The Basin is similar to the Depot, but can hold Items and Fluids. 

This will be helpful for using the Mechanical Mixer to Mix and Brew. 

And with the Mechanical Press to Autocraft!

quests.title: Fluid Pipe
quests.description:
Fluid Pipes are what we'll use to actually move Fluids automatically from one Inventory to another! 

You can place them down and they will automatically connect to Inventories and other Pipes. 

With a Wrench you can add Windows to a Pipe. These won't connect to parallel Pipes without Windows. 

The Pipes themselves won't move Fluids though, we'll need a Mechanical Pump for that! 

When we do get Pipes to start flowing though, we can use them to take Fluids out from a Source Block or the opposite with placing down Source Blocks. 

The Pipe will need to have an Open End to do so though, so there can't be Blocks in the way.

quests.title: Rotational Power
quests.description:
Rotational Power is the most important and confusing part of Create. 

All Machines will need some sort of Rotational Power to work, but what is it and how do we use it? 

Rotational Power is simply our Machines moving. Blocks like Shafts and Cogs will move that Rotational Power to our Machines. 

Talking about Shafts, that is our start to Rotational Power. They can be placed in a straight line, next to each other. 

When one Shaft is moved, all Shafts connected to it (on the same axis) will move with it. 

Craft 2 Andesite Alloys to create 8 Shafts.

quests.title: Cog Teamwork!
quests.description:
Cogs and Large Cogs can interact with each other to change Speed and Stress! 

If you connect a Cog, diagonally from a Large Cog, the Cog will double in Speed! This is because the Large Cog has more Teeth than the Cog, it takes longer to take a full Rotation. 

This also works in the reverse, if you put a Large Cog diagonal to a Cog, the Large Cog will spin at half Speed. 

These will also change the Stress Units from the Cogs. More Speed, more Stress. Less Speed, less Stress.

quests.title: Stress
quests.description:
Stress, like Rotational Power, is important and confusing. 

Stress Units (Su) are power loads for our Machines. Some Machines will have a minimum Stress, that means you'll need that much Stress in your System to work the Machine. 

Deployers, Mechanical Saws, and Encased Fans are examples of those! 

Some Machines also have a maximum Stress Units. That means if it goes over the amount, it will most likely stop working. Or blow up, either or! 

Stress Units are developed from Cogs and from our Machines that make Rotational Power. Water Wheels give little Stress while Steam Engines can give a ton!

quests.title: Fluid Valve
quests.description:
Fluid Valves can be used to stop Pipes from moving Fluid. 

Give them a Rotation, most likely from a Valve Handle, to stop moving Fluids. 

Just Rotate it again to get the Fluids back!

quests.title: Speed
quests.description:
Speed is distance over time, AKA how long it takes to get from point A to point B... well... we are working with Revolutions, it is more how long it takes to get from point A to point A in this big of a Circle. 

Anyways it is how quick our Machines move, including Cogs and Shafts! 

This is important because Speed will effect how other Machines work. Some will need a certain Speed and others will work more efficiently at higher Speeds. 

We can place a Speedometer (yes, like in a car) into our Kinetic System to see how fast everything is moving.

quests.title: Fluid Tanks
quests.description:
Fluid Tanks can hold Fluids. Like Chests, but for Water and such! 

You can only Input Fluids with Buckets but with Pipes you can Input and Output Fluids from them. 

Each Fluid Tank can hold 8 Buckets or 8000mB of Fluid. But that number will rise when we combine them! 

Yes, you heard me right! We can place multiple Fluid Tanks next to each other to connect their Inventories. They will stack when placed on top of each other up to 32, or by 2x2 or 3x3.

quests.title: Fluid Logistics
quests.description:
Fluids and Liquids aren't the most important in every aspect of Create, but luck is, you'll most likely run into them anyways! 

You'll need to learn the difficult path of Fluid Logistics in order to use and move them. 

And to start, you'll need Copper!

quests.title: Create
quests.description:
Most Players will already know of Create especially its billions of Addons! Not that many Mods have whole Modpacks based around them! 

If you aren't used to Create, these Quests should help you to learn the Mod. And with many Items and Machines there is a Ponder Option! Hold W while viewing the Item to watch a schematic that will teach you to understand the Item or Machine. 

And trust me, you'll want to learn Create, it is super useful! 

To start you'll need Andesite and lots of it.

quests.title: Andesite Alloys
quests.description:
What will we need all that Andesite for? We'll need Andesite Alloys! 

Andesite Alloys are made by combining 2 Andesite with either 2 Iron Nuggets or 2 Zinc Nuggets. 

Andesite Alloys don't do much on their own, rather they are the Crafting Ingrediant for almost all Machines and Items. So yeah, we'll need a few.

quests.title: Mechanical Press
quests.description:
The Mechanical Press is very helpful for making even more Machines! 

When powered with Rotational Power (and a lot of Stress Units) it will send the Metal Press down to Blocks below it. Like a Hydraulic Press! 

Any Items below it: either on a Belt, Depot, or even just dropped, will be Pressed. 

This is mainly for turning Ingots into Plates with no charge. You can also use it to get Paper from Sugarcane and Paths from Dirt! 

If you place a Basin beneath it you can then use the Press to combine Liquids, Items, and Blocks to create new Items. 

Another option with the Basin below our Press is Compacting Crafting. This is automated Crafting for Recipes that contain only one type of Item, like 9 Iron Ingots into an Iron Block.

quests.title: Mechanical Mixer
quests.description:
The Mixer can do quite a few different Recipes but all will need a Basin below it! 

We can Mix, this combines Liquids and Items into new Items. Like Baking! 

Brewing can combine the right Liquids and Items to make Liquid Potions. These can then be scooped out into Empty Bottles to get Potions. You'll need Heat from a Blaze Burner to Brew though. 

Last is Automated Shapeless Crafting. To the normal Player this might be a confusing statement but trust me it ain't that bad. Shapeless Crafting is a Recipe that can be made with the ingrediants in any pattern. 

Like Dying Wool, the Dye and Wool can be anywhere in the Crafting Table. Or even Silent Gear parts and patterns!

quests.title: Spout
quests.description:
Spouts are used with systems to fill Items with Fluid. 

First, you'll need to fill the Spout by Piping Fluid into it! 

Then, if there is a Fluid Holding Item: Bucket or Bottle, then it will be filled with the Fluid in the Spout. 

It will automatically fill it, it doesn't need Rotational Power it uses Gravity!

quests.title: Blaze Cakes
quests.description:
Blaze Cakes can be used to Super-Heat Blaze Burners! A Heat that has never been seen before! 

But how do we Bake them? 

First, we'll need to make the Blaze Cake Base. To get it, process an Egg, Sugar, and Cinder Flour in a Mechanical Press and Basin. 

Cinder Flour is created by Crushing Netherrack through two Crushing Wheels. 

Then, once we have our Blaze Cake Base, we can fill it with Lava from a Spout to make our Blaze Cake!

quests.title: Copper Casings
quests.description:
Copper Casings will be needed for most Machines involved in Fluid Logistics. 

You wanna place Water? You'll need Copper Casings. You wanna pick up Water? You'll need Copper Casings. 

They are made just like Andesite Casings, apply a Copper Ingot to a Stripped Log.

quests.title: Millstone
quests.description:
Before we get into the many Items we can get from the Millstone, let's talk about how to use it! 

First, it will need some Rotational Power, don't worry it only needs a little. 

Then, you'll need to Drop the Item you want Milled, into the top of the Millstone. After it gets Milled, just Right Click the Millstone to take out your Items. 

Now, what Items can we get from the Millstone? We can get Dyes from pretty much every Flower, we can crush Stone into Gravel or other Stone like Blocks into similar Gravel Items. You can even get Wheat Flour from Wheat!

quests.title: Machines
quests.description:
With our Andesite Alloys we can now make Andesite Casing. 

Get some Wood, Strip it with an Axe, and then Right Click the Stripped Wood with the Andesite Alloy. 

That will give us our Andesite Casing! 

Andesite Casing will be needed for many, many, many Machines! And looks good for decoration.

quests.title: Deployer
quests.subtitle: Poke
quests.description:
Deployer is a very fun Machine for poking! 

By poking, I mostly mean Item Interactions that we can preform. Place an Item into the Deployer Hand, and then give it Rotational Power. It will then place the Item into the Block on a Depot or Belt below. 

This will mimick many actions that we can do, like adding Wax to Copper. 

You'll most likely use it for Andesite/Copper/Brass Casings and Polished Rose Quartz.

quests.title: Hose Pulley
quests.description:
The Hose Pulley is used to take and place full Source Blocks of Fluids, yes not just Water. 

First, set how far the Hose actually goes down or up with the Shaft at one side. Either with a Cog, Shaft, or Hand Crank which is easiest. 

Then, on the other side of the Hose Pulley we can put some Fluid Pipes. With Mechanical Pumps we can choose whether the Hose Pulley picks up Fluid Sources or place them down. 

The Hose Pulley only has an Inventory of 1.5 Buckets or 1500mB, but the Fluids can be Piped into other Inventories or Tanks! 

If the Water Source is infinite, the Hose Pulley won't take out Source Blocks, but will keep taking Fluid out. 

This will also work with Lava Source Blocks, but those aren't infinite. So you might want to check out The Nether for that as it is pretty much infinite there!

quests.title: Portable Fluid Interfaces
quests.description:
Portable Fluid Interfaces are used with Contraptions that are using Fluid Tanks. 

In order to access the Fluid Tanks you'll need two Portable Fluid Interfaces, one connected to the Contraption and one connected to Fluid Pipes. 

The Portable Fluid Interfaces will need a 1 or 2 Block gap between a meeting point in order for them to work. 

If we have all that, the Portable Fluid Interface connected to the Contraption will stop the Contraption to either take Fluids in or out from the second Portable Fluid Interface to add it to the Fluid Tanks within the Contraption.

quests.title: Brass Casing
quests.description:
Brass Casings are made the same way as Andesite and Copper Casings. Just apply the Item to Stripped Wood. 

But with Brass Casings giving us some of the most powerful Machines, it won't be as easy to get as Andesite or Copper. 

Thankfully this is ATMons so you can make Brass in many different ways! 

But the Create way would be to throw a Copper Ingot and Zinc Ingot into a Basin below a Mechanical Mixer, while the Basin is heated.

quests.title: Item Drain
quests.description:
Item Drains are what we can use to mass extract Fluid from Items! 

If a Bottle or Bucket is thrown on top of the Drain: either by Belts, Chutes, or Hands, the Fluid will be emptied into the Drain. 

The now empty Item will then be pushed off the Drain in the opposite direction, and the Fluid will be sitting in the Drain waiting to be Piped out.

quests.title: Super-Glue
quests.description:
Super Glue is used to attach Blocks together! In order to move them with Contraptions. 

To Glue Blocks together, Right Click two different Blocks and all between them will be Glued. If you want to Unglue them, just Left Click them with the Super-Glue. 

There is some requirements though, each Block must be connected to the other ones and not diagonally. 

You can also combine other Glued Blocks to different Glued Blocks. Everyone gets Glue! 

Plus this will effect other Blocks near the originally Glued one. Blocks adjacent to Glued Blocks will be moved with them. Same with Blocks that are attached to Glued Blocks, like Torches or Signs.

quests.title: Wrench
quests.description:
Trust me when I say, you'll need a Wrench! 

The Wrench is the perfect Swiss Army Knife like Tool for Create. You can rotate Blocks, break them, set their configs, what can't you do with it! 

To break Blocks just Shift Right Click any Create Block and it'll break them. 

To Rotate a Block just normal Right Click them with the Wrench. Unfortunately this doesn't give us free Rotational Power, but it is still useful for slip ups! 

It will also be useful for setting up Contraptions, but that is for later.

quests.title: Encased Fan
quests.subtitle: This blows!
quests.description:
The Encased Fan is one of the most underrated Machines in Create. 

You can place it down and it'll face you, or Shift Right Click to place it facing away from you. 

When given Rotational Power Clockwise, it will blow air away from it. When given Rotational Power Counter-Clockwise it will suck air toward it.
