These sucks and blows will also effect Items and Entities near them, and yes the faster it spins the more it sucks and blows! 

We also get extra Recipes we can make by putting a Block in front of the Fan. This will then effect the Items being blown on by the Fan. 

We can use Lava to Blast Items like a Furnace. Getting Ingots from Ores, Stone from Cobble, and Nuggets from Tools. 

If we put Fire in front of the Fan we can Smoke Items. Like Cooking them! 

Instead of Lava we can also place Water in front of it. This will wash whatever is in front of it like Concrete Powder into Concrete. 

And last, instead of Fire we can use Soul Fire to haunt Items! This will change Items either into Nether variants or entirely different Items.

quests.title: Blaze Burner
quests.description:
Blaze Burners are pretty easy to Craft, you'll just need some Iron Plates with a singular Block of Netherrack. 

Then you'll need to use a Mysterious Conversion to make it less Empty! That is just Right Clicking a Blaze with your Empty Blaze Burner. 

When we place him though, he seems a little small and... lukewarm... 

We'll need to feed him! No, not Steak, Blazes don't like Steaks. He'll need either Furnace Fuels like Wood or Coal, or his favorite: the Blaze Cakes! 

The Furnace Fuel will get them only a bit Heated, but the Blaze Cakes will make them Super-Heated! Yes, Super-Heated is hotter than Orange Hot. 

Some Recipes and Machines will need to be Heated, like Automated Brewing, Mixing, and the Steam Boiler will!

quests.title: Crushing Wheels
quests.description:
You'll need Mechanical Crafters to make the Crushing Wheels, they are too big for a 3x3 Crafting Table. You'll also need a ton of Andesite Alloys. 

BTW, you'll need 2 to actually use them. 
Once you have 2, place them next to each other. Then, feed them both Rotational Power and a lot of Stress Units. 

Make sure that the Crushing Wheels are spinning in opposite directions or else it won't Crush! The left one must be spinning Clockwise, and the right one must spin Counter-Clockwise. 

Once they are spinning (fast and in the right directions) you can have Items Dropped in between them and they will be Crushed. 

What Items? Crushed Ores from Ores, Items from Stones and Netherrack, Sand and Flint from Gravel, and even Netherwart from Netherwart Blocks!

quests.title: Mechanical Crafter
quests.description:
Mechanical Crafters can be used for Auto-Crafting and Recipes that are bigger than 3x3 Crafting Grid like the Crushing Wheel. 

Place the Mechanical Crafters in the order that is needed, then you'll need to set which direction the Items in the recipe go. 

The direction is known by the arrows on the edge of the Crafters. These can be changed by Right Clicking them with a Wrench! 

Then, just place Items into the Mechanical Crafters either with your Hands or automated with Funnels. 

After that, you can supply Rotational Power to any of the Mechanical Crafters (they share Cogs) to start up the Recipes. 

If it isn't working, check to make sure every Item is in, every arrow is facing the right way, and it has enough Rotational Power.

quests.title: Engineer's Goggles
quests.description:
Engineer's Goggles are perfect for you little know-it-alls. 

When worn it will tell just about everything the Block or Machine has to tell! 

Stressometers will tell how much Stress is given and how much it can take. Speedometers will tell how much Speed is within your system. 

Steam Boilers will tell how big, how much Water, and how much Heat they have. 

Other Machines, like Deployers or Mechanical Presses, will show how much Stress Units is being used up.

quests.title: Precision Mechanism
quests.description:
To make the Precision Mechanism we'll need 3 Deployers, 3 Depots/Belts, 1 Gold Plate, 5 Cogs, 5 Large Cogwheels, and 5 Iron Nuggets, as well as luck! 

Take your Gold Plate (which can be made from Pressing a Gold Ingot) and place it beneath each of the Deployers in order. 

The first will need a Cog, the second will need a Large Cog, and the third will need an Iron Nugget. 

Then, once it has been processed through all 3 of them, repeat it! And do it 5 times in a row. 

At the end, there is only an 80% chance it will actually make it. The other 20% will see all your work going POOF!

quests.title: Linear Chasis
quests.description:
Linear Chasis work like Puddy in real life, only connecting to each other. 

Linear Chasis, which are facing the same way, will automatically connect as if they were Glued. Other Linear Chasis or ones facing different ways, will not stick together. 

You can then use Glue on the Top and Bottom of the Linear Chasis to connect a line of Blocks from it. So all Blocks on top of those will be Glued to the Linear Chasis. Very helpful for saving Glue! 

With the Wrench you can set how many Blocks get Glued on the Top or Bottom of the Linear Chasis.

quests.title: Radial Chasis
quests.description:
Radial Chasis work similar to Linear Chasis in connecting to other Radial Chasis but everything else changes. 

You can connect other Radial Chasis on the top or bottom of other ones and they will automatically connect. 

Then, Glue the sides of the Radial Chasis to Glue every Block within a set Radius of the Chasis. BTW Radius means circle! 

You can change how far the circle goes with a Wrench to the Radial Chasis.

quests.title: Contraptions
quests.description:
Contraptions are very difficult to understand but pretty much it is the art of combining different Blocks and Machines into one moving systems. 

You'll need Machines to actually move the Contraption like Linear Chasis, you'll need the Machines you want to work like Drills, and you'll need Glue to hold it all together! 

Once it is all Glued it should move when Rotational Power is given to the moving Machine of the Contraption.

quests.title: Mechanical Arm
quests.subtitle: Why do it yourself when Robot can do it better?
quests.description:
Mechanical Arms must be configured before Placing them, like the Weighted Ejector. 

It has a 4 Block Range and can pick up from Belts and Depots. It can also deposit into Belts, Depots, and Funnels. 
While Holding the Mechanical Arm, Right Click Blocks to set as Input, then Click again to change it to Output. You can Left Click to deselect the Blocks. You can select as many are in range! 

Once it has Rotational Power, an Item in any Input Block, and space in any Output Block, it will start moving Items. It will go faster the more Speed is given to it. 

Like the Brass Tunnel, the Mechanical Arm has Distribution Modes. Thankfully a lot less! Round Robin: will go in order for Inputs and Outputs. Forced Round Robin: will wait until every Output has space or every Input has Items available. Prefer First Target: will go for the closest Block to it.

quests.title: 0CF69DBA9573A7B3
quests.description:
The Schematic Table will read and write structures to/from your schematics.
You can use it to copy buildings or to share them with others!

quests.title: 7D67058592EE5958
quests.description: The Cannon will build the structures from Schematics, taking materials from nearby chests and using gunpowder as fuel.

quests.title: Cart Assembler
quests.description:
The Cart Assembler can be placed on tracks. Anything you build on top of it will be picked up by a Minecart if the Assembler has a Redstone signal.
The Blocks must be Glued together and any Blocks requiring Rotational Power will automatically be working.
To "unmount" the Blocks from the Minecart, simply turn off the Redstone signal and let the Minecart ride through.

quests.title: Mechanical Bearing
quests.description:
Mechanical Bearings are the most simple forms of Contraption movement. 

When given Rotational Power from their bottom, they will rotate any Blocks above at the same Speed and Direction. 
Blocks will automatically be Glued to the Mechanical Bearing, but any other Blocks will need to be Glued to that Block to move as well! 

If you use a Mechanical Bearing within a Contraption itself, it will try and keep the Block attached still instead of Rotating.

quests.title: Mechanical Pistons
quests.description:
Mechanical Pistons act like normal Pistons with Moving Blocks, but after that the similarities end! 

They don't work off Redstone, instead they use Rotational Power. The Rotational Power will determine how fast and the direction the Piston moves. 

They also can have Slime Balls added to Stick to Blocks. And those Blocks can be Glued to have everything moving with the Piston. 

Best part is that we can add Piston Extension Poles to the back of the Piston to change how far the Piston can move! 

Each new Pole adds a new Block of distance. I'm not sure of the max you can add, maybe that is something you can find out yourself!

quests.title: Trains
quests.description:
Create 1.21 also now comes with Trains included with the base Mod. 

First, you'll need Sturdy Metal! 

Crush Obsidian to get Obsidian Dust. Then, use a Spout to place Lava into the Crushed Obsidian. 

After that, Press it twice with Mechanical Presses and you'll get Sturdy Metal. 

Sturdy Metal can then be applied to a Brass Casing to make Train Casings.

quests.title: Piston Extension
quests.subtitle: Why only move so far?
quests.description: Piston Extension Poles are how we can make and expand Mechanical Pistons. \n\nNot normal Pistons, sorry!

quests.title: Train Tracks
quests.description:
Train Tracks are... well what you'll use to move Trains! 

You'll need to Deploy 2 Iron Nuggets onto a Stone Slab, then Press it with a Metal Press to get 1. 

These will be the first Block you place in order to get Trains as it will be needed to place Train Stations. 

They have some limitations though, they can't go at steep angles to turn, or elevate. You'll need 4 Blocks of space to get up a Block with Train Tracks. To turn it is even worse! Let's just say, if you want a perfect circle with Train Tracks, it'll need a diameter of 18 Blocks.

quests.title: Train Stations
quests.description:
Train Stations are the most important Blocks for Trains! We need them for making Trains, breaking down Trains, and Scheduling them! 

To use them, you'll need to select a Train Track with them. Hold the Train Station in your Hand and Right Click a Train Track. 

I don't know the max distance a Train Station can be placed, it is atleast 10 Blocks! (I don't have that much room to test). 

Once placed you can Rename it with the Text Bar at the top. 

You can also Click "Create New Train", to start making your first Train. After you Clicked it, one of the Tracks will appear Blue, this is the Track you can place Boogeys on. 

Right Click that Track with a Train Casing to make a Boogey, AKA Train Wheels. Right Click the actual Wheels to change its design. Then you can...

quests.title: Gantry Carriage
quests.subtitle: Barbershop Poles
quests.description:
Do you like your Contraptions going only on a straight line? Then, the Gantry Carriage is perfect for you! 

Place down the Gantry Shafts down in the line you wish your Contraption to go and give it Rotational Power. 

Then, place down your Gantry Carriage on top of the Gantry and Shaft and it will move along with it. 

You can Glue Blocks and Machines on top of the Gantry Carriage to also move with it! 

The Gantry Shafts can be stopped by giving it a Redstone Signal. Do you also notice how they look like those poles Barbershops have?

quests.title: Mechanical Plough
quests.description:
The Mechanical Plough will plough through anything in its way! Well, that it can move atleast. 

Blocks with weak connections will immediately break when the Plough hits them. Blocks like Torches, Buttons, and Vines. 

When used above Dirt or Grass, it will make Farmland! Perfect for Mega-Farms! 

You can also use the Plough to move Mobs without killing them. Well the Plough won't kill them, whatever they hit might.

quests.title: Mechanical Drill
quests.description:
The Mechanical Drill can be used within a Contraption or without. The without will need Rotational Power but still does the same task. 

The Mechanical Drill will Mine any Block in front of it (that it can). 

It will Mine as fast as the Rotational Power will give. And if there is an Inventory connected to the Contraption, the Mined Block will be put into it, instead of on the floor. 

Yes, the Drill has a limit, it only has Diamond Tier for Mining. So, no Mining AllTheModium!

quests.title: Rope Pulley
quests.description:
Rope Pulley will move any Blocks that are attached to its Rope at the bottom of it. This will also move any Blocks Glued to that Block! 

When moved Clockwise by Rotational Power, it will lower the Rope until it hits another Block, or to where it is set. 

When given Counter-Clockwise Rotational Power it will move the Rope toward the Pulley until it hits the Pulley or it goes where it is set to go. 

Why do I keep saying "set to go"? Because there is destination settings with Movement Mode! 

These will decide where the Blocks end up stopping!

quests.title: Clockwork Bearing
quests.description:
Clockwork Bearings will move based on the Time of Day when given Rotational Power. 

The Block in front of the Clockwork Bearing will automatically Glue to it, but other Blocks can be Glued to that Block to join it! 

If you want more Hands to your Clock, add more Blocks in front of the first Block, but make sure these aren't Glued together. 

You can change which Hands are which by Holding on the Bearing to change whether the first Hand (closest Block) is the Hour or Minute Hand.

quests.title: Decorating your Train
quests.description:
Like the entirity of Building Tips in ATMons, I can't teach you how to design your Train... but I can give Tips! 

There is tons of different Building Blocks you can use, lots of the Create Casings look clean and Concretes can help give a more slick look. 

You can also use Doors and Trapdoors within the Train which can also be used when the Train is moving. 

What about making it look pretty? Well Stairs, Slabs, and Trapdoors help give Shape to it as well as the Flywheel or Cogs give nice round edges. 

Heck you can even put a Campfire on it to make a Steam Engine!

quests.title: Constructing Trains
quests.description:
Finally make a Train! 

We should have our Boogeys from the Train Station Quest, no the design of Boogey doesn't matter. 

Then, we can place Blocks onto the Boogey with Super-Glue. It doesn't matter what Blocks, pretty much any Block that can be moved can be Glued! 

This is when you try and make it look pretty! Check out Artwork-Builds Showoff in Discord to see a few of them. 

The most important Block for our Train is the Train Controls. You'll need one in order to actually move the Train. 

You can also add a Seat for Conductors (more on that later) or even yourself! 

Once it is all ready, just hit "Assemble Train" and either your Train will be made, or it will tell you what you did wrong!

quests.title: Controlling your Train
quests.description:
Okay we got our fully Assembled Train, now how do we use it? 

If you are Controlling it, you'll need to Right Click the Train Controls. 

Then, you can Hold W to move Forward or Hold S to go Backwards. No, Trains don't turn like Cars do, they just follow the Tracks. 

Going Forward you'll pick up a lot of Speed, you can see it in the Bar that replaces your Experience Bar. Backwards won't give as much Speed. 

If you are getting near a Train Station and not moving at the speed of light, you can Hold Space to stop the Train at the Station. This is helpful for disassembling them or even connecting more Boogeys.

quests.title: Mechanical Harvester
quests.description:
The Mechanical Harvester will automatically Farm Mature Crops, and Replant them. 

Obviously it has to be moved by a Contraption to work. 

It will also automatically place the collected Crops into Inventories connected to the Contraption. If not, it will drop the Crops on the ground.

quests.title: Mechanical Saw
quests.description:
To see Mechanical Saws on their own, check out the second Page! This one talks about them in Contraptions. 

When moved in a Contraption, the Mechanical Saw will break any Tree that it comes in contact with! It will need to hit the bottom of the Tree and break all of the Logs on the lowest part of the Tree. 

Once it breaks those Logs, the entire Tree will be cut down into Item form. 

If the Contraption has an Inventory, the Tree parts will be collected into it. If not, the Tree will remain in nature... on the ground.
{@pagebreak}
The Mechanical Saw can also do other tasks when not used in a Contraption. Instead they can be placed down and used with Rotational Power. 

The Saw can also cut down Trees that are near them. Yes, they'll still need to cut down the lowest Logs. 

But it can be used as a Stonecutter/Woodcutter as well! To use it like that it'll need to be placed faced up, like normal. 

Then, we can either feed it Blocks from our Hands (with the correct protection on) or through Belts. Logs will be Stripped and Stone Blocks will be Cut. 

If the Block has multiple Recipes through the Cutter, you can Filter which one you want by placing that Block in the Mechanical Saw's Filter.

quests.title: Train Observer
quests.description:
Train Observers work like a fancy Detection Rail. 

When a Train rolls over it the Track it is set to (which is chosen like the Train Station) it will give a Redstone Signal. 

You can also place Filters into the Observer to only get Redstone Signals when the Train has that Item or Fluid within.

quests.title: Train Signals
quests.description:
Train Signals are used with Conductors who aren't Players. 

They place just like Train Stations and Observers, but the way they are placed determines the Arrow placement. 

The Arrows will restrict where Conductors can pass their Trains, if the Arrow is facing the opposite way, the Train won't pass. 

You can add two Signals facing opposite directions to let Conductors pass wherever you want. 

With a bunch of Signals we can make Stop Lights for Track intersections. Place the Signals to where there are Arrows on both sides of the intersection. 

This will make it so Trains will stop if another Train is in the intersection. That prevents collisions which Derail Trains. Derailed Trains will need a Wrench to put them back on Track!

quests.title: Conductors
quests.description:
Yay, complicated subjects! This time it is Conductors and Train Schedules. 

First is getting our Conductor, these are any Lead-able Mobs or Blaze Burners. If we have a Seat next to the Train Controls we can Lead a Mob into the Seat where it will wait to become a Conductor. 

Blaze Burners work similar, just without the need for a seat, they bring their own. 

Then, we can hand our Mob or Blaze Burner, a filled out Schedule to give them that task plus a Conductor's Hat. 

Schedules are Items that can be "Coded" to order our Conductors to preform certain tasks. The tasks are either: go to Station, pickup or drop off Packages, change title, or change max speed. 

Once we add a task, we can edit its configs to change when it will start the next task! These can be either a certain Time waited, Time of Day, amount of stuff in Train, or even Redstone!

quests.title: Draconic Evolution
quests.description: Welcome to Draconic Evolution, a very fun and OP mod! To get started you'll need to mine Draconic Ore to get Draconic Dust. It spawns in all (Vanilla) Dimensions but the most is in the End!

quests.title: 366431661CC43A6E
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks.
As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by the AllTheMods Team, without explicit permission.
This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Where is he?
quests.subtitle: Finding Chaos Island
quests.description: To get into Draconic Evolution you'll need Chaos Shards. Chaos Shards are in Chaos Islands guarded by Chaos Guardians in the End. Go to the End at an X/Z coordinate that is a multiple of 10k. 10k, 10k / 10k, 20k / 20k, 20k etc.

quests.title: It's tough you'll need to prepare
quests.description: Now before you get to the Chaos Island I recommend preparing, he may look like the Ender Dragon but this one is much more difficult. You'll want Draconic Weapons or Tools that do a lot of damage as those will make it easier. He will also do a crap-ton of damage good Armor like Unobtainium or Meka-Suit will be recommeneded. (Also effects of Regeneration, Absorption, and Resistance will help you survive}. Don't worry you can always come back to fight another day if you aren't ready.

quests.title: Basic Energy Module
quests.description: Energy Modules are the most important Modules and are needed for using DE items. The amount in them determines how much OP an item can hold and take in, check out the Energy Infuser to learn more about charging. The later the Tier of Energy Module the more OP items can hold and use. This is important as when items are upgraded they use more OP per use.

quests.title: Wireless Energy Link
quests.description: Wireless Energy Links help to make it so Wireless Crystals can charge your items. The more modules, the more OP it can take it and at a better rate.

quests.title: Quantum Energy Tunnel
quests.description: The better the Energy Link or Tunnel obviously the more OP it can transfer, but also you might have noticed sonething missing with the Energy Link. It doesn't work between Dimensions! Thankfully the better ones can, just make sure the other side is chunkloaded.

quests.title: Basic Speed Module
quests.description: Speed Modules are fun, they work in just about everything and make them faster! Swords swing faster, Pickaxes mine faster, Axes chop faster, Bows shoot faster, and Chestplate makes you faster. The better the Speed Module the faster they go! (BTW good time to mention most stats stack up. 2 Basic Speed Modules increase Speed by 20%% then!)

quests.title: Locate and Destroy 14 Guardian Crystals
quests.description:
The first stage of the fight involves breaking the Crystals that hold the Chaos Guardians Shield. You can't hurt him until they are destroyed. Destroying these crystals is no easy task without a Draconic weapon. Chaos Guardian fire balls can weaken this shield allowing you to destroy it. (Yes, he will need too shoot at you/hitting the crystals). You'll notice particles being produced when it's vulnerable to damages and when hit will make a noise. The closer to destruction the deeper the noise and dimmer the Crystal will get. Once they are destroyed you can finally damage him!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/draconic/draconic_end_crystal.png width:150 height:100 align:1}

quests.title: Wyvern Projectile Damage Module
quests.description: These Modules are only for the DE Bows, unlike the previous ones. The Projectile Damage Module increases the damage of Arrows shot by the Bow. Some Modules happen to have negative effects with it, like these give a slight more Inaccuracy to Bows. All of these can stack!

quests.title: Basic (Draconium) Core
quests.description: Draconium Cores are a vital Ingrediant in many recipes in Draconic Evolution. Especially for Basic Tier items.

quests.title: Modules!
quests.description: Modules are very important to our DE items. So important they don't work without them! Most Modules are made from a Module Core or a previous Module. Hold an item and press Shift and C to open the Module Menu. There you'll see some slots and buttons! The Slots are where Modules will actually go and the Grid is what determines how many Modules can go. When a Module says 1x1 it'll only take 1 Slot, while one that says 2z2 will take uo 4 slots. The lowest button on the right will show what Modules can be applied to the Item you are holding. The rest just change the look of GUI.

quests.title: Wyvern Projectile Velocity Module
quests.description: Velocity is the speed of an item at a certain direction. Since our Arrow aren't from Guardians of the Galaxy it basically just means the Speed of an Arrow. With each upgrade it takes less time from the Arrow to go from your Bow to your Target. Comes at a cost of a little inaccuracy.

quests.title: Projectile Immunity Cancellation Module
quests.description: Thanks to Newton we know for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. Basically when an Arrow hits a mob the force of the Mob applies to the Arrow which will slow it down. Unless you have this Module. It doesn't act as if every mob was paper, it acts as if every mob isn't in the way. Arrows won't slow down after Piercing a target.

quests.title: Wyvern Projectile Penetration Module
quests.description: If you haven't played Minecraft since 1.13 this might confuse you, but you know Crossbows and Piercing. They have an enchantment which allows their Arrows to go through multiple targets and continuously dealing damage. This Module does exactly that!

quests.title: Kill the Chaos Guardian
quests.description:
Now the actual fight starts, he has two health bars both need to get taken to 0 to get the Chaos Shards. Don't get too close or he'll hit you with a barrage of Fireballs! {BTW in older versions the Chaos Guardian could even kill someone in Creative mode! Fortunately it can't anymore)
{image:atm:textures/questpics/draconic/draconic_guardian.png width:150 height:100 align:1}

quests.title: Fusion Crafting
quests.description: Fusion Crafting is how most (atleast the fun items) will be made. To get started you need a Fusion Crafting Core, place it down about a block above the ground. The Core is where recipes can be autoplaced in from JEI, where the middle item goes, and where the end item will be put. It will need the Injectors put a few blocks away from it looking toward the Core on two sides of it. Check next Quest to find more on those. The Injectors will also need Energy which will be explained more in the Crystal Binding Quest.

quests.title: Wyvern Projectile Accuracy Module
quests.description: With something so primitive as a Bow you can't expect perfect Accuracy. Well you can if you use these Modules. The Arrow is much more likely to hit its target and not go off course.

quests.title: Auto Fire Module
quests.description: Most Bows are Semi-Automatic. You have to draw the string, release, and put another Arrow in the bow, and repeat. Instead skip all that let the Bow automatically fire everytime it's fully drawn. Just hold Right Click and watch it go!

quests.title: Wyvern Projectile Gravity Compensation Module
quests.description: What is up with Physics and De and betraying them? Gravity pulls the Arrow down over the time it's shot. Gravity Compensation makes us worry less about that.

quests.title: Chaos Shard{s}
quests.description:
Once defeated he'll drop EXP, a Dragon Heart, and most importantly free the Chaos Shards. Look to where Lightning will strike then mine below it. There you will find the Chaos Shard. Mine it to be granted 5 Chaos Shards which can be crafted into smaller parts of it!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/draconic/draconic_shard.png width:150 height:100 align:1}

quests.title: Basic Energy Relay Crystal
quests.description: Basic (Energy Relay) Crystal is the start to moving Energy with Draconic Evolution!

quests.title: Basic Tier
quests.description: Fusion Crafting has Tiers which is determined by the Injectors. The Tiers go in ascending order: Draconium (I refer to it as Basic to help differentiate), Wyvern, Draconic, and Chaotic. The Injectors need to be placed on the Left and Right of the Fusion Crafting Core, a few blocks away from it. They can be placed in a cross shape at a max of 5 on each side of the Crafting Core. To give them Energy putting Relay IO Crystals connected to them will work, check out Crystak Binding to learn more.

quests.title: Draconium Chest
quests.description: 1 of the 2 Basic Tier Infusions but don't underestimate the Draconic Chest. It holds more space than a double chest, it can smelt and craft items, and best of all it can change colors! Easily my favorite Chest in any mod!

quests.title: Basic Area-Of-Effect Module
quests.description: Area of Effect is a phrase most Gamers would know. Basically it upgrades the working area of the Tool it's on. Pickaxes with 3x3 AOE will mine in a 3x3 area. Swords with 3x3 AOE will kill all mobs hit within that area. The better the upgrade the bigger the area. No, it's not stackable!

quests.title: Ender Collection Module
quests.description: Items gotten from the Tool this is on will go to your Ender Chest. The Minecraft one not modded one.

quests.title: Filterable Ender Collection Module
quests.description: Same deal but with options of filtering.

quests.title: Selective Incineration Module
quests.description: Filtering isn't enough?!?! You want the items destroyed?!?! You monster!

quests.title: Wyvern Energy Relay Crystal
quests.description: Wyvern (Energy Relay) Crystal. Does exact same as the Basic Crystal just more Energy and more Links.

quests.title: Awakened Draconium
quests.description: Awakened Draconium comes from Fusion Crafting the blocks. The blocks can be uncrafted into 9 Ingots. These are the second most important Ingots in Draconic Evolution and very necessary for the Wyvern and Draconic Tiers.

quests.title: Draconic Core
quests.description: I know it's Wyvern Tier so why is a Draconic item in here? In order to get to Draconic Tier you need Draconic Injectors. To get Draconic Injectors you'll need Draconic Cores. See why they are here now?

quests.title: Wyvern Capacitor
quests.description: The Capacitors act as the Batteries for Draconic Evolution. They need Energy Modules to actually hold Energy and remember, 'The more the merrier!'.

quests.title: Wyvern Tier
quests.description: In order to Tier up in Draconic Evolution Fusion Crafting, the needed Injectors for a recipe must be atleast the Tier or higher. Like if you want to make the Wyvern Axe you need atleast 6 Wyvern Injectors, with 3 on each sides. Don't worry the Crafting Core stays the same!

quests.title: Wyvern Bow
quests.description: Check out the Modules to learn more on how to use and upgrade the DE items! Works as a normal Bow does by shooting arrows. Each shot takes an amount of Energy from the Bow itself, so yes you'll need Energy Modules atleast.

quests.title: Wyvern Sword
quests.description: Check out the Modules to learn more on how to use and upgrade the DE items! Swing it and hit something with it. Come on, it's a sword I can't explain it anymore.

quests.title: Wyvern Pickaxe
quests.description: Check out the Modules to learn more on how to use and upgrade the DE items! Pickaxes work as a normal Tier 6 Pickaxe. They can mine every level of block, from Stone to Unobtainium. Items mined will automatically go to your Inventory.

quests.title: Wyvern Axe
quests.description: Check out the Modules to learn more on how to use and upgrade the DE items! The Wyvern Axe is similar to Minecraft Axes after Combat Updates. They can designed off a weapon to slay foes, or a tool to chop down trees.

quests.title: Wyvern Shovel
quests.description: Check out the Modules to learn more on how to use and upgrade the DE items! I know what you fellow Player really care about the Wyvern Shovel. You don't need to spend anymore sleepless nights because now you know, the DE Shovels can make pathways.

quests.title: Wyvern Hoe
quests.description: Check out the Modules to learn more on how to use and upgrade the DE items! It can make farmland or take your money. Oh wait Minecraft Hoe sorry I was thinking of a different one.

quests.title: Wyvern Chestplate
quests.description: Draconic Evolution doesn't see the need for covering the whole body in pathetic armor when you can use a single Chestplate with built in shields. Wait, they aren't built in you need Modules for them... sorry.

quests.title: Basic Damage Module
quests.description: Pretty simple premise, Axes and Swords can do more Damage. Yes, it stacks!

quests.title: Wyvern Tree Harvester
quests.description: All Trees attached to whats chopped down, comes with it.

quests.title: Draconic Energy Relay Crystal
quests.description: These can move more Energy and have more links. The highest level Energy Crystals go.

quests.title: Chaotic Core
quests.description: This will be needed for the last Tier, Chaotic Tier. Hopefully you followed the branch of quests that explain how to get Chaos Shards!

quests.title: Draconic Capacitor
quests.description: Even more Operation Potential!

quests.title: Draconic Tier
quests.description: This is what Draconic Cores are for.

quests.title: Draconic Bow
quests.description: Upgraded version of the Wyvern Bow.

quests.title: Draconic Sword
quests.description: Upgraded version of the Wyvern Sword.

quests.title: Draconic Pickaxe
quests.description: Upgraded version of the Wyvern Pickaxe.

quests.title: Draconic Axe
quests.description: Upgraded version of the Wyvern Axe.

quests.title: Draconic Shovel
quests.description: Upgraded version of the Wyvern Shovel.

quests.title: Draconic Hoe
quests.description: An upgraded hoe, so would just be a fine and nice lady?

quests.title: Draconic Staff
quests.description: You know the legendary Paxel? A combination of Picks, Axes, and Shovels? This is similar, being a combination of Swords, Pickaxes, and Shovels! It does everything the Draconic Tools do!

quests.title: Draconic Chestplate
quests.description: Upgraded version of the Wyvern Chestplate.

quests.title: Wyvern Undying Module
quests.description: Undying acts as the thing that makes it, the Recovery Totem! When your hearts are down to 0 instead of dying the Module will activate, giving you Absorption and Regeneration, saving your life. It has a Cooldown and needs to use OP to power up again. Try not to die during that time! Better upgrades means less cooldowns.

quests.title: Wyvern Shield Capacity Module
quests.description: Chestplates work similar to the Meka-Suit. Any damage that would be dealt to you is negated and instead taken off your Shield. Shield capacity is how much Shield you can hold, recharge rate is how fast it fills up, and OP will be used when recharging.

quests.title: Chaotic Capacitor
quests.description: Best Energy Battery DE will give.

quests.title: Chaotic Tier
quests.description: End of the road for Crafting Infusions, Chaotic Tier. Everything can be created once you are here. Not just the Tools but also everything you'll need for the Reactor.

quests.title: Chaotic Bow
quests.description: Best Bow from Draconic Evolution, also with more Module slots!

quests.title: Chaotic Sword
quests.description: It's like the Netherite Sword but much better and much cooler!

quests.title: Chaotic Pickaxe
quests.description: All Pickaxes mine at the same Mining Tier so the only need to upgrade is to be faster and get the Staffs.

quests.title: Chaotic Axe
quests.description: This is where it comes down to, do you like to hurt your enemies like a Truck but much slower? Or would you rather be a normal person who uses a Sword.

quests.title: Chaotic Shovel
quests.description: Also can make Pathways!

quests.title: Chaotic Hoe
quests.description: A Chaotic Hoe, I dated one of those while back.

quests.title: Chaotic Staff
quests.description: The best Sword plus the fastest Pickaxe plus the Shovel?!?! What more could you want!

quests.title: Chaotic Chestplate
quests.description: Hopefully this should protect you.

quests.title: Wyvern Large Shield Capacity Module
quests.description: Same as the previous quest, just more, a lot more.

quests.title: Wyvern Shield Recovery Module
quests.description: Want your Shield to come back and not just when you almost die? Then, you'll need Recovery Modules. The more Modules the faster it recovers.

quests.title: Night Vision Module
quests.description: Unless you're a little cheater who uses Night Vision Texture Packs, you might find the dark a little worry some. Thankfully Night Vision Module in a DE Chestplate helps get over the fear of not being able to see in the dark. Not the fear of what's in the dark though...

quests.title: Tier 2
quests.subtitle: Stores: 273,000,000 RF

quests.title: Wyvern Shield Control Module
quests.description: Shield Control changes the actual Shield you have and when it regenerates.

quests.title: Aqua Adapt Module
quests.description: Water is a little viscous, or atleast more dense than air. Because of that Mining Underwater is slower. You can use the Enchantment of Aqua Affinity, or use this Module. Your choice!

quests.title: Tier 8
quests.subtitle: Stores: Near Infinite

quests.title: Tier 1
quests.subtitle: Stores: 45,500,000 RF

quests.title: Tier 3
quests.subtitle: Stores: 1,640,000,000 RF

quests.title: Reactor Stabilizers
quests.description: Stabilizers are what form the Containment Field (Force Shield around the Reactor Core). Once Containment Shield is down to 0 while Reactor is turned on it will begin a Meltdown. All 4 Stabilizers need to be a few blocks away (5 or more) from the Core and need to be around same Axis as the Core to work. These are also where you will pipe out OP from the Reactor, just not too mcuh!

quests.title: Wyvern Flight Module
quests.description: With this on your Chestplate you can Glide! As if you were using an Elytra (But without cost of Armor). I don't like to call it flying, rather 'falling with style'.

quests.title: Draconic Flight Module
quests.description: Okay now this ones give both Gliding and actual Flying, Creative Flight to be more exact.

quests.title: Mining Stabilizer Module
quests.description: When 'falling' your Mining is slowed down. That includes when creative flying or even bouncing in water. Thankfully you can use Air Affinty Enchantment to negate that! Not a vanilla Enchantment but still helpful! Oh wait I was supposed to talk about the Module... same thing!

quests.title: Tier 7
quests.subtitle: Stores: 2,140,000,000,000 RF

quests.title: Power comes and goes through these
quests.description: Pylons are how you get OP in and out of the Energy Core. Place them atleast close to the Core, 2 of them 1 for input and 1 for output (you can use more). Then, place Glass over them and they will be assembled automatically targeting the closest Energy Core. Right Click the newly formed balls ontop of the Pylons to change whether they are Input or Output (you'll know from the arrows and design of them). Then, you can attach Crystals to them to move OP in and out!

quests.title: Energy Core Mulitblock
quests.subtitle: Draconic Power Storage
quests.description: The Energy Core is one, if not the, greatest Energy bank in all of Minecraft. And it all starts with the Core. This is the middle and heart of the Energy Core Multiblock (make sure it's a bit off the ground). When you place it down you can see it's GUI with the: Build Guide, Tier Down, Tier Up, and Assemble Core. The Tiers determine how big and powerful the Core is. The Build Guide shows you how to assemble this Tier of Core. If you have all the blocks necessary you can press Assemble Core and it will automatically make it!

quests.title: Energy Core Stabilizers
quests.description: Energy Core Stabilizers... stabilize? The Core. For the first 4 Tiers of Cores you need only 4 Stabilizers around it. You can access the GUi of the Core through the Stabilizers as well. If they are placed too close to the Core or in the wrong spots it will tell you it's incorrect.

quests.title: Tier 4
quests.subtitle: Stores: 9,880,000,000 RF

quests.title: What is Energy or as we call it, OP?
quests.description: Operational Potentional is the Energy source of Draconic Evolution. The main way (not the only way) of moving OP is with IO Relay Crystals. To actually get OP into items you'll need an Energy Transfer.

quests.title: Fuel for our Reactor
quests.description: The Reactor takes Awakened Draconium as Fuel, don't worry its efficient! Fuel Conversion determines when the Awakened Draconium will change to Chaos. It can take only 8 BLocks at a time and can only be Fueled or Refueled when the Reactor is shut off. SAS mode helps to make that easier! Also Fuel goes into the bottom right Slots.

quests.title: Basic Jump Module
quests.description: Legit just Jump Boost.

quests.title: Hill Step Module
quests.description: Basically it turns auto-jump on. Personally I like it but it's up to you to use it!

quests.title: Building the Reactor
quests.subtitle: UNLIMITED POWER

quests.title: Activating the Reactor
quests.subtitle: Now we pray and hope...

quests.title: Basic Auto Feed Module
quests.description: Auto-Feed will automatically feed you any food in your Inventory when hungry. It has a max Food Point storage though, each full bar is 2 Food Points. So the Basic one can only hold 8 Steaks worth.

quests.title: Tier 6
quests.subtitle: Stores: 356,000,000,000 RF

quests.title: Tier 5
quests.subtitle: Stores: 59,300,000,000 RF

quests.title: Advanced Stabilizers
quests.description: For Tier 5-8 you'll need Advanced Stabilizers. What's an Advanced Stabilizer? It's 9 Stabilizers all in a 3x1x3 Area. When made right it'll transform into a circle! Just do that same way you'd do 1 Stabilizer.

quests.title: Moving OP
quests.description: The IO Crystals work as blocks that can connect to each other and move power from one another. To link them Shift Right Click with a Crystal Binder to set one and then right click whichever Crystal you want connected. When you look at the Crystal it will say either Input from block or Output to block. Input is the one you want to take OP from and Output to where you want it to go.

quests.title: Adding OP to items
quests.description: Before you get here first you need an item that needs OP in it: Wyvern Bow, Chaotic Capacitor, Staff of Power whatever. Then you need an Energy Module in the item, that determines the OP storage in the item and that's what the item will use to power up. Once you have that, make and place the Energy Transfuser, get OP in it, then place your item into it! You'll know it's working when the OP in it lights up and moves.

quests.title: A jump start
quests.description: The Reactor can only hold 1 Billion OP and while that may seem like a far number, it won't be for long. When Energy Saturation reaches 100%% it will increase Heat a ton which can lead to Meltdown. It will need 500,000,000 OP to activate and a Flux Gate will help limit how much OP comes in and out. (BTW 1 RF = 1 OP) They need Redstone to activate and can be used for both adding OP and taking out OP. You'll need Energy out to not Meltdown, try putting it in an Energy Core!

quests.title: More Pylons {optional)
quests.description: Technically this is optional but recommended! You can use more Pylons to take in and out more OP!

quests.title: Reactor Energy Injector
quests.description: The Injector needs to be on a different side of all the Stabilizers and has to share the same Axis as the Core. This is where OP will need to pumped in from! To activate and make OP the Energy Saturation needs to be raised up a bit. Energy Saturation is the stored Energy and soon to be made Energy.

quests.title: Safe for Skyhook usage!
quests.description: Hemp Rope and Steel Cables are placed like normal Wires on Connectors and Relays but won't transfer Energy. \n\nInstead they are for Decor or using the Engineer's Skyhook!

quests.title: Specialized Projectiles
quests.description:
High Explosive Cartridges will shoot explosives at your Enemies, blowing up everything nearby like TNT would! 

Dragon's Breath Shells work like Buckshot, but now the Projectiles are on Fire!!!!! 

Phial Cartridges give Potion Effects based on the Potion used in its creation. 

Flare Shells work like Fireworks in a Crossbow. 

Homing Cartridges will aim after whatever Mob is closest to you... let's hope it's a dangerous Mob. 

Wolfpack Shells are like Buckshot Shells but now the Projectiles are Homing Cartridges!

quests.title: Railgun Ammo from IE
quests.description:
Aluminum Rod - 10 
Iron Rod - 16 
Steel Rod - 24 
Sawblade - 12 
Graphite Electrode - 30

quests.title: Common Projectiles
quests.description:
Casull Cartridges are the default Bullets. They deal 5 Hearts of Damage, and that's it! 

Armor Piercing Cartridges will have a higher chance of ignoring Armor Points. This is perfect against Mobs like the Bulwark. 

Buckshot Shells will instead of shooting 1 Projectile, it will shoot multiple Projectiles. Use in close range for best effects! 

Silver Cartridges will act like Casull Cartridges but with higher Damage to the Undead Mobs: Zombies and Skeletons!

quests.title: Railgun Ammo from Minecraft
quests.description:
End Rod does 10 Damage as well as hits Endermen. 
Enderpearls won't hit Mobs, rather they will teleport you much farther when shot. 
Trident acts like a normal Trident throw, dealing 8 Damage. 
Blaze Rods deal 10 Damage and set the Mobs on Fire!

quests.title: Engineer's Skyhook
quests.subtitle: Booker catch!
quests.description:
The Skyhook works both as a Tool and Weapon. 

You can just smack Mobs with it as if it were a Sword or you can use it for moving around you base! 

When you get close to a Wire (LV, MV, HV, Insulated, Hemp, Steel, Redstone) you can Hold Right Click to attach to them. Then, you can move around to slide down the Wires! 

If you want to use it on active Wires, you'll need some Upgrades! Upgrades like: High Torque Motor, Insulated Grip, and Heavy Impact Hooks. 

It can hold 2 Upgrades.

quests.title: Revolver
quests.subtitle: Do you feel lucky, Punk?
quests.description:
The most basic Gun we can find in ATMons, the Revolver! 

Shift Right Click to open the Revolver, then move some Ammo into the Slots. After that, just Right Click to shoot! 

You can apply 2 Upgrades to it. The Upgrades being: Bayonet, Speedloader, Extended Magazine, Amplifier Electron Tubes, and Precision Scope. 

The Revolver can only hold 2 Upgrades but the Speedloader is technically different.

quests.title: Railgun
quests.description:
Yes, it is just like the ones on giant Battleships! 

The Railgun is a special Gun. For 1. it uses special Ammo, not Cartridges like the Revolver uses 2. it uses Energy and needs to charge before shooting. 

The Ammo it uses is Items from your Inventory: Aluminum, Iron, and Steel Rods, Graphite Electrodes, Sawblades, Enderpearls, Tridents, Blaze Rods, and End Rods. 

It'll take whatever is in your Inventory, to change what it Shoots, Hold Shift and Scroll. 

Next, it needs Energy within it to Shoot, to charge it we can use any Item Charger, including the one added by Immersive Engineering! 

Once we have all this, Hold Right Click until the Railgun gets to Level 99, then release! 

The Railgun's Upgrades are: Precision Scope and Heatsinks. 

It can hold 2 Upgrades, well that makes sense it can't use anymore than that!

quests.title: Ammo for Buzzsaw
quests.description:
First, is the Sawblade. This is used for cutting down Trees. It will chop every Log and Leaf in the Tree above the Log that is cut. 

Second, is the Rockcutter Blade. This one can not break Trees, rather it is used as a Pickaxe with Silk Touch. It will break Stone and give you Stone instead of Cobble. 

Third is the Grinding Disk. It won't break Trees or Stone rather it'll break Metal Blocks! Good for Steel Scaffolding and scraping Oxidization off Copper!

quests.title: Drill Heads
quests.description:
The Mining Drill doesn't have many choices, we have an Iron Drill Head or a Steel Drill Head. 

Iron Drill Heads Mine in a 2x2 Area at the Tier of an Iron Pickaxe. It also does 6 Damage and has less Durability than the... 

Steel Drill Heads Mine in a 3x3 Area at the same Tier of a Diamond Pickaxe. These do 7 Damage and have more Durability!

quests.title: Buzzsaw
quests.description:
The Buzzsaw works similar to the Mining Drill, just for Trees! 

It requires Bio-Diesel as Fuel, which I won't explain how to get here either! 

And some sort of Sawblade. Which you can attach via the Top Slot in the Engineer's Workbench. 

Simply break Logs on a Tree and every Log, Leaf, and Birds Nest will come down with it! You can hold Shift to not break everything attached. 

The Buzzsaw also does 10 Damage! Dang, why even use a Sword? Oh yeah Saws have Durability and it needs Bio-Diesel. 

The Buzzsaw can hold 1 Blade or Disk and 2 Upgrades.

quests.title: Warning Signs Blueprints
quests.description: These Blueprints can be Crafted and boy are they cheap! \n\nWarning Signs are very simple decorations we can make with Metal Plates, Dyes, and this Blueprint.

quests.title: Specialized Projectiles Blueprints
quests.description:
These can only be Traded with Gunsmiths for. 

Specialized Projectiles are ones that do unique things! 

Homing, Explosive, and Flares are needed to be Crafted with these Blueprints.

quests.title: Mining Drill
quests.subtitle: Would you kindly?
quests.description:
The Mining Drill does as the name suggests, it Mines! 

It works like a Pickaxe, just needing Drill Heads and Bio-Diesel. Drill Heads determine its Mining Level and have Durability which means they'll need to be replaced. You can attach Drill Heads in the Engineer's Workbench, in the Top Slot. 

Bio-Diesel is a Liquid Fuel which has a very difficult recipe to make... that's for a different Quest though we're just looking for how to Fuel it! You can use the Drill on any Tank or Machine holding Bio-Diesel to fill it. 

The Mining Drill will mine in a 3x3 or 2x2 area, unless you are Shifting while breaking! 

You can also Hit Mobs with it to do the same amount of Damage as a Netherite Sword, this takes up Fuel as well as Durability though. 

The Mining Drill can hold 1 Drill Head and 3 Upgrades.

quests.title: 341BB1353A1E45EA
quests.description:
Gun Turrets will act as a Revolver with a Computer brain! 

They'll need Energy from below it, and a Redstone Signal to turn on. Or use an Engineer's Screwdriver on it to make it always on. 

It uses the same Ammo as a Revolver, that includes Speciality Projectiles! You can Input Bullets into it and Output the Casings, or just have them dropped out with the Expel Casing Button. 

Before it starts shooting, we'll need to set its targeting. First, it won't attack the person who placed it. We also have a Type Bar we can add any Player or Mob name to Add in. These will make it so it spares them! 

It is automatically set to Blacklist, if it is Blacklisted that means it'll Shoot what is listed. We then have Animals which means Passive Mobs. Players means just Players. Neutral stands for any Neutral Mobs and Villagers. Don't worry it was always target Hostile Mobs!

quests.title: 4295C863C9A81F28
quests.description:
The Telsa Coil is a very fun and Energy hungry home defence! 

First, power it with Energy from any of its Ports. Then, either give it a Redstone Signal to turn it on, or use a Engineer's Screwdriver to make it always on! 

Once it is on it will be actively using Energy and when a Mob comes near it, it will Stun them and hurt them! Hurting Mobs makes it take more Energy though. 

You can Shift Right Click with an Engineer's Screwdriver to set it to low power mode. It will take less Enery but also have less Range and deal less Damage!

quests.title: Chemical Thrower
quests.description: This one is supposed to shoot Chemicals like Fluids or Gases... but it won't do it for me. \n\nIt can hold 2 Upgrades atleast! Those work!

quests.title: Crafting Components Blueprints
quests.description:
These can be Crafted. 

The Crafting Component Blueprint is one of the most important Blueprints. 

It is used to help the Engineer's Workbench make small Mechanical Components for cheaper than Crafting Tables. 

It also can be used for Crafting unique Items like Light Bulbs and Circuits!

quests.title: Common Projectiles Blueprint
quests.description: Can be Traded with a Gunsmith or Crafted. \n\nGuns aren't much fun without Bullets, so let's Craft some! In order to Craft them though we'll need this Blueprint.

quests.title: Heavy Plated Shield
quests.description:
The Heavy Plated Shield is used just like a normal Shield, hold it in your Offhand and use it to defend yourself. 
The Heavy Plated Shield does have much more Durability and protects from more Damage. 

Oh yeah it also has Upgrades! These upgrades can be added on with the Engineer's Workbench. 

The Shield can hold 2 Upgrades.

quests.title: 251464B43353D4C6
quests.description:
Our beloved Garden Cloche! It is an automatic Farm, and with this Quest is simple to use! 

To start it will need Energy Input from either the Left, Right, or Top! 

It will then need Water from Back Port, (try using a Sink). 

Next, we'll need to Input our Seeds, Farmland, and optional Fertilizer by the Item Input at the Bottom! 

It will need the correct Farmland for the Seeds, you can check this all by Right Clicking the Cloche to see its GUI BTW! 

Once it has all that, it will quickly grow and harvest your Crops and Output them on the Front of the Dome. 

Last notes: it will keep the original Seed and Farmland and won't use them up, Dirt will be made into Farmland, and the Fertilizers are Sulfur, Slag, Nitrate, and Industrial Fertilizer.

quests.title: 34D09336FA3E272A
quests.description:
The Chemthrower Turret has the same exact targeting as the Gun Turret so check there for more info! 

Just like the Gun Turret, the Chemthrower Turret needs Energy from its ports. But it will also need Fluids Piped in to hold and shoot. Input Fluids with Pipes as you can't use Buckets to fill it, only Pipes. 

The Chemthrower Turret has a storage of 4,000mB or 4 Buckets. You can also press a Button to Ignite Fluids that are thrown. This will set Flammable Fluids, on fire!

quests.title: 79BEECD4E545793F
quests.description:
Razor Wire works like Cobwebs... just sharper! 

The Razor Wire will Damage and Slow anything that tries to go through it, including us! 

We can safely take it apart with our Engineer's Wirecutters. 

Or we can use LV Wires to make it do more Damage and a Stun Effect!

quests.title: Banner Patterns Blueprints
quests.description:
This Blueprint, like many others, can be Crafted. 

Immersive Engineering comes with it's own Banner Patterns! 

You'll need Blueprints to craft them though.

quests.title: Metal Press Molds Blueprints
quests.description:
Metal Press Mold Blueprints can be Crafted. 

Metal Press Multiblock will automate the creation of Metal Plates and Items. 

To press the Metals we'll need Molds. 

In order to make the Molds will need these Blueprints!

quests.title: 0AE6AD813928DE4F
quests.description:
The External Heater can be used with Furnaces, like the Vanilla ones, not Crude Blast Furnace! 

It takes in Energy from the Bottom and uses it for Heat. 

The Heat comes out of the other sides of it, to adjacent Blocks. 

It is technically used for the Improved Blast Furnace, by Crafting the Preheaters but I don't count that!

quests.title: 6B2BD6F939136F50
quests.description:
Turntable is pretty simple. The Top face with the Grey square will be the moving part. 

The other faces are the Redstone Ports, where you will give a Redstone Signal to activate it. 

When activated it will rotate whatever Block is attached to the Top. 

You might need to use your Engineer's Hammer on it to change how it rotates!

quests.title: Offense and Defense
quests.description:
To start a war we need to first declare it! 

Just kidding, we just go straight to shooting! No diplomatic crap around here! 

To start, shoot a Pillager with a Revolver. 

This will start the spawning of new and harder Pillagers!

quests.title: Accumulator Backpack
quests.description:
The Accumulator Backpack doesn't do much on your own, we'll need to give it an Accumulator in order to get some work out of it! Any Accumulator it's not judgy! 

Once you give it an Accumulator in an Engineer's Workbench, you can now charge it up. Once charged it will provide Energy to Items in your Hand and Armor you are wearing. 

You can wear it on your Back Slot in Curios, your Chestplate Slot, or combine it with a Chestplate in a Crafting Table. 

The Backpack can hold 1 Accumulator and 3 Upgrades.

quests.title: Engineer's Workbench
quests.description:
The Engineer's Workbench is a necessary Block needed for many Crafts and Upgrades. 

We can use it with Blueprints to Craft special Items that we can't Craft elsewhere. Put the Blueprints in the Left Slot, and our Crafting Items into the Right Slots.

Or we can throw our Tools into it, to add Upgrades to them, like the Revolver or Mining Drill! 

Also when you add Items and Blueprints you can see them on the Block itself, pretty cool!

quests.title: Engineer's Toolbox
quests.description:
The Engineer's Toolbox works as a segregated Shulker. 

It has sections: Food, which you can only put Food in. Tools, which can hold IE Tools or other Tools just not Buckets. Wiring, which can have Wires, Connectors, or Relays. And Anything, which doesn't discriminate. Try to be more like the Anything section! 

Some Items can't be held within it though, like Buckets full of Fluids or Accumulator Backpacks. 

You can Shift Right Click to place down the Toolbox to make it act like a Chest, then you can do the same to pick it up.

quests.title: Small Machines
quests.description: Some Machines in IE aren't Multiblocks, rather they are single-blocked! \n\nDon't think that, just because they are made with 1 Block that, they aren't important though!

quests.title: Fusilier
quests.description:
The Fusilier is the medium unit of the new Pillagers! 

They have 12 Hearts and no Armor. 

Their weapon of choice is a Railgun that is charged by their Accumulator Backpack they wear! 

On death they will drop Emeralds and Iron Rods.

quests.title: Commando
quests.description:
Commandos are the light troops. 

They have 12 Hearts and no Armor. 

Their weapon is a Revolver and a Shield they hold in their Offhand. 

On death they will drop Revolver parts with different stats, similar to Apotheosis stats!

quests.title: 7060290E107D92AB
quests.description:
A lot of things will need Energy, including some Items that can't be placed down, like the Railgun! So how do we charge them? 

The Charging Station is our man for that job! 

Simply Input Energy from either the Back or Bottom, and it will be ready to charge any Item put within it! 

This includes Railguns, Accumulators, and stuff from other Mods! It can't charge Blocks near it though...

quests.title: 257C80468B080B3C
quests.description:
The Electromagnet is IE's take on the Absorption Hopper. 

Well, kinda! It won't hold the Items rather they will be moved closest to the Top face of the Electromagnet. 

This can be used to get them onto Belts or hoppers! 

It will require Energy to be used though.

quests.title: Bulwark
quests.description:
The Bulwark are the heavy units of these militants. 

They have 12 Hearts with 18 Armor Points! 

Their weapon is the Chemthrower with a Heavy Plated Shield in the Offhand. 

If you somehow kill one you will get Emeralds and Masterwork Shader Bags!

quests.title: 231E0C0A9B0C0509
quests.description: This one can attach to your Accumulator Backpack. \n\nWhen the Backpack is worn, Items nearby will be sucked into your Inventory!

quests.title: 662DD269B027B6C8
quests.description: You can't wirelessly charge your Accumulator Backpack... but you can charge it wired! \n\nSimply attach your Charging Antenna to your Accumulator Backpack and walk up to any Wires transporting Energy and some of it will come to your Backpack.

quests.title: 4B42D962FE910CB3
quests.description: With this added on to your Revolver, your Bullets will give the Mobs you hit the Stunned Effect.

quests.title: 5E228ACA1B13AD04
quests.description: Now it shoots and smacks!

quests.title: 72CE46D28C9E7452
quests.description: The Precision Scope can be used on both the Railgun and the Revolver. \n\nWith the Revolver and Railgun you can press down Middle Click to use the Scope, then you can Scroll to adjust the magnification.

quests.title: 4E297778DCEEC963
quests.description: Advanced Heatsinks are our only Railgun exclusive Upgrades. \n\nIt will make it so the Railgun charges up much faster!

quests.title: 2F19529214CA9559
quests.subtitle: Blitz?
quests.description: It's like Thorns but doesn't Damage, just disorients Attackers. \n\nIt'll just stop Mobs for a little, it is much more effective (and aggravating) to Players!

quests.title: 35E399D88D2EDCB6
quests.subtitle: Clash?
quests.description: With this Upgrade everyone who attacks you will 1. be Stunned which will stop them for a second 2. hurt them and 3. destroy any Projectiles. \n\nI think it's worth the Upgrade!

quests.title: 13AF35A3108B02AF
quests.description: Gotta go fast!

quests.title: 5218DAE147AC9F44
quests.description:
The Blade Quiver allows you to hold more Blades or Blade like Items on the Buzzsaw. 

To switch between the Blades (or Blade like Items) Hold Shift and Scroll. 

This is useful for replacing broken Blades or even switching to Grinding Disks!

quests.title: 553ADA7040B652CD
quests.description:
The Mining Drill, Buzzsaw, and Chemical Thrower normally hold 1,000mB or 1 Bucket worth of Fluid. 

Normally doesn't mean always! With the Large Tank they can now hold 2,000mB or 2 Buckets worth. 

It doesn't sound like a lot but trust me it is.

quests.title: 6D42D0102D1CBC19
quests.description: The Additional Augers are Sharpness... just for the Drill though! \n\nOh yeah and you can have 3 at a time, for stacked power.

quests.title: Engineer's Crafting Table
quests.description:
Everybody loved the Crafting Stations from Tinker's Construct and apparently so did the IE Devs! 

The Engineer's Crafting Table will act like a normal Crafting Table, with an added 18 Slots of Storage in it, plus it keeps your Items in the Grid when you stop viewing it! 

What more could you want!

quests.title: 27FA2DB7839172BB
quests.description: The Backpack by default will only charge Items in your Hand and Armor you are wearing. But what if we wanted to charge more than that! \n\nThen we'll need the Induction Charger! With this attached, every Item in your Inventory that can take charge, will charge.

quests.title: 38C98FCB6A2D4226
quests.description: The Miniture Telsa Coil will act like the Thorns Enchantment. \n\nAnyone who hits you, while you are wearing the Backpack, will be Shocked. Dealing Damage and giving an Effect!

quests.title: 2224AA108FC006F3
quests.subtitle: Did I shoot 6 times? Or only 5?
quests.description: The Revolver Speedloader isn't actually an Upgrade, rather it is a seperate Item that's used to help. \n\nFill it with Cartridges like the Revolver, but now whenever you need to Reload the Revolver you can just Right Click with it to instantly reload!

quests.title: 407C2D00F22BD89D
quests.description: This Upgrade gives space for 6 more Bullets! Making the total up to 14.

quests.title: 340F93695FFF8D76
quests.description: With this the Chemical Thrower will be more of a Chemical Shooter. \n\nThe range will be increased but the spray width will be decreased. So it is more accurate!

quests.title: 598DE7CEDA864B50
quests.description:
Why just have 1 Tank, when we can use 3! 

You can now hold 3 different Fluids in your Chemical Thrower. Hold Shift and Scroll to switch between them. 

This can't be used with the Large Tank though...

quests.title: 0D2D1F99945BA209
quests.description: It is supposed to Equip your Heavy Plated Shield when you Double Tap S... emphasis on supposed to. \n\nReminder that IE is in Beta still! Mod Development takes a lot of time and effort, be respectful of such!

quests.title: 520904C106D7D93D
quests.subtitle: Press LMB to Skystrike
quests.description: These make the Skyhook act similar to a Mace, you'll do extra Damage hurting Mobs if you are falling while you hit them. \n\nIn Bioshock Infinite it's called a Skystrike!

quests.title: 4D8190E94851C546
quests.description: Live Wires (Wires transporting Energy are Live Wires) will hurt you when using a Skyhook on them. \n\nUnless you Insulate your Grip!

quests.title: 1A3F053E0F693002
quests.subtitle: Stop laughing at its name!
quests.description: The Advanced Lubrication System will act like Unbreaking to our Drill Heads and Buzzsaw Blades. \n\nThey will lose less Durability on use.

quests.title: 7744BEC5CD328262
quests.description: In order to mine Blocks underwater you'll need this Upgrade. \n\nIt also gives you Aqua Affinity! (That means being in Water doesn't slow down your Mining.)

quests.title: 33732EE8110A0911
quests.description: The IE Dev forgot the Mining Drill can also be used for Mining so last minute he put in Fortune III. \n\nThat being the Rock Softening Acid.

quests.title: Creosote Oil
quests.description:
Creosote Oil is a byproduct of the Coke Oven. 

Its main use will be for making Treated Wood, an essential Building Block of IE. 

You will also need it for a different Fluid later, we'll worry about it when we get there.

quests.title: Constantan Ingot
quests.description: Copper and Nickel will make Constantan! \nFinally this one is used quite a bit in IE, especially in Machines or Items using Heat and Metal, like Generators.

quests.title: Bronze Ingot
quests.description: This one is a combination of Copper and Tin! \n\nIt's used a ton in Modern Industrialization! But in IE... not that much...

quests.title: Treated Wood
quests.description:
By combining 8 Planks of any Wood, with a Bucket of Creosote Oil, we'll get Treated Wood! 

Treated Wood is used in almost every single Item IE gives us, plus most of the simple Machines. 

Most important is the Engineer's Workbenches! These will give us a ton of new Recipes.

quests.title: Coke Oven
Immersive Engineering
quests.description:
Industrial Foregoing has its sleak futuristic design, Mekanism has its dull modern design, and Immersive Engineering takes it much more retro! 

Everything is Brown, Grey, and Dark Grey! 

The Mod all starts with the Engineer's Hammer. These can be used to make Plates, Dust, or just building our Multiblocks! 

BTW, did I tell you we'll be making a lot of those in this Mod? Hope you like them!

quests.title: Alloy Kiln
Brass Ingot
quests.description: A mix of Copper and Zinc. \n\nNot really used for much in IE... You can make Signs with it I guess...

quests.title: Coke
quests.description:
By Smelting Coal in a Coke Oven we can get Coal Coke! Or as I will call it, just Coke! 

It pretty much is just Coal but has more uses in IE. 

You can combine it with Iron to get Steel, Crush it to get Coke Dust which will be needed for Graphite, or use as Fuel for a Blast Furnace.

quests.title: Electrum Ingot
quests.description: Electrum is an Alloy made from Gold and Silver. \n\nYou can guess by its name it is used a ton in everything electricity related. Wires, Connectors, Transformers, ETC!

quests.title: Invar Ingot
quests.description: Invar Ingots are made with Iron and Nickel. \n\nLike a lot of these Alloys they aren't useful in IE.

quests.title: Pipe Valve
quests.description:
Pipe Valves work at helping sort and stop Fluid flow! 

When used with Fluid Pipes, they will make it so the Fluid only goes in direction with the arrows on the Pipe Valve. 

You can also send it a Redstone Signal to which it will completely stop Fluid flow!

quests.title: Fluid Outlet
quests.description:
Now this is a fun one! 

Fluid Outlets can be set to Input Fluids, and then we can have it so it places those Fluids as Source Blocks next to the Output Sides! 

This means we can automate placing of Water, Lava, or pretty much any Fluids!

quests.title: Crude Blast Furnace
3A4A8EAA3022C7BA
quests.description:
Water Wheels are one of the Machines we can use for the Kinetic Dynamo. 

These are much more compact but also expensive, compared to the Windmill. 

To use them you'll need Water flowing over the Waterwheel. The more Water around it, the faster it'll go. Just make sure the Water isn't flowing in 2 different ways! 

Being more compact means we can place 3 Waterwheels on 1 Kinetic Dynamo to get even more Energy.

quests.title: Cold Items
quests.description:
Blue Ice- 200 K 
Packed Ice- 240 K 
Ice- 260 K 
Snow- 273 K 
Water- 300

quests.title: Fluid Pump
quests.description:
Fluid Pumps aren't just used for Bottlers, they can also be used to move Fluids... quicker! 

Using an Engineer's Hammer we can set Sides of the Fluid Pump to Inputs and Outputs. 

Then, we can Power it with Redstone or Energy, with Energy moving Fluids much faster than Redstone.

quests.title: Moving Fluids
quests.description:
Moving Fluids is an essential part of IE, just think of the Creosote Oil and Plant Oil! 

Fluid Pipes are our basic ways of moving Fluids, if you want them faster check out Fluid Pumps. 

Fluid Pipes, like Energy Connectors, are determined where to Input and Output from what they are connected to. Some Machines need Redstone Signals to Output to Fluid Pipes, like the Tank! 

We can use an Engineer's Hammer to change what the Pipes connect to, plus we can use Steel Scaffolding on them to cover them, or Dye to dye them!

quests.title: Fluid Router
quests.description: Fluid Routers sort and filter Fluids passing through. \n\nYou'll need to set configs within its UI to set the Filters and which Side. Once you do that, it will take all Fluids coming in and send them to where they are set to go!

quests.title: 6F3C82072672FD17
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks. 

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission. 

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Steel Ingot
quests.description:
I don't care how you got it, I just need you to get it! 

Immersive Engineering adds a whole lot more uses to Steel than just simple builds, almost everything will need Steel to make it! 

Tools, Mechanical Parts, and Building Blocks mainly. A lot are made with Steel Plates or Scaffolding. 

You'll need a lot of it but the Crude Blast Furnace and Alloy Kin can't be automated so we might need a...

quests.title: 7AE85F4FF4DDF4F2
quests.description:
The Windmill is another option we can use with the Kinetic Dynamo! 

These will automatically start moving and with its speed we get Energy, so more speed more Energy. 

How do we get speed? Well for one, it needs space in front of it to work. The less blocks in front of it, the quicker it goes! 

Another factor into speed is Windmill Sails. You can add 8 Windmill Sails in total by Right Clicking the middle Windmill Block with the Sails in hand.

quests.title: Energy from moving things!
quests.description:
The Kinetic Dynamo is a Generator which uses momentum to make Energy! 

To start making Energy you'll need either a Waterwheel or Windmill attached to the side with the giant gaping hole in it! 

The Kinetic Dynamo doesn't have an internal Energy storage, rather it provides Energy to connected Blocks like Connectors or Accumulators.

quests.title: Energy from Temperature
quests.description:
The Thermoelectric Generator, which I am going to just be calling a Thermo, is a unique Generator. 

On its own it won't do anything, what we'll need to do is place Blocks or Fluids of differenting Temperatures on different sides of the Thermo. 

The bigger the difference in Temperature the more Energy it creates!

quests.title: Warm Items
quests.description: Magma- 1300 K \nLava- 1300 K \nUranium- 2000 K

quests.title: Silo
Storing Items
quests.description:
Wooden Crates act as Barrels... but Minecraft ones, so Chests that can be opened from any side! 

They have 27 Slots but can be Shift Right Clicked with an Engineer's Hammer (multiple times) to shut them closed! This means they can be broken and preserve the Items inside. 

You can also edit the Text of the Crate to change its name as if it were in an Anvil. 

The Reinforced Crate works exactly the same as the normal one, just can't be blown up!

quests.title: Immersive Engineering Logistics
quests.description: Like every Machine Mod, Immersive Engineering needs a way of moving Items, Fluids, and more! \n\nMost Machines will have default set Outputs and Inputs but these can be configured, like with the Engineer's Screwdriver! You also might need to use an Engineer's Hammer but that's different.

quests.title: Storing Fluids
quests.description:
Barrels are simple ways of holding Fluids. 

There's Wooden Barrels and Metal Barrels. Wooden ones can only hold cold and room temperature Fluids, not warm Fluids or Gases. While Metal Barrels can hold all types of Fluids and Gases. 

Both Barrels can hold 12 Buckets of Fluid. They automatically Input from the Top side and Output to the Bottom but this can be changed.

quests.title: Tank
56E30438AE512475
quests.description:
Let's get these flames burning! 

The Preheater is a very simple addition to the Improved Blast Furnace. 

Simply place them on the Left and Right of the Improved Blast Furnace. Then, connect power to the top of it and it will start speeding up the Improved Blast Furnace.

quests.title: Improved Blast Furnace
38F01BAEC74D5D68
quests.description: It's the same as the other Preheater I just wanted it to be symmetrical :D.

quests.title: Immersive Engineering Power!
quests.description:
Lots of things need Energy, especially in IE. To get started we'll need some Engineer's Wire Cutters! 

You can use those to snip some Plates into Wires which can then be put into Coils, ready for use. 

They are also used for taking Wires off Connectors.

quests.title: Diesel Generator
Lightning Coil
Light Engineering Block
quests.description:
The Light Engineering Block is pretty easy recipe. 

You'll need 1 Copper Ingot, which I shouldn't have to explain it's literally a Vanilla feature. 

4 Ironsheetmetal, which are just 4 Iron Plates combined with each other! 

You'll also need 4 Iron Mechanical Components, which are either 4 Iron Plates and a Copper Ingot in a Crafting Table, or 2 Iron Plates and a Copper Ingot in the Engineer's Workbench.

quests.title: Heavy Engineering Block
quests.description:
Think of the Light Engineering Block, now just make all its components much harder to make! 

1st we need Electrum, which is an Alloy of Gold and Silver made in the Alloy Kiln. 

2nd we need 4 Steel Sheetmetal, which like the Iron Sheetmetal, needs 4 Plates combined together. 

3rd is our Steel Mechanical Components which are either one Copper Ingot and 4 Steel Plates in a Crafting Table. or made cheaper in the Engineer's Workbench.

quests.title: Generator Block
quests.description:
You can check previous Quests to learn how to build some of these: Iron Mechanical Components in the Light Engineering Blocks and Steel Sheetmetal in Heavy Engineering Blocks. 
The Electrum Coils will be a bit different though... 

Electrum Coils need an Iron Ingot and 8 MV Wire Coils. To get MV Wire Coils we'll need to cut up some Electrum with Engineer's Wire Cutters.

quests.title: Radiator Block
quests.description: For Radiators we'll need the usual Steel Sheetmetal, a Water Bucket which is a new one! And Constantan Plates. \n\nConstantan is an Alloy made by combining Copper and Nickel in an Alloy Kiln.

quests.title: Redstone Engineering Block
quests.description: Easily the simplest of these Blocks to make. \n\nIron and Redstone you'll just get from Vanilla gameplay, the only "difficult" Item is the Iron Sheetmetal.

quests.title: Wire Coils
quests.description:
Most Machines in IE will need Energy to work, and Wires are how we move it! 

Wires are attached by Right Clicking one part with the Wire Coil, then Right Clicking the second part with the same Coil. Their way can't be obstructed or else it won't connect. 

To pick up Wires we can break what they are connected to, or use our trusty Wire Cutters! 

The different Tiers of Wires effect how much they transfer, HV moving the most.

quests.title: Chutes
quests.subtitle: No Ladders?
quests.description:
Chutes can take Items (and some Entities) and drop them without worry of despawning! 

They also drop Items pretty darn quickly. 

You can use the Engineer's Hammer to make a Chute curve to toss the Items onto a Belt!

quests.title: Moving Items
quests.subtitle: and some Entities!
quests.description:
Conveyor Belts are how we can move Items (and some Entities). 

When Items are dropped onto Belts they will hold them and move them. These can then be moved into different Inventories, if we want to extract from Inventories we'll need a special type of Belt! 

The way you place your Belt will determine where it moves, this can also be changed with the Engineer's Hammer! 
They need to be placed on Blocks but funny enough don't need Blocks below to keep standing and working!

quests.title: Item Router
quests.description: Item Router will Input Items and Output them to certain locations based on the Filtering set in its UI! \n\nThese can be set to Belts, Crates, or other Inventories.

quests.title: Connectors
quests.description:
Connectors are what... well connect! They connect Wires from Machines, to Accumulators, to Generators, from pretty much everything! 

Whether a Connector Inputs or Outputs is determined by the configuration of what it is attached to! 

They also have their own internal Energy storage, the Tier of Voltage determines how much.

quests.title: Relays
quests.description:
Relays don't connect Wires to Machines, rather they connect Wires to more Wires! 

Relays work by combining a bunch of Wires into one spot, so it will take all the Input Energy and send them to Connectors to all the Outputs connected. 

This is helpful for when you have either one Power Generator that you want to charge multiple Machines!

quests.title: Tiered Voltage
quests.description:
Everything related to Wires and power in IE can be Tiered. Low Voltage (LV), Medium Voltage (MV), and High Voltage (HV). 

The higher the Voltage the more Energy can be moved and used. Some Machines will need higher Voltage to be used. 

In order to transfer different Voltages you'll need Transformers, check out their Quest!

quests.title: Types of Belts
quests.description:
Belts come in all different shapes and sizes and uses! 

First, all Conveyor Belts can be Crafted with Steel Scaffolding to give them covers. Covered Belts will make it so Items can't be picked up from Players while on it. 

The first and simplest version of the Belt is the Vertical Belt. It simply takes Items upwards! 

Splitting Belts... split the directions the Items going in, go. It will switch for every Item: 1 goes Left, 1 goes Right, 1 goes Left, 1 goes Right. 

Dropping Belts will drop the Items either into an Inventory below it, or if there is open space it will just drop the Items. These can be configured with Redstone to not drop Items. 

The last is the Extracting Belt, this one will automatically take Items out from Inventories and deploy it on its Belt. These can also be used with some Machines!

quests.title: Item Batcher
quests.description:
Item Batcher works kinda like the line for a Roller Coaster. 

The Roller Coaster won't leave until all seats are filled! The same way the Batcher won't Output Items until the set Filter and Amount has been matched. 

Perfect for stuff like Mekanism Ore Processing which needs certain amounts of Items Inputed or else it will bottleneck.

quests.title: Accumulators
quests.description:
Accumulators are IE's version of batteries. 

They hold Energy with LV holding 100kFE, MV holds 1MFE, and HV holds 4MFE!
