The Fluid Port is used to insert vapors like Steam, or extract exhaust, like water. Because of this, you'll need two for your Turbine.

The Power Tap extracts power, and is required to complete the multiblock.

quests.title: Turbine Construction
quests.description: Just like the Reactor, the frame must be built out of Casings, but the walls can be Turbine Glass instead!

quests.title: Welcome to Extreme Reactors!
quests.subtitle: It's not edible... trust me
quests.description:
Based off of the original mod Big Reactors, Extreme Reactors allows you to build customizable multiblock Reactors!

The main element is of course, Uranium. You'll need this and a lot of coal and iron to get building.

If you're ever lost along the way, refer to The Extreme Book for help!

quests.title: Graphite for Casings
quests.subtitle: Hardened Carbon
quests.description: Before we can start building our reactor, we'll need to smelt some Coal or Charcoal to create Graphite Ingots.\n\nGraphite, coupled with Iron, is one of the main materials when making a Reactor.

quests.title: Reactor Building Components
quests.description:
To build a reactor, you'll need to start by making Reactor Casings.

These make up the frame and walls of your reactor, although the walls can be replaced by Reactor Glass if you'd like to see inside of your reactor.

For future reference, when a part says "Basic", this means that it can only be used with other basic parts. The Basic parts can also only be used to build smaller reactors, as it has a certain size limit. Keep this in mind!

quests.title: The Turbine Interface
quests.description:
Right-clicking on a Turbine Controller when it is fully built will show you the Turbine Interface.

Here, you can see all of the stats for the Turbine. Hovering over each will tell you more info about each one.

On the bottom left, you'll have 2 arrows to control the Flow Rate. This controls how much heated vapor is pumped into the Turbine. To know how much you should set this to, check your reactor's Vapor Production Rate as a starting point.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/extremereactors/turbineui.png width:200 height:150 align:1}

quests.title: Reactor Control Rods
quests.description:
Every reactor needs Reactor Control Rods and Fuel Rods. These control how fuel is inserted into the reactor.

The Control Rods are placed on the top face of the reactor. You can also have more than one per reactor, but you must have at least 1. Typically, the more you have, the more fuel the reactor can use and burn. That can mean more overall power, but at the cost of higher burn rates, depending on the setup of your reactor.

For every Control Rod, you'll need enough Fuel Rods to extend to the base of the reactor. For example, if your reactor is 5 blocks tall, you'll need 3 Fuel Rods extending from each Control Rod.

If you right-click on a Control Rod, you can control how much fuel is burned in the reactor by inserting or retracting the fuel rods. The further that you extend the rods, the less fuel that will be burned.

quests.title: Interacting with the Reactor
quests.description:
To extract power or items from your reactor, or even input fuel, you'll need these required blocks.

The Power Tap provides a way for you to "tap" into the power that a passive reactor makes. You can attach pipes and cables to extract the power from it.

The Access Ports are required for every reactor, and allows you to both input fuel from the reactor, or extract waste. It's usually a good idea to have 2 per reactor, one for each job.

quests.title: Building An Actively Cooled Reactor
quests.subtitle: To Make Steam!!
quests.description:
Reactors can also be used to heat up coolants like water to create vapor, like Steam.

To do this, you'll need to build a reinforced reactor. This is built in the same way that you built your 3x3x3 reactor, but all of the parts will need to be Reinforced Reactor Parts instead. I'd also suggest on it being bigger than a 3x3x3.

To input a coolant, you'll need a Forge Fluid Port. This will port in any fluids like Water into the reactor. This will also be used to export the vapor created in the reactor.

If you want, you can create a Mekanism Fluid Port to convert the fluid Steam into the Mekanism gas Steam instead.

quests.title: Making Turbines
quests.description:
With Cyanite, we can create the heart of the Turbine, the Turbine Controller.

Turbines are multi-block structures, just like Reactors! They input vapors like Steam made by Actively Cooled Reactors to create TONS of power! We'll need a few other pieces to be able to build our first one.

Note: Basic Turbine parts can only be used to build a max size Turbine of 5x5x10. To build a bigger Turbine, you must use Reinforced Turbine Parts.

quests.title: 75AD0CEBC1335915
quests.subtitle: The Heart of the Reactor
quests.description:
The Reactor Controller is the heart of the reactor. When a reactor is formed, you can right-click the terminal to open up the reactor interface.

Depending on if it is a Passively Cooled or an Actively Cooled reactor, the interface will change. Passively Cooled reactors are used to produce power directly by burning fuel. Actively Cooled Reactors use the heat created to vaporize the coolant, which is then sent into a Turbine to create power.

In the interface of a passive reactor, you can see and toggle the status and waste ejection. You'll also see the temps, how much FE/t the reactor is producing, and how much fuel the reactor is burning per tick.

quests.title: Expanding Our Reactors
quests.description:
Reactors are multi-block structures, meaning you can create your own custom size!

If you're using Basic Reactor Parts, the largest size reactor you can build is 5x5x5.

The Biggest Reactor that you can make using Reinforced Reactor Parts is 32x32x48. There are a lot of variables that contribute to the overall output of a reactor, so make sure to experiment!

Some overall tips:

The taller the reactor, the more fuel it can hold and burn because there are more fuel rods, meaning more overall power. This also means a higher burn rate.

The wider the reactor, the more efficient it is, as long as you don't add more fuel rods to the design. This means less consumption overall.

quests.title: Our First Reactor
quests.subtitle: Learning the Basics

quests.title: Dealing with Waste
quests.subtitle: Waste Not Want Not or something....
quests.description: When the reactor burns up fuel, it creates waste or a Reactant that you'll also want to extract. That is what the other Solid Access Port is for! Make sure to set it to output, then pipe it into some type of storage.

quests.title: Reprocessing our Waste
quests.description:
Now that we have some Cyanite from our baby reactor, we'll want a way to reprocess that waste into something useful.
To do this, we'll need to build another multiblock: the Reprocessor.
This takes a lot of Cyanite, so start stocking up! You might want to upgrade to a bigger reactor as well.

quests.title: Fueling our Passive Reactor
The Fluidizer
quests.description: Now that we are collecting some waste from our reactor, part of the progression requires you to "Fluidize" some of the ingots you get. You know what that means?\n\nWe need to make a Fluidizer! The main component is the Fluidizer Controller. Once built, you can right-click on this to open up the interface. Here, you can turn it on or off, see what's inside, and the current power level.

quests.title: Importing Waste
quests.description:
When building the Reprocessor, you will need at least one Collector and Waste Injector.

The Reprocessor Collector must be placed in the center of the bottom face of the structure.

The Waste Injector must go in the center of the top face, which is where you'll pipe in or insert waste like Cyanite Ingots.

quests.title: 2AF31F1769085641
quests.description:
The Reprocessor is a 3x3x7 multiblock structure that has specific rules to complete the construction of the multiblock.
The heart of this multiblock is the Controller, and can be placed on any vertical face as long as it isn't on the frame.

quests.title: 3C3FE45CEF5E242B
quests.description:
While the other Reprocessor Parts have a mandatory spot when building, these three parts can be placed on any vertical face as long as they aren't on the frame!

The Power Port is used to give power to the multiblock machine to process waste.

The Fluid Injector Port is used to inject the liquid needed, which will depend on the type of waste injected. For Cyanite, that means water!

The Output Port is used to output the reprocessed material. You can right click it to grab the material out by hand, or pipe it out for automation.

quests.title: Building The Frame
Fluidizer Construction
quests.description: The Fluidizer is a customizable multiblock that has a minimum size of 3x3x3. Just like the other multiblocks, the frame will need to be made out of Casings, while the faces can be made out of Glass.

quests.title: Required Ports
quests.description: If you want to get your hands on the product the Fluidizer makes, you'll need an Output Port on one of the faces.\n\nThe Fluidizer will need power to operate, so a Power Port is required to complete the structure.

quests.title: Operational Modes
quests.description:
The Fluidizer can operate in one of 3 modes: Solid to Fluid, Combining 2 Solids into a Fluid, or combining 2 Fluids into a new Fluid. This all depends on the type of Injectors you use for the multiblock.

For example, if you want to convert Blutonium into a fluid, you can use 1 Solid Injector.

If you want to combine two solids together into something new, you'll build the multiblock with 2 Solid Injectors.

If you want to combine two fluids, you'll use 2 Fluid Injectors.

This might seem confusing, but is important for progression. For example, you'll want to convert Magentite into a fluid in the Fluidizer first, then send it to a Reprocessor with Ludicrite to create Ridiculite.

quests.title: Blutonium
quests.description:
Once you've built a fully functional Reprocessor, you can pump in power, water, and Cyanite to create Blutonium.
This can be used as a fuel for your reactor, and creates its own waste called Magentite.

quests.title: Rossinite
quests.description:
By using the Fluidizer, we can combine Blutonium with Yellorium to make Verderium.

When used as fuel in a reactor, Verderium produces Rossinite as a reactant. We need this!

To use Verderium as a fuel, you'll need to make Fuel Injection Ports for your reactor.

Note: You might need to empty out the fuel currently in your reactor, or make a new reactor for this purpose.

quests.title: Inanite
quests.description: Combining Ridiculite Ingots with Rossinite in a Reprocessor will create Inanite Ingots.\n\nWe can now use these to make a block of Inanite.

quests.title: Ludicrite & Ridiculite
quests.description: Using the Reprocessor, we can combine everything we've made so far to make a few new ingots.\n\nNote: You might need a Fluidizer to complete this step!

quests.title: Insanite
quests.description: Now that you have Rossinite, you can mix it with Benitoite to create Insanite ingots.\n\nBenitoite Ore can be found in the Nether.

quests.title: Insanite Block
quests.description: One of the hardest materials to get in the mod!\n\nThis is also used to create the ATM Star!

quests.title: AllRightsReserved
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks. 

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission. 

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: The Furnace
quests.subtitle: It all starts here
quests.description: Generator's Galore and Iron Furnaces are two different but also similar mods. Both start with the legendary Furnace!

quests.title: Augments
quests.description:
Augments are Upgrades to Iron Furnace Furnaces!
In the Top Right of the Furnace GUI will be the button to look at the Augment Section. There will be a Red, Green, and Blue spot, each can hold 1 of their colored Augments.

quests.title: Copper Furnace
quests.description:
Copper is one if not the most common Ore you can find, so why not use a bunch of spare Copper to upgrade your furnace!
Normal Furnaces take 200 Ticks to smelt 1 Item, (20 Ticks = 1 Second) while Copper Furnaces take 180 Ticks.
They can be crafted into either Silver or Iron Furnaces.

quests.title: Iron Furnace
quests.description: Iron Furnaces (Don't be confused with each of the titles with Iron Furnaces being the mod name and an Item name) work even faster than Normal and Copper Furnaces. They take 160 Ticks to work, or 8 seconds.\n\nThese can be crafted from either a normal Furnace or Copper Furnace! And they can be made into either a Silver Furnace or Gold Furnace.

quests.title: Silver Furnace
quests.description: Following the same pattern, these ones smelt at 140 Ticks or 7 Seconds.\n\nThey can be crafted with Copper or Iron Furnaces and can be used to craft a Gold Furnace.

quests.title: Copper Generator
quests.description: Generator's Galore adds very simple Generators. The most basic ones act like Furnaces with Augment: Generator. They'll take Fuel and make it into Energy! \n \nYes you have to start with Copper Generator.

quests.title: 8x What a deal!
quests.description: Crafting 8 of the same Generators together with an Echo Shard combines them into 1 massive Generator! Works the same as 8 regular generators but only takes up the space of 1.

quests.title: Augment: Blasting
quests.description: Augment: Blasting transforms your Iron Furnace to an Iron Blast Furnace! It will now only smelt Ores but at twice the speed! Yes this stacks with the effects of other Augments and different Tiers of Furnace.

quests.title: Augment: Smoking
quests.description: Augment: Smoking transforms your Iron Furnace into an Iron Smoker. Now it will only smoke Food items but twice as fast! Like Augment: Blasting this one also stacks with other upgrades!

quests.title: &zRainbow Core
quests.description: For this you need 2 Netherite Furnaces and 7 pieces of glass which are each the color of the Rainbow. Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indig- Purple, and Vi-Magenta. Yep! The whole Roy G. Bpm!

quests.title: &zRainbow Plating
quests.description: You'll need every Furnace before Netherite for these. Yes all, even the Copper! Even the Silver! Even the Crystal!

quests.title: &zRainbow Coal
quests.description: You blew up the &zRainbow Furnace?!?! Just lit TNT right next to it? Are you mad? That took so many Furnaces and resources and you just blew it up!!! Did you atleast get something good from it? &zRainbow Coal? Coal that lasts a very long time? Actually that's pretty worth it.

quests.title: Iron Generator
quests.description: Each upgrade upgrades everything, from the amount it makes to how much it can hold to what it can transfer to other blocks! \n \nYou'll need a Copper Generator to make an Iron Generator, sorry Copper haters.

quests.title: 64x Generators
quests.description:
Crafting 8 of the same 8x Generators together with a Conduit combines them into 1 massive Generator! Works the same as 64 regular generators but only takes up the space of 1.
A 64x Magmatic Generator is needed to craft the ATM Star.

quests.title: Augment: Factory
quests.description: Augment: Factory makes your Furnace more like the Smelting Factory from Mekanism. Instead of using Fuel it will now use Energy! Pipe in some Energy and it will start Smelting.

quests.title: Augment: Generator
quests.description:
Augment: Generator is the opposite of the Augment: Factory, instead of using Energy to Smelt, it Smelts for Energy. You will no longer smelt items in it, every Fuel used will be made into Energy!
(I wonder if it's better to connect a Generator and Factory Furnaces instead of just using Fuel in one)

quests.title: Configurations
quests.description: Like most Modded machines, Iron Furnaces has Configurations. Configs can be found by clicking the Top Left. There will be the Inputs, Outputs, and Redstone activation. The Redstone activation changes when the Furnace will smelt. The top buttons determine if it auto Inputs or Outputs, which means it will automatically move to and from connected Inventories. The boxes are each side of the Furnace and determine whether it Inputs, Outputs, does both, Inputs Fuel, or does nothing. This matters for Items being Piped in or out. The Furnace Settings Linker will copy all of these settings to other Furnaces!

quests.title: Netherite Furnace
quests.description:
The best Vanilla gets! Netherite! Don't worry you won't need Smithing Template for it, just a lotta Netherite. 
 
It smelts an item every 5 Ticks which means 4 Items Smelted every Second. Yes it's no longer S.P.S. (Seconds per Smelt) it's now S.P.S. (Smelts per Seconds). 
 
Crafted from Obsidian Furnace... wait this isn't the final Furnace?

quests.title: Obsidian Furnace
quests.description:
It may be Obsidian but don't worry you don't need a Diamond Pickaxe to pick it up, just to craft it.
It works every 20 Ticks or every Second. Yeah not Seconds just Second.
It can be crafted with a Crystal Furnace or Emerald Furnace, and can be crafted into a Netherite Furnace!

quests.title: &zRainbow Generator
quests.description: The &zRainbow Generator is a boost to the &zRainbow Furnace while using Augment: Generator. If all other 9 Furnaces (not counting AllTheModium Furnaces and above) are around the &zRainbow Furnace, have Augment: Generator, and are actively making Energy (fueled up and not full) they will give a boost to a &zRainbow Furnace that has Augment: Generator and is working. It will make 2kFE a tick more!

quests.title: Golden Furnace
quests.description: The Gold Furnace is better than the Iron ones with a Cooktime of 120 Ticks.\n\nIt can be crafted with Silver or Iron Furnace and is crafted into a Diamond one!

quests.title: Gold Generator
quests.description: Why are you surprised that Gold is actually used in mods? You've seen it in real life it does plenty! Also opens up for more unique Generators that don't just take Furnace Fuel!

quests.title: 1C73E60FC70408D4
quests.description: Finally a unique Generator! Culinary is the name for the art of Food. These Generators don't take Coal, Lava, or even logs, they take Food. Anything with Food Points can be used to make Energy, the amount it makes is based off the amount of Food Points the Food consists of. Steak will give more Energy than a Carrot.

quests.title: Honey Generator
quests.description: If you know Productive Bees you should know LobsterJonn. He made Productive Bees and Generator's Galore (along with many others). The Honey Generator is a good way of connecting both these mods! Honey Generator uses Liquid Honey to make Energy.

quests.title: Augment: Speed
quests.description: Augment: Speed makes it so your Furnace is faster! Diamond Furnace will instead smelt every 40 Ticks instead of 80 Ticks. At the cost of twice the Fuel usage.

quests.title: Augment: Fuel Efficiency
quests.description: Augment: Fuel Efficiency is for all you Earth-Loving, Tree-Hugging, Captain Planet Embracing, Hippies. The Furnace consumes half of the amount of Fuel at the cost of half the time. Coal will not Smelt 8 items but rather 16!

quests.title: Allthemodium Furnace
quests.description: The Allthemodium Furnace is pretty much the same as the Netherite Furnace. You will need this to craft the Vibranium Furnace.

quests.title: &zRainbow Furnace
quests.description:
The &zRainbow Furnace needs quite literally every other Furnace to Craft. 8 &zRainbow Plating and 1 &zRainbow Core gives us the best Furnace we could imagine!
Yes it takes 20 Ticks to smelt or 1 Second to smelt, but it doesn't smelt 1 item. How many items you ask? How many are in a stack of items?

quests.title: 1843C79133DFB024
quests.description: The most powerful and efficient Generator, the Netherstar Generator. Take a guess what it uses to make Energy!

quests.title: Netherite Generator
quests.description: Makes Energy at the same rate as an Emerald Generator but has a much higher Transfer Rate. Also arguably cheaper as it takes less items but that item is also Netherite so...

quests.title: Diamond Generator
quests.description: Diamonds are usually expensive... for Vanilla, but this is modded you'll have enough for atleast 1 Diamond Generator. Still uses normal Furnace Fuel.

quests.title: Emerald Generator
quests.description: Very fast Rate of making Energy from Fuel which makes it the very efficient. Only problem is it can't be upgraded anymore. Still uses normal Furnace Fuel.

quests.title: Potion Generator
quests.description: Want something exciting and new to make Energy? What about using Potions for it! That's what the Potion Generator does, it will take your Potions and make Energy out of it depending on its strength and duration.

quests.title: 20EC8001A05CE2C8
quests.description: Wireless Heat is a fun and easy way of powering Furnaces. First place the Wireless Heat Transmitter and put Energy into it. Then put the Receiver into the Transmitter to bind it. Finally put the Receiver into the Furnace Fuel section to start powering it!

quests.title: Unobtainium Furnace
quests.description: The Unobtainium Furnace smelts items faster than any other Furnace in the pack!

quests.title: Vibranium Furnace
quests.description: The Vibranium Furnace is even better than the Allthemodium Furnace!

quests.title: Crystal Furnace
quests.description:
If Emeralds aren't your thing the Crystal Furnace might be what you want! 
 
Works the same as an Emerald Furnace at 40 Tick. 
 
Made with a Diamond Furnace and can be made into an Obsidian Furnace. 
 
(No you can't see the Items smelting inside it, it's just transparent)

quests.title: Emerald Furnace
quests.description:
The Emerald Furnace, I wonder if Villagers will trade for it? 
 
It works at 40 Ticks or only 2 Seconds to smelt! Blink and you might miss it. 
 
These are crafted by Diamond Furnace and can be made into an Obsidian Furnace.

quests.title: Diamond Furnace
quests.description:
Diamonds the staple of Minecraft, and of upgraded Furnaces apparently...
 
These work even faster only taking 80 Ticks or 4 Seconds to smelt items. That's even faster than a Blast Furnace! 
 
These are only crafted by Gold Furnaces and can be crafted into Crystal or Emerald Furnaces.

quests.title: Halitosis Generator
quests.description:
Dragon's Breath is a powerful, (stinky), and mysterious item. Powerful means we can make Energy from it, and lots of it! Halitosis Generator makes Energy from Dragon's Breath!
(BTW you can farm Dragon's Breath with an Extrator from XyCraft with a Dragon's Head).

quests.title: Ender Generator
quests.description: I always hate when I have an Endermen Farm for either XP or Apotheosis Gems but end up with all these Ender Pearls (hehe end up, ender pearls). Now you can use those Ender Pearls for Energy with the Ender Generator. You can even make Eyes of Ender for even more Energy!

quests.title: Obsidian Generator
quests.description: The Obsidian Generator is slower than the Emerald and Netherite Generators but it has more upgrades than all of those combined!

quests.title: Enchantment Generator
quests.description: There's so many useless Enchantments out there, why not get some Energy out of them! The Enchantment Generator uses Enchanted Books to make Energy. The Level and Rarity of Enchanted Books changes the amount of Energy you get from them.

quests.title: 686B25F2E9D8CC97
quests.subtitle: "This is Halloween"
quests.description: At the time of writing this it's the end of July so I've got about 3 months until Halloween. But it's never to early to start getting Spooky! Just like Spirit Halloween we can get Spooky 3 months before it actually starts. This time by Right Clicking a Furnace with the Spook-alator! Once it's time to start getting ready for Thanksgiving Shift Right Click them to Un-Spook-Alate!

quests.title: 553220A2CD7CAFE4
quests.subtitle: All Wrapped up
quests.description: During Christmas all the Chests look like Presents... but the Furnaces just stick out like a sore thumb! Now that can be changed with the Wrapping Paper! You can Right Click it onto any Iron Furnace and it'll be all set for the holiday season! And after the season is over you can Shift Right Click it to unwrap it!

quests.title: Magmatic Generator
quests.description: Lava goes in. Energy comes out.

quests.title: 08245411AFDB63DB
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks.

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission.

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Welcome to Powah!!!
quests.description: Powah is a tech mod that's all about generating, storing, and transmitting Power. Ranging from basic FE generation to Reactors that produce 250k FE/t, Powah has you covered!\n\nTo get started, go out and mine some Uraninite!

quests.title: Starting with Dielectric Mats
quests.description: Almost every single machine you can make in the mod will require a Dielectric Casing.\n\nYou'll need to make the Paste first, as well as some Rods to progress!

quests.title: The Energizing Orb
quests.description:
In the beginning, you can get by with creating the Starter and Basic tier machines using Iron, but you'll eventually need to create energized mats using the Energizing Orb.

The Energizing Orb will energize items using nearby Energizing Rods within a 9x9 area around it, creating better materials for you to use to progress through the Tiers in Powah.

To power the orb, you'll need to attach Energizing Rods to Energy Cables that are being supplied with energy. If you want the Orb to energize faster, either make more rods, upgrade to higher tier rods, or both! To see if the Rods are connected, set your Wrench to link mode and you can link any Rod to the Orb.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/powah/powah_energizing.png width:200 height:200 align:1}

quests.title: 33816AF0E699F19F
quests.description: This block will drain FE from any charged item.

quests.title: 5BCA3F716348ECCD
quests.description: The Energy Hopper will charge any chargeable item inside of the inventory of the block it is pointed to, like a chest.

quests.title: Binding Cards
quests.description:
The Player Transmitter will charge a player's items wirelessly. You must first bind this to a player using a Binding Card. This is the basic card which allows the transmitter to only work in the same dimension. You can upgrade this by using a Binding Card (Dimensional) instead.
Note: To get a Player Aerial Pearl, use an Aerial Pearl on a Zombie or Husk.

quests.title: 61A8FAEC4FF18449
quests.description: These can be used to charge items in your inventory, or can be used to increase the overall power capacity of an Ender Network channel.

quests.title: 1C273D9E046FD18A
quests.description: Used to energize items using the Energizing Orb.

quests.title: 700F3FF7C23D0C0F
quests.description: The Ender Cell will store power for a channel in your Ender Network. To increase the power capacity of the network, right click on the Ender Cell to open up the interface, then add either a Battery or an Energy Cell to increase the overall capacity.

quests.title: 78202A1CF5D86B94
quests.description: The Power Bank of Powah.\n\nThese can also be used to upgrade the total power storage capacity of your wireless Ender Networks.

quests.title: 7D52DD751DDADA1B
quests.description: The basic cables for transferring power.

quests.title: 3CB6DC5B09C62CFE
quests.description:
Ender Gates are used to transfer power wirelessly to and from an adjacent block into the Ender Network.

Think of these like wireless access points to your wireless network of power.

Note: You can only add power storage capacity using an Ender Cell.

quests.title: 0FD62827710F0AC6
quests.description: The Magmator will generate FE when supplied with Lava.

quests.title: 3D5F87F8E6B89C1B
quests.description: The Furnator will burn items like coal and wood to produce FE.

quests.title: 52E59FCB39D66BCF
quests.description: One of the best options for "Passive Power", the Thermal Generator will produce FE when placed over a Heat Source and given a steady supply of water.\n\nThere are currently 3 blocks you can place this over: a Magma block which produces the lowest, a lava source block which is a little better, or a Block of Blazing Crystal, which provides the most heat.

quests.title: Reactor (Starter)
quests.description:
The Reactor is a 3x4x3 multiblock generator that burns Urananite as fuel to produce FE.

To build it, you'll need to make a total of 36 Reactor Blocks. While holding 36 in hand, placing one block will auto-build the reactor. Make sure to clear out some room first!

You'll want to cool the reactor down for it to create more FE, and you can do this with either solid or liquid coolant. To use a solid coolant, you'll also need to give it some liquid coolant as well. Dry Ice makes for a great solid coolant! (Note: 1 Water Bucket will do).

You can also increase the FE generation by keeping the fuel buffer full, as well as adding both Coal and Redstone to the Reactor. Using Blocks of either will also work!

quests.title: 7678B5DD1339833E
quests.description: The Solar Panel generates FE when given direct access to the sun. However, you can use a Lens of Ender to ignore blocks in its way.

quests.title: Eterna
quests.description:
Eterna sets the Enchantment Level which determines what Enchantments you can or will get! 

It's default is 0 and max is 100. 

Almost all Bookshelves will give Eterna but each has max they can set it to.

quests.title: Quanta
quests.description:
Quanta helps to mix up the Enchantment Pool, making it easier to get a whole bunch of different Enchantments. 

Quanta can work against you though, the more you have it, the more common weaker Enchantments will get. 

Before we used Rectification, instead we now use Geode-Encased Bookshelves of Stability! 

Default Quanta is 15% and its max is 100%.

quests.title: Negative amounts
quests.description:
Some Infusions need very, very exact amounts of Eterna, Quanta, or Arcana. 

To get these you might need one of these Shelves. 

Each lowers the amount of its respective quantities.

quests.title: Enchanting Clues
quests.description:
You ever spend 3 months studying Galatic Code to finally understand Enchantment Table language just for it to be gibberish? 

No? 

Me either, but Enchanting Clues are your actual translator for it! 

Each Enchanting Clue will tell you 1 Enchantment before you actually use it.

quests.title: Blazing Hellshelf
quests.description: Blazing Hellshelves give a bit of Quanta and Eterna but they aren't the cheap option we are looking for, for our Infusions!

quests.title: Arcana
quests.description:
Arcana is very important quantity, it increases the amount of Enchantments you get; and makes rare Enchantments more common. 

An example with Swords would be like, Smite is a very common Enchantment but Looting is much more rare. 

Arcanas default is 0% and max is 100%.

quests.title: Infused Hellshelves
quests.description:
Once we get those 15 Hellshelves around our Enchantment Table, we'll have 45 Eterna and 30% Quanta in our Table. 

This is the perfect amount to Infuse our Hellshelves! 

Infused Hellshelves give 5 Eterna with a max of 60 Eterna, along with 5% Quanta. 

These can be Crafted with other Items to make different Bookshelves, for the ones we want we'll need 12 Infused Hellshelves! 

Of course, with me being soooo generous, you'll only need to collect 8!

quests.title: Soul-Touched Sculkshelf
quests.description:
To upgrade Deepshelves even farther, surprisingly we don't need Infusion! Instead we need more Crafting! 

First, is 5 Sculk Blocks and a Sculk Catalyst. Both can be found within the Deep Dark and will need Silk Touch to collect. 

Last is the Warden Tendril... this is a Drop from the Warden... Yes, you'll need to kill the Warden. 

Once you have all that you can Craft one of the best Bookshelves! One that gives 10 Eterna, 15% Quanta, and 10% Arcana. 

And most importantly, gives us a max Eterna of 80! Almost to 100!

quests.title: Hellshelves
quests.description:
Hellshelves are your introduction to Quanta, they give 3% Quanta and 3 Eterna. 

Better than normal Shelves right? 

You're going to want 16 of them for the next step, 15 Hellshelves around the Enchantment Table, with 1 in your Inventory. 

Make the first 11 and I'll give you the last 5 Hellshelves!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/apothic/enchant_hellshelf.png width:100 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Glowing Hellshelf
quests.description:
By combining an Infused Hellshelf with some Glowstone we can make Glowing Hellshelves! 

These have the same Eterna and Quanta, but give 3% Arcana. 

This will be helpful in later Infusions, like if we wish to use 12 of them to Infuse a Dormant Deepshelf into a Deepshelf!

quests.title: Soul-Touched Deepshelf
quests.description:
Soul-Touched Deepshelves are an upgrade to Deepshelves. 

They are Crafted with a Soul Lantern and 3 Sculk Blocks. You'll need Silk Touch to pick up Sculk Blocks. 

Then, we can Craft our Soul-Touched version. These will give a ton more Quanta at 15%! 

It also increases max Eterna to 75.

quests.title: Pearlescent Endshelf
quests.description:
The Pearlescent Endshelf is an alright Shelf especially for the price. 

It is created by combining an Endshelf with 4 End Rods and 2 Ender Pearls. 

It will give us max Eterna 90, but this isn't what we want for max Enchanting.

quests.title: Apothic Enchanting
quests.description:
Enchanting gets a few changes with Apotheosis. 

To summarize it, 15 Bookshelves won't be enough now. 

There's new Bookshelves and actions you can do with Enchantment Tables now and hopefully these quests will help you understand.

quests.title: Vanilla Max is just the start
quests.description:
Bookshelves are your starting point, but definitely not your end point. Atleast not normal Bookshelves. 

With only normal Bookshelves you can only get Eterna up and to a max of 30. 
(I will explain the Enchantment Levels soon but just know you need them up)

quests.title: Infusing
quests.description:
Infusion is a special version of Enchanting which ironically is used for better Enchantments. 

When the right amount of Eterna, Quanta, and Arcana is reached the Enchantments will offer Infusion. 

(To know the Levels needed you can check JEI or follow these Quests)

quests.title: Negative Enchantments Removal
quests.description:
All Enchantments from the Enchantment Table is determined by the Levels of Eterna, Quanta, and Arcana. 

We can see the Pool of Enchantments available by clicking the ? in the Top Right of the Enchantment Table's GUI when an Item is being Enchanted. 

The higher the Quanta is, the better the chance we get a weaker Enchantment gets. 

With the Geode-Encased Bookshelf of Stability it will get rid of the increased chances of worse Enchantments.
{@pagebreak}
To Craft it we'll need a Bookshelf, 7 Calcite, and 1 Budding Amethyst. 

Budding Amethyst can not be collected from Mining, even with Silk Touch. You'll need either a Ritual or Infusion to get one then!

quests.title: Deepshelf
quests.description:
This is where the seperation of Hellshelves and Seashelves end! 

First, we'll need to Craft a Dormant Deepshelf. These are just 6 Cracked Deepslate Tiles and 3 Books. 

Then, we'll need 60 Eterna, 40% Quanta, and 40% Arcana. We can get that with 12 Crystalline Seashelves or 12 Glowing Hellshelves! 

Finally, we can Infuse our Dormant Deepshelves into regular Deepshelves!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/apothic/enchant_deepshelf.png width:100 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Infused Dragon's Breath
quests.description:
Now that we have our max Eterna of 80, we can start Infusing Dragon's Breath! 

Dragon's Breath can be obtained when fighting the Ender Dragon. When she is perched above her nest she might shoot a Pink mist at you. When in it, you can Right Click with an Empty Bottle, to obtain Dragon's Breath! 

The best way to get our Levels is with 4 Echoing Sculkshelves, 4 Soul-Touched Sculkshelves, and 6 Geode-Encased Bookshelves of Stability. 

These will give us 80 Eterna, 25% Quanta and 100% Arcana. Perfect for Infusion!

quests.title: Endshelves
quests.description:
The last and greatest of the Bookshelves, the Endshelves! 

These are created with 6 Endstone Bricks, 1 Ender Pearl, 1 Bookshelf, and of course the Infused Dragon's Breath. 

Their stats aren't currently the best, only giving 5 for each. But their max Eterna of 90 is incredible! 

Oh yeah plus they can be Crafted with other Items to upgrade them!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/apothic/enchant_endshelf.png width:100 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Best Enchanting set-up
quests.description:
Ever want the most perfect Enchantments? Like, every stat maxed out, every good Enchantment available? Then, you'll need these! 

First, is the 5 Soul-Touched Sculkshelves and 5 Echoing Sculkshelves. These will give us all the Quanta and Arcana we need! 

Next, is the Draconic Endshelf which will give us 100 Eterna, as in amount of Eterna and the max level. 

Third, is the Geode-Encased Bookshelf of Stability, this will make it so the Quanta doesn't backstab us with awful Enchantments! 

Last is optional but you should add it, the Deepshelf of Arcane Treasures. That Bookshelf will allow us to get Enchantments we normally wouldn't, like Mending!

quests.title: Seashelves
quests.description:
The Nether can be pretty scary, if you'd rather voyage the Sea, use Seashelves! 

Seashelves are your introduction to Arcana, they give 3% Arcana and 3 Eterna. 

Better than normal Shelves right? 

You're going to need 16 for Infusing... well 15 for Infusing, 1 to be Infused! 

Like the Hellshelves, I'll give you extra, just collect 11 now!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/apothic/enchant_seashelf.png width:100 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Crystalline Seashelf
quests.description:
We can Craft Infused Seashelves with Prismarine Crystals to get Crystalline Seashelves. 

The Crystalline Seashelves will keep the same 5 Eterna, 5% Arcana, and now have 3% Quanta. 

With 12 of them, we can get enough Levels to Infuse Dormant Deepshelves into normal Deepshelves!

quests.title: Echoing Deepshelf
quests.description:
For the Echoing upgrade we'll need a few different Items. 

Candles which are relatively easy to get! And Echo Shards... which definitely aren't... 

The best chance at getting them is by Looting an Ancient City, but you can Craft them with a few different Rituals. 

(Or even later on with Enchanting!) 

The Echoing Deepshelves will give a whole lot more Arcana at 15%! Along with raising the max Eterna to 75.

quests.title: Draconic Endshelf
quests.description:
The Draconic Shelf is the last Shelf we'll need for perfect set up. 

It might only give Eterna but it has the max Eterna of 100. 

To Craft it we'll need 5 Ender Pearls and a Dragon Head. That is what makes it Draconic! 

To get them you can either use MA or find them on End Ships. End Ships are Structures in The End, on the bow (front) is the Dragon Head.

quests.title: Echoing Sculkshelf
quests.description:
To upgrade Deepshelves even farther, surprisingly we don't need Infusion! Instead we need more Crafting! 

First, is 5 Sculk Blocks and a Sculk Catalyst. Both can be found within the Deep Dark and will need Silk Touch to collect. 

Last is the Warden Tendril... this is a Drop from the Warden... Yes, you'll need to kill the Warden. 

Once you have all that you can Craft one of the best Bookshelves! One that gives 10 Eterna, 10% Quanta, and 15% Arcana. 

And most importantly, gives us a max Eterna of 80! Almost to 100!

quests.title: Other Infusion Items
quests.description: It's not just Bookshelves that can be Infused!

quests.title: Infused Seashelf
quests.description:
With the 15 Seashelves around the Enchanting Table, we can Infuse our last Seashelf! 

Infused Seashelves give more Eterna at 5 with a max of 60. Also more Arcana at 5%. 

These can be Crafted into different Bookshelves, the ones we're looking for, for Max Enchanting is the Crystalline Seashelf. 

We'll need 12 of those, so we'll need 12 Infused Seashelves. Craft 8 and I'll reward you the rest!

quests.title: Remove Enchantments from Pool
quests.description:
If you want to remove a specific Enchant from Enchantment Pool, you can use this Bookshelf in your Enchanting set up! 

Place an Enchantment Book, you want to Blacklist, in an empty spot in this Seashelf. 

Then, when you Enchant, this Enchantment won't show up on Items or Books.

quests.title: Heart-Forged Seashelf
quests.description:
The Heart-Forged Seashelf is another upgrade to the Infused Seashelf. 

It's a little expensive but gives lots of Arcana! 

This will be very helpful for later Infusions needing lots of Arcana.

quests.title: Tool Tomes
quests.description:
The Tome of Miners will help you with all your Mining. It will give Efficiency, Fortune, and Silk Touch. 

These work for Pickaxes, Axes, Shovels, and even Hoes! 

Tome of the Fishers will only give Fishing Rod Enchantments, and yeah there is a lot.

quests.title: Tomes
quests.description:
Tomes are Books... just more useful Books! 

Each Tome is Crafted with Books, Sticks, Blaze Rods and Powder. 

Tomes can be Enchanted, like Items, to get certain Enchantments. 

There is also the Tomes of Scrapping which can be used in Anvils to take Enchantments off Items.

quests.title: Tome of Scrapping
quests.subtitle: Half Enchantments, breaks Items
quests.description:
With 8 Books and an Anvil we can make the Tome of Scrapping. Well actually 8 of them, but you get the picture! 

By combining an Item with the Tome in an Anvil, we can take half the Enchantments off the Item. 

This will end up breaking and voiding the Item after it is done. I don't recommend using it, rather you should upgrade it!

quests.title: Tome of Superior Scrapping
quests.subtitle: All Enchantments, breaks Item
quests.description:
The Tome of Scrapping will only take off half the Enchantments, while the Tome of Superior Scrapping will take every Enchantment off the Item! 

Both of these Tomes will break the Item in use though. 

To Infuse our Tome of Scrapping into a Tome of Superior Scrapping we can use 3 Echoing Sculkshelves and 15 Bookshelves, or 4 Draconium Blocks.

quests.title: Making Budding Amethyst
quests.description:
Budding Amethyst can be useful for Crafting Recipes and even just Growing Amethyst! 

With a Amethyst Block, 60 Eterna, between 30% and 50% Quanta, and 50% Arcana we can Infuse one. 

To get all those stats we can use 15 Glowing Hellshelves and 4 Melonshelves.

quests.title: Making a real Trident
quests.description:
Apotheosis knows how annoying Tridents can be to get so they made it easier... well kinda easier! 

You can now make an Inert Trident and Infuse it to get a normal Trident. 

The Trident requires between 40 Eterna, 20%-50% Quanta, and atleast 35% Arcana. 

You can get this with 1 Bookshelf, 4 Echoing Sculkshelf, and 1 Melonshelf.

quests.title: Library of Alexandria
quests.subtitle: Just imagine if Rome never burned...
quests.description:
The Library of Alexandria is a better Enchantment Library. 

It can hold higher Levels of Enchanted Books, but it will still need the Level of Book to get taken out at that Level. 

It will also hold more Points. The Enchantment Library can hold 32768, while the Library of Alexandria can hold 1.1 Billion Points of each Book! 

To obtain it, we'll need to Infuse the Enchantment Library. 

Use 4 Soul-Touched Sculkshelves, 4 Echoing Sculkshelves, 1 Draconic Endshelf, 5 Geode-Encased Bookshelves of Stability, and a Skeleton Skull.

quests.title: Flimsy Ender Lead
quests.description: Ever wanted to pick up mobs? We...have Soul Gems, Mob Imprisonment Tools, and Creature Catchers for that.\n\nLet's just ignore those for now and focus on the option Apotheosis offers. The Flimsy Ender Lead is the cheapest variant of Ender Lead, but also the weakest, and most fragile. It can only hold animals, and breaks after 8 uses.

quests.title: Ender Lead
quests.description: A considerable step up from the Flimsy Ender Lead. Now, it can hold hostile mobs as well, and will break after 64 uses. To get this, we will need at least 45 Eterna, 25% Quanta, and 40% Arcana.\n\nThis can be achieved with 9 Crystalline Seashelves, or, if you prefer Hellshelves, 9 Glowing Hellshelves and 8 Candles (Tip: You can fit up to 4 candles into one block)

quests.title: Armor Tomes
quests.description:
Armor Tomes are used to get Enchantments which are only used on Armor. All of the Tomes can get Protection, Blast Protection, and Fire Protection. 

Each also gives ones reserved for a certain part of the Armor. Boots will give Depth Strider and Helmets will give Aqua Affinity. 

If you want the best chance for just Protection try the Chestplate Tome!

quests.title: ETC. Tomes
quests.description: The rest of the Enchantments come from this Tome. \n\nUnbreaking... I don't really know what else...

quests.title: Infinite Echo Shards?
quests.description:
Echo Shards can be pretty annoying to farm, plus we'll need a lot of them! So why not have an easier way of Farming them. 

With Infusion we can make 1 Echo Shard into 4! 

We'll need 70 Eterna, 50% Quanta, and 50% Arcana. 

To get that, we can use 12 Glowing Hellshelves and 2 Deepshelves, that aren't Dormant!

quests.title: Occult Ender Lead
quests.subtitle: Nothing to do with Occultism I swear
quests.description: The third and final tier of Ender Lead is here! This one is unbreakable and can even bind mobs to Spawners. It will require a considerably more tricky Infusion setup. We'll need at least 75 Eterna, 85% Quanta, and between 60-85% Arcana.\n\nYou can get this with 4 Soul-Touched Sculkshelves, 4 Echoing Sculkshelves, 3 Stoneshelves, and 2 vanilla Bookshelves. Oh, and you also need a Witch in the Ender Lead used for this Infusion.

quests.title: Weapon Tomes
quests.description:
Tomes of Weaponry will give Enchantments for Swords and Axes. 

Mostly the ones that help with Killing things! Like Sharpness and Fire Aspect. 
Tomes of Archery will give Enchantments for ranged Weapons, the Bow and Crossbow. 

Piercing, Power, and Knockback!

quests.title: 3D31B94CC42BCE43
quests.subtitle: All Enchantments, doesn't break
quests.description:
The Tome of Extraction is the Tome we are looking for! It will take off all Enchantments and leave the Item alone! 

To make it we'll need to Infuse our Tome of Superior Scrapping. 

We can just use our previous setup for this.

quests.title: Unbreakable Charms
quests.description:
The worst part about Charms is that they break! Why would these OP Potion Effects have to have Durability! 

Well don't you worry, Apotheosis has a cure for that... with Infusions! 

You'll need 100 Eterna, between 8.5% and 13.5% Quanta, and between 32.5% and 37.5% Arcana. 

You can use 10 Glowing Hellshelves, 4 Geode-Encased Bookshelves of Stability, 2 Draconic Endshelves, and a Skeleton Skull! 

Yes, some Skulls and other Items besides Bookshelves give stats!

quests.title: Crafting EXP?
quests.description:
EXP is very important for Apotheosis Enchanting! Every Enchant requires it! (Why do you think I give it in every Reward?) 

With Infusion we can transform Honey Bottles into Bottles O' Enchanting. Actually we get 3 different Infusions for it! It goes from 1 Bottle O' Enchanting, to 8, to 32! 

First, is for 1 Bottle and needs only 2 Echoing Sculkshelves. 

Second, is for 8 Bottles and needs 5 Echoing Sculkshelves and 1 Soul-Touched Sculkshelf. 

Last, is for 32 Bottles O' Enchanting and will need 5 Echoing Sculkshelves, 3 Soul-Touched, and 1 Draconic Endshelf!

quests.title: Enchantment Library
quests.description:
The Enchantment Library is the single greatest Enchanted Book storage, ever! 

To Craft it you'll need 4 Ender Chests, 1 Enchanting Table, and 4 of any of the Infused Bookshelves: Infused Hellshelf, Infused Seashelves, and Deepshelves. 

To use it, you can either Shift Left Click Enchanted Books or bring them into the Blue Slot. This will add the Books to the Library. 

The Books are sorted by name and are held in Points. Each Level of Enchanted Book determines the Level, and it is reflected on how many Books would be needed to get that Level. Level 1, is 1 Point. Level 2 is 2 Points. Level 3 is 4 Points. Level 4 is 8 Points. 

Each Book is stored to a max of 32768 Points, and they can be extracted by Left Clicking the stored Book. Each Click will add another Level to the Book in the Orange Slot. 

You can Click different Books to add to the Book in the Orange Slot, similar to combining Books in an Anvil. 

The max Level of Enchanted Book is determined by the highest Level of Book you've put in. It doesn't matter if you have 32000 Points, if you only put in Sharpness III, you can only take out Sharpness III.

quests.title: Tier 1 Glyphs
quests.description: Tier 1 Glyphs require 3 levels of experience to be made.

quests.title: Tier 2 Glyphs
quests.description: Tier 2 Glyphs require 5 levels of experience to be made. \n\nThey also require a Mage's Spell Book to create.

quests.title: Tier 3 Glyphs
quests.description: Tier 3 Glyphs require 10 levels of experience to be made. \n\nThey also require an Archmage Spell Book.

quests.title: 3D4D88B8BE881351
quests.subtitle: Upgrading Spells
quests.description:
If you want to cast better spells, you'll need a Scribe's Table to unlock new glyphs for your spellbook. 

There are 3 tiers of glyphs to unlock, and each one requires some experience and items. 

The Scribe's Table is also used to attach spells to Spell Parchments. To do this, place a Spell Parchment on the table, select the spell in your Spellbook, then sneak right-click the book on the table. 

To create a Glyph, right-click on the Scribe's Table with your spellbook. Search for the glyph you want to make, then click Select at the bottom. Right-click the table with the items required, and the glyph will be created. Use the glyph to learn it. 

Note: The table can pull items from nearby inventories.

quests.title: Creating Your First Spell
quests.description:
While holding your Spellbook, you can press C to open up the spell creation page. 

Each spell must have a form. You start off with 3 basic forms: Projectile, Self-cast, and Touch. 

For the Effect, this determines what happens when you cast the spell. You can have up to 9 effects per spell. 

For starters, you have Harm and Break. 

Select one Form and one Effect, name your spell, and click create!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/ars/spellbook.png width:200 height:150 align:1}

quests.title: Mana
quests.subtitle: Mage Power
quests.description: In the bottom left of your screen, you'll see a bar. This bar is your mana pool! \n\nThere are several ways to increase your mana pool, or increase the efficiency of your spells as you progress through the mod. Upgrading your spellbook can also increase your mana!

quests.title: Summoning Help!
quests.description: The Dominion Wand is used for controlling the creatures you might encounter in the world! Each being responds differently to the wand, so make sure to read up in the Worn Notebook!

quests.title: 36CDA39C23D3AA2B
quests.description:
This Quest has been authored by AllTheMods Staff, or a Community contributor for use in AllTheMods Modpacks. 

As all AllTheMods packs are licensed under All Rights Reserved, this Quest is not allowed to be used in any public packs not released by AllTheMods Team without explicit permission. 

This quest is intentionally hidden, if you're seeing this, you're in editing mode.

quests.title: Welcome to Ars Nouveau!
quests.description: Welcome to Ars Nouveau! \n\nArs Nouveau is a magic mod that allows you to create custom spells with the different Glyphs made within the mod!

quests.title: Spell Books
quests.subtitle: Our First Spellbook
quests.description:
To get started, you'll need to craft yourself a Novice Spellbook! 

This is where you create and store your spells. 

Hitting the C key will open up the 'Create a Spell' page. On the left, there are several tabs, but the main 3 are: Spell Creation, Color Picker, and Familiars. 

This spellbook will only allow you to create and use Tier 1 Glyphs. To create better spells, you'll need to upgrade your Spellbook!

quests.title: Archwood Logs
quests.description: To gain further knowledge of spells, we'll need a specific type of magical wood! \n\nArchwood trees can be found in the overworld.

quests.title: 5766C8B9E850C186
quests.subtitle: Creating Source Gems
quests.description:
To create one of the main crafting items in Ars, the Source Gem, we'll need to make an Imbuement Chamber. 

The Imbuement Chamber requires Source to imbue items. It produces a small amount of Source by itself, but can also use Source Jars as a power source. 

Several recipes also require Arcane Pedestals to be placed around it as well.

{image:atm:textures/questpics/ars/imbuement.png width:200 height:150 align:1}

quests.title: Source Gems
quests.description: To create Source Gems, we'll need to put either Lapis or Amethyst Shards into the Imbuement Chamber. Over time, these will convert to Source Gems!

quests.title: Sourcestone
quests.subtitle: Formerly "Arcane Stones"
quests.description: With Source Gems, you can get started crafting the various machines by creating Sourcestones.

quests.title: Arcane Pedestals
quests.subtitle: Fancy Tables
quests.description: Arcane Pedestals are needed for the Ritual Brazier and crafting items with an Enchanting Apparatus. \n\nGo ahead and make yourself 8 of them!

quests.title: Enchanting Apparatus
quests.description:
The Enchanting Apparatus is used to craft various items within the mod. It requires Source to work.

It is also a multiblock structure that utilizes Arcane Pedestals to craft.

Start by placing an Arcane Core in the ground, then place the Enchanting Apparatus on top of it. Surround the Apparatus with Arcane Pedestals.

{image:atm:textures/questpics/ars/enchanting_app.png width:200 height:175 align:1}

quests.title: Magebloom Seed
quests.subtitle: Growing Magic
quests.description: Using our Enchanting Apparatus structure, we'll want to craft our first seed, the Magebloom Seed. \n\nThis will be used to create us some magical clothing!

quests.title: 542C6D76B579886C
quests.description: Using our Enchanting Apparatus structure, we'll want to craft our first seed, the Magebloom Seed. \n\nThis will be used to create us some magical clothing!

quests.title: 0E2AD156E5EF263A
quests.description: Used to inscribe spells on with the Scribe's Table.

quests.title: 0D330FAD6C993DBC
quests.description: This is the next upgrade to your Spellbook! \n\nThis will increase your overall mana and mana regen, as well as allowing you to create and use Tier 2 Glyphs.

quests.title: 3142A40E1EAEBAA3
quests.subtitle: Magic Finder
quests.description: The Dowsing Rod gives you Magic Find and Scrying when used. \n\nThis allows you to see nearby magic creatures as well as helping you find amethyst!

quests.title: 111649D7E16D869F
quests.description:
The Caster's Wand only accepts a single spell, and is inscribed using the Scribe's Table. 

Wand spells always start with Projectile > Accelerate, and MUST be inscribed with a spell that does not have another method (like touch, self, etc). 

This allows you to cast spells beyond the 10 spell cap. If you want to use Break, just inscribe the wand with Break by itself.

quests.title: 227DBA8836021B0B
quests.subtitle: Storing Source
quests.description:
In Ars Nouveau, the power system for machines is called Source. 

To start collecting some Source, we'll need a Source Jar. 

Source can also be moved with buckets, or by breaking and picking up Source Jars.

quests.title: 151648179684B088
quests.subtitle: Placeable Spells
quests.description:
Runic Chalk is used to draw permanent Runes on that ground. These runes will cast spells on entities that walk over them. 

To attach a spell to a rune, inscribe a Spell Parchment using a Scribe's Table.

Note: The Rune will need Source to operate.

quests.title: 2D0CF18C8B2ABB7D
quests.subtitle: Creates Source using the growth of Plants
quests.description: Placing this near growing plants or saplings will provide Source. Archwood trees provide more Source! \n\nNote: Bonemealing does not produce Source.

quests.title: 19D02325579F2AA8
quests.description:
The Volcanic Sourcelink generates Source by consuming burnable items. Archwood logs will generate bonus Source. 

As it burns items, it will convert nearby stone into lava. 

This also generates Lava Lilys.

quests.title: 14DB8A515CA50932
quests.description:
The Enchanter's Sword allows you to attach a Touch Spell to the sword. 

All spells on the Sword gain 1 additional Amplify augment to the last effect on the spell. 

To apply a spell to the sword, use a Scribe's Table. Create the spell without using a form.

quests.title: 17D7D34F519F7E5F
quests.description: To create the final tier of your Spellbook, you'll need to have killed the Wilden Chimera. \n\nThis is a Ritual that you'll need to complete using a Ritual Brazier.

quests.title: 51162B9185A45BB1
quests.description:
This bow can be inscribed with a spell using a Scribe's Table. 

At the cost of mana, arrows will become Spell Arrows and will apply the spell on their target. 

If you have no arrows, a spell arrow that deals 0 damage will be cast. If there is not enough mana, regular arrows will be fired instead. 

The Enchanter's Bow can also use special Augment Arrows that empower the inscribed spell.

quests.title: 3182E8AF755104E4
quests.description: When blocking damage, the Enchanter's Shield will give the user Mana Regen and Spell Damage for a short amount of time. \n\nAdditionally, the shield will repair itself over time using the wearer's mana.

quests.title: 77145113CD5B26FB
quests.subtitle: Generates Source from Nearby Food
quests.description: Source Berries produce more Source than other sources. \n\nThis will also convert grass or dirt into Mycelium in a 3x3 area around it. It will also grow mushrooms around it if the space is empty.

quests.title: 04D9F6587EF8D9B7
quests.subtitle: Storing Potions
quests.description: The Potion Jar stores up to 100 potions. You can remove them by using an empty bottle or a potion flask on the jar. \n\nWixies will use these jars during Potion Autocrafting.

quests.title: 295C77EEC89000FC
quests.subtitle: Generates Source from Mob Deaths and Animal Breeding

quests.title: 457DE8C154641437
quests.description:
The Ritual Brazier is used to cast rituals. It can also be used for decoration. If you want to light the Brazier, use a Light spell on it. 

To perform rituals, you'll need Arcane Pedestals as well. As there are so many rituals to cast, make sure to check out each of them using the Worn Notebook! 

This can be done by holding Ctrl on the Ritual Table while the book is in your inventory.

quests.title: 632BC46928CC9A8C
quests.description:
The Enchanter's Mirror will apply a self spell when used. 

Spells cast with this mirror are discounted and gain additional bonus duration. 

To apply a spell, use a Scribe's table. Create a spell without using a form.

quests.title: Rings of Discount
quests.description: The Rings of Discount provides a small bonus to max mana and mana regen. It also reduces the total cost to cast a spell.

quests.title: 088FCB5267CB7A89
quests.description: This belt will give random positive potion effects for a short duration. These will vary in strength.

quests.title: 41A0BE357C8A74E1
quests.subtitle: Power through Potions
quests.description: The Alchemical Sourcelink produces Source from adjacent potion jars. \n\nThe amount of source varies per potion and complexity.

quests.title: The Amulets
quests.description: The Amulet of Mana Boost gives a boost to max mana. \n\nThe Amulet of Mana Regen gives a boost to your mana regen.

quests.title: 3FD702B5AB006402
quests.description: Have you ever wanted to just hover everywhere you go? \n\nThis belt allows you to levitate. To activate, just sneak while in the air, either while falling or from jumping.

quests.title: The Jars
quests.description:
The Jar of Light summons a floating light source that follows you. 

The Jar of Voiding destroys items you pick up in exchange for mana. This can be filtered. 

To add or remove an item to be destroyed by the jar, use the jar with the item in your off hand, or use an item on the Scribe's Table with the jar placed on it. 

The jar must be on your hotbar to function.

quests.title: Relics
quests.description:
Relics are rare finds around your Minecraft World! 

They can be used in your Forge, in the squares around the center slot, these open up more the more you upgrade the Tiers! 

Or you can use them in the Clibano. 

Some are Creative Mode only, don't worry we know how much you love your OP Items and will be looking into ways of adding them!

quests.title: Crimson Stone
quests.description: Crimson Stones are found within Pillager Outposts, they are a little rare but doesn't help they only give us 2 Chests! \n\nThey aren't used for new Recipes rather they will decrease Soul usage in the Forge.

quests.title: Divine Pact
quests.description: Divine Pact is the most difficult to obtain, you'll need to search Piglin Villages and Ancient Pyramids in The Other to find them! \n\nIt's used to craft the Soul Binding Crystal and the End Game Multiblocks!

quests.title: Arcane Crystal Obelisk
quests.description:
You want to slowly automate Aureal for your Forge? Then, you'll need 2 Arcane Crystal Blocks, Arcane Polished Darkstone, and Mundabitur Dust! 

Place down the Arcane Polished Darkstone, then on top of it place both Arcane Crystal Blocks. 

Once you get this 1x3x1 Structure, Right Click it with Mundabitur Dust to make the Obelisk! 

You can place these, where the Pedestals usually go, in the Forge Multiblock in order to automate Aureal!

quests.title: 4A564E8FE587C7E4
quests.description:
The best way of getting Souls is via the Soul Extractor! 

For a few Nether Items and Blocks and an Utrem Jar (which does need Edelwood to craft) you can get your tool to Soul-Finding! 

Hold Right Click with it on Soul Sand and it'll extract the Souls from it. 

Leaving it as Sand... no wait it is Soulless Sand... what the heck is Soulless Sand?!?!?!

quests.title: Lost Souls
quests.description:
Nether too scary for you? Then, you can look for Souls in the Overworld!

Within your World (I made you go to Dark Forests because old Forbidden & Arcanus used to have Blocks there) you might find some Lost Souls wandering around.

You can kill them for the Souls that they drop! It is much less efficient though...

If you are having troubles finding Souls, you might wanna look into Soul Looting enchantment on your sword. Killing mobs with this enchantment will occassionally spawn Souls.

quests.title: Artisan Relic
quests.description:
The Artisan Relic is found within a few Buildings in Villages. 

When used in the Clibano it will allow you to make Obsidiansteel. 

When used in Forges it will give you a discount on Experience used!

quests.title: Elementarium
quests.description:
Prisms are important for many of Forbidden & Arcanus recipes and other Mods later! 

In order to craft them we'll need Elementarium, which is found in Jungle Temples, Desert Pyramids, and Underwater Ruins. 

I think it would be easier to tell us where you can't find it!

quests.title: Arcane Crystal Dust
quests.description: Arcane Crystal Dust is pretty simple, just Smelt Arcane Crystals and boom! \n\nYou can also use the Clibano Multiblock in order to get a few bits of Arcane Crystals back!

quests.title: Mundabitur Dust
quests.description:
For a few Mob Drops plus Arcane Crystal Dust you can make Mundabitur Dust! 

This is a very important part in crafting and making of Multiblocks! 

And you can find it in End Cities which most just end up doing...

quests.title: Spectral Eye Amulet
quests.subtitle: Very popular in ATM6!
quests.description:
Quite expensive recipe but most definitely worth it! 

Using the Spectral Eye will give you the Spectral Vision Effect. This Effect gives Glowing to every Mob within a 100 Block radius in every direction! 

Perfect for finding structures underground, or Bastions in the Nether, or even finding your friends hidden Axolotl farm!

quests.title: Deorum
quests.description:
Combining Mundabitur Dust, Arcane Crystal Dust, Charcoal, and a Gold Ingot we'll get our first Alloy! The Deorum Ingot! 

This is the foundational Ingot of Forbidden & Arcanus, you will need dozens of it! 

It is especially used for Building Blocks for our Multiblock Machines.

quests.title: Aureal
quests.description:
Aureal is the first and most important Slot in the Forge. 

You can either automate it with Arcane Crystal Obelisks or deposit Aureal Bottles/Potions! 

You can either find Aureal Bottles in Chests in most Structures, or you can craft them with Arcane Crystal Dust and a Potion of Regeneration II.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/forbidden/forbidden_aureal.png width:135 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Souls
quests.description:
Souls is the 2nd Slot needed for the Forge, also the smallest one: only needing 10 to fill it! \n\nEach Soul and Corrupt Soul will count as 1 Soul. While Enchanted Souls count as the whole 10!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/forbidden/forbidden_souls.png width:135 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Quantum Injector
quests.description: 4 Quantum Cores and a Mundabitur Dust and you can get the Quantum Injector. \n\nQuantum Injectors aren't used much at this stage but will be needed later!

quests.title: Stellarite Pieces
quests.description:
Stellarite spawns between Y Level 42 and -44. 

You'd think, with having such a huge radius it'll be easy to find! It isn't, it is very rare! 

Be careful when Mining it though, when broken it will EXPLODE!

quests.title: 0AC8FE3B59D1B09D
quests.description:
The Quantum Catcher is a very useful Tool for moving Mobs. 

Simply Right Click a Mob to "catch" them, then Right Click again to let them go. 

You'll need a set amount of Aureal on you in order to use it though, this is dependent on the Health of the Mob. More Health, more Aureal needed! It won't cost anything to let Mobs go though, that's free. 

Oh wait, I probably should tell you how to Craft it! You'll need a Quantum Core which is crafted with Runes, Mundabitur Dust, and Flint! 

The Spawner Scraps are drops from Mining a Spawner without Silk Touch, so it'll break the Spawner.

quests.title: Eternal Stella
quests.description:
The poster child of Forbidden & Arcanus, the Eternal Stella. 

For 1 Allthemodium Ingot, 3 Xpetrified Orbs, and a Stellarite Piece we can make one of the most overpowered Items in this Modpack! 

You can use the Eternal Stella with an Item and an Apply Item Modifier to make Items lose their Durability. No, wait I mean lose their need for Durability! Basically Indestructible Items. 

This can be used on almost every Item with Durability from Diamond Axes, to Fishing Rods, to even Refined Glowstone Armor! 

There are some limitations, it only works with Items with Durability not uses: like Infusion Crystals or Energy: like Meka-Tool!

quests.title: 487C70679535DDDB
quests.description:
Don't you hate those stupid limitations on your Quantum Catcher? Can't put Wardens in your friends base! 

Well now there is no worries for we can upgrade our Quantum Catcher with 3 Stellarite Pieces and a Nether Star to make the Boss Catcher. 

Now we can transport our Bosses wherever we want!

quests.title: Forbidden & Arcanus
quests.description:
Welcome to Forbidden & Arcanus! 

To start this Mod we'll need to start Mining underground... deep underground. 

Like Y Level 1 and below.

quests.title: Arcane Crystals
quests.description:
Arcane Crystals can spawn from Y Level 14 to -40. 

It is fairly common; but trust me, you'll need a lot of it, so be thankful! 

Like Diamonds there is a Y Level that it spawns most common at, for Arcane Crystals that Y Level is -13.

quests.title: Darkstone
quests.description:
Darkstone appears deep underground near Lava Lakes, like at Y Level -54. 

It is the most used Block for Forbidden & Arcanus, all Multiblocks will use them for their base. 
Make sure to grab a ton of them!

quests.title: Building the Forge
Tier 1 Forge
Finishing the Ritual
quests.description:
We got our Items on Pedestals, we got our Aureal, Souls, Blood, and Experience... and it isn't finishing? Why isn't it finishing? 

In order to actually finalize the Ritual we'll need to use a Gavel! 

It works like a Pickaxe but it also has a limited amount of uses for finishing Rituals, just Right Click the Forge with it!

quests.title: 07BEE6FEC14765DC
quests.description:
Pretty simple recipe needing Clay, Iron, Slimeballs, and more... 

Lodestones are best to loot for, Mods add these in Loot Pools all over The Nether so don't craft one just find one! 

Wax is a new Item added by Forbidden & Arcanus which is a mix of Bottle of Honey and Slimeballs! 

You can use it on a Darkstone Pedestal to get Magnetized Pedestals which work in hand with Hoppers (and Hopper like Items like Pipes). 

You can also use it with Boots to increase how close Items can be to get dragged into your Inventory!

quests.title: Tier 2 Forge
quests.description:
Tier 1 not enough for you? Then, you'll need to upgrade it! 

Put an Edelwood Plank in the center Slot of the Forge and place 4 Arcane Crystals and 4 Spawner Scrap onto the Pedestals. 

Smack it with a Gavel and your Tier 1 will upgrade into a Tier 2 Forge! 

Now, new Rituals will be available, the Forge can hold more Essences, and you can use a second Relics!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/forbidden/forbidden_tier1.png width:100 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Terrastomp Prism
quests.description:
The only recipe which needs Tier 2, the Terrastomp Prism! 

You'll need Dripstone, Dripstone, and Flint along with a Diamond Block! 

Like the other Prisms this will need Elementarium Relic in order to be made. 
Like the Fiery Prism, the Terrastomp Prism can be used with Tools. These Tools will be able to mine in a 3x3 Area, instead of only 1 Block Mined it'll mine 9!

quests.title: Tier 3 Forge
quests.description:
This is where it gets fun! 

Use 4 Deorum Ingots, 4 Arcane Crystals, and a Chiseled Polished Darkstone to upgrade from Tier 2 to Tier 3. 

Now we can hold even more Essences, even more Relics, and even more Recipes!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/forbidden/forbidden_tier2.png width:100 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Tier 4 Forge
quests.description:
This one needs another Chiseled Polished Darkstone, just now with 4 Runes and 4 Stellarite Pieces. 

This Forge is the last for the basic Forbidden & Arcanus. 

Of course it has the rest of the Recipes plus every space for Relics is open now!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/forbidden/forbidden_tier4.png width:100 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Tier 5 Forge
quests.description:
The last most powerful Forge so of course that means it is the most expensive! 

You'll need 2 Dark Nether Stars which are made from combining 4 Obsidiansteel and a Nether Star. 

2 Dragon Scales which are dropped when the Ender Dragon on death. 

4 Sculk Catalysts which are dropped from the Warden, or can be Silk-Touched in the Deep Dark. 

And Stellarite Block which are just 9 Stellarite Pieces! 

This allows even more Essences and End Game Recipes.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/forbidden/forbidden_tier5.png width:100 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Sea Prism
quests.description:
This one is probably one of the most annoying to craft, it needs Prismarine, Turtle Scute, Lapis, and a Heart of the Sea. 

Hope you like MA! 

It combines with Helmets... most likely to give Respiration or Aqua Affinity, but I can't get it to work...

quests.title: Soul Binding Crystal
quests.description:
The last of the Prisms, well this one's a Crystal but you get the idea! 

First, you'll need a Divine Pact Relic, which are found in The Other. 

Then, you'll need Enderpearl Fragments, Amethyst, and Nether Quartz. Don't worry it gets harder! 

Now we'll need every type of Soul. I taught you how to get Souls and Corrupt Souls in other Quests now I'll teach you about Enchanted Souls. 

Find a Lost Soul flying around in your world, then toss a Splash Potion of Aureal at them! Then, they'll become a Lost Enchanted Soul, kill them! 

With that you can now make the Crystal, which can be applied to Tools and Armor to give it Soulbound. This means when you die, you'll respawn with these Items in your Inventory still.

quests.title: Runes
quests.subtitle: These used to be Purple!
quests.description: Runes can spawn from Bedrock to Y Level 2. That includes near Darkstone! \n\nThey're more useful than Stellarite but less useful than Arcane Crystals.

quests.title: Smelter Prism
quests.description:
Smelter Prism is probably the most used Item from these Rituals, like how it is needed for the ATM Star! 

You'll need 4 Blaze Powder, 2 Coal, and a block of Arcane Crystal to make it. And don't forget the Elementarium Relic! 
Obviously and what you are most likely wanting the Smelter Prism for is the ATM Star. It can also be used with Tools to Smelt the Items that they break: Raw Ore to Ingots, Logs to Charcoal, Sand to Glass. 

You can also use it for Furnace Fuel, but it kinda sucks. Which is dumb because the name suggests it would be better!

quests.title: Blood
quests.description:
Blood is the 3rd Slot needing filling in the Forge. 

You can either kill Mobs on/near the Forge in order to add Blood. 

Or you can deposit filled Test Tubes to put that Blood into the Forge. 

To fill a Test Tube, have it in your Offhand when killing Mobs.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/forbidden/forbidden_blood.png width:135 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: Experience
quests.description:
Experience is the 4th Slot and material needed for the Forge. 

To add in Experience you'll need to put 1 of 3 things into the Experience Slot. 

1. Xpetrified Orbs, these give the most EXP. 

2. Bottle 'O Enchanting, gives a little bit of EXP but easy to get! 

3. Enchanted Item, the Forge will scrap the Enchantments off of it keeping it as EXP!
{image:atm:textures/questpics/forbidden/forbidden_experience.png width:135 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: 5F00A66CC1FE1F9F
quests.description: Honestly the only difficult part of this recipe is the Bat Wing, how many times are you killing Bats let alone Farming them? \n\nThis one is pretty new and doesn't combine with Armor, it is only used for the end game!

quests.title: Buying Edelwood
quests.subtitle: From Wandy T'
quests.description:
If you'd rather not use Corrupt Souls to grow Edelwood, you can rest on Luck! 

The Wandering Trader has a chance of selling Growing Edelwood to you, which can be planted to grow Edelwood. 

Wandering Trader is very random though, try using Trader Carpets to atleast know where he'll spawn!

quests.title: Clibano
Obsidiansteel
quests.description:
An Alloy added by Forbidden & Arcanus is Obsidiansteel. 

It's created in the Clibano, by combining Raw Iron and Obsidian. 

You'll need an Artisan Relic in order to actually make the Alloy! 

Also you'll get Copper as residue, which probably isn't supposed to happen...

quests.title: Black Hole
quests.description:
Dark Matter is created by Smelting Edelwood. 

Corrupti Dust is made with Obsidiansteel and some Mob Drops. 

Throw both these on the ground together and a Black Hole will spawn! 

The Black Hole will void every Item or Projectile that comes near, but what we want to feed it is Experience! 

When you feed it enough EXP it will give back an Xpetrified Orb.
{image:atm:textures/questpics/forbidden/forbidden_blackhole.png width:150 height:100 align:center}

quests.title: 5CD0E6F349F2F32D
quests.description:
Don't be afraid, this isn't an oogly boogly, it's a fully grown Edelwood! 

The Tree will have a Carved Edelwood Log on top and Edelwood Branches coming from it, these can be broken for Edelwood Sticks. 

The Logs are hollow on the inside, similar space as a Cauldron. Funny enough it can also hold Water like a Cauldron!

quests.title: Corrupt Souls
quests.description:
Corrupt Souls are used for 2 things! 

1. Crafting recipe with the Tier 4 Forge, which we don't need to worry about right now. 

2. Growing Edelwood! 

Growing Edelwood acts as the Sapling for Edelwood, these are the only way of getting Edelwood now.

quests.title: Soul Looting Enchantment
quests.description:
In order to get our Corrupt Souls we'll need to do some Enchanting! 

We are looking for the Soul Looting Enchantment. It goes on Weapons, and everytime you kill a Mob it has a chance to spawn a Corrupt Soul. 

These can then be killed to get them as Items. Try to do it quickly as they like to fly away. 

Maybe they know you want to kill them?

quests.title: Obsidian Skull
quests.description:
The Obsidian Skull is a Helmet that when worn can protect you from Fire/Lava damage! 

Overtime it will wear down to which you'll need to repair it with Obsidiansteel. 

That is also how you craft it, a Skeleton Skull with 8 Obsidiansteel.

quests.title: 52D4FCE72B15BC46
quests.description:
Ever want a "better Bucket"? Well you can with the Edelwood Bucket! 

For just a few Edelwood Planks you can get a better Bucket, which can hold 4 Buckets of Water or Milk. 

You can also hold 3 Buckets of Lava! It weighs more so you can only hold 3 instead of 4.

quests.title: 12D3C7FC4B3DAB23
quests.subtitle: An Eye on the environment
quests.description: The Environmental Eye can be made using the Ritual of the Forest and can be worn in your Charm slot to monitor the aura levels in the top left corner of the screen.

quests.title: Ancient Trees
quests.subtitle: Not those Ancient Saplings
quests.description: Ancient Saplings are created using the Ritual of the Forest. When they are grown, the trees attempt to maintain normal levels of aura (not too high or too low).\n\nIf the aura drops, the leaves will start to decay and reverse the process.

quests.title: Other Tokens
quests.description: You will need to craft these Tokens too for other items.

quests.title: Catalysts
quests.description: These Catalysts can be added as pillar toppers to your Natural Altar. They allow you to turn more items into other items or to break them down.\n\nThe Crumbling Catalyst allows you to turn each Gold Leaf into 4 Gold Powder instead of 2!

quests.title: Welcome to Nature's Aura
quests.description:
Nature's Aura is a magic mod about using and replenishing Aura. These quests will just go over some of the basics.

To get started, make some Brilliant Fiber which is made with Gold Nuggets, Leaves and Grass. Right-clicking on any leaves with Brilliant Fiber will turn them into Golden Leaves.

Make sure to read the Book of Natural Aura, you can also use it to show how to make the multiblocks in Nature's Aura.

quests.title: Gold Leaves
quests.subtitle: Aura with Fireflies
quests.description: Breaking Golden Leaves has a high chance to drop a Gold Leaf, which is needed for Gold Powder.

quests.title: Ritual of the Forest
quests.description:
